Parliament calls on the Philippine National Police and other law enforcement authorities to investigate at once the shooting of 2 young adults, both huffadh (memorizers of the Qur'an), in Shariff Aguak, Maguindanao del Sur, and to act decisively for justice and community safety.

It urges the Police Regional Office for the region to investigate impartially, arrest and prosecute the suspects, step up patrols and police visibility in Shariff Aguak, work with local governments, elders and religious leaders, support the victims' families, review security across Maguindanao del Sur, and report regularly to Parliament. Copies go to the regional police, the Ministry of Public Order and Safety, the Bangsamoro Human Rights Commission and the Office of the Chief Minister. Adopted on 11 February 2025.
readings.whyProposed: The 2 huffadh were shot in Shariff Aguak on 14 November 2024. The resolution calls the killing of people who devoted their lives to memorizing the Qur'an a wound to the moral and spiritual fabric of the community, and a threat to public safety and trust in law enforcement.
whoIsAffected: The families of the 2 victims.
Residents of Shariff Aguak and Maguindanao del Sur.
implementedBy: Philippine National Police
Police Regional Office – Bangsamoro Autonomous Region
Ministry of Public Order and Safety (copy furnished)
Bangsamoro Human Rights Commission (copy furnished)
whatChanges: Asks the regional police to report regularly to Parliament on the investigation, the only follow-up it sets.
Copies go to 4 named offices.
readings.insight: The resolution never names the victims. It was adopted 89 days after the shooting. Resolution 529, adopted the same day by the same 6 authors, concerns another shooting on the same date, 14 November 2024, in Datu Odin Sinsuat, and uses an almost identical 7-point list of demands. Filed by MP Tawakal B. Midtimbang, MP Mohammad Kelie U. Antao, MP Mosber E. Alauddin, MP Bassir D. Utto, MP Suwaib L. Oranon and MP Mudjib C. Abu.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament calls on the Philippine National Police and other law enforcement agencies to investigate thoroughly and at once the shooting of Engineer Darline Pacete in Datu Odin Sinsuat, Maguindanao del Norte, and to ensure justice, accountability and better security there.

It urges the Police Regional Office for the region to investigate impartially, prioritise arrest and prosecution, add personnel and intelligence work in Datu Odin Sinsuat and nearby towns, coordinate with local governments, protect and support the engineer and her family, assess public safety in the municipality, and submit a detailed progress report to Parliament. Copies go to the regional police, the Ministry of Public Order and Safety, the Bangsamoro Human Rights Commission and the Office of the Chief Minister. Adopted on 11 February 2025.
readings.whyProposed: Engineer Pacete was shot on 14 November 2024 in Datu Odin Sinsuat. The resolution describes her as a respected professional who contributes to the community's progress and condemns the attack as a threat to peace and security.
whoIsAffected: Engineer Pacete and her family.
Residents of Datu Odin Sinsuat and neighbouring towns.
implementedBy: Philippine National Police
Police Regional Office – Bangsamoro Autonomous Region
Ministry of Public Order and Safety (copy furnished)
Bangsamoro Human Rights Commission (copy furnished)
whatChanges: Asks the regional police for a detailed progress report to Parliament, with recommendations for systemic improvement.
readings.insight: The victim's first name is spelled 2 ways in the signed text: 'Darline' in the title and the first RESOLVED clause, 'Darlene' in the WHEREAS clause and the list of demands (confirmed on the page image). The resolution was adopted 89 days after the shooting, the same day and by the same 6 authors as Resolution 528 on the Shariff Aguak shooting of the same date, with the same structure. Filed by MP Tawakal B. Midtimbang, MP Mohammad Kelie U. Antao, MP Mosber E. Alauddin, MP Bassir D. Utto, MP Suwaib L. Oranon and MP Mudjib C. Abu.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament requests the Office of the Chief Minister to grant inflation relief assistance of at least ₱10,000 to every employee of the Bangsamoro Government, whatever their employment status, including contract-of-service and job-order workers, subject to the availability of funds. It asks that the money be released, as far as possible, before the end of March 2025.

A copy goes to Chief Minister Ahod Balawag Ebrahim. Adopted on 11 February 2025.
readings.whyProposed: Ramadhan was expected to begin on or about 28 February 2025, bringing extra household spending. The resolution cites the Philippine Statistics Authority's regional figures released on 7 January 2025: overall inflation fell from 6.3% in 2023 to 3.9% in 2024, but rose for health (0.8% to 2.1%), transport services (0.6% to 3.1%), housing and utilities (3.0% to 3.4%) and education services (5.0% to 6.8%). It notes the Bangsamoro Government has given similar assistance in past Ramadhans.
whoIsAffected: All Bangsamoro Government employees, including contract-of-service and job-order workers.
implementedBy: Office of the Chief Minister

funding.detail: At least ₱10,000 per employee, 'subject to the availability of funds'. No total cost or source of funds is named, and the resolution appropriates nothing.

whatChanges: A request to the executive. Whether to pay, and how much, is left to the Chief Minister and the funds available.
readings.insight: This is the 5th Ramadhan in a row in which Parliament adopted such a request: Resolution 120 in 2021 and 237 in 2022 (a Ramadhan allowance), 323 in 2023 (up to ₱15,000, excluding MPs, ministers and heads of office), 441 in 2024 (at least ₱10,000), and this one. The resolution's own figures show headline inflation falling by 2.4 points, so the case rests on specific categories and on Ramadhan. It gives no headcount or total cost. It has 29 authors, led by MP Susana S. Anayatin.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament strongly condemns the killing of Dr. Sonatria D. Gaspar, Assistant Schools Division Superintendent of the Ministry of Basic, Higher and Technical Education in Sulu, and urges the authorities to investigate justly, speedily and transparently.

It calls on the Bangsamoro Government, the regional police and the National Bureau of Investigation to investigate; urges the Bangsamoro and national governments to protect officials, educators and community leaders at risk; and asks civil society, religious leaders and communities to cooperate. Copies go to the education ministry, the Ministry of the Interior and Local Government, the PNP and the NBI Director. Adopted on 11 February 2025.
readings.whyProposed: On 7 February 2025 Dr. Gaspar was shot several times in the head inside her office in Barangay San Raymundo, Jolo, Sulu. The resolution calls her a dedicated public servant and says violence against educators and officials spreads fear and obstructs public services. Parliament extends condolences to her family and colleagues.
whoIsAffected: Dr. Gaspar's family and colleagues.
Teachers and education officials in Sulu.
implementedBy: Bangsamoro Government
Police Regional Office – Bangsamoro Autonomous Region
National Bureau of Investigation
Philippine National Police
whatChanges: A condemnation and a call to investigate. It asks for no report back to Parliament.
readings.insight: Adopted 4 days after the killing, much faster than the 89 days taken for Resolutions 528 and 529 adopted the same day. The victim was an official of a Bangsamoro ministry working in Sulu, a province the Supreme Court had by then excluded from the region with finality; the resolution does not address that. It has 7 authors, led by MP Eddie M. Alih.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament requests the Ministry of Basic, Higher and Technical Education to report to Parliament on the region's comparative education performance from school year 2018-2019 to school year 2023-2024.

A copy goes to the Ministry for appropriate action. Adopted on 12 February 2025.
readings.whyProposed: A government news report of 23 July 2024 said the Ministry expected 1,100,838 students for school year 2024-2025, against 1,079,253 the year before, counting public and private schools and local universities and colleges. The resolution wants performance indicators, including enrolment and participation rates at every level and in Madaris education, broken down by area so policy can respond to local differences.
whoIsAffected: Students and schools in the region, whose data would be reported.
Members of Parliament, who would use the report.
implementedBy: Ministry of Basic, Higher and Technical Education
whatChanges: A request for a report; no deadline or format is set.
readings.insight: The figures cited differ by 21,585 students, about 2%, though the text phrases the total as 'an increase of more than' 1,100,838. The request covers 6 school years and sets no deadline. Resolution 533, adopted the same day by the same author, asks the same ministry for a second report on textbooks, classrooms and teachers. Parliament last asked the ministry for a report in Resolution 81 in 2020, on the pandemic. Filed by MP Susana S. Anayatin.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament requests the Ministry of Basic, Higher and Technical Education to give it a comprehensive report on the current state of textbook availability, school buildings and classrooms, and teacher sufficiency.

A copy goes to the Ministry for appropriate action. Adopted on 12 February 2025.
readings.whyProposed: The resolution asks for 3 things in detail: textbook distribution, shortages and delays; the condition of school buildings and classrooms, including whether they need condemnation, demolition, repair or replacement and whether they have water, toilets and electricity; and the teacher workforce, including shortages and teacher-student ratios. It wants the data broken down by area and education level so resources can be distributed fairly.
whoIsAffected: Students and teachers in schools under the Ministry.
Members of Parliament, who would use the report.
implementedBy: Ministry of Basic, Higher and Technical Education
whatChanges: A request for a report; no deadline is set.
readings.insight: Adopted the same day as Resolution 532, by the same author, MP Susana S. Anayatin, to the same ministry; one of the WHEREAS clauses, on enrolment updates, appears word for word in both. Neither sets a deadline, and the repo holds no record of either report being delivered.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament congratulates Kakaw Meranaw for winning the AVPA Paris 2023 Medaille Gourmet for chocolate of local origin, and resolves to present the resolution to the enterprise.

Adopted on 16 November 2023.
readings.whyProposed: Kakaw Meranaw, a social enterprise making chocolate bars in Barangay Tagoranao, Bayang, Lanao del Sur, to give livelihood to Maranao cacao farmers, was the lone Philippine contestant at the 3rd International Contest for Chocolate Processed at Origin, run by the Agency for Valorization of Agricultural Products (AVPA) in Paris, and won the Medaille Gourmet on 25 April 2023. The resolution notes that the contest's 2 earlier editions tasted nearly 200 chocolates from some 20 countries.
whoIsAffected: Kakaw Meranaw and the Maranao cacao farmers of Barangay Tagoranao, Bayang, Lanao del Sur
whatChanges: A copy of the resolution is presented to Kakaw Meranaw.
Nothing else follows; it is a congratulation.
readings.insight:
The WHEREAS clauses record the government money already behind the winner: livelihood assistance from the Ministry of Trade, Investments and Tourism through the 2022 Transitional Development Impact Fund (TDIF) of MP Diamila Disimban Ramos, and assistance from the Ministry of Science and Technology through the 2023 TDIF of MP Rasol Y. Mitmug Jr., who is also the resolution's sole author. Neither amount is stated.

The text spells the enterprise both "Kakaw Meranaw" and, once, "Kakaw Maranao".

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament thanks the Mennonite Church of Canada for facilitating a study visit to Canada by members of Parliament, and acknowledges its role in making the visit a success. It commends Deputy Floor Leader MP Mary Ann M. Arnado for arranging the visit on Parliament's behalf, and states Parliament's commitment to use what was learned to improve its legislative practice and its relationship with indigenous communities in the region.

The resolution is presented to the Mennonite Church of Canada and furnished to MP Arnado. Adopted on 16 November 2023.
readings.whyProposed: Some members of Parliament travelled to Canada to study its legislative system, including the House of Commons and the Senate, and to meet indigenous communities there. The Mennonite Church handled the logistics, planning and running of the visit, which MP Arnado arranged with it.
whoIsAffected: The members of Parliament who joined the study visit
The Mennonite Church of Canada
MP Mary Ann M. Arnado
whatChanges: Copies go to the Mennonite Church of Canada and MP Arnado.
Parliament records a commitment to apply the visit's lessons, with no mechanism or report attached.
readings.insight:
The resolution does not say when the visit took place, how many members went, or who paid for travel. Its 22 authors, led by MP Lanang T. Ali Jr., include MP Arnado herself, so it is in part a commendation its subject co-signed.

It is one of a run of thank-you resolutions to foreign partners in this period; Resolution 411, adopted on 23 October 2023, thanked the Konrad Adenauer Stiftung for its work in the region since 2001.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament congratulates and commends Bai Rehana Marajan Lauban for ranking 9th in the October 2023 Fisheries Technologist Licensure Examination, along with all Bangsamoro passers, and resolves to present the resolution to her.

Adopted on 20 November 2023.
readings.whyProposed: The Professional Regulation Commission gave the exam on 25 to 26 October 2023 at 16 testing centres and announced on 6 November 2023 that 716 of 2,124 examinees, or 33.71%, had passed. Ms. Lauban, 23, a Maguindanaon from Kabuntalan, Maguindanao del Norte, and a cum laude graduate of Mindanao State University-Maguindanao, placed 9th with an average of 84.50%.
whoIsAffected: Bai Rehana Marajan Lauban
Bangsamoro passers of the October 2023 Fisheries Technologist Licensure Examination
whatChanges: A copy is presented to Ms. Lauban.
The other Bangsamoro passers are commended but not named or counted.
readings.insight: It consolidates 3 proposed resolutions (Nos. 453, 458 and 460) filed between 13 and 17 November 2023, and carries 9 authors led by MP Kadil M. Sinolinding Jr. It is one of roughly 30 adopted resolutions honouring Bangsamoro board and bar exam passers; in the preceding 2 months Parliament had also commended a psychometrician (Resolution 390) and a CPA topnotcher (Resolution 400).

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament grants a posthumous award and honour to Edison B. Morales for his contributions to education in Cotabato City and the Bangsamoro region, and furnishes the resolution to his family and to Albert Einstein School.

Adopted on 20 November 2023.
readings.whyProposed: Mr. Morales founded Albert Einstein School in Cotabato City in 1982. Under him the school produced regional and national finalists and champions in science, mathematics, cultural dance, essay writing and the arts, under the motto "Mens sana in corpore sano". The resolution cites a Parliament policy of honouring notable Bangsamoro figures so that their legacies are passed on.
whoIsAffected: The family of Edison B. Morales
Albert Einstein School, Cotabato City
whatChanges: Copies go to the Morales family and the school.
The "award" is the resolution itself; no medal, prize or money is attached.
readings.insight: The resolution does not give the date of Mr. Morales's death. Its sole author is MP Rasol Y. Mitmug Jr.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament urges the leaders of the Senate and the House of Representatives to prioritise creating the National Transitional Justice and Reconciliation Commission for the Bangsamoro (NTJRCB), and urges President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. to certify the bill as urgent.

Copies go to the Office of the President, the Senate President and the Speaker of the House. Adopted on 20 November 2023.
readings.whyProposed: The 2014 Comprehensive Agreement on the Bangsamoro required a Transitional Justice and Reconciliation Commission to document the grievances, historical injustices and human rights abuses suffered by the Bangsamoro and indigenous peoples. That commission reported in March 2016, and its core recommendations were a national transitional justice programme and the NTJRCB. 7 years on, neither exists. The resolution lists the bills filed to create it, from House Bill 5669 in the 17th Congress to House Bills 2975 and 4330 and Senate Bills 2043 and 2392 in the 19th, all still pending in committee, and warns the delay could affect the exit agreement under the peace deal.
whoIsAffected: Victims of the conflict whose grievances the commission would document
Both houses of Congress and the President
The peace process's normalization track
implementedBy: Senate of the Philippines
House of Representatives
Office of the President
whatChanges: Copies of the resolution go to the President, the Senate President and the House Speaker.
It binds none of them; certification as urgent is the President's call alone.
readings.insight: This is the 2nd time Parliament has asked for the same commission. Resolution 56, adopted on 24 January 2020, already called for the creation of the NTJRCB and a national transitional justice programme. Nearly 4 years passed between the 2, and in that time the bills were refiled in each new Congress. The repo does not record whether any of the 19th Congress bills passed. Its sole author is MP Mohagher M. Iqbal.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament reiterates its call for an unconditional ceasefire in Gaza and all the occupied territories of Palestine, calls for an end to violence and abuses in the West Bank, and urges the Bangsamoro Government to send aid and assistance to the people of Gaza by every appropriate means.

Copies go to the Office of the Chief Minister, the Department of Foreign Affairs, the embassies of Palestine and Israel, and the Organization of Islamic Cooperation. Adopted on 18 December 2023.
readings.whyProposed: More than 70 days into Israel's war on Hamas, the resolution recites the toll: civilian deaths above 11,000, more than 40% of them children, and a Euro-Med Human Rights Monitor report of 18 December 2023 of over 25,000 deaths, including 5,390 women and 10,091 children, more than 52,000 injured and over 1.85 million displaced. It cites more than 41,000 housing units destroyed and 222,000 damaged, 279 schools damaged as of 15 November 2023, and none of Gaza's 625,000 students able to attend school.
whoIsAffected: Civilians in Gaza and the West Bank
The Bangsamoro Government, urged to send aid
implementedBy: Office of the Chief Minister

funding.detail: The resolution appropriates nothing. It urges the Bangsamoro Government to send aid but names no amount or source of funds.

whatChanges: The Chief Minister's office receives a request to send aid, with no amount, channel or deadline.
The Department of Foreign Affairs, both embassies and the OIC receive copies.
readings.insight:
"Reiterating" is literal: Resolution 407, adopted 2 months earlier on 17 October 2023, condemned the collective punishment of Palestinians and called for an unconditional cessation of hostilities, and Resolution 124 in June 2021 condemned violence against Palestinians during Ramadhan. This one adds a concrete ask of the regional government: send aid.

The WHEREAS clauses carry 2 different death tolls side by side, "more than 11,000 civilians" and the Euro-Med figure of over 25,000, without reconciling them. 19 MPs authored it, led by MP Anna Tarhata S. Basman.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament strongly condemns the bombing of a religious gathering at the Dimaporo Gymnasium, Mindanao State University-Main Campus, Marawi City on 3 December 2023, and requests the appropriate government agencies to investigate it thoroughly and quickly. The resolution is forwarded to those agencies.

Adopted on 18 December 2023.
readings.whyProposed: A bomb exploded during a religious gathering at the gymnasium, killing 4 and injuring many others. The resolution cites the Organic Law's guarantees of religious freedom and protection from violence on account of religion, calls schools zones of peace, and quotes the Qur'an and a hadith to state that Islam prohibits such killing, including of non-Muslims under agreement with Muslims.
whoIsAffected: The victims and their families
Students and staff of Mindanao State University-Main Campus
implementedBy: Appropriate government agencies, unnamed
whatChanges: A copy is forwarded to "the appropriate government agencies", none of which is named.
No report back to Parliament is requested.
readings.insight:
It consolidates 8 proposed resolutions (Nos. 469, 470, 471, 473, 474, 476, 480 and 485) filed between 6 and 15 December 2023, and carries 42 authors led by MP Diamila D. Ramos, an unusually broad response. Yet the request for investigation names no agency, sets no deadline and asks for no update.

Parliament had condemned the 2020 Jolo twin bombings in similar terms in Resolution 88.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament congratulates and commends Abdulquddos D. Mohamad, champion of the 55-kg category, and Ahmadinnie Yusop U. Talapas, 2nd place in the 65-kg category, at the 1st KyokushinRyu World Tournament. Copies go to both athletes and to Sensei Engr. Usman Baraguir, newly elected Philippine country director of the International Karate Alliance KyokushinRyu.

Adopted on 15 January 2024.
readings.whyProposed: The tournament was held at the Caloocan Sports Complex on 11 to 12 November 2023, hosted by the International Karate Alliance, KyokushinRyu and Kyokushin Karate-do Philippines. Mr. Mohamad is of Iranun descent from Sultan Mastura and Cotabato City; Mr. Talapas is Maguindanaon from Cotabato City. The resolution cites the Organic Law's mandate to promote youth fitness through sports.
whoIsAffected: Abdulquddos D. Mohamad and Ahmadinnie Yusop U. Talapas
The IKAK Philippines country director
whatChanges: Copies go to the 2 athletes and the IKAK country director.
Nothing else follows; it is a commendation.
readings.insight: It consolidates 2 proposed resolutions (Nos. 459 and 467) and carries 20 authors led by MP Suharto S. Esmael. Athletes from the Cotabato and Sultan Mastura dojo were congratulated again in Resolution 475 of July 2024, for awards at the 19th National Full Contact KyokushinRyu Karate Tournament.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament commends the Bangsamoro scholars who graduated in Islamic studies from Al-Azhar University in Cairo, Egypt, and furnishes the resolution to them.

Adopted on 15 January 2024.
readings.whyProposed: 13 Bangsamoro scholars completed courses at Al-Azhar for academic year 2022-2023, and the resolution lists each by name and course, among them Shari'ah wal Qanoon, Shari'ah Islamia, Usuluddin majors in Hadith and Tafseer, and Kulliyyatu Da'wah. It calls Islamic scholars "the backbone of Bangsamoro liberation".
whoIsAffected: 13 Bangsamoro graduates of Al-Azhar University
whatChanges: Copies go to the 13 named graduates.
Nothing else follows; it is a commendation.
readings.insight: Its 7 authors are led by MP Abdulkarim T. Misuari. Parliament had commended an earlier cohort of Al-Azhar graduates in Resolution 362 of July 2023, and 6 weeks later commended 36 graduating students of the Islamic University of Madinah in Resolution 437.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament congratulates the new lawyers from the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region who passed the 2023 Bar Examination, and resolves to present the resolution to them.

Adopted on 15 January 2024.
readings.whyProposed: Results released on 5 December 2023 showed 3,812 of 10,387 examinees, or 36.77%, passed. The resolution notes that Mindanao State University-Marawi produced 23 passers and Notre Dame University in Cotabato City 32.
whoIsAffected: Bangsamoro passers of the 2023 Bar Examination
whatChanges: The resolution is to be presented to the new lawyers, who are not named or counted.
readings.insight: It is an annual fixture: Parliament congratulated Bangsamoro bar passers for 2019 (Resolution 71), commended the MSU and Notre Dame law schools for 94 new Bangsamoro lawyers in 2022 (Resolution 243) and for 46 in 2023 (Resolution 337), and commended the 2022 passers (Resolution 345). The 55 passers credited here are the 2 schools' totals, not a count of Bangsamoro lawyers. Its sole author is MP Susana S. Anayatin.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament commends Sakinur-ain Mugong Delasas of Tawi-Tawi for being proclaimed 1 of 9 Manlilikha ng Bayan by President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., and for safeguarding and promoting the Sama Igal dance tradition. The resolution is presented to her.

Adopted on 15 January 2024.
readings.whyProposed: Under Republic Act No. 7355, the Manlilikha ng Bayan or National Living Treasures award honours practitioners of traditional arts. Proclamation No. 427 named 9 awardees for 2023, among them Ms. Delasas, a Sama master of traditional dance from Simunul, Tawi-Tawi. The resolution describes the Igal as a fast but gentle dance rooted in worship and a mark of Sama identity.
whoIsAffected: Sakinur-ain Mugong Delasas
Sama practitioners of the Igal tradition
whatChanges: A copy is presented to Ms. Delasas.
Nothing else follows; it is a commendation.
readings.insight: It consolidates 3 proposed resolutions (Nos. 489, 490 and 491) and has 11 authors led by MP John Anthony L. Lim. Its first 2 RESOLVED clauses say the same thing twice. An earlier Manlilikha ng Bayan from the region, Ambalang Ausalin of Basilan, was honoured in a condolence resolution, Resolution 219 of February 2022.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament strongly requests the national Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) to prioritise the immediate repair, reconstruction, rehabilitation, improvement and maintenance of national highways and bridges in the Bangsamoro region, and furnishes the resolution to the DPWH central office.

Adopted on 15 January 2024.
readings.whyProposed: Under the Organic Law, the national government funds and maintains national roads and bridges in the region; the resolution counts about 992.62 km of national highway and 210 bridges under DPWH. Tropical Storm Paeng in October 2022 severely damaged the Nituan Bridge in Parang, Darapanan Bridge in Sultan Kudarat, Labu-labu 1 Bridge in Datu Hoffer, Oring Bridge in Buldon and Kusiong-Tapian Bridge in Datu Odin. The Quirino and Simuay bridges are worn by age, and the Cotabato-Alabel-Gensan National Highway and Narciso Ramos Highway are pitted with large potholes.
whoIsAffected: Commuters and traders using national roads and bridges in Maguindanao del Norte and del Sur
Residents near the bridges named
implementedBy: Department of Public Works and Highways (national)
whatChanges: The DPWH central office receives a copy.
It is a request; DPWH is not bound, and no deadline or report is set.
readings.insight:
It took 14 months to adopt. The 2 proposals behind it were filed on 14 and 17 November 2022, referred to the Committee on Public Works in December 2022, deferred in July 2023 and adopted on 15 January 2024 through Committee Report No. 8.

The same roads kept coming back. Resolution 511 of October 2024 asked the Intergovernmental Infrastructure Development Board to prioritise the Narciso Ramos Highway, and Resolution 559 of August 2025 urged DPWH to fast-track the renovation of Quirino Bridge, 2 of the assets this resolution named.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament congratulates Lanao del Sur 2nd District Representative Yasser Alonto Balindong on his election as a Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives in the 19th Congress, and presents the resolution to his office.

Adopted on 16 January 2024.
readings.whyProposed: Rep. Balindong was elected Deputy Speaker on 7 November 2023 and took his oath on 13 November 2023 before Speaker Ferdinand Martin Romualdez. The resolution lists his record: assemblyman of the old ARMM Regional Legislative Assembly from 2005 to 2016, representative since the 18th Congress, chair of the House Committee on Mindanao Affairs, an author of the Marawi Siege Victims Compensation Act of 2021, and filer of bills on Muslim cemeteries, a Marawi congressional library, internally displaced persons and raising Wao District Hospital from 25 to 100 beds.
whoIsAffected: Representative Yasser Alonto Balindong
whatChanges: A copy goes to the congressman's office.
Nothing else follows; it is a congratulation.
readings.insight: The resolution's own first WHEREAS clause identifies the congressman as the son of Parliament's Speaker, Atty. Pangalian M. Balindong, whose signature attests the resolution. Its sole author is MP Omar Yasser C. Sema. The 4 bills it lists were, by its own account, still in committee.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament commends and congratulates MP Sha Elijah B. Dumama-Alba on her designation as Minister of the Interior and Local Government, and the other MPs designated or re-designated to the cabinet. Copies go to the Minister and the re-designated members.

Adopted on 16 January 2024.
readings.whyProposed: After Chief Minister Ahod B. Ebrahim ordered all senior officials to tender courtesy resignations under Memorandum Circular No. 189, s. 2023, he named MP Dumama-Alba to replace Naguib Sinarimbo at the Ministry of the Interior and Local Government; she assumed office on 7 December 2023. The resolution lists the other moves: MP Anna Tarhata S. Basman as Attorney-General, MP Susana S. Anayatin as executive director of the Office of the Settler Communities, MP Said M. Sheik as Assistant Cabinet Secretary for the Marawi rehabilitation programme, and re-designations of Ministers Iqbal (education), Guerra (public works), Tago (transportation), Silongan (science) and Munoz (public order and safety).
whoIsAffected: MP Sha Elijah B. Dumama-Alba
The MPs designated or re-designated to the cabinet
whatChanges: Copies go to the new MILG Minister and the re-designated members.
Nothing else follows; the appointments were the Chief Minister's, not Parliament's.
readings.insight:
Parliament adopted 2 resolutions congratulating MP Dumama-Alba on the same appointment on the same day: this one, by MP Baintan A. Ampatuan, and Resolution 428, with 22 authors. Both proposals were filed on 15 December 2023. Resolution 430, adopted the same day, thanked the minister she replaced.

The WHEREAS clauses record that a majority of the cabinet must come from Parliament under the Organic Law, which is why a reshuffle here reads as a list of MPs.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament congratulates MP Sha Elijah B. Dumama-Alba and welcomes her as the new Minister of the Interior and Local Government, and presents the resolution to her office.

Adopted on 16 January 2024.
readings.whyProposed: The resolution calls hers a historic appointment as the 1st woman to head the Ministry of the Interior and Local Government. It cites her role as Parliament's Floor Leader, her degrees from UP Diliman and San Beda, a master's in public management, her Career Executive Service eligibility, her part in the GPH-MILF peace process and her last post as Bangsamoro Attorney-General.
whoIsAffected: MP Sha Elijah B. Dumama-Alba
whatChanges: A copy goes to MP Dumama-Alba's office.
Nothing else follows; it is a congratulation.
readings.insight: It duplicates Resolution 427, adopted the same day for the same appointment. The 2 differ only in emphasis: 427 also congratulates the other MPs moved in the reshuffle, while this one, led by MP Baileng S. Mantawil with 22 authors in all, adds the claim that she is the ministry's 1st female minister.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament congratulates sisters Dr. Ayeza-Saphia Tammang Madjid, Dr. Zerfa-Nishreen Tammang Madjid and Dr. Dana Tammang Madjid for passing the 2023 Physicians Licensure Examination, and presents the resolution to them.

Adopted on 16 January 2024.
readings.whyProposed: The Professional Regulation Commission announced on 10 November 2023 that 4,083 of 6,456 examinees, or 63.24%, passed. The Madjid sisters, twins aged 25 and a younger sister aged 24, are registered nurses from Jolo, Sulu, who studied nursing at the University of Santo Tomas and medicine at San Beda University. The resolution says they are the first siblings to pass the same examination simultaneously.
whoIsAffected: The 3 Madjid sisters of Jolo, Sulu
whatChanges: A copy is presented to the 3 sisters.
Nothing else follows; it is a congratulation.
readings.insight: The "record" claim, that they are the first siblings to pass the same exam together, appears in the resolution with no source. The signed text says it was adopted on 16 January 2024, matching the history of the proposal; Parliament's adopted-resolutions index lists it under 15 January. Its sole author is MP Susana S. Anayatin.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament expresses its appreciation, gratitude and commendation to former Minister of the Interior and Local Government Atty. Naguib G. Sinarimbo for his leadership as minister and his lifelong work for the Bangsamoro cause, and presents the resolution to him.

Adopted on 16 January 2024.
readings.whyProposed: The resolution recounts his record: a member of the MILF legal team in the peace negotiations, spokesperson of the BARMM government from its start, deputy secretary in the founding of the United Bangsamoro Justice Party, present in Marawi City during the siege supporting local officials, and a consultant to Senator Juan Miguel Zubiri during the Senate's passage of the Bangsamoro Organic Law.
whoIsAffected: Atty. Naguib G. Sinarimbo
whatChanges: A copy is presented to Atty. Sinarimbo.
Nothing else follows; it is a commendation.
readings.insight: It was adopted the same day as Resolutions 427 and 428 congratulating his successor, MP Sha Elijah B. Dumama-Alba, who is herself 1 of this resolution's 25 authors, led by MP Baileng S. Mantawil. The resolution does not say why he left the ministry; Resolution 427 places the change in a cabinet reorganisation that followed the Chief Minister's call for courtesy resignations.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament condemns the killing of Betty Cadulong Lu and her son Jonard Lu in Poblacion, Pikit, North Cotabato, extends condolences to their family, and calls on all concerned authorities to speed up the investigation. The resolution goes to the family and to local authorities, and asks government agencies in the region, particularly in Pikit, to disseminate it widely.

Adopted on 16 January 2024.
readings.whyProposed: On 9 January 2024, Mrs. Lu, a senior citizen who ran an eatery, was shot at her shop and the money she had earned that day was taken; her son, 47, chased the suspect and was also shot. Both died in hospital. CCTV caught the attack but not the suspects' faces; 4 men on 2 motorcycles were reported. Mrs. Lu's brother, Dr. Robert Cadulong, owner of Cadulong Hospital and a retired municipal physician, had been shot dead on 23 July 2021.
whoIsAffected: The Lu and Cadulong families
Residents of Pikit
implementedBy: Concerned authorities, unnamed
Government agencies in the region, asked to disseminate the resolution
whatChanges: Copies go to the bereaved family and to local authorities.
Agencies are asked to circulate the resolution in Pikit; no investigating body is named and no report is requested.
readings.insight:
The proposal was filed on 15 January 2024 and adopted the next day, 1 week after the killing; its sole author is MP Susana S. Anayatin. It draws from a radio report, Brigada News FM Cotabato City, and keeps a line from the draft calling the shooting "yesterday at noon".

It sits in a long series of condemnations of killings in and around the region, among them a doctor in Resolution 387 of August 2023 and, 5 weeks later, the ambush of a doctor in Resolution 434.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament urges the Ministry of Health to strengthen the voluntary blood donation programme and blood transfusion services in the region, and forwards the resolution to the ministry for immediate action.

Adopted on 16 January 2024.
readings.whyProposed: The resolution says that implementation gaps leave blood supply short, especially in rural areas, and stored where it is not needed. It cites 1st-to-3rd-quarter figures from the Cotabato Regional and Medical Center blood bank: in 2021, BARMM collected 6,505 units against demand of 27,089, while Region XII collected 12,849 against demand of 5,239; in 2022, BARMM collected 7,448 against 27,429, and Region XII 13,183 against 8,141. It invokes the National Blood Services Act of 1994.
whoIsAffected: Patients in the region who need transfusions
Blood donors and the Ministry of Health's blood services
implementedBy: Ministry of Health
whatChanges: The Ministry of Health receives the resolution for "immediate action".
No target, deadline or report back is set.
readings.insight:
The figures are the case. On the resolution's own numbers, BARMM met about 24% of demand in the first 3 quarters of 2021 and 27% in 2022, while neighbouring Region XII collected well over its demand both years. The resolution asks for a stronger programme without saying what that would be.

It was slow to pass: filed on 16 June 2023, referred to the Committee on Health, deferred on 16 November 2023 and 15 January 2024, and adopted on 16 January 2024 through Committee Report No. 45.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament expresses its sense in support of charter change to resolve the constitutional issues blocking full implementation of the Comprehensive Agreement on the Bangsamoro, and its full support for amending the 1987 Constitution for that purpose. It calls on the national government to entrench the Bangsamoro in the Constitution in the ongoing charter change discussion, and calls on stakeholders, civil society and indigenous peoples to join consultations to build support.

Copies go to the Office of the President, the Senate President, the Speaker of the House and the Philippine Congress-Bangsamoro Parliament Forum. Adopted on 21 February 2024.
readings.whyProposed: The peace process has 3 tracks, political, normalization and constitutional, and the constitutional track has not moved: parts of the peace agreement could not fit within the 1987 Constitution. With proponents of charter change aiming only at economic provisions, the resolution argues the moment should also carry peace provisions, listing the power-sharing between national and regional governments, the Shari'ah justice system, policing, regional supervision over local governments, the powers of constitutional bodies in the region, and the qualifications of the Chief Minister.
whoIsAffected: The Bangsamoro region and its government
Congress and the President, who would propose amendments
implementedBy: Office of the President
Senate of the Philippines
House of Representatives
Philippine Congress-Bangsamoro Parliament Forum
whatChanges: Copies go to the President, both houses and the Congress-Parliament forum.
It is a statement of position; it amends nothing and binds no one.
readings.insight:
This is the only adopted resolution in the registry on charter change, and it carries weight in its authorship: 27 authors led by Chief Minister Ahod B. Ebrahim, with MP Mohagher M. Iqbal and Speaker Pangalian M. Balindong. It consolidates proposed resolutions 521 and 509, the latter a call to entrench the "Bangsamoro narrative" in the Constitution.

Its list of amendments is specific and far-reaching, from policing to the Chief Minister's qualifications, but it names no text, process or deadline. The resolution notes that BTA members have sworn allegiance to the Constitution and argues it "is not cast in stone".

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament condemns in the strongest terms the ambush of Dr. Sharmaine Ceballos Barroquillo and calls on all concerned agencies of the Bangsamoro Government to speed up their investigation. Copies go to the Ministry of the Interior and Local Government, Police Regional Office-BAR, NBI-BARMM, the Ministry of Public Order and Safety and the Bangsamoro Human Rights Commission for appropriate action.

Adopted on 21 February 2024.
readings.whyProposed: On 3 February 2024, Dr. Barroquillo, a 28-year-old physician driving to work at Sultan Kudarat Provincial Hospital, was shot by 2 men on a motorcycle on a highway in Datu Paglas, Maguindanao del Sur. Wounded, she drove toward Buluan District Hospital, lost control, hit a tricycle and damaged a house, injuring its 4 passengers. An injury near her spine left her lower body unresponsive after multiple surgeries.
whoIsAffected: Dr. Sharmaine Ceballos Barroquillo and her family
The 4 injured tricycle passengers
Health workers travelling in the region
implementedBy: Ministry of the Interior and Local Government
Police Regional Office-BAR
NBI-BARMM
Ministry of Public Order and Safety
Bangsamoro Human Rights Commission
whatChanges: 5 named offices receive copies for appropriate action.
No deadline or report back is set.
readings.insight: Unlike many condemnation resolutions, this one names the agencies it is addressed to, 5 of them, though it still asks for no report back. It consolidates 3 proposed resolutions (Nos. 507, 514 and 517). Its 3 authors are MPs Kadil M. Sinolinding Jr., Susana S. Anayatin and Hashemi N. Dilangalen. Parliament had condemned the killing of another doctor, Dr. Marivic Tello, in Resolution 387 of August 2023.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament congratulates and commends Abdurahim Moh. Sali Abdulla for ranking 10th in the November 2023 Nursing Licensure Examination, along with all Bangsamoro passers, and presents the resolution to him.

Adopted on 26 February 2024.
readings.whyProposed: The exam was held on 11 to 12 November 2023 at 19 testing centres; the Professional Regulation Commission announced on 2 December 2023 that 25,761 of 32,203 examinees, or 80%, passed. Mr. Abdulla, a Tausug cum laude graduate of Western Mindanao State University in May 2023, placed 10th with 89.20%, the only Bangsamoro in the top 10.
whoIsAffected: Abdurahim Moh. Sali Abdulla
Bangsamoro passers of the November 2023 nursing exam
whatChanges: A copy is presented to Mr. Abdulla.
Nothing else follows; it is a commendation.
readings.insight: It consolidates proposed resolutions 475 and 499; the first was filed on 11 December 2023 and deferred before the 2 were merged, so the commendation came nearly 3 months after the results. It is one of roughly 30 adopted resolutions honouring Bangsamoro board and bar passers.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament commends President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. for establishing the Situmi'at Wakhamsun Aldhikra National Committee (SWANC) to commemorate the 650th anniversary of the Islamic presence in the Philippines in 2030, and presents the resolution to the Office of the President.

Adopted on 26 February 2024.
readings.whyProposed: Scholars place the arrival of Islam in the Philippines between 1350 and 1380, which the resolution says makes it the country's oldest monotheistic religion; the National Historical Institute marked 1380 with a historical marker in 1980. The President created SWANC through Administrative Order No. 10 to plan programmes for the 650th anniversary.
whoIsAffected: The Office of the President
Muslim Filipinos, whose history the commemoration marks
whatChanges: A copy goes to the Office of the President.
Nothing else follows; it is a commendation.
readings.insight: The resolution does not give the date of Administrative Order No. 10 or the committee's membership or budget. Its sole author is MP Hashemi N. Dilangalen. The title spells the committee "Situmia't" while the body spells it "Situmi'at".

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament commends and honours 36 Bangsamoro students graduating from the Islamic University of Madinah in Saudi Arabia in the fields of Islamic studies, and furnishes the resolution to them.

Adopted on 26 February 2024.
readings.whyProposed: The 36 students, listed by name and hometown, were due to graduate in 1445/2024 in Qur'an, Shari'ah, Da'wah and Usuluddeen, Arabic language, and law and judicial studies. The resolution describes the university, founded by royal decree in Medina in 1961, and notes that only Muslim men may attend.
whoIsAffected: 36 Bangsamoro students graduating from the Islamic University of Madinah
whatChanges: Copies go to the 36 students.
Nothing else follows; it is a commendation.
readings.insight:
It honours graduates in advance: the students "will graduate". Not all are from the region: the hometowns listed include General Santos City for 4 students, plus Polomolok, Isulan, Palimbang, Pagadian City and Naga, Zamboanga Sibugay. Because the university admits only men, all 36 are men.

It follows Resolution 422, adopted 6 weeks earlier, honouring 13 Al-Azhar graduates. Its 6 authors are led by MP Lanang T. Ali Jr.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament commends and congratulates Cotabato State University on its centennial, celebrated on 8 February 2024, and presents the resolution to the university.

Adopted on 26 February 2024.
readings.whyProposed: The university began as Cotabato High School on 8 February 1924, became Cotabato City National High School in 1977 and Cotabato City State Polytechnic College in 1983, and was converted into Cotabato State University by Republic Act No. 10585 on 24 May 2013.
whoIsAffected: Cotabato State University and its community
whatChanges: A copy is presented to the university.
Nothing else follows; it is a commendation.
readings.insight: Its sole author is MP Susana S. Anayatin. The same university hosts the 10th peace monument of the group honoured in Resolutions 439 and 440, adopted the same day.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament declares 24 January "Peace Day" in the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region, to be celebrated during the Bangsamoro Foundation Week, and furnishes the resolution to the region's ministries.

Adopted on 26 February 2024.
readings.whyProposed: The date comes from the Heavenly Culture, World Peace, Restoration of Light (HWPL), a peace group. On 24 January 2014 it brokered a civilian Mindanao Peace Agreement in General Santos City signed by then Maguindanao Governor Esmael G. Mangudadatu and Archbishop-Emeritus Fernando Capalla. Mangudadatu proclaimed 24 January as Peace Day in 2015; HWPL built peace monuments in Buluan and at Camp Darapanan, where the MILF leadership also proclaimed the day in 2016, and a 10th monument at Cotabato State University on 27 January 2023.
whoIsAffected: Ministries of the Bangsamoro Government
The HWPL
implementedBy: Ministries of the Bangsamoro Government
whatChanges: 24 January becomes Peace Day by declaration of Parliament, observed within Foundation Week.
It is not a holiday: the resolution suspends no work and sets no programme or budget.
readings.insight: The date marks a civilian agreement brokered by a single Seoul-registered NGO, the HWPL, not a government-MILF accord. Resolution 440, adopted the same day by the same 18 authors led by Chief Minister Ahod B. Ebrahim, endorses the same group's international declaration. The resolution does not refer to the Bangsamoro Holidays Act of 2023.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament supports the efforts of Heavenly Culture, World Peace, Restoration of Light (HWPL) to win recognition of its Declaration of Peace and Cessation of War (DPCW) as an international instrument of peace, and furnishes the resolution to all ministries in the region.

Adopted on 26 February 2024.
readings.whyProposed: The resolution describes HWPL as an NGO founded by Lee Man-Hee in 2013 and registered in Seoul, whose international law committee introduced the DPCW on 14 March 2016 and which wants it adopted as a binding covenant. It ties the declaration's principles to the 1987 Constitution's renunciation of war, and records that Chief Minister Ahod B. Ebrahim declared support for it at Camp Darapanan on 26 January 2023, saw HWPL's Religious Peace Academy open in Cotabato City on 23 August 2023, and signed a joint statement for its implementation in South Korea on 19 September 2023.
whoIsAffected: The HWPL
Ministries of the Bangsamoro Government
whatChanges: The region's ministries receive a copy for information.
Parliament goes on record behind an NGO's campaign for an international instrument; nothing in the region changes.
readings.insight: Parliament here endorses a specific organisation's document, not a principle, and the Chief Minister, who had already signed on for it, leads the 18 authors. The resolution gives HWPL's founder by name but says nothing more about the organisation beyond its own description. It pairs with Resolution 439, adopted the same day, which made the HWPL's 24 January anniversary the region's Peace Day.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament requests the Office of the Chief Minister to grant inflation relief assistance of at least ₱10,000 each to all employees of the Bangsamoro Government of whatever status, including contract of service and job order workers, to be released during Ramadhan 1445, subject to availability of funds. The resolution is forwarded to Chief Minister Ahod B. Ebrahim for appropriate action.

Adopted on 29 February 2024.
readings.whyProposed: The resolution cites the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas forecast of 2.8% to 3.6% inflation for January 2024, driven by rice, meat, fruit and fish prices, fuel, power and water rates, sin tax adjustments and a weaker peso, and the usual price rise during Ramadhan, expected to begin no earlier than 11 March 2024. It notes the regional government has granted similar Ramadhan relief before.
whoIsAffected: All Bangsamoro Government employees, including contract of service and job order workers
implementedBy: Office of the Chief Minister

funding.detail: The resolution appropriates nothing. It asks the Chief Minister to grant at least ₱10,000 per employee from available funds, and names no fund source or total cost.

whatChanges: The Chief Minister receives a request; the grant remains his decision and depends on available funds.
The request expressly covers contract of service and job order workers, not only regular employees.
readings.insight:
This is a yearly request. Parliament asked the Chief Minister for a Ramadhan allowance in Resolution 120 (2021), authorised one in Resolution 237 (2022), asked for inflation relief not exceeding ₱15,000 in Resolution 323 (2023), and asked again for at least ₱10,000 in Resolution 530 (2025). So the 2023 request set a ceiling of ₱15,000 and this one a floor of ₱10,000.

The repo does not record whether, or how much, was paid in 2024.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament adopts its calendar for the Third Regular Session of the Second BTA Parliament. The session opens on 14 May 2024 and then sits in 20 Monday-to-Thursday blocks, in the 3rd and 4th weeks of most months from May 2024 to February 2025, ending with mandatory adjournment on 27 February 2025.

There are no sittings scheduled in the first half of any month, and none between 25 July and 19 August 2024 or between 24 December 2024 and 20 January 2025. Adopted on 29 February 2024.
readings.whyProposed: Parliament's rules, Resolution No. 268, require it to convene each year on the 2nd Tuesday of the month after Eid al-Fitr, and to hold plenary sittings from 1 pm, Monday to Thursday, in the 3rd and 4th weeks of the month. A calendar sets the actual dates so members can plan legislative and constituency work.
whoIsAffected: Members and staff of Parliament
Anyone tracking when bills can move on the floor
implementedBy: Bangsamoro Parliament
whatChanges: Fixes the sitting dates for the Third Regular Session; this binds Parliament itself.
The week of 23 December 2024 is cut to 2 sitting days.
readings.insight:
Unlike most resolutions, this one has real force: it sets when Parliament can meet in plenary. It is part of an annual series, following Resolution 336 for the 2nd session and preceding Resolution 538 for the 4th, adopted on 18 February 2025, 9 days before this calendar's mandatory adjournment.

Counting the dates, the calendar schedules 79 sitting days, the opening day plus 19 4-day weeks and a 2-day week, across 9 and a half months: fewer than 10 a month.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament authorises all its parliamentary and statutory committees to hold meetings, hearings and consultations during the recess of the Second BTA Parliament, but not on Fridays. Members may join by Zoom at the committee's discretion. The resolution takes effect on adoption and stays in force until amended or repealed.

Adopted on 29 February 2024.
readings.whyProposed: The Second Regular Session adjourned sine die on 29 February 2024 under Resolution 336, with priority measures still pending, among them Parliament Bill No. 273, the proposed Bangsamoro Indigenous Peoples Development Act of 2024, and with inquiries in aid of legislation under way. The recess fell over Ramadhan, so committees are told to schedule around the fast.
whoIsAffected: Parliament's committees and their members
Resource persons called to hearings during recess
implementedBy: Parliamentary and statutory committees of the Bangsamoro Parliament
whatChanges: Committees may sit during the recess.
Fridays are off limits for committee work during recess.
Remote attendance by Zoom is allowed if the committee agrees.
readings.insight:
This is an internal rule that does bind Parliament, and it repeats yearly: Resolution 324 did the same in March 2023 and Resolution 539 in February 2025. It is open-ended, staying in force until amended or repealed, yet Parliament adopted a fresh one the next year anyway.

The bill it singled out did pass: Parliament Bill No. 273 became Bangsamoro Autonomy Act No. 64, the Bangsamoro Indigenous Peoples' Act of 2024, passed on 10 December 2024 and approved by the Chief Minister on 11 December 2024.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament commends and congratulates Brigadier General Nasser P. Lidasan, PhD, on his appointment by President Ferdinand R. Marcos, Jr. as Chairperson of the Government of the Philippines Coordinating Committee on the Cessation of Hostilities (GPH CCCH), and more broadly for his contributions to the Bangsamoro region and the country.

A copy of the resolution is to be presented to BGen. Lidasan, and the resolution is entered in the official records of the Bangsamoro Transition Authority. Adopted on 29 February 2024.
readings.whyProposed: The WHEREAS clauses record that BGen. Lidasan was the first Bangsamoro Muslim to become Assistant Commanding General of the Philippine Army's 6th Infantry Division, and that the President then named him to chair the government side of the ceasefire committee in the peace process. Authored by MP Baileng S. Mantawil.
whoIsAffected: BGen. Nasser P. Lidasan, PhD, the honoree.
whatChanges: Nothing outside Parliament. A copy goes to BGen. Lidasan and the resolution becomes part of the BTA's records.
readings.insight:
Parliament's index shows the proposal, Proposed Resolution No. 532, was filed on 28 February 2024 and adopted the next day, the closing stretch of the Second Regular Session. The proposal described the post as chair of the GPH-MILF ceasefire committee; the adopted title calls it the Government of the Philippines committee.

The title calls him the first Bangsamoro Muslim chairperson of the CCCH, but the body of the resolution attaches the word first only to his earlier post as Assistant Commanding General of the 6th Infantry Division. It does not say when the CCCH appointment was made.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament records its consensus that Sheikh Muslim Masaglang Guiamaden be appointed Wali, the ceremonial head of the Bangsamoro Government, under Article VIII of the Bangsamoro Organic Law (Republic Act No. 11054).

A copy goes to the Office of the Wali, addressed to Sheikh Guiamaden, for information. Adopted on 13 May 2024, at Special Session No. 4.
readings.whyProposed: The Organic Law provides for the Wali, and the Bangsamoro Administrative Code (BAA No. 13) requires Parliament to pass a resolution stating its consensus on a choice from a list of eminent residents submitted by the Council of Leaders. The Council met on 9 May 2024 and, in Council Resolution No. 01, Series of 2024, endorsed 2 names: Sheikh Guiamaden and Dr. Muhammad Nadheer Ebil. The resolution describes Sheikh Guiamaden as a former Chief Justice of the MILF Shari'ah Court in Camp Abubakar, born in 1963 in Buluan, Maguindanao del Sur, a 1989 Shari'ah graduate of the Islamic University of Madinah, and for 27 years associated with Qatar's Ministry of Endowments and Islamic Affairs. Authored by MP Sha Elijah B. Dumama-Alba, MP Raissa H. Jajurie, MP Anna Tarhata S. Basman, MP Mary Ann M. Arnado and MP Jose I. Lorena.
whoIsAffected: Sheikh Muslim Masaglang Guiamaden, selected as Wali.
The Bangsamoro Government, whose ceremonial head the Wali is.
implementedBy: Office of the Wali
whatChanges: This is the step the Administrative Code requires before a Wali is appointed: Parliament's recorded consensus on the Council of Leaders' list.
It names the choice; the resolution itself does not perform the appointment.
readings.insight:
This is the third Wali resolution in the index. Resolution No. 1 (29 March 2019) recorded consensus on Sheikh Khalipha Usman Nando, and Resolution No. 266 (21 September 2022) reaffirmed it. Resolution No. 315 (17 February 2023) mourned his death, and Resolution No. 327 (15 May 2023) authorised MP Said Z. Salendab to act as Wali only to open the Second Regular Session. The index has no Wali consensus between February 2023 and this resolution.

The Council of Leaders met on 9 May 2024. Proposed Resolution No. 570 was filed and adopted on 13 May, 4 days later. One clause credits Sheikh Guiamaden with more than 60 years of contributions; with a 1963 birth year, that is close to his whole life.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament thanks President Ferdinand R. Marcos, Jr. for appointing Sheikh Sabuddin N. Abdurahim as Secretary of the National Commission on Muslim Filipinos (NCMF), and congratulates Sheikh Abdurahim as the first Tawi-Tawian to hold the post.

Copies go to the President, Sheikh Abdurahim and the NCMF for their information and record. Adopted on 20 May 2024.
readings.whyProposed: The WHEREAS clauses describe the NCMF as central to the rights and welfare of Muslims in the Philippines and read the appointment of a Tawi-Tawian as a sign of inclusive representation among the country's Muslim communities. Filed in the name of all BTA Members; the adopted record lists the Government of the Day as author.
whoIsAffected: Sheikh Sabuddin N. Abdurahim, the new NCMF Secretary.
The Office of the President, thanked for the appointment.
whatChanges: Nothing beyond the copies sent to the President, Sheikh Abdurahim and the NCMF.
readings.insight: Proposed Resolution No. 549 was filed on 1 April 2024 and adopted 7 weeks later. Parliament has thanked a President for an NCMF appointment before: Resolution No. 231 (16 March 2022) thanked President Duterte for appointing, among others, Atty. Guiling A. Mamondiong as NCMF Secretary. Resolution No. 470, 2 months after this one, thanks President Marcos for another Bangsamoro appointee.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament congratulates and commends Al Hafidz Muzaher Suweb Bito for placing 3rd in the 27th Dubai International Holy Quran Competition 2024.

Copies go to the Office of the Chief Minister, the Bangsamoro Commission for the Preservation of Cultural Heritage and Bito himself, for their information and consideration. Adopted on 20 May 2024.
readings.whyProposed: Bito, 17 years old and from Datu Abdullah Sangki, Maguindanao del Sur, represented the Philippines in the competition held in the United Arab Emirates from 12 to 23 March 2024 among 70 contestants, and won a cash prize. The resolution cites Resolutions No. 97 and No. 306, which provide plaques for winners of international Qur'an competitions, and notes that Chief Minister Ahod B. Ebrahim presented him a plaque on 26 March 2024. Authored by MP Diamila D. Ramos, MP Jamel B. Macacua and MP Suharto S. Esmael.
whoIsAffected: Al Hafidz Muzaher Suweb Bito, the honoree.
whatChanges: Nothing new. The plaque the earlier resolutions provide for had already been given by the Chief Minister before this resolution was adopted.
readings.insight: 3 MPs filed separate proposals for the same win: Proposed Resolutions No. 550 (MP Ramos, 1 April 2024), No. 561 (MP Macacua, 30 April) and No. 566 (MP Esmael, 8 May), consolidated into this one. A similar honour went to Sabaha Pato Salik in Resolution No. 396 (19 September 2023) for 3rd place in Qur'an recitation at the 63rd Malaysian international assembly.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament commends Roslaine B. Maulana and Fatima Aiza R. Majad for ranking 3rd and 6th in the Philippine Academy of Microbiology (PAM) Certification Examination for Registered Microbiologists, and congratulates all Bangsamoro passers.

Copies go to Ms. Maulana and Ms. Majad as a token of recognition. Adopted on 21 May 2024.
readings.whyProposed: The examination was held on 20 and 21 January 2024 in Taguig. Ms. Maulana, an Iranun and Maguindanaon graduate of the University of Southern Mindanao from Sultan Mastura, Maguindanao del Norte, rated 84.45%. Ms. Majad, a Mindanao State University-Iligan Institute of Technology graduate from Tipo-Tipo, Basilan, rated 83.48%. Authored by MP Mosber E. Alauddin, MP Dan S. Asnawie, MP Muslimin A. Jakilan, MP Kadil M. Sinolinding, Jr. and MP Diamila D. Ramos.
whoIsAffected: Roslaine B. Maulana and Fatima Aiza R. Majad, the 2 topnotchers.
Bangsamoro passers of the examination, congratulated as a group.
whatChanges: Nothing beyond the copies given to the 2 honorees.
readings.insight:
The resolution gives 2 different totals for the same examination: one clause says PAM announced 213 successful examinees on 23 February 2024, and the next places Ms. Maulana 3rd among 1,203 passers. Both figures are on the adopted page.

It consolidates 3 proposals: No. 529 (filed 27 February 2024), No. 531 (28 February) and No. 536 (4 March). It is one of 5 resolutions in May and June 2024 honouring Bangsamoro licensure or certification results, with Nos. 449, 463, 468 and 469; MP Kadil M. Sinolinding, Jr. is an author of all 5.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament congratulates and commends 6 Bangsamoro topnotchers and all Bangsamoro passers of the February 2024 Respiratory Therapy Licensure Examination: Hannah Acosta Sangkay (3rd, 91.25%), Hafsin A. Eisa (6th, 90.50%), Muhammad Alnashri D. Ismail (8th, 90.00%), Abdul Salam S. Abdulhamid (9th, 89.75%), and Nadjahsalam G. Dimaudtang and Norliza S. Salamun (both 10th, 89.50%).

Copies go to the 6 as a token of recognition. Adopted on 21 May 2024.
readings.whyProposed: The Professional Regulation Commission gave the examination on 6 and 7 February 2024 and announced on 12 February that 1,077 of 1,383 examinees passed. The resolution counts 6 Bangsamoro examinees among the top 10 places. Authored by MP Kadil M. Sinolinding, Jr. and MP Diamila D. Ramos.
whoIsAffected: The 6 named topnotchers.
Bangsamoro passers of the examination, congratulated as a group.
whatChanges: Nothing beyond the copies given to the 6 honorees.
readings.insight:
3 of the 6 topnotchers studied at San Pedro College in Davao City; none of the 4 schools named is inside the region. The pass rate the resolution's figures imply is about 78%.

It consolidates 2 proposals: No. 530 (MP Sinolinding, 28 February 2024), which named only Ms. Sangkay, and No. 535 (MP Ramos, 4 March), which counted 5 topnotchers. The adopted text counts 6.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament strongly condemns the killing of Christhia "Thia" Angela O. Aragoncillo, a Logistics Management Officer at the Maguindanao Provincial Office of the Ministry of Social Services and Development (MSSD), and wishes a speedy recovery to a colleague injured in the same shooting.

Copies go to Ms. Aragoncillo's family, the injured colleague and the MSSD, for information. Adopted on 21 May 2024.
readings.whyProposed: On 17 April 2024 the MSSD issued a statement condemning the fatal shooting of Ms. Aragoncillo moments after she left her workplace; a colleague was wounded, and the gunman was unidentified. The resolution calls violence against government employees unacceptable and extends condolences to her family. Authored by MP Diamila D. Ramos, MP Eddie M. Alih and MP Susana S. Anayatin.
whoIsAffected: The family of Ms. Aragoncillo.
Her injured colleague.
MSSD staff.
whatChanges: Nothing beyond the condemnation and the copies sent. No office is asked to investigate.
readings.insight:
The WHEREAS clauses set up an investigation that the RESOLVED clauses never order. They cite the Bangsamoro Human Rights Commission's power to investigate under BAA No. 4, the jurisdiction of Parliament's Committee on Bangsamoro Justice System, and Parliament's power to form ad hoc committees for matters needing immediate action. None of these is invoked in what Parliament resolved.

The resolution consolidates 3 proposals filed on 22 and 23 April 2024. No. 557 called on authorities to expedite the investigation, and No. 558 was titled as a call for a swift and thorough investigation. Neither call survived into the adopted text. Parliament has condemned killings this way before, for example in Resolutions No. 387 (August 2023) and No. 434 (February 2024).

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament congratulates and commends Deputy Floor Leader and Social Services Minister Atty. Raissa H. Jajurie and MP Froilyn T. Mendoza for receiving the Philippine Daily Inquirer's 2024 Women of Power Award on 11 March 2024.

Copies go to the offices of Minister Jajurie and MP Mendoza. Adopted on 22 May 2024.
readings.whyProposed: The resolution cites the Constitution and the Organic Law on the role of women in governance. It summarises Atty. Jajurie's career (Ateneo and University of the Philippines Law, admitted to the Bar in 1995, more than 20 years with SALIGAN, co-founder of Nisa Ul Haqq Fi Bangsamoro, member of the MILF peace implementing panel and the Bangsamoro Transition Commission) and MP Mendoza's (a Teduray from South Upi, co-founder of the Teduray Lambangian Women Organization, 2019 N-Peace awardee, and the first indigenous woman on the transition commission that drafted the Basic Law in 2013). Authored by MP Susana S. Anayatin.
whoIsAffected: MP Raissa H. Jajurie and MP Froilyn T. Mendoza, both sitting members.
whatChanges: Nothing outside Parliament. It is Parliament commending 2 of its own members.
readings.insight:
Proposed Resolution No. 552 was filed on 8 April 2024 and became this resolution on 22 May. On 4 June 2024, 13 days after adoption, a second proposal for the same award was filed, No. 586 with 71 authors. The index still shows it as filed only.

Parliament adopted this on the same day as Resolution No. 453, which honours 3 more Bangsamoro women for a Mindanao Development Authority award.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament calls on the Bangsamoro Commission for the Preservation of Cultural Heritage (BCPCH) to lead the campaign to nominate the late Tausug artist Rameer Amilasan Tawasil for the 2025 Order of National Artists.

The resolution is forwarded to the BCPCH for its information, guidance and appropriate action. Adopted on 22 May 2024.
readings.whyProposed: The National Commission for Culture and the Arts and the Cultural Center of the Philippines had opened public nominations for 2025 National Artists. The resolution notes that sculptor and painter Abdulmari Asia Imao, named in 2006, is the first and only Muslim National Artist. Tawasil, who died in 2023, exhibited in Manila, London and Kuching, and his 2006 peace dove design received the Peace Citation Award. The BCPCH is named because the Organic Law gives it primary responsibility for the region's history and cultural institutions. Authored by MP Amilbahar S. Mawallil and 9 others.
whoIsAffected: The BCPCH, asked to lead a nomination campaign.
The family and legacy of Rameer Amilasan Tawasil.
implementedBy: Bangsamoro Commission for the Preservation of Cultural Heritage
whatChanges: A request to the BCPCH to prepare and file a nomination. Parliament does not nominate him itself, and the BCPCH is not obliged to act.
readings.insight:
This follows Resolution No. 343 (21 June 2023), which mourned Tawasil and commended his work. The repo does not record whether the BCPCH filed a nomination or what came of it.

The proposal, No. 553, was filed on 17 April 2024 and adopted 5 weeks later. The resolution sets no deadline, although the nomination window it cites was already open.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament congratulates and commends 3 Bangsamoro women who received the Mindanao Development Authority's first Mindanao Women in Development Awards in 2024: Dr. Sitti Zayda B. Halun, Social Security System Commissioner Bai Norhata M. Alonto, and Fatima Pepe Kanakan.

Copies go to the 3 women, MSU Tawi-Tawi College of Technology and Oceanography, the SSS, the Rajah Mamalo Descendants Organization of Southern Philippines, Inc., the Bangsamoro Women Commission and the Mindanao Development Authority. Adopted on 22 May 2024.
readings.whyProposed: The resolution recognises Dr. Halun for seaweed research at MSU Tawi-Tawi, Commissioner Alonto for work on gender equality and women's economic development, and Ms. Kanakan for advocacy for indigenous communities, particularly women. Authored by MP Eddie M. Alih and 71 others.
whoIsAffected: Dr. Sitti Zayda B. Halun, Commissioner Bai Norhata M. Alonto and Fatima Pepe Kanakan.
whatChanges: Nothing beyond the copies sent to the honorees and 5 institutions.
readings.insight: 72 MPs are listed as authors. Proposed Resolution No. 564 was filed on 3 May 2024. Parliament adopted it on the same day as Resolution No. 451, which honours 2 of its own members for a different women's award.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament expresses its deepest condolences to the family of the late Rostom Saaban, 3rd Base Commander of the 106th Base Command of the Southern Mindanao Front.

The resolution is presented to his family. Adopted on 22 May 2024.
readings.whyProposed: Saaban, from Barangay Malibpolok, Rajah Buayan, Maguindanao del Sur, joined the Bangsamoro struggle in the 1970s, taught the Qur'an in Camp Abubakar and lived a low-profile life. He died before Fajr on 24 March 2024. The resolution also thanks him for his philanthropy to the region. Authored by MP Ahod Balawag Ebrahim and 40 others.
whoIsAffected: The family of the late Rostom Saaban.
whatChanges: Nothing beyond the copy presented to the family.
readings.insight: Chief Minister Ahod Balawag Ebrahim is the first of 41 authors. Proposed Resolution No. 569 was filed on 8 May 2024, about 6 weeks after the death. Parliament passed a similar condolence for a base commander in Resolution No. 270 (21 September 2022), for Abdulwalid "Jimmy" M. Radiamoda of the 122nd Base Command.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament asks the Ministry of Health (MOH) for a progress report on the immunisation of babies and children in the region, including updates on its information campaign, and for its action plans to reach the region's target immunisation rate.

The resolution is forwarded to the MOH for proper action. Adopted on 22 May 2024.
readings.whyProposed: The resolution cites a 2019 World Bank household survey: only 34% of children aged 12 to 23 months had basic vaccine coverage, 24% had no vaccine history, 25% to 50% who got a first dose missed the 2nd and 3rd, only 50% of respondents had heard why all recommended vaccines matter, and only 8.2% knew to return for later doses. It also cites the Department of Health's 2021 Field Health Services Information System: about 61% of eligible children fully vaccinated, against a 95% target and a 63% national average. Authored by MP Hashemi N. Dilangalen, MP Eddie M. Alih, MP Amilbahar S. Mawallil and MP Hamid U. Malik.
whoIsAffected: Babies and children in the region, and their parents.
The Ministry of Health, asked to report.
implementedBy: Ministry of Health
whatChanges: A request to the MOH for a progress report and an action plan. It sets no deadline and no format.
readings.insight:
The title says the resolution requires a report, but its clauses only call on and urge the MOH. There is no deadline and no committee to receive the report.

Proposed Resolution No. 189 was filed on 20 February 2023, referred to the Committee on Health in July 2023, and adopted with Committee Report No. 44 on 22 May 2024, 15 months later. By then its newest figures were from 2021. Parliament had already directed its Committee on Health to inquire into vaccination in Resolution No. 378 (27 July 2023), and earlier asked the MOH about vaccines in Resolutions No. 107 (2021) and No. 212 (2022).

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament urges the Office of the Civil Registrar General, the Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA) and the Shari'ah courts to reiterate strict adherence to the registration of Muslim divorces under Administrative Order No. 1, Series of 2005.

Copies go to the same offices for appropriate action. Adopted on 22 May 2024.
readings.whyProposed: Under the 2005 order, a Muslim husband who pronounces talaq must file written notice with the Clerk of Court of the Shari'ah Circuit Court, and 5 copies of the certificate of divorce or court decree must be submitted for registration within 30 days. Those copies go to the husband, the wife, the Civil Registrar General, the District Registrar and the court's file. The resolution observes that most people do not register divorces, and that the PSA issues birth, marriage and death certificates but has no certification for Muslim divorce. It quotes the penalties in the Code of Muslim Personal Laws: arresto mayor or a fine of ₱200 to ₱2,000 under Article 183, and ₱100 to ₱1,000 for failure to report under Article 184. Authored by MP Suharto S. Esmael and 5 others.
whoIsAffected: Muslim couples who divorce, whose divorce goes unrecorded if it is not registered.
Shari'ah Circuit Court clerks and civil registrars.
implementedBy: Office of the Civil Registrar General
Philippine Statistics Authority
Shari'ah courts
whatChanges: An appeal to national offices outside the region's control to remind the public of an existing rule. It changes no rule and creates no new duty.
readings.insight:
The resolution names a system gap, that the PSA has no Muslim divorce certification, but asks only for strict adherence to the existing order. It does not ask the PSA to create the missing certificate. The copy clause names the Office of Civil Registrar, dropping the word General used in the title.

Proposed Resolution No. 246 was filed on 17 May 2023, referred to the Committee on Bangsamoro Justice System, and adopted with Committee Report No. 53 a year later.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament asks the Philippine Judicial Academy (PHILJA) to offer a separate Pre-Judicature Program for applicants for judgeships in the Shari'ah courts within the region.

The resolution is forwarded to the Judicial and Bar Council (JBC) for its consideration. Adopted on 22 May 2024.
readings.whyProposed: Under the 2020 Revised JBC Rules, all judicial applicants must complete PHILJA's Pre-Judicature Program, except those applying to Shari'ah Circuit Courts outside the region. The resolution says the program's syllabus mostly covers regular Philippine law, not the Code of Muslim Personal Laws and the special procedural rules Shari'ah courts apply, and that a separate program would encourage qualified candidates. The JBC opened applications for judgeships in Regions IX to XII on 19 May 2023. Authored by MP Sha Elijah B. Dumama-Alba.
whoIsAffected: Applicants for Shari'ah judgeships in the region.
Litigants in Shari'ah courts, who depend on those posts being filled.
implementedBy: Philippine Judicial Academy
Judicial and Bar Council
whatChanges: A request to a national judicial body that Parliament cannot direct. The only office actually sent a copy is the JBC, not PHILJA.
readings.insight:
The addressee and the recipient differ because the request changed. The original proposal, No. 297 (filed 15 June 2023), asked the JBC to exempt Shari'ah applicants in the region from PHILJA's program altogether. It was amended through Committee Report No. 54 into a request that PHILJA offer a separate program, but the copy still goes only to the JBC.

Vacancies remained an issue afterwards. Resolution No. 516 (23 January 2025) asked the President, through the JBC, to appoint judges to vacant Shari'ah district courts.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament asks the Supreme Court to facilitate the immediate organisation of the Shari'ah High Court in the region.

Copies go to the Office of the Chief Justice, the Office of the Clerk of Court and the Office of the Court Administrator. Another goes to the Philippine Congress-Bangsamoro Parliament Forum for inclusion on its agenda, and another to Chief Minister Ahod Balawag Ebrahim for favourable endorsement to the Supreme Court. Adopted on 22 May 2024.
readings.whyProposed: The Organic Law creates a Shari'ah High Court of 5 Justices, including a Presiding Justice. Its Justices have the rank and pay of Court of Appeals Justices, and it hears appeals from Shari'ah courts inside and outside the region. Its decisions are final except on questions of law. Until it is organised, Shari'ah court decisions go to the Court of Appeals. The Supreme Court appoints its personnel, and the Bangsamoro Administrative Code lets Parliament recommend that it be completely organised in Cotabato City. The resolution notes that a Shari'ah appellate court was first provided for in Republic Act No. 6734, the first ARMM Organic Act. Authored by MP Don Mustapha A. Loong and 11 others.
whoIsAffected: Parties appealing Shari'ah court decisions, which now go to the Court of Appeals.
The Supreme Court, which alone can organise and staff the court.
implementedBy: Supreme Court of the Philippines
Office of the Chief Minister, for endorsement
Philippine Congress-Bangsamoro Parliament Forum
whatChanges: A request to the Supreme Court, which Parliament cannot direct.
It routes the matter through the Chief Minister and the intergovernmental forum as well.
readings.insight:
The 2nd WHEREAS clause cites the Organic Law as Republic Act No. 11504; it is Republic Act No. 11054. The typo is on the adopted page.

Proposed Resolution No. 311 was filed on 19 June 2023 and adopted, as amended, with Committee Report No. 55, 11 months later. The repo does not record whether the High Court has been organised. In August 2024 Parliament thanked Congress and the President for Republic Act No. 12018 (Resolution No. 488), which adds 3 Shari'ah judicial districts and 12 circuit courts, not the High Court.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament urges the Bangsamoro Government to prohibit the use of vapes, e-cigarettes and other vaporized nicotine and non-nicotine products inside its office premises, except in designated vaping areas.

The resolution is forwarded to the Office of the Chief Minister for information and appropriate action. Adopted on 22 May 2024.
readings.whyProposed: The resolution relies on Republic Act No. 11900, the Vaporized Nicotine and Non-Nicotine Products Regulation Act, which lapsed into law on 25 July 2022. Section 15 already bans vaping in all indoor public places except designated vaping areas, and within the buildings and premises of government offices.
