Section 17 sets standards for those areas: signage barring under-18s and pregnant women, no location within 10 metres of entrances or exits, no more than 1 per building, and separate ventilation. The resolution adds that some substances in e-cigarette vapour are linked to cancer. Authored by MP Baintan A. Ampatuan.
whoIsAffected: Employees and visitors in Bangsamoro Government offices.
implementedBy: Office of the Chief Minister
whatChanges: A request to the executive to apply a ban that national law already imposes on government offices. It does not itself prohibit anything.
readings.insight:
The proposal, filed on 24 July 2023 and referred to the Committee on Health, was titled a resolution prohibiting vaping in the Bangsamoro Government Center. It was adopted as amended 10 months later as a resolution urging the government to prohibit it. The rule it asks for is already in Republic Act No. 11900, and its implementing rules require every government agency to enforce it.

The adopted copy's header reads Proposed Resolution No. 346, but Parliament's index lists this proposal as No. 364. No. 346 is a different resolution by the same MP, on rules for learners with disabilities.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament congratulates and commends the Mindanao State University Karate Club's athletes for their medals at the 5th Karate Pilipinas National Championship in Tagaytay City: gold for Abdulhakim A. Abdulrakim (Junior Male Kumite, -76kg), silver for Ahmad G. Ali III (Junior Male Kata), and bronze for Al-majeed C. Alonto (U21 Men's Kumite, +84kg), Pipay Minalang (Senior Female Kumite, -56kg) and Duma G. Sani II (8 to 9 Years Old Boys Kumite, +140cm).

Copies go to the 5 athletes. Adopted on 18 June 2024.
readings.whyProposed: The championship ran from 1 to 3 March 2024 at the Tagaytay Combat Sports Center with 60 teams and 1,231 athletes, organised by Karate Pilipinas, the federation recognised by the World Karate Federation, the Asian Karate Federation and the Philippine Olympic Committee. The club is led by Hanshi Prof. Punduma B. Sani, former dean of MSU-Marawi's College of Sports, Physical Education and Recreation. Authored by MP Diamila D. Ramos.
whoIsAffected: The 5 named MSU Karate Club athletes.
whatChanges: Nothing beyond the copies given to the 5 athletes.
readings.insight: 5 medals: 1 gold, 1 silver and 3 bronze. Proposed Resolution No. 551 was filed on 1 April 2024 and adopted 11 weeks later. It is one of 4 resolutions honouring Mindanao State University or its people adopted between 18 and 24 June 2024, with Nos. 461, 463 and 466.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament congratulates the Mindanao State University-Sining Kambayoka Ensemble on winning Outstanding Cultural Theater Group at the Philippine Live Entertainment, Arts, and Festival (LEAF) Awards.

The resolution is presented to the ensemble. Adopted on 19 June 2024.
readings.whyProposed: The ensemble received the award at the Metropolitan Theater on 8 February 2024. Founded at MSU-Marawi in 1974, it stages productions drawn from the cultures of Mindanao's tri-peoples, particularly the Meranaw, and is described as the only folk theatre group in the country that established and popularised the Kambayoka theatre form. Authored by MP Rasol Y. Mitmug, Jr.
whoIsAffected: The MSU-Sining Kambayoka Ensemble.
whatChanges: Nothing beyond the copy presented to the ensemble.
readings.insight: Proposed Resolution No. 533 was filed on 29 February 2024, deferred on 22 May and adopted on 19 June, 4 months after the award. It is one of 4 MSU-related commendations adopted in the same week, with Nos. 460, 463 and 466.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament congratulates and commends the Commission on Elections (COMELEC), the security sector, the Ministry of Basic, Higher and Technical Education and the Provincial Government of Cotabato for the orderly and peaceful plebiscite in the 63 barangays of the Special Geographic Area that ratified the creation of 8 new municipalities.

Copies go to the same bodies. Adopted on 19 June 2024.
readings.whyProposed: COMELEC held the plebiscite on 13 April 2024. The resolution reports that 72,658 of 89,954 eligible voters cast ballots, with 72,358 voting yes and 273 no. The new towns are Pahamuddin (12 barangays), Tugunan (9), and Kadayangan, Nabalawag, Old Kaabakan, Kapalawan, Malidegao and Ligawasan (7 each), carved from barangays of Aleosan, Carmen, Kabacan, Midsayap, Pigcawayan and Pikit in Cotabato that joined the region in the 2019 plebiscite. Authored by MP Susana S. Anayatin.
whoIsAffected: Residents of the 63 Special Geographic Area barangays, now 8 municipalities.
COMELEC, the police, the military, MBHTE teachers and the Cotabato provincial government, commended.
whatChanges: Nothing new. The municipalities were created by Parliament's own acts and ratified by the vote; this resolution only commends those who ran it.
readings.insight:
The 8 municipalities are the ones created by BAA Nos. 41 to 48, and this plebiscite ratified those acts. The resolution states turnout as 81.10%, but its own figures, 72,658 of 89,954, work out to 80.77%. Both are printed on the adopted page.

Parliament commended much the same bodies for the 2022 plebiscite that divided Maguindanao, in Resolution No. 272. This proposal, No. 556, was filed on 22 April 2024.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament congratulates and commends Engr. Saadany Panumpang Aminoden and Mindanao State University-Main Campus for his 4th-place finish in the 2024 Registered Electrical Engineers Licensure Examination, and all Bangsamoro passers.

Copies go to Engr. Aminoden and MSU-Main Campus. Adopted on 19 June 2024.
readings.whyProposed: The Professional Regulation Commission announced on 2 May 2024 that 4,436 of 7,005 examinees passed. Engr. Aminoden, from Tugaya, Lanao del Sur, and a magna cum laude graduate of MSU-Main Campus, placed 4th with a general average of 93.50%. Authored by MP Kadil M. Sinolinding, Jr.
whoIsAffected: Engr. Saadany Panumpang Aminoden.
Mindanao State University-Main Campus.
whatChanges: Nothing beyond the copies given to the honoree and the university.
readings.insight: Proposed Resolution No. 571 was filed on 13 May 2024 for Engr. Aminoden alone and was adopted as amended to add his university. It is one of 5 exam-result commendations adopted in May and June 2024, all with MP Sinolinding among the authors.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament condemns the grenade attack on 19 May 2024 at Sto. Niño Chapel, Purok Bagong Silang, Rosary Heights 3, Cotabato City, and appeals to the concerned authorities to expedite the investigation and bring the perpetrators to justice.

A copy goes to concerned authorities, for information. Adopted on 19 June 2024.
readings.whyProposed: A hand grenade exploded inside the chapel during the Liturgy of the Word on Pentecost Sunday. Police reported 2 people injured: Marybel Atis, 40, and Rosita Tubilo, 65. The resolution recalls the bombing of a Catholic mass at the MSU gymnasium in Marawi 5 months earlier (4 dead, 50 injured) and the January 2019 Jolo cathedral bombings. It warns that such attacks make settler communities afraid to worship, and cites the Organic Law's guarantee of religious freedom and the Anti-Terrorism Act's definition of terrorism. Authored by MP Susana S. Anayatin and MP Diamila D. Ramos.
whoIsAffected: The 2 people injured and the chapel's congregation.
Settler and Christian communities in Cotabato City.
whatChanges: An appeal to unnamed authorities. The copy clause names no agency, so no specific office is asked to report back.
readings.insight: The investigation appeal is addressed to concerned authorities and the copy goes to concerned authorities, so no office is named. The Jolo clause gives the injured as eighty in words and 82 in figures, on the adopted page. Parliament condemned the Marawi gymnasium bombing in Resolution No. 420 (18 December 2023). Proposed Resolution No. 577 was filed on 21 May 2024, 2 days after the attack.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament urges the Bangsamoro Government, through the Ministry of Transportation and Communications (MOTC), the Ministry of Trade, Investments and Tourism (MTIT) and the Bangsamoro Board of Investments (BBOI), to promote, encourage and incentivise investment in maritime transport and logistics, especially in the island provinces.

Copies go to the 3 offices for information and appropriate action. Adopted on 19 June 2024.
readings.whyProposed: The resolution argues that shipping is the main link between islands and that private shipping lines need incentives to serve the region's ports. It cites the Organic Law's grant to the region of power over regional franchises for sea transport, and the Domestic Shipping Development Act of 2004 (Republic Act No. 9295), which offers incentives to domestic ship operators and lets them set their own rates. It asks the 3 offices to come up with an incentive and coordinated program. Authored by MP Baintan A. Ampatuan.
whoIsAffected: Residents and traders of the region's island provinces.
Shipping operators who might invest in the region's routes.
implementedBy: Ministry of Transportation and Communications
Ministry of Trade, Investments and Tourism
Bangsamoro Board of Investments
whatChanges: A request to 3 executive offices. It names no incentive, route, port, budget or deadline.
readings.insight: Proposed Resolution No. 217 was filed on 13 April 2023 and adopted with Committee Report No. 50, 14 months later. A related proposal on maritime programmes, No. 253, filed in May 2023, was referred to the Committee on Transportation and Communications and is not shown as adopted. The resolution names no island province or port.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament congratulates Mindanao State University Main Campus-Marawi on being ranked the top university in Mindanao and 10th in the Philippines in the latest EduRank ranking.

Copies go to the MSU President, the Chancellor of the Marawi campus, the Ministry of Basic, Higher and Technical Education and relevant stakeholders. Adopted on 24 June 2024.
readings.whyProposed: The resolution traces MSU's origins to the Hadji Kamlon uprising, a Congressional committee study of conditions in Mindanao, and the Commission on National Integration (1957), leading to the university's founding on 1 September 1961 under Republic Act No. 1387. Its mandate was to widen education for Muslims and other cultural minorities in the south. Filed in the name of all BTA Members; the adopted record lists the Government of the Day as author.
whoIsAffected: Mindanao State University Main Campus-Marawi.
whatChanges: Nothing beyond the copies sent, which ask for appropriate action without saying what action.
readings.insight: Proposed Resolution No. 540 was filed on 19 March 2024 and adopted 3 months later. Parliament has honoured MSU-Marawi before: Resolution No. 149 marked its 60th anniversary in 2021, and Resolution No. 273 (October 2022) commended its 6th-place national ranking in the September 2022 social worker licensure examination. This is one of 4 MSU-related commendations adopted between 18 and 24 June 2024.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament thanks the Support to Bangsamoro Transition (SUBATRA) programme for supporting the benchmarking visit of Parliament's Committee on Women, Youth, Children and Persons with Disabilities to the House of Representatives and the Senate.

Copies go to the SUBATRA office, the House Speaker and the House Committee on Women and Gender Equality, and the Senate Committee on Women, Children, Family Relations and Gender Equality and the Senate President. Adopted on 24 June 2024.
readings.whyProposed: SUBATRA is a 5-year programme funded by the European Union and co-financed by the Spanish Agency for International Development Cooperation. It had supported the committee's staff training and planning, and facilitated a 3-day benchmarking visit from 7 to 9 May 2024, covering most of the costs: transport, hotel and meals. The resolution lists what the members took away: oversight of laws on women, public consultation, intersectionality, using the Gender and Development budget, a proposed sisterhood agreement with the House committee, and a reciprocal House committee visit to the region. Authored by MP Diamila D. Ramos and 9 others.
whoIsAffected: The committee members and staff who made the trip.
SUBATRA, thanked as funder.

funding.detail: The resolution appropriates nothing. It records that SUBATRA, an EU-funded programme co-financed by the Spanish Agency for International Development Cooperation, covered most of the visit's transport, hotel and meal costs, without stating an amount.

whatChanges: Nothing beyond the copies sent. The sisterhood agreement and reciprocal visit appear only as takeaways, not as anything Parliament resolved to do.
readings.insight:
Every MP the resolution names on the delegation is also among its 10 authors, so the members are thanking the programme that paid for their trip. The resolution gives no cost figure.

3 separate proposals were filed on 28 May 2024 to thank the House committee (No. 583), the Senate committee (No. 584) and SUBATRA (No. 585). They were merged into one resolution whose title and RESOLVED clause thank only SUBATRA; the 2 congressional committees get copies.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament congratulates and commends 3 Bangsamoro topnotchers in the May 2024 Certified Public Accountant Licensure Examination, Abdel-Nasher Sarail Tanggor and Norjannah Khalid Tanoga (both 7th, 89.67%) and Rustom Dipaling Lamosao (10th, 89.17%), and all Bangsamoro passers.

Copies go to the 3 topnotchers. Adopted on 27 June 2024.
readings.whyProposed: The Professional Regulation Commission released results on 1 June 2024: 3,155 of 10,421 examinees passed, 30.275%. Mr. Tanggor graduated from MSU-Iligan Institute of Technology and lives in Bayang, Lanao del Sur; Ms. Tanoga graduated from MSU-Marawi and lives in Cotabato City; Mr. Lamosao graduated from Notre Dame University and lives in Cotabato City. Authored by MP Kadil M. Sinolinding, Jr.
whoIsAffected: The 3 named topnotchers.
Bangsamoro passers, congratulated as a group.
whatChanges: Nothing beyond the copies given to the 3 honorees.
readings.insight: Parliament has honoured Bangsamoro CPA results several times: Resolution No. 257 (5th place, 2022), No. 360 (2nd place, May 2023) and No. 400 (topnotcher, September 2023). Proposed Resolution No. 587 was filed on 4 June 2024 and adopted 23 days later.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament congratulates and commends 7 Bangsamoro topnotchers in the March 2024 Licensure Examination for Professional Teachers, and all Bangsamoro passers. At elementary level: Fatmah Aliah T. Mandi (8th, 91.00%), Naharah D. Abdulazis and Rahima A. Akmad (both 9th, 90.80%) and Hanania P. Dimacaling (10th, 90.60%). At secondary level: Kawther Sacor I. Abdulhalim and Nidzraleen J. Abdurahim (both 9th, 91.00%) and Almira O. Mimbala (10th, 90.80%).

Copies go to the 7. Adopted on 27 June 2024.
readings.whyProposed: The examination was held on 17 March 2024 at 36 testing centres, with results released on 24 March. 20,890 of 44,764 elementary examinees passed (46.67%), and 50,539 of 85,980 secondary examinees (58.78%). Authored by MP Kadil M. Sinolinding, Jr.
whoIsAffected: The 7 named topnotchers.
Bangsamoro passers, congratulated as a group.
whatChanges: Nothing beyond the copies given to the 7 honorees.
readings.insight: All 7 topnotchers are women. Earlier teacher-exam commendations include Resolutions No. 205, No. 309, No. 339 and No. 340. Proposed Resolution No. 588 was filed on 10 June 2024, and Parliament adopted it the same day as Resolution No. 468.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament thanks President Ferdinand R. Marcos, Jr. for appointing Amilbahar P. Amilasan Jr. as Acting Chairman and Chief Executive Officer, and Member of the Board of Directors, of Al-Amanah Islamic Investment Bank of the Philippines, and congratulates Mr. Amilasan.

Copies go to the Office of the President and Mr. Amilasan. Adopted on 15 July 2024.
readings.whyProposed: The President made the appointment on 19 June 2024. Under its charter (Republic Act No. 6848), the bank exists to promote the socio-economic development of the autonomous region through Islamic banking. The resolution notes that it operates 9 branches, and that the Organic Law has the region, the Bangko Sentral, the Department of Finance and the NCMF jointly promote Islamic finance. Mr. Amilasan was then Deputy Minister of Finance, Budget and Management in the regional government, previously a consultant to the Office of the Chief Minister and the Bangsamoro Board of Investments, and a Metrobank Cotabato City manager from 2004 to 2020. Authored by MP Susana S. Anayatin.
whoIsAffected: Amilbahar P. Amilasan Jr., the appointee.
whatChanges: Nothing beyond the copies sent to the President and Mr. Amilasan.
readings.insight: The appointee was a sitting deputy minister in the Bangsamoro Government. This is the 2nd resolution in 2 months thanking President Marcos for a Bangsamoro appointee, after Resolution No. 446 on the NCMF Secretary. Parliament's interest in Islamic banking goes back to Resolution No. 24 (June 2019), which backed the bill regulating Islamic banks.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament congratulates its Speaker, Pangalian M. Balindong, on receiving a Doctor of Laws honoris causa from Manuel L. Quezon University on 25 June 2024, and acknowledges his contributions to peace, justice and governance.

Copies go to Speaker Balindong and Manuel L. Quezon University. Adopted on 15 July 2024.
readings.whyProposed: The resolution recounts that the Speaker earned his political science degree in 1962 and his law degree in 1966 from the same university. It lists his service as a delegate to the 1973 Constitutional Convention, as Deputy Speaker in Congress, as Speaker of the ARMM assembly, as a member of the Consultative Committee to review the 1987 Constitution, and as Speaker of the Bangsamoro Parliament, and his long advocacy of peaceful pluralism. Authored by MP Eddie M. Alih and 41 others.
whoIsAffected: Speaker Pangalian M. Balindong.
whatChanges: Nothing outside Parliament. It is Parliament honouring its own presiding officer.
readings.insight: The resolution is attested, as every adopted resolution is, by the Speaker himself, so Speaker Balindong signed his own commendation. Proposed Resolution No. 602 was filed on 2 July 2024 with 42 authors, including Chief Minister Ahod Balawag Ebrahim, and adopted 13 days later.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament asks the Philippine National Police regional office (PRO-BAR) to set up tourist-police assistance desks in major hotels and inns in the region's popular tourist destinations. It also urges the PNP to provide the name of each city or municipal chief of police and the hotline numbers of each station.

Copies go to PRO-BAR and other concerned agencies, for information and consideration. Adopted on 15 July 2024.
readings.whyProposed: The resolution argues that tourists' safety drives tourism and that the region's history of armed conflict deters visitors. It cites the Tourism Act of 2009 (Republic Act No. 9593), which has the PNP set up a Tourism Security Force, and points to Davao City as a model. It cites Philippine Statistics Authority growth figures (5.8% in 2019, -1.9% in 2020, 7.5% in 2021) and a PNP report that index crimes fell from 1,676 in 2017 to 710 in 2021. Authored by MP Don Mustapha A. Loong.
whoIsAffected: Tourists and visitors staying in hotels and inns in the region.
PRO-BAR and municipal police stations.
implementedBy: Philippine National Police, Police Regional Office BAR
whatChanges: A request to a national police office that Parliament cannot direct. It names no destination, hotel, number of desks or deadline.
readings.insight:
The crime figures do not match the percentage given for them. The resolution says the regional crime index fell by more than 42%, but a fall from 1,676 to 710 is about 58%; 710 is about 42% of 1,676. Both numbers are on the adopted page.

Proposed Resolution No. 230 was filed on 10 May 2023. Its committee report (No. 51) was adopted and deferred on 16 November 2023, and the resolution was adopted 14 months after filing.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament commends the Philippine Drug Enforcement Agency's Bangsamoro regional office (PDEA-BARMM), under Regional Director Gil Cesario P. Castro, for a series of anti-drug operations in the region.

The resolution is presented to the Office of the Regional Director. Adopted on 16 July 2024.
readings.whyProposed: The resolution reports more than 20 operations from January to March 2024. They seized 7,841.476 grams of shabu valued at ₱62,731,808, about 15,000 fully grown marijuana plants, and about 50 grams of dried marijuana valued at ₱25,000. 32 suspects were arrested and 4 drug dens dismantled, with no deaths or serious injuries on either side. Authored by MP Jamel B. Macacua.
whoIsAffected: PDEA-BARMM and its Regional Director.
whatChanges: Nothing beyond the copy presented to PDEA-BARMM.
readings.insight: The shabu valuation works out to exactly ₱8,000 per gram (₱62,731,808 for 7,841.476 grams), so the peso figure is a computed estimate, not a market observation. The resolution covers operations from January to March 2024. Proposed Resolution No. 560 was filed on 30 April 2024 and adopted in mid-July.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament congratulates and commends Samsodin Abdulrahman for winning gold in the 81-kilogram bodyweight category of the Singapore Weightlifting International 2023, held at D'Marquee, Singapore, and for bringing pride and honour to the Bangsamoro people. A copy is to be presented to him as a token of recognition.

Adopted on 18 July 2023.
readings.whyProposed: Abdulrahman, a Meranaw from Saguiaran, Lanao del Sur, won the 81-kg gold on 3 June 2023 at the 2–4 June meet, which offered 150 competition spots across men's and women's categories. The resolution describes an 18-year weightlifting career that began in fitness training in Dubai, work as a head coach, personal trainer and rehabilitation specialist, and calls him the first Meranaw athlete to win the distinction. The win qualified him for an international weightlifting event in Poland on 18–26 August 2023.
whoIsAffected: Samsodin Abdulrahman, the honoree.
whatChanges: A copy of the resolution is presented to the honoree. Nothing else follows from it.
readings.insight: Filed by MP Baintan A. Ampatuan and MP Diamila D. Ramos; the adopted text notes it consolidates 2 proposals, PR 307 and PR 309. It cites the Bangsamoro Organic Law's mandate to promote youth fitness through sports, but the honoree's career as described is largely an adult one built abroad. The PDF Parliament posted for this resolution carries a file name about oxygen generators (the subject of Resolution No. 369, adopted the same day); the document inside is Resolution No. 368.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament congratulates Fatima Aliah Quibranza Dimaporo on her appointment as Undersecretary of the Department of Social Welfare and Development, and directs that the resolution be presented to her.

Adopted on 14 August 2023.
readings.whyProposed: Malacañang released her appointment paper, signed by President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr., on 28 July 2023. The resolution describes the post as Undersecretary for Operations, which oversees 3 sub-clusters: statutory programs, specialized programs and disaster response management. It notes she is a native of Lanao del Norte and Lanao del Sur, daughter of former Lanao del Norte governor Abdullah Dimaporo and incumbent governor Imelda Quibranza Dimaporo, a former 2nd District Representative of Lanao del Norte in the 15th Congress, and a former executive director of the World Youth Alliance Foundation in New York. Parliament reads the appointment as recognition of Bangsamoro women's capability.
whoIsAffected: Undersecretary Fatima Aliah Quibranza Dimaporo.
whatChanges: A copy of the resolution is presented to the honoree. Nothing else follows from it.
readings.insight: MP Rasol Y. Mitmug Jr. and 63 others are listed as authors, close to the whole house. It belongs to a steady run of resolutions congratulating or thanking the President for national appointments of Bangsamoro figures in 2023, among them Resolution No. 330 (Abdulraof A. Macacua as officer-in-charge governor of Maguindanao del Norte), No. 351 (Suharto T. Mangudadatu as TESDA Director General) and No. 380 (General Romeo Saturnino Brawner Jr. as AFP Chief of Staff), adopted the same day as this one.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament condemns "in the strongest possible sense" the death of Ezell A. Tan and requests the appropriate agencies of the Bangsamoro Government to speed up their investigation so that his family can obtain justice. Copies go to the family and to the appropriate agencies, for information.

Adopted on 15 August 2023.
readings.whyProposed: A fisherman found a body floating off Barangay Molimoc, Balabagan, Lanao del Sur, at twilight on 20 July 2023. The Balabagan police chief, P/MAJ Michael Yap, said the family identified it as Tan, and that swelling and marks on the head and body suggested he was tortured before he was killed. Cotabato City Police Station 2 had listed him missing since 18 July 2023 together with his Toyota Avanza. Tan was 34, a resident of Rosary Heights V, Cotabato City, a Philippine Navy reservist and an Accountant II at the Commission on Population and Development XII. The resolution calls the killing the latest in an unexplained series of killings in the region.
whoIsAffected: Ezell A. Tan's family.
Bangsamoro agencies with a hand in the investigation, which are not named.
implementedBy: Appropriate agencies of the Bangsamoro Government (unnamed)
whatChanges: A request, with no deadline, for unnamed regional agencies to expedite an investigation.
Copies are sent to the family and to the agencies, for information only.
readings.insight:
The request goes to "appropriate agencies" without naming one, and the copy is sent "for information" rather than for action, so no office is on notice to report back. The underlying killing happened in Balabagan, Lanao del Sur, and was handled by municipal police, a national force. MP Susana S. Anayatin and 14 others filed it; the adopted text notes it consolidates PR 366 and PR 376.

It was adopted the same day as Resolution No. 387 on the killing of Dr. Marivic Tello, and a month before Resolution No. 392 on 2 more Cotabato City shootings. The condemnation-and-investigate form recurs through the registry, from Resolution No. 276 (October 2022), which ordered a committee inquiry into a series of killings, to Resolutions No. 431, 434, 450, 484 and 527 to 531 in 2024 and 2025.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament condemns "in the strongest possible terms" the killing of Dr. Marivic Tello and urges the Cotabato Regional and Medical Center (CRMC) to take the steps needed to secure its personnel and clients. The resolution is forwarded to her family and to CRMC, for information.

Adopted on 15 August 2023.
readings.whyProposed: Dr. Tello, an obstetrician-gynecologist and the wife of retired police general Agustin Tello, a former Maguindanao provincial police director, was reported missing on 23 July 2023 and last seen at CRMC. On 27 July 2023 her body was found buried in the Cotabato Medical Society Building inside the CRMC compound. The same day her secretary surrendered to police and confessed to killing her inside the compound. The resolution adds a general tribute to doctors' sacrifices during the COVID-19 pandemic.
whoIsAffected: Dr. Tello's family.
Staff, patients and visitors of the Cotabato Regional and Medical Center.
implementedBy: Cotabato Regional and Medical Center
whatChanges: An urging to CRMC to improve security, with no measures specified and no report required.
Copies are forwarded to the family and CRMC, for information.
readings.insight: Unlike most killing resolutions in this registry, this one does not ask for an investigation: by the resolution's own account a suspect had already surrendered and confessed. Its only practical ask is aimed at the hospital, because the killing happened inside a hospital compound, yet it names no measure and asks for no report. Filed by MP Kadil M. Sinolinding Jr. and 12 others (PR 377 per the adopted text), and adopted the same day as Resolution No. 386 on Ezell A. Tan. Parliament's index gives its session number as 387, an apparent data-entry slip; the other resolutions adopted on 15 August 2023 are recorded under session 37.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament congratulates Jamal Rahmat Pandi of Lanao del Sur for winning gold in Badminton Secondary at the Palarong Pambansa 2023, and commends all athletes and coaches who took part. The resolution is presented to Pandi, with copies to the athletes and coaches.

Adopted on 15 August 2023.
readings.whyProposed: The 63rd Palarong Pambansa ran in Marikina City from 29 July to 5 August 2023, with student-athletes from 17 athletic associations. The region came home with 2 gold, 2 silver and 2 bronze medals by the resolution's own summary. Pandi, from the Schools Division of Lanao del Sur I and coached by Aisah Mae Mina Penduma, had earlier won silver at the 2022 Asia Junior Sports Exchange Games. The resolution lists the other medallists: the Maguindanao II volleyball team (elementary boys, gold); taekwondo bronzes for Dhan Joseph Eligio, Johari O. Bones and Dhivine Iriz Quine A. Lerado of Cotabato City; wrestling bronze for Angel T. Apolinario of Lamitan City; demonstration-sport pencak silat bronzes for Mahdum J. Maddatal of Basilan and Mojib M. Omar of Cotabato City; and 2 silver and 1 bronze in para swimming for Jhon Rhey M. Bondan of Lamitan City.
whoIsAffected: Jamal Rahmat Pandi.
The region's Palarong Pambansa 2023 athletes and coaches.
whatChanges: The resolution is presented to Pandi and furnished to the participating athletes and coaches. Nothing else follows.
readings.insight: The resolution's own tallies do not agree. It says the region won 2 gold, 2 silver and 2 bronze, but its list of medallists shows 2 golds and at least 5 bronzes in regular and demonstration sports, plus 2 silvers and a bronze in para swimming. The "6", "2" and "3" headings count medal lines, not medals by colour. Filed by MP Marjanie S. Macasalong, MP Eddie M. Alih, MP Nurredha I. Misuari, MP Rasol Y. Mitmug Jr. and MP Abdullah B. Hashim; the text notes it consolidates PR 383 and PR 387.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament congratulates Mohammad Nur Guma-os Casib, a native of Lanao del Sur, for winning bronze at the International Chemistry Olympiad in Zurich, Switzerland, and directs that the resolution be presented to him.

Adopted on 15 August 2023.
readings.whyProposed: The 55th International Chemistry Olympiad ran in Zurich from 16 to 25 July 2023, with 107 participants from 88 countries; each country sends 4 students, who sit a 5-hour practical and a 5-hour theory examination. Casib, a student of Philippine Science High School, Central Mindanao Campus, in Baloi, Lanao del Norte, qualified by winning the 2023 Philippine Chemistry Olympiad. The resolution notes that his parents, Dr. Norodin Casib and Dr. Sittienor Guma-os Casib, are natives of Marawi City and victims of the siege, and lists earlier wins at the International Mathematics and Science Olympiad in Zhejiang, China, and the Metrobank-DepEd Math Challenge.
whoIsAffected: Mohammad Nur Guma-os Casib.
whatChanges: A copy of the resolution is presented to the honoree. Nothing else follows from it.
readings.insight: MP Marjanie S. Macasalong and 68 others are listed as authors, far more than any other resolution adopted that day. The adopted text notes it consolidates PR 384 and PR 388. The registry holds a few other olympiad commendations, including Resolution No. 403 for 4 young mathematicians and Resolution No. 485 for a nuclear science olympiad gold medallist.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament congratulates Fadzrati D. Asarud, a Bangsamoro youth from Tawi-Tawi, for placing 5th with a rating of 88.20% in the August 2023 Psychometricians Licensure Examination, and directs that the resolution be presented to her.

Adopted on 18 September 2023.
readings.whyProposed: Results came out on 9 August 2023: 6,133 of 8,370 examinees passed, a rate of 73.27%. Asarud graduated cum laude from Ateneo de Zamboanga University and is an alumna of the MSU Tawi-Tawi College of Technology and Oceanography Science High School and the Child Development Center-Laboratory Elementary School. The resolution credits those schools as well.
whoIsAffected: Fadzrati D. Asarud.
whatChanges: A copy of the resolution is presented to the honoree. Nothing else follows from it.
readings.insight: 1 of 33 adopted resolutions whose titles name a licensure or bar examination, the registry's most common kind of commendation for individual achievement. Resolution No. 257 (July 2022) likewise singled out a 5th placer, in the 2022 CPA examination. MP Eddie M. Alih and 34 others are listed as authors; the page header records 2 proposals behind it, P. P. Res. Nos. 390 and 403.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament expresses its deepest condolences and sympathy to the family of Amelita A. Piang, wife of MP Ramon A. Piang Sr., and directs that the resolution be presented to the family.

Adopted on 18 September 2023.
readings.whyProposed: Mrs. Piang died on 4 August 2023. The resolution records her as president of the Upi Women's Federation, which was recognised by the Maguindanao provincial government for its anti-trafficking program STEP-UP; a director of the Philippine Red Cross Cotabato City-Maguindanao Chapter from February 2020, chairing its welfare and services committee; and, with her husband, chapter head of Couples for Christ in Upi. She was the mother of the incumbent Upi mayor, Ma. Rona Cristina P. Flores, and residents called her "Ina ng bayan ng Upi".
whoIsAffected: The Piang family.
whatChanges: The resolution is presented to the family. Nothing else follows.
readings.insight: Filed in the name of the Government of the Day rather than named MPs. Condolences are among the most frequent kinds of resolution in the registry, and this one follows the usual form: tribute, condolence, a copy to the family.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament condemns "in the strongest possible terms" the killing of Mohammad Hessam A. Midtimbang and the ambush of Cotabato City General Services Officer Pedro D. Tato Jr., which wounded Tato and killed his driver, Dandy Anonat. It calls on all concerned agencies of the region to investigate speedily so the families get justice.

Copies go, for information and appropriate action, to Cotabato City Mayor Bruce Dela Cruz Matabalao, the Bangsamoro Human Rights Commission, Cotabato City Police Director PCOL Querubin L. Manalang Jr., the Office of the Chief Minister, NBI-BARMM, the Police Regional Office-BAR and the Ministry of Public Order and Safety.

Adopted on 18 September 2023.
readings.whyProposed: On 15 August 2023 unknown gunmen shot at Tato's vehicle in Rosary Heights X, killing Anonat and wounding Tato, according to the city's public safety officer. On 21 August 2023, on Governor Gutierrez Avenue, Rosary Heights VII, motorcycle gunmen shot and killed Midtimbang, host of a Bangsamoro Darul-Ifta' radio programme and a member of the Darul-Ifta', the region's Islamic advisory council. The resolution says such killings have been rampant in Cotabato City, that the city government and police need to strengthen security, and that the Bangsamoro Human Rights Commission should monitor the case.
whoIsAffected: The families of Mohammad Hessam A. Midtimbang and Dandy Anonat, and Pedro D. Tato Jr.
Cotabato City residents and government employees.
implementedBy: Bangsamoro Human Rights Commission
Cotabato City Government and City Police
NBI-BARMM and Police Regional Office-BAR
Office of the Chief Minister and Ministry of Public Order and Safety
whatChanges: A call, with no deadline, for a speedy investigation of both shootings.
Copies go to 7 named offices "for information and appropriate action", a stronger referral than "for information" alone.
readings.insight:
This resolution merges 3 proposals, P. P. Res. Nos. 401, 407 and 411, 1 on the Tato ambush and 2 on Midtimbang's killing, into a single text. It names more recipients than the killing resolutions adopted a month earlier, and it is the only one of them to say the Bangsamoro Human Rights Commission should monitor the case, though that appears in a WHEREAS clause, not as a directive. Filed by MP Susana S. Anayatin and 27 others.

It came a month after Resolutions No. 386 and 387 condemned 2 other killings, and the same form continued into 2024 and 2025 (Resolutions No. 431, 434, 450, 484 and 527 to 531). The registry does not record any report back to Parliament on these investigations.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament congratulates the Province of Tawi-Tawi and its people on the province's 50th Kamahardikaan (founding anniversary) and on contributions that have brought honour to the region and the nation. A copy is presented to the office of Governor Yshmael "Mang" I. Sali.

Adopted on 18 September 2023.
readings.whyProposed: Presidential Decree No. 302 created Tawi-Tawi on 27 September 1973; it now comprises 11 municipalities: Bongao, Languyan, Mapun, Panglima Sugala, Sapa-Sapa, Sibutu, Simunul, Sitangkai, South Ubian, Tandubas and Turtle Islands. The resolution credits it with making the region the country's top fish producer, seaweed included, per Philippine Statistics Authority data, calls it the unofficial seaweed capital of the Philippines, and notes the soft launch of Bangsamoro Barter Trade in Bongao on 18 July 2023. The province planned a month-long celebration themed "Tawi-Tawi to the World: Bangsa, Hulah, Agama", featuring the Agal-Agal (seaweed) and Lepa festivals.
whoIsAffected: The Province of Tawi-Tawi.
whatChanges: A copy is presented to the provincial governor's office. Nothing else follows.
readings.insight: Adopted 9 days before the anniversary date. Filed by MP John Anthony L. Lim (P. P. Res. No. 404 per the page header). Parliament has marked other institutional anniversaries the same way, including Mindanao State University's 60th (Resolution No. 149) and Cotabato State University's centennial (Resolution No. 438).

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament encourages all officials and employees of the region's ministries, agencies and offices, local government units included, to take part in the Values Transformation Trainings. Copies are furnished to all concerned agencies, for information.

Adopted on 19 September 2023.
readings.whyProposed: The resolution grounds itself in moral governance as defined in the Bangsamoro Administrative Code (BAA No. 13): governance free of graft and corruption and driven by dedication, devotion, honesty, justice and integrity. It notes that the Civil Service Commission-BARMM runs a Values Orientation Workshop and that the Development Academy of the Bangsamoro is the government's central training arm. It says the Values Transformation Training builds participants' faith, self-development and commitment to service, and suggests each office name a Values Reformation Officer from its human resources unit to plan the training with the Academy.
whoIsAffected: Officials and employees of regional ministries, agencies and offices.
Officials and employees of local government units in the region.
implementedBy: Ministries, agencies and offices of the Bangsamoro Government
Local government units in BARMM
Development Academy of the Bangsamoro (named in the WHEREAS clauses as training partner)
whatChanges: Participation is encouraged, not required.
The suggestion that each office designate a Values Reformation Officer sits in a WHEREAS clause and binds no one.
readings.insight: "Encourage" is the weakest verb Parliament uses, and nothing here sets a deadline, a target or a reporting line. The resolution does not say who runs the Values Transformation Training or how it relates to the Civil Service Commission workshop it also mentions. It follows Resolution No. 252 (June 2022), which urged all ministries through the Chief Minister's office to develop and integrate values transformation programs, and Resolution No. 128 (June 2021) on the oath of moral governance. Filed by MP Tawakal B. Midtimbang and 20 others (P. P. Res. No. 397).

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament honours and recognises the members of the local and foreign media for their role in the peace process and in promoting transparent and accountable governance. Copies go to media organisations, the Bangsamoro Information Office and other stakeholders as an expression of appreciation.

Adopted on 19 September 2023.
readings.whyProposed: Republic Act No. 11699 declares 30 August of every year National Press Freedom Day, in honour of Marcelo H. del Pilar. The resolution credits the media with sustaining the gains of the peace agreements with the MILF and MNLF, helping people understand the Bangsamoro's quest for peace and self-determination, and keeping government accountable. It states that the Bangsamoro Government will continue to foster an environment where journalists work without fear or intimidation.
whoIsAffected: Local and foreign journalists covering the region.
whatChanges: Copies go to media organisations and the Bangsamoro Information Office. The commitment to press freedom is stated in a WHEREAS clause and creates no obligation.
readings.insight: Adopted 20 days after the Press Freedom Day it marks. Filed by MP Sha Elijah B. Dumama-Alba (P. P. Res. No. 398). The registry's nearest sibling is Resolution No. 373 (July 2023), congratulating MindaNews journalist Carolyn O. Arguillas on the 2023 Luxembourg Peace Prize. Parliament's own media access came up again in Resolution No. 566 (January 2026), which allowed live-streaming of committee meetings.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament congratulates and commends Sabaha Pato Salik of Datu Anggal Midtimbang, Maguindanao del Sur, for placing 3rd in Qur'an recitation at the 63rd Malaysian International Al-Quran Recitation and Memorization Assembly 2023. The resolution is presented to her.

Adopted on 19 September 2023.
readings.whyProposed: The assembly ran from 19 to 24 August 2023 at the Kuala Lumpur World Trade Centre, with 76 contestants from 52 countries in separate men's and women's categories. Salik, 31, of Barangay Tulunan, represented the Philippines in women's recitation and placed 3rd with an average score of 91.50%. The resolution presents her as an example to Bangsamoro youth, especially women, in Qur'anic and Islamic studies.
whoIsAffected: Sabaha Pato Salik.

funding.detail: No amount is stated. A WHEREAS clause says Salik shall be awarded a plaque of appreciation and a cash incentive under BTA Resolution No. 97, series of 2020, as amended by BTA Resolution No. 306, series of 2023; the amount and source are set in those resolutions, not here.

whatChanges: The resolution is presented to Salik.
Through BTA Resolution No. 97 (2020) as amended by Resolution No. 306 (2023), she becomes entitled to a plaque and a cash incentive, per the WHEREAS clause.
readings.insight: Unlike most commendations, this one carries money, and the money is set elsewhere. Resolution No. 97 (December 2020) recognised top-ranked Bangsamoro Qur'an reciters since 1969, and Resolution No. 306 (January 2023) amended it; this resolution simply triggers that standing award. Filed by MP Diamila D. Ramos, MP Michael E. Midtimbang, MP Mudjib C. Abu and MP Tawakal B. Midtimbang (P. P. Res. No. 399).

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament congratulates Miriam Coronel-Ferrer for being one of the laureates of the 65th Ramon Magsaysay Awards, and directs that the resolution be presented to her.

Adopted on 19 September 2023.
readings.whyProposed: She was named an awardee on 31 August 2023. The resolution recalls that she chaired the government's peace panel in the talks with the MILF that ended 17 years of negotiation with the 2014 Comprehensive Agreement on the Bangsamoro. It also lists her co-founding of the Southeast Asian Women Peace Mediators in 2020, her appointment in 2018 as a Senior Mediation Adviser on the UN Standby Team (the only one from Southeast Asia), her role in the country's first Action Plan on Women, Peace and Security in 2010, her co-chairing of a working group of the International Campaign to Ban Landmines, and her years as a professor at UP Diliman.
whoIsAffected: Miriam Coronel-Ferrer.
whatChanges: A copy of the resolution is presented to the honoree. Nothing else follows from it.
readings.insight: The honoree is tied directly to this Parliament's origins: the resolution credits her with leading the government side of the talks that produced the 2014 Comprehensive Agreement on the Bangsamoro. Filed by MP Susana S. Anayatin (P. P. Res. No. 409).

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament invites officials of the Civil Aviation Authority of the Philippines (CAAP), DPWH Region XII, the MOTC-Bangsamoro Airport Authority, and the airport managers of Philippine Airlines and Cebu Pacific to explain the status of the rehabilitation of Awang Airport, in aid of legislation.

The resolution is to go immediately to the Committee on Transportation and Communications, which is to convene no later than 26 September 2023. Copies go to the agencies concerned, for information and appropriate action.

Adopted on 19 September 2023.
readings.whyProposed: On 21 June 2023 CAAP issued a Notice to Airmen closing the airport in Barangay Awang, Datu Odin Sinsuat, Maguindanao del Norte, for a ₱340,000,000 runway and airport rehabilitation, and PAL and Cebu Pacific cancelled all flights from 22 June. The closure came without advance notice; the resolution quotes the region's own transport minister, MP Paisalin Tago, saying "we were not even informed about it". The runway works were done by the DPWH office for SOCCSKSARGEN. The airport reopened on 19 August 2023 for private and military flights only, and the Cotabato Airport Authority manager said commercial flights would resume on 1 October 2023. Before the closure the 2 airlines ran 31 weekly flights from Cotabato.
whoIsAffected: Travellers and businesses relying on the region's main air gateway at Awang.
CAAP, DPWH Region XII, the MOTC-Bangsamoro Airport Authority, PAL and Cebu Pacific, whose officials are invited.
implementedBy: Committee on Transportation and Communications (to convene by 26 September 2023)
Civil Aviation Authority of the Philippines
DPWH Region XII
MOTC-Bangsamoro Airport Authority
Philippine Airlines and Cebu Pacific airport managers

funding.detail: The resolution appropriates nothing. It cites a ₱340,000,000 national runway and airport rehabilitation project as background.

whatChanges: The Committee on Transportation and Communications must convene within 7 days of adoption, a rule Parliament sets for itself.
National agencies and private airlines are invited, not compelled, to attend.
readings.insight: The resolution sets a hard deadline, which is rare, and the deadline binds Parliament's own committee, not the agencies. The invitees are mostly national bodies or private airlines that the BTA cannot summon; the resolution notes the Bangsamoro Organic Law leaves maintenance of existing airports to the national government. The airport issue had been raised before: Resolution No. 305 (January 2023) urged CAAP to finish renovating Cotabato Airport and determine accountability for delays. Filed by MP Baintan A. Ampatuan; P. P. Res. No. 415 was filed and adopted the same day, 19 September 2023. The registry does not record whether the committee hearing took place.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament directs the Ministry of Environment, Natural Resources and Energy (MENRE) to intensify its reforestation programs, especially in landslide-prone areas, and to submit a list of the region's landslide- and flood-prone areas and facilitate its publication. A copy is forwarded to MENRE.

Adopted on 19 September 2023.
readings.whyProposed: The resolution draws on Severe Tropical Storm Paeng (Nalgae), which on 27 October 2022 caused landslides and severe flooding in Maguindanao del Norte, Maguindanao del Sur and Cotabato City. As of 31 October 2022 the NDRRMC counted 110 dead, 101 injured and 33 missing, 59 of the dead from BARMM, and President Marcos called for more tree planting after noting the worst-hit areas were deforested. It cites the Integrated Bangsamoro Greening Program under Executive Order No. 007 (2020), which aims to grow 171.2 million trees on about 159,000 hectares, and MENRE's report that about 11.5 million seedlings had been planted on 10,401 hectares.
whoIsAffected: Communities in landslide- and flood-prone areas.
MENRE, which receives 2 directives.
implementedBy: Ministry of Environment, Natural Resources and Energy
whatChanges: MENRE is directed to intensify reforestation in landslide-prone areas, with no target or deadline.
MENRE is directed to submit a list of landslide- and flood-prone areas and have it published; no deadline or recipient is set.
readings.insight: The concrete ask is the hazard list, and it is the only part that could be checked; the resolution gives no date for it or say whom it goes to. By MENRE's figures as quoted, about 11.5 million of 171.2 million target trees (under 7%) had been planted. The proposal, P. P. Res. No. 91 by MP Baintan A. Ampatuan, was filed on 17 December 2022, 7 weeks after Paeng, and adopted 9 months later. A later resolution, No. 525 (January 2025), urged annual tree planting across ministries and LGUs every 21 January.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament congratulates and commends Hebban Talib Tawantawan for topping the September 2023 Certified Public Accountant Licensure Examination, and directs that the resolution be presented to him.

Adopted on 16 October 2023.
readings.whyProposed: On 6 October 2023 the Professional Regulation Commission announced that 2,740 of 8,734 examinees passed, a 31.25% rate. Tawantawan scored 91.17%, sharing 1st place with Allaine Beduya Collamar of UP Tacloban. He is 23, of Maranao descent, from Poblacion, Salvador, Lanao del Norte, and graduated magna cum laude in accountancy from the University of San Jose-Recoletos.
whoIsAffected: Hebban Talib Tawantawan.
whatChanges: A copy of the resolution is presented to the honoree. Nothing else follows from it.
readings.insight: 5 separate proposals, P. P. Res. Nos. 432, 433, 434, 435 and 439, were merged into this single commendation, adopted 10 days after the results. It is 1 of 33 adopted resolutions whose titles name a licensure or bar examination; Resolution No. 360 (June 2023) commended the 2nd placer in the May 2023 CPA examination. MP Ubaida C. Pacasem and 12 others are listed as authors.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament congratulates and commends the BARMM Men's Volleyball Team for winning gold at the National State Colleges and Universities Athletic Association Games 2023, and directs that the resolution be presented to the team.

Adopted on 16 October 2023.
readings.whyProposed: The games ran at New Clark City Athletics Stadium in Capas, Tarlac, from 1 to 6 October 2023, with more than 60,000 student-athletes from 114 state universities and colleges. On 5 October the team, representing Tawi-Tawi Regional Agricultural College, beat Region VI (Western Visayas) in 3 straight sets. The resolution names all 15 players, head coach Abraham J. Tandi, assistant coach Edward R. Lee and 4 coaching staff.
whoIsAffected: The 15 players and coaching staff of the BARMM Men's Volleyball Team.
Tawi-Tawi Regional Agricultural College.
whatChanges: The resolution is presented to the team. Nothing else follows.
readings.insight: Adopted 11 days after the final. Filed by MP Diamila D. Ramos (P. P. Res. No. 436). Its WHEREAS clauses repeat, nearly word for word, the constitutional and Organic Law sports clauses of Resolution No. 368 on weightlifter Samsodin Abdulrahman, which she also co-authored.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament calls on the Government of the Day, through the Bangsamoro Darul-Ifta' and other appropriate ministries and offices, to hold an annual pre-Ramadhan and Ramadhan symposium and to produce modules for it, to educate and remind the Bangsamoro people about the virtues of the holy month. Copies go to the Darul-Ifta' and other concerned offices for information and appropriate consideration.

Adopted on 17 October 2023.
readings.whyProposed: The resolution cites Surah Al-Baqarah 2:185 on the fast and Surah Az-Zariyat 51:55 on reminding believers, and the Administrative Code's mandate for the Darul-Ifta' to strengthen Islamic preaching and guidance. It argues that not every Bangsamoro has had proper Islamic education, so symposiums and modules on Ramadhan's obligatory and recommended acts would help. It suggests the Darul-Ifta' and the Regional Mufti live-stream lectures, and that ministries fold these activities into their gender and development plans.
whoIsAffected: Muslims in the region.
The Bangsamoro Darul-Ifta', which would develop the modules and run the symposiums.
implementedBy: Bangsamoro Darul-Ifta'
Other appropriate ministries and offices (unnamed)
whatChanges: A call for a recurring annual event, with no budget, lead ministry beyond the Darul-Ifta', or report required.
Copies go "for information and appropriate consideration".
readings.insight: The proposal, P. P. Res. No. 313 by MP Don Mustapha A. Loong, was filed on 19 June 2023 and adopted 4 months later. Its footer on both pages reads "Resolution No. 313", the proposal number, not 402. The proposal asked for a pre-Ramadhan symposium; the adopted title adds a Ramadhan one. Earlier resolutions also assigned the Darul-Ifta' tasks: Resolution No. 111 (March 2021) on a unified moon-sighting declaration, and Resolution No. 130 (June 2021) on a fatwa on halal conduct of officials.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament congratulates and commends 4 young Bangsamoro students for their awards at the Thailand International Mathematical Olympiad (TIMO) Final Round 2022-2023 and the Hong Kong International Mathematical Olympiad (HKIMO) Final Round 2023. Copies go to each of them.

Adopted on 17 October 2023.
readings.whyProposed: TIMO's final round was held in Pattaya on 1–2 April 2023 and HKIMO's in Hong Kong on 25–28 August 2023. The resolution names the honorees: Aishah Ambor Gandarma, 11, of Tambo Central School, Iligan City (TIMO gold and HKIMO silver, Primary 4); Alan Nageena Arumpac Mamutuk, 13, of Philippine Science High School-Main Campus (TIMO gold, Secondary 2); Aqeel Nikolai Arumpac Mamutuk, 11, of Project 6 Special Science Elementary School (TIMO and HKIMO gold, Primary 5); and Ameer Khan Khayzan Mansanadez Cabaro of Tambo Central School (TIMO silver and HKIMO gold, Primary 6). All 4 qualified for the 2024 World International Mathematical Olympiad.
whoIsAffected: The 4 student honorees and their schools.
whatChanges: Copies are furnished to the 4 students. Nothing else follows.
readings.insight: 2 slips are visible on the page itself: the second honoree's award is dated "TIMO Final Round 2022-2024" where every other line says 2022-2023, and the first honoree's surname is printed Gandarma while her parents are listed as Gandamra. Aqeel Nikolai Arumpac Mamutuk was commended again in Resolution No. 474 (July 2024) for gold at the 2024 TIMO. Filed by MP Diamila D. Ramos and 6 others (P. P. Res. Nos. 414 and 419).

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament calls on all ministries, agencies and offices of the region, local government units included, to observe, comply with and monitor the implementation of Republic Act No. 7277, the Magna Carta for Persons with Disability, as amended. Copies go to all ministries, agencies, offices and LGUs "for their immediate information and compliance".

Adopted on 17 October 2023.
readings.whyProposed: The resolution focuses on employment. Republic Act No. 10524 requires government agencies, offices and corporations to reserve at least 1% of all positions for persons with disabilities, encourages private firms with more than 100 employees to do the same, and its rules make each agency responsible for monitoring its own offices' compliance. It cites the Organic Law's mandate for a special agency and services for persons with special needs, and the Bangsamoro Civil Service Code of 2021's bar on employment discrimination on account of disability.
whoIsAffected: Persons with disabilities seeking government jobs in the region.
Every regional ministry, agency and office, and every LGU.
implementedBy: All ministries, agencies and offices of the Bangsamoro Government
Local government units in BARMM
whatChanges: A call to comply with a national law that already binds these offices; it adds no new duty.
No office is asked to report its 1% compliance, and no monitoring body is named.
readings.insight: The 1% reservation in Republic Act No. 10524 is already law, so the resolution's force is as a reminder; what it lacks is a way to tell whether anyone complies, since it asks for no headcount and names no monitor. Resolution No. 118 (March 2021) had already called on the Ministry of the Interior and Local Government to monitor mechanisms for implementing the same Magna Carta. Filed by MP Don Mustapha A. Loong (P. P. Res. No. 319).

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament directs the Bangsamoro Planning and Development Authority (BPDA) to brief Parliament on the overall status of the region's housing program in relation to the first Bangsamoro Development Plan. The resolution is forwarded to the BPDA for information and appropriate action.

Adopted on 17 October 2023.
readings.whyProposed: The Organic Law requires Parliament to pass a law creating a housing and human settlements agency, and requires the Bangsamoro Government to deliver affordable housing. The first Bangsamoro Development Plan, 2020-2022, found high housing demand driven by decommissioned combatants under the Normalization Program, people displaced by the 2017 Marawi siege, and the addition of Cotabato City and 63 North Cotabato barangays to the region. The resolution cites UNHCR figures of 32,216 families and 158,725 individuals still displaced in Mindanao as of 30 November 2022, and says that 3 years into the plan, with new BTA members seated, Parliament needs to identify gaps in the housing program.
whoIsAffected: Displaced families, decommissioned combatants and others awaiting housing.
The BPDA, which must report.
implementedBy: Bangsamoro Planning and Development Authority
whatChanges: The BPDA is directed to brief Parliament; no date, format or committee is specified.
readings.insight: A directive to a regional office Parliament oversees, with nothing to say when the briefing is due. It went through committee: P. P. Res. No. 264 by MP Baintan A. Ampatuan was filed on 22 May 2023, referred to the Committee on Human Settlements and Development, and adopted 5 months later on Committee Report No. 46. A related request, Resolution No. 356 (June 2023), had urged ministries and LGUs to house Typhoon Paeng victims left homeless. The development plan it asks about covered 2020 to 2022 and had already ended when the resolution was adopted.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament tasks the Office of the Secretary-General to print and distribute the priority laws Parliament has passed. The resolution is forwarded to that office for information and appropriate action.

Adopted on 17 October 2023.
readings.whyProposed: The Organic Law requires the BTA to enact priority codes during the transition. The resolution counts 5 of 7 as enacted (the Administrative, Civil Service, Education, Electoral and Local Governance Codes), with the Revenue Code and the Indigenous Peoples Code still pending. It argues that awareness of the codes needs a deliberate push, and suggests printing and distributing at least 10,000 copies to stakeholders, especially ministries, agencies, offices and LGUs.
whoIsAffected: Ministries, agencies, offices and LGUs, the main intended recipients of printed codes.
The Office of the Secretary-General, which does the work.
implementedBy: Office of the Secretary-General, BTA Parliament

funding.detail: The resolution appropriates nothing. It suggests at least 10,000 printed copies in a WHEREAS clause but names no cost or fund source.

whatChanges: An instruction to Parliament's own secretariat, which Parliament can enforce.
The 10,000-copy figure appears only in a WHEREAS clause; the operative text sets no number, deadline or budget.
readings.insight:
This is an internal instruction, so unlike most resolutions it actually binds the office it addresses. The original proposal, P. P. Res. No. 424 by MP Baintan A. Ampatuan, would have urged the Office of the Chief Minister, through the Bangsamoro Information Office, to do the printing; the adopted text gives the job to Parliament's own Secretary-General instead.

The registry dates the 5 codes as BAA No. 13 (October 2020), No. 17 (February 2021), No. 18 (May 2021), No. 35 (March 2023) and No. 49 (28 September 2023, 3 weeks before this resolution). The Indigenous Peoples' Act followed as BAA No. 64 in December 2024; the registry's list of enacted acts holds no revenue code.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament condemns the acts of violence and collective punishment against the people of Palestine and calls for an immediate, unconditional cessation of hostilities between Israel and Hamas and a humanitarian corridor for Gaza. It also calls for an end to attacks on Palestinian civilians, especially in Gaza, their safe return and dignified treatment, and full rehabilitation, and calls on Israel and Hamas to let the UN set up a humanitarian corridor for protection and relief.

Copies go to the UN Resident Coordinator in the Philippines, the Organization of Islamic Cooperation in Jeddah, and the Embassies of Israel and of Palestine.

Adopted on 17 October 2023.
readings.whyProposed: The resolution recounts the 7 October 2023 Hamas attack, which killed hundreds of Israeli soldiers and civilians; Israel's declaration of war and "complete siege" of Gaza, cutting off electricity, food, water and fuel; Israel's statement that it had dropped 6,000 bombs weighing 4,000 metric tons in 6 days; damage counts as of 13 October (90 educational facilities, 11 water sanitation facilities, 19 health centres, 20 ambulances, 18 places of worship including 11 mosques destroyed, and 64,283 homes damaged with 5,540 destroyed); the order for 1.1 million people north of Wadi Gaza to move south within 24 hours; and deaths as of 15 October of 1,300 in Israel and 2,300 in Gaza. It cites the Rome Statute's treatment of collective punishment and attacks on civilians, medical units and places of worship as war crimes, and says the crisis is "primarily human and humanitarian", not religious or political.
whoIsAffected: Civilians in Gaza.
The UN, the OIC and the 2 embassies, which receive copies.
whatChanges: A statement of position addressed to foreign and international bodies; it binds no one.
Copies go to 4 international recipients, all of them outside the Philippine government.
readings.insight:
Adopted 10 days after 7 October. It merges 2 proposals filed on 16 October: P. P. Res. No. 442 (11 authors), calling for an end to hostilities against Palestinian civilians, and No. 443 (1 author), titled as "equally condemning" violence by Israel against Palestinians and by Hamas against Israeli civilians. Parliament's index records debate deferred on 16 October and adoption the next day. The adopted operative text condemns violence against Palestinians and calls on both sides for a ceasefire; the Hamas attack appears only in the WHEREAS clauses. Filed by MP Anna Tarhata S. Basman and 11 others.

Parliament had condemned Israeli violence against Palestinians before, in Resolution No. 124 (June 2021), and returned to it in Resolution No. 419 (December 2023), which reiterated the ceasefire call and urged the Bangsamoro Government to send aid to Gaza.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament directs its Committee on Health to conduct an inquiry, in aid of legislation, into the Ministry of Health's overall plan for establishing and upgrading hospitals, including the budget it needs. The resolution is forwarded to the committee chair for information and appropriate action.

Adopted on 17 October 2023.
readings.whyProposed: The resolution cites the Organic Law's rule that Parliament give the highest budget priority to education, health and social services, and the Administrative Code's commitment to a general hospital system. It says Parliament had established 1 hospital and upgraded 6, with more hospital bills filed, and that the Ministry of Health needs an overall plan to guide those decisions. It also invokes the continuing COVID-19 pandemic as a reason to build and upgrade facilities.
whoIsAffected: Patients in areas where hospitals are proposed or being upgraded.
The Ministry of Health, whose plan is the subject of the inquiry.
implementedBy: Committee on Health, BTA Parliament
Ministry of Health (subject of the inquiry)
whatChanges: Parliament's own Committee on Health is directed to hold an inquiry, which Parliament can enforce.
No deadline or report date is set.
readings.insight:
The original proposal, P. P. Res. No. 92 by MP Baintan A. Ampatuan, filed on 17 November 2022, would have required the Ministry of Health itself to present the plan with indicative budget figures. The adopted version turns that into a committee inquiry. Parliament's index still lists PR 92 as referred to the Committee on Health, though the adopted text cites it.

The registry shows hospital bills kept coming: 6 hospital acts were enacted in June 2022 (BAA No. 25 to 30), and 10 more hospital acts were enacted between December 2024 and August 2025 (BAA No. 66 to 69, 73, 74, 76 and 78 to 80). The registry does not record a hospital master plan. Resolution No. 195 (November 2021) had already urged the finance ministry to fund hospital upgrades in every province.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament requests the Department of Health to establish a Food and Drug Administration (FDA) Regional Field Office in BARMM. A copy is forwarded to the Department of Health, for information.

Adopted on 17 October 2023.
readings.whyProposed: Section 36 of the FDA Act of 2009 (Republic Act No. 9711) requires the FDA to set up field offices in all regions, with licensing, inspection and compliance, satellite laboratory and administrative divisions. The resolution says BARMM has none and the nearest are in Koronadal City and Zamboanga. It notes the regional Ministry of Health was then meeting the FDA central office on a memorandum of agreement to explore an FDA office in the region.
whoIsAffected: Manufacturers, distributors and retailers of food, drugs and cosmetics in the region, who would deal with a local office.
Consumers, through closer inspection and post-market surveillance.
implementedBy: Department of Health (national)
Food and Drug Administration
whatChanges: A request to a national department, which Parliament cannot direct.
The copy is sent for information only; no response is requested.
readings.insight: The request is grounded in national law: Republic Act No. 9711 itself says the FDA shall have field offices in all regions. The proposal, P. P. Res. No. 318 by MP Don Mustapha A. Loong, was addressed to the regional Ministry of Health; after review by the Committee on Health (Committee Report No. 42), the adopted text redirects it to the national Department of Health, which controls the FDA. The registry does not record a reply.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament congratulates the Republic of Türkiye on its 100th anniversary, extends the greetings of the Bangsamoro people, and commends President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan for his efforts for the country's advancement. The resolution is presented to the Embassy of Türkiye as an expression of solidarity.

Adopted on 23 October 2023.
readings.whyProposed: Türkiye marked its centenary on 29 October 2023. The resolution praises its progress over its first century and refers to Türkiye's "indelible contribution" to the Bangsamoro peace process, without saying what that contribution was.
whoIsAffected: The Republic of Türkiye and its embassy in the Philippines.
whatChanges: The resolution is presented to the Turkish embassy. Nothing else follows.
readings.insight: The third Türkiye resolution of 2023: Resolution No. 316 (February) conveyed condolences after the 6 February earthquake, and Resolution No. 350 (June) congratulated President Erdoğan on his re-election. Filed by MP Sha Elijah B. Dumama-Alba, MP Suharto S. Esmael and MP Marjanie S. Macasalong (P. P. Res. No. 446), and adopted 6 days before the anniversary.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament commends and thanks the Konrad Adenauer Stiftung (KAS) for its contribution since 2001 to autonomy, peace and development in the Bangsamoro, and extends recognition for its continuing support. The resolution is to be presented to KAS Philippines Country Director Daniela Braun on her official visit to the BTA on 28 November 2023.

Adopted on 23 October 2023.
readings.whyProposed: KAS is a German political foundation named after the first Chancellor of the Federal Republic, with 70 offices abroad and projects in 120 countries, active in the Philippines since 1964 and in the Bangsamoro since 2001. The resolution lists its work: with the European Union, party-development programs from 2014 to 2022 that trained civil society and emerging parties including those of the MILF and MNLF; the Support to Bangsamoro Transition Programme with PARTICIP Germany; training for the ARMM Regional Legislative Assembly, the Bangsamoro Transition Commission and the BTA; study visits to Germany and Europe; an indigenous peoples' rights program; the annual Kusog Mindanaw Conference; and policy publications.
whoIsAffected: The Konrad Adenauer Stiftung.
whatChanges: The resolution is to be presented to the KAS country director on 28 November 2023. Nothing else follows.
readings.insight: The resolution was adopted more than a month ahead of the visit at which it was to be presented. Its 2nd RESOLVED clause largely restates the 1st. It thanks a foundation that has trained Parliament's own predecessors and members, which is the context for the commendation. A later resolution, No. 467 (June 2024), thanked the Support to Bangsamoro Transition programme for a committee benchmarking visit. Filed by MP Baintan A. Ampatuan (P. P. Res. No. 447).

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament urges the Bangsamoro Information Office (BIO) to devise an information, education and communication (IEC) campaign for the region's voters on the provisions of the Bangsamoro Electoral Code. The resolution is forwarded to the BIO for information and appropriate action.

Adopted on 23 October 2023.
readings.whyProposed: The Bangsamoro Electoral Code (BAA No. 35) was adopted unanimously on 8 March 2023, 64 votes to 0, after public consultations from October 2022 to January 2023 in Manila, Basilan, Sulu, Tawi-Tawi, Maguindanao, Lanao del Sur, Cotabato City and the Special Geographic Area. The resolution expects the first regular Bangsamoro election to be held with the 2025 national and local elections, and argues voters, especially disadvantaged and vulnerable sectors, need to understand the Code through materials, seminars and orientations. It encourages ministries to support the BIO-led campaign.
whoIsAffected: Voters in the region, especially first-time and vulnerable voters.
The Bangsamoro Information Office, which is asked to design the campaign.
implementedBy: Bangsamoro Information Office
whatChanges: An urging to the BIO, with no deadline, budget or report back.
readings.insight:
The resolution's timetable did not hold. It was written for elections synchronised with the 2025 national polls; the registry's record of the Electoral Code now puts the first parliamentary elections on 14 September 2026, and the Code itself was amended twice in January 2026 (BAA No. 87, removing the "none of the above" ballot option, and BAA No. 88). An IEC campaign built on the 2023 text would need updating.

The proposal, P. P. Res. No. 219 by MP Baintan A. Ampatuan, filed on 13 April 2023, also named the Ministry of the Interior and Local Government; the version adopted on Committee Report No. 47 leaves only the BIO.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament humbly and earnestly appeals to President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. to grant an absolute pardon to former ARMM Governor Datu Zacaria Candao, former ARMM Executive Secretary Dr. Abas Candao and Israel Haron. The resolution is forwarded to the Office of the President in Malacañang for his information and appropriate action.

Adopted on 24 October 2023.
readings.whyProposed: The 3 men were convicted of malversation in 2009 for acts during Zacaria Candao's term as ARMM governor, and the resolution accepts that the Supreme Court has settled the case. It argues that the charges arose from administrative lapses in the newly formed ARMM, with no evidence of who benefited; that both Candaos spent decades negotiating peace in Mindanao without personal gain; and that Zacaria, now 80, and Abas, now 77, are in frail health. It states plainly that the 3 are "considered in hiding and are fugitives from justice", and argues a pardon would serve the healing and transitional justice aims of the normalization process. It says the Bureau of Pardons and Parole has favourably endorsed the pardon, and notes that absolute pardons have gone to murderers, bigger plunderers and coup plotters.
whoIsAffected: Datu Zacaria Candao, Dr. Abas Candao and Israel Haron.
implementedBy: Office of the President (appeal only)
whatChanges: An appeal to the President, whose pardon power Parliament cannot direct.
The resolution is forwarded to Malacañang for information and appropriate action.
readings.insight:
This is Parliament's second appeal for the Candaos in 4 months. Resolution No. 355 (22 June 2023) asked that Zacaria and Abas Candao be granted executive clemency; this one adds Israel Haron and asks specifically for absolute pardon. The proposal, P. P. Res. No. 451, was filed and adopted on the same day, 24 October 2023. Its 21 authors are led by MP Ahod Balawag Ebrahim, then Chief Minister, and include Speaker Pangalian M. Balindong.

The text is unusually candid for a formal appeal: it acknowledges the 3 are fugitives, and it addresses the President personally, recalling that he watched his own father "wither away and die in a foreign land". The registry does not record whether a pardon was granted.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament congratulates and commends Aqeel Nikolai Arumpac Mamutuk, a 12-year-old from Cotabato City, for winning a gold medal at the 2024 Thailand International Mathematical Olympiad, held in Bangkok from 26 to 29 April 2024, where he also made a perfect score in Logical Thinking.

A copy of the resolution is to be presented to him as a token of recognition. Filed by MP Diamila D. Ramos. Adopted on 16 July 2024.
readings.whyProposed: The WHEREAS clauses describe the competition, which drew entrants from 14 countries and territories, and the boy: of Maranao descent, the son of Judge Jamel Tabao Mamutuk and Atty. Aelan Biruar Arumpac, competing internationally since the age of 5, and already a Legend Awardee of the Math Olympiads Training League after gold awards in the final rounds of 3 competitions (the Hong Kong International Mathematical Olympiad, TIMO and the Greater Bay Area contest).
whoIsAffected: Aqeel Nikolai Arumpac Mamutuk and his family
whatChanges: Nothing outside Parliament changes. The resolution is a commendation, and a copy is presented to the honoree.
readings.insight:
This is the second time the Parliament has honored Bangsamoro children at this olympiad: Resolution 403 (17 October 2023) commended the young Bangsamoro representatives at the TIMO 2022-2023 and Hong Kong 2023 final rounds.

It also belongs to the last stretch of the honorific resolutions. 5 weeks later Resolution 494 moved recognitions and commendations into a 3-minute speech slot in plenary, and congratulatory resolutions for individual achievers all but stopped after that.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament congratulates the athletes of the Bangsamoro Cotabato Dojo and the Sultan Mastura Dojo for their awards at the 19th National Full Contact KyokushinRyu Karate Tournament in Dolores, Eastern Samar, on 22 and 23 June 2024.

It also urges the Bangsamoro Sports Commission to keep supporting Bangsamoro athletes in credible competitions with finances, logistics, opportunities or resources, and encourages the Commission to include in its annual budget proposal a supplementary allocation for the activities, facilities and development of sports institutions in the region. Copies go to the athletes, the Sultan Mastura Dojo and the Commission for information and appropriate action. Filed by MP Romeo K. Sema. Adopted on 16 July 2024.
readings.whyProposed: The Organic Law tells the Bangsamoro Government to promote fitness through sports, and the WHEREAS clauses present the 2 dojos, headed by Sensei Usman Baraguir and Coach Senpai Ahmadinnie Talapas, as partners in that work. At the tournament the Cotabato dojo brought home 10 trophies (4 championships, 2 second places and 4 third places) and the Sultan Mastura Dojo 4 (2 championships and 2 second places), 14 trophies in all.
whoIsAffected: The athletes of the Bangsamoro Cotabato Dojo and the Sultan Mastura Dojo
Bangsamoro athletes competing in national and international events
The Bangsamoro Sports Commission
implementedBy: Bangsamoro Sports Commission

funding.detail: The resolution appropriates nothing. It encourages the Bangsamoro Sports Commission to propose a supplementary allocation for sports institutions in its annual budget proposal, but names no amount.

whatChanges: A copy goes to the Bangsamoro Sports Commission with a request to keep supporting athletes and to propose a sports allocation in its budget.
No amount, deadline or report is attached, so the request depends on the Commission and on Parliament's own budget deliberations.
readings.insight:
The money request points back at Parliament. The Commission can only propose a supplementary allocation; it is Parliament that appropriates, and the resolution does not say how much it thinks sports institutions need.

Karate drew 2 honorific resolutions in a month: Resolution 460 (18 June 2024) commended the Mindanao State University karate club. Resolution 522 (23 January 2025) later backed the Commission's inter-government agency sports festival.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament urges the Government of the Day to work with the relevant government agencies and provide the funding needed to extend for 2 years the land lease agreements under the temporary shelters of people displaced by the 2017 Marawi siege.

The resolution goes to the Office of the Chief Minister "with prayer for prompt and appropriate action". Filed by MP Diamila D. Ramos and 10 others. Adopted on 17 July 2024.
readings.whyProposed: After the siege, the Marawi City government leased private land for temporary shelters: 20 hectares in Sagonsongan, 20 in Boganga, 5 in Dulay and 3 in Patani and Rorugagus, all on 5-year terms that ended in the first quarter of 2023. The National Housing Authority counted 1,972 occupied temporary shelters and Task Force Bangon Marawi 4,916 families still in transitory shelters. In September 2023 landowners served eviction notices and rent demands on at least 1,419 families (1,189 in Boganga and 270 in Rorugagus), with eviction set for 15 October 2023 and rent of ₱500 to ₱1,000 plus a ₱600 water bill to follow.
