Congress concurred, and the proclamations took effect on 24 January 2022, so by the resolution's count barely 2 months were left. It notes that only 2 of the 3 Commission members had been appointed, the chairperson's post still empty, and quotes Senator Panfilo M. Lacson on giving 'over 7,600 prospective applicants' a second chance.
whoIsAffected: MILF and MNLF members eligible for amnesty who had not yet applied.
implementedBy: Office of the President
National Amnesty Commission
whatChanges: Nothing changes unless the President acts. The deadline is set in the proclamations; the resolution is an appeal.
Copies go to Congress, the National Amnesty Commission, the Intergovernmental Relations Body and OPAPRU.
deliberation: 21 November 2022: MP Mary Ann M. Arnado said 2 of the 3 National Amnesty Commission members had been appointed but not the chair, and only 2 months remained to process MILF and MNLF amnesty applications.

21 November 2022: MP Baintan A. Ampatuan argued that the President could appoint the chair at any time, rendering the resolution moot; MP Mary Ann M. Arnado answered that the chair and implementing rules were still lacking and the application period needed extending.

21 November 2022: MP Nabil A. Tan objected that the title carried more than 1 subject, contrary to the Rules; MP Mary Ann M. Arnado replied the action points were interrelated, and MP Nabil A. Tan suggested “respectfully urge” instead of “the President must”.

21 November 2022: MP Baintan A. Ampatuan’s amendments, accepted by the proponent, deleted whereas clauses on the unconstituted commission and retitled the measure as an appeal to extend the amnesty application period for qualified MILF and MNLF members.
21 November 2022: MP John Anthony L. Lim had a clause on fast-tracking the implementing rules deleted because issuing them is not within the President’s ambit; accepted.

21 November 2022: MP Nabil A. Tan and MP Sha Elijah B. Dumama-Alba added a clause furnishing copies to Congress, the National Amnesty Commission and the Intergovernmental Relations Body, to which MP Baintan A. Ampatuan added OPAPRU.
21 November 2022: Adopted and approved, subject to style, with all Members present included as co-authors.
readings.insight: The WHEREAS clauses say the Commission chairperson's appointment should be fast-tracked, but the RESOLVED clauses ask only for the extension. It follows Resolution No. 121 (24 March 2021), which urged Congress to concur in the proclamations, and comes before Resolution No. 377 (July 2023), thanking the President for his amnesty commitment in his State of the Nation Address, and Resolution No. 561 (November 2025) on safe conduct passes for applicants. The adopted text is marked PR70.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament congratulates the students from the region who won 20 medals at the 2022 Smart/MVP Sports Foundation National Interschool Taekwondo Championships, and recognizes their trainers, referees and schools. A copy is to be presented to the medalists and their schools.

The resolution names each medalist. In sparring (Kyorugi): gold for Guthrie Ferrer and Arran Ace Ambasa, silver for Aevemech Monteclaro and 7 bronze medals. In forms (Poomsae): gold for Althea Laureigne Juanitez Juachon, Sittie Shamera C. Samanodin, Jabbar Abdul and Dhan Joseph Eligio, silver for Arran Ace Ambasa and 5 bronze medals. It also recognizes Robert John Cabañog for the Best Male Referee Special Award and coaches Byron B. Betita and Jan Rae Mijares Cañabano.

Authored by MP Marjanie S. Macasalong, MP Ubaida C. Pacasem and MP Amilbahar S. Mawallil. Adopted on 22 November 2022.
readings.whyProposed: The Philippine Taekwondo Association held the championships on 1 to 2 October 2022 at Ayala Malls Manila Bay, Pasay City, with about 2,000 students. Students from 10 schools in the region, trained by the HOTC team, won 6 gold, 2 silver and 12 bronze medals. The 10 schools range from Notre Dame of Upi and Notre Dame of Cotabato to Camp Siongco National High School and several elementary schools.
whoIsAffected: The student medalists, their coaches and their 10 schools.
whatChanges: Nothing changes in law. This is a commendation.
A copy is presented to the medalists and their schools.
deliberation: 22 November 2022: MP Baintan A. Ampatuan asked how many Bangsamoro participants competed and how the region ranked; MP Marjanie S. Macasalong said almost 2,000 students took part and only medal counts were available.

22 November 2022: Asked by MP Baintan A. Ampatuan what government support the schools received, MP Marjanie S. Macasalong cited technical assistance through MBHTE and said the schools paid for training gyms.

22 November 2022: MP Suharto M. Ambolodto pressed on whether any assistance, even transportation, had been given; co-author MP Amilbahar S. Mawallil said they had no concrete data but the Bangsamoro Sports Commission could still extend incentives.

22 November 2022: MP Amilbahar S. Mawallil suggested asking the Bangsamoro Sports Commission for its list of programs while its budget was under deliberation, to inform policies on sports development.
22 November 2022: Approved, subject to style, with no amendments offered.
readings.insight: The medal lists add up: 10 medals in each event, 6 gold, 2 silver and 12 bronze in all, won by 13 students, 7 of whom medalled in both events. The training team is called the 'Heart of the Champion' in a WHEREAS clause and the 'Home of the Champion' in the RESOLVED clause, and one medalist is spelled 'Aevemech' on page 1 and 'Aevemelech' on page 2 (both confirmed on the page images). The adopted text is marked PR67.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament congratulates and commends Kuraiz Alamada Abubakar of Cotabato City for placing 8th in the September 2022 Philippine Veterinarian Licensure Examination. A copy is to be presented to him.

Authored by MP Diamila D. Ramos, MP Baintan A. Ampatuan and MP Eddie M. Alih. Adopted on 22 November 2022.
readings.whyProposed: The examination was held on 27 to 29 September 2022 in 8 testing centers, and the Professional Regulation Commission announced on 3 October 2022 that 335 of 928 examinees passed. Abubakar ranked 8th with an average of 82.82%. The resolution describes him as an Iranun from Cotabato City who graduated from the University of Southern Mindanao in Kabacan at 25.
whoIsAffected: Kuraiz Alamada Abubakar.
whatChanges: Nothing changes in law. This is a commendation.
A copy is presented to him.
deliberation: 22 November 2022: MP Mary Ann M. Arnado asked whether commendations should carry tangible value such as a plaque; MP Diamila D. Ramos answered that incentives for achievers, such as scholarships, should be institutionalized by law.
22 November 2022: MP Nabil A. Tan supported the resolution but suggested guidelines on the extent of commendations and congratulations the Parliament gives to achievers.

22 November 2022: Treated as a simple resolution; after MP Diamila D. Ramos’s authorship speech and brief exchanges, interpellations and amendments were dispensed with and it was approved, subject to style; the journal’s heading paragraph calls it Proposed Resolution No. 60 before printing No. 69.
readings.insight: The national passing rate from the resolution's figures is about 36.1% (335 of 928). It is one of several commendations of exam topnotchers that session, with Resolution No. 273 (MSU social work, 6th) and Resolution No. 295 (civil service exam, 10th). The adopted text is marked PR69.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament thanks President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. for appointing the Secretary of the Office of the Presidential Adviser on Peace, Reconciliation and Unity (OPAPRU), and congratulates Secretary Carlito G. Galvez Jr. on his reappointment. Copies are to be presented to the President and to Secretary Galvez.

Authored by MP Susana S. Anayatin and 7 others. Adopted on 22 November 2022.
readings.whyProposed: Galvez had been President Rodrigo Duterte's peace adviser and stayed on in a holdover capacity before Marcos reappointed him. The resolution credits him with the ratification of the Organic Law during his term, the swearing-in of the new Bangsamoro Transition Authority members, the absence of major conflict since the 2017 Marawi siege and the bringing together of the Moro fronts in the Bangsamoro Government. It lists OPAPRU's mandate, including completing the agreements with the MILF and MNLF.
whoIsAffected: Secretary Carlito G. Galvez Jr. and the Office of the President.
whatChanges: Nothing changes in law. This is an expression of thanks.
Copies are presented to the President and to Secretary Galvez.
deliberation: 22 November 2022: Treated as a simple resolution, sponsored by MP Susana S. Anayatin, consolidated with Proposed Resolution No. 73 and approved together without interpellation or amendment, subject to style.
readings.insight: The adopted text is marked 'Con: PR73 and PR80', a consolidation of 2 proposals. It is the first of a series on Galvez: 55 days later Resolution No. 299 (16 January 2023) thanked the President for moving him to the Department of National Defense; Resolution No. 363 (17 July 2023) thanked him for reappointing Galvez to OPAPRU; Resolution No. 548 (29 May 2025) urged that he be kept; and Resolution No. 574 (29 April 2026) thanked him as former Secretary.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament encourages all Bangsamoro ministries, local government units, bureaus, government-owned or -controlled corporations and other instrumentalities to adopt 'Assalamu Alaykum (Peace be upon you) and/or other culture-based greetings and smile' as their way of greeting visitors.

It also encourages them to put into their budgets and Work and Financial Plans information materials such as pin buttons, posters, standees and pamphlets promoting 'Salam and Smile' among all BARMM employees, especially frontline staff such as security personnel and receptionists. Copies are to be disseminated to all of these offices 'for their information and immediate action'.

Authored by MP Hashemi N. Dilangalen and MP Khalid M. Hadji Abdullah. Adopted on 22 November 2022.
readings.whyProposed: The resolution grounds itself in the courtesy required of public servants by Republic Act No. 6713, the Code of Conduct and Ethical Standards for Public Officials and Employees, and in the Bangsamoro Civil Service Code of 2021 (Bangsamoro Autonomy Act No. 17), which calls for moral governance. It says courtesy and respect in receiving visitors are prerequisites of public trust.
whoIsAffected: Visitors to Bangsamoro government offices.
Bangsamoro government employees, especially security personnel and receptionists.
implementedBy: Bangsamoro ministries, bureaus and offices
Local government units
Government-owned or -controlled corporations

funding.detail: The resolution appropriates nothing. It encourages offices to include the cost of information materials in their own budgets and Work and Financial Plans, without naming an amount.

whatChanges: Nothing is required. The resolution 'encourages'; offices may adopt the greeting and fund the materials or not.
Copies are sent to all Bangsamoro offices.
deliberation: 22 November 2022: MP Omar Yasser C. Sema suggested using the full greeting “Assalamu alaikum warahmatullahi wabarakatuhu” rather than only “Salam”.
22 November 2022: MP Froilyn T. Mendoza noted that Indigenous Peoples greet with “Fiyo bagi” or “Mauyag”, not “Salam”, and asked for an inclusive standard.

22 November 2022: MP Omar Yasser C. Sema’s amendment, accepted by the author MP Hashemi N. Dilangalen, retitled the policy as “Assalamu Alaykum (Peace Be Upon You) and/or other culture-based greetings and smile”.
22 November 2022: Approved, subject to style.
readings.insight: The resolution appropriates nothing and names no amount; it asks offices to pay for the pin buttons and posters out of their own budgets. It addresses offices 'within and outside' the region. No other adopted resolution in the index takes up greetings or the 'Salam and Smile' campaign. The adopted text is marked PR74.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament commends the security sector and the volunteers who took part in the search, rescue and retrieval of victims of Severe Tropical Storm Paeng in Datu Odin Sinsuat and Datu Blah Sinsuat, Maguindanao del Norte. A copy is to be presented to them. The resolution also commiserates with the families who lost loved ones.

Authored by MP Baintan A. Ampatuan. Adopted on 20 December 2022.
readings.whyProposed: Paeng (international name Nalgae) hit the country on 26 to 29 October 2022. On 2 November 2022 Proclamation No. 84 placed CALABARZON, Bicol, Western Visayas and BARMM under a state of calamity for 6 months. The resolution cites the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Council's 6 November count: a death toll of 156, of which 121 confirmed, with 141 injured and 37 missing, and BARMM with the most deaths at 63. Barangay Kusiong in Datu Odin Sinsuat, buried by a mudslide, is called ground zero. It names the 6th Infantry Division, the Police Regional Office, the Philippine Coast Guard, the Bureau of Fire Protection and Bangsamoro READi, and credits local volunteers who searched before the security teams arrived.
whoIsAffected: The security units and volunteers commended.
Families in Datu Odin Sinsuat and Datu Blah Sinsuat who lost relatives in the storm.
whatChanges: Nothing changes in law. This is a commendation.
A copy is to be presented to 'the Security Sector and Volunteers', without a named recipient.
deliberation: 20 December 2022: Treated as a simple resolution, sponsored by MP Baintan A. Ampatuan; interpellations and amendments dispensed with and unanimously approved.
readings.insight: Its death count for the region, 63 from the national council, differs from the 53 fatalities from the Bangsamoro council cited in the 10 Paeng thank-you resolutions adopted the same day (Nos. 283 to 292). It is the only one of the Paeng resolutions addressed to rescuers rather than donors. The adopted text is marked PR90.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament strongly condemns the killing of 3 minors in Lambayong, Sultan Kudarat. A copy goes to the victims' family, for information.

Authored by MP Lanang T. Ali Jr. Adopted on 20 December 2022.
readings.whyProposed: The resolution says that at midnight on 1 December 2022 the minors, Samanuden Ali, Arshad Ansa and Horton Ansa, were killed and declared dead on arrival at the hospital. According to a witness it cites, police on patrol approached and shot them while they begged not to be shot, and their necks bore ligature marks from being strangled with their own shirts. It says the killing was allegedly committed by Lambayong police officers and should be investigated to identify those responsible.
whoIsAffected: The families of Samanuden Ali, Arshad Ansa and Horton Ansa.
whatChanges: Nothing changes in law. This is a condemnation.
A copy goes to the family. No copy goes to the police, the Commission on Human Rights or any investigating body.
deliberation: 20 December 2022: MP Lanang T. Ali, Jr. said the 3 victims were shot at close range, 1 bore signs of strangulation, and the parents had consented to forensic examination.

20 December 2022: MP Amilbahar S. Mawallil asked that the resolution quote the incident report it calls deceptive; MP Lanang T. Ali, Jr. said the Lambayong police report of 2 December 2022 neither named the victims nor described them as minors.

20 December 2022: MP Don Mustapha A. Loong warned that calling the report deceptive amounts to a Parliament finding of guilt against the police and moved to delete that clause and 3 others citing Commission powers; accepted.
20 December 2022: MP Amilbahar S. Mawallil had the word “incidents” removed and the 4th whereas clause attributed to the witness’s account of the strangulation; accepted.
20 December 2022: Approved, subject to style.
readings.insight: A WHEREAS clause says the killing should be investigated and the officers identified, but the RESOLVED clauses only condemn it, and the resolution is sent to the family alone. The account rests on one unnamed witness. It is the only adopted resolution in the index on Lambayong. The adopted text is marked PR121.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament commends Al-Basher 'Basty' Jumangit Buto for earning the Candidate Master title at the 6th Eastern Asia Youth Chess Championship 2022 in Bangkok, Thailand. A copy is to be presented to him.

Authored by MP Ubaida C. Pacasem and 8 others. Adopted on 21 December 2022.
readings.whyProposed: At the championship, held on 4 to 12 November 2022 with about 200 players from 12 countries, the Philippine team placed first overall with 32 gold, 27 silver and 22 bronze medals. Al-Basher, 12, won silver in the boys under-12 standard, rapid and blitz individual events, and team gold (standard) and silver (blitz). The resolution calls him the youngest Bangsamoro to hold both National Master and Candidate Master titles. He is a Maranao living in Cainta, Rizal, the 8th son of Bong and Jamellah Buto, whose support it notes came despite financial constraints.
whoIsAffected: Al-Basher 'Basty' Jumangit Buto.
whatChanges: Nothing changes in law. This is a commendation.
A copy is presented to him.
deliberation: 21 December 2022: MP Baintan A. Ampatuan asked that the resolution connect to the first BTA’s earlier commendation of the same player; MP Mary Ann M. Arnado agreed and cited a Philippine Sports Commission mechanism to support young athletes.
21 December 2022: MP Jose I. Lorena urged a program in the Bangsamoro Youth Commission or Bangsamoro Sports Commission, ideally funded in the 2023 budget, to sustain chess players in tournaments.
21 December 2022: MP Hatimil E. Hassan proposed adding “Special Autonomous Region” after Hong Kong and “China” after Taiwan; the proponent did not accept it.

21 December 2022: MP Omar Yasser C. Sema had the title narrowed to the Candidate Master world title and “SAR” inserted after Hong Kong; accepted, while MP Muslimin A. Jakilan’s bid to include the delegation was answered as already covered.
21 December 2022: Approved.
readings.insight: Parliament commended him once before, in Resolution No. 110 (16 March 2021), whose title also speaks of 'providing support for his future development'. This one mentions his family's financial constraints but offers nothing. The adopted text is marked PR87.

Authored by MP Ubaida C. Pacasem and 8 others. Adopted on 21 December 2022.
readings.whyProposed: Of the 117,938 professional-level examinees, 22,241, or 18.86%, passed. Binsuan earned a Bachelor of Science in Accountancy from Notre Dame University in Cotabato City in June 2022, where he was a dean's lister and college governor. The resolution says he aims to become a public accountant and then a lawyer.

whatChanges: Nothing changes in law. This is a commendation.
A copy is presented to him.

readings.insight: The resolution gives 7 August 2022 both as the day the Civil Service Commission released results and as the day the exam was held (confirmed on the page image), so one of the 2 dates is off. The pass rate checks: 22,241 of 117,938 is 18.86%. It was adopted the same day, by the same 9 authors, as Resolution No. 294 on the young chess player. The adopted text is marked PR88.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament strongly appeals to the Department of Foreign Affairs to reopen its consular services office in Cotabato City to serve BARMM residents. A copy goes to the Department, for information.

Authored by MP Baintan A. Ampatuan. Adopted on 21 December 2022.
readings.whyProposed: The DFA had closed its consular office in Cotabato City, the seat of the regional government, so residents travel to Davao City, General Santos City, Cagayan de Oro City or Zamboanga City, and sometimes to the Visayas or Luzon, for passports. The resolution says passports are needed by workers seeking jobs abroad and by Muslims going on Hajj, most of whom are expected to come from the region, and that foreign officials and donors visit the region regularly. It points to the Organic Law's provision for a Bangsamoro Pilgrimage Authority and to BARMM's role in BIMP-EAGA.
whoIsAffected: BARMM residents who need passports, including overseas job seekers and Hajj pilgrims.
implementedBy: Department of Foreign Affairs
whatChanges: Nothing changes unless the DFA acts. The resolution is an appeal.
A copy goes to the DFA.
deliberation: 21 December 2022: MP Omar Yasser C. Sema recalled that the Cotabato City consular office was a revenue-generating office and passports served as valid identification.
21 December 2022: MP Nabil A. Tan inserted “services” after “consular” and MP Randolph C. Parcasio replaced “cater” with “serve”; both accepted.

21 December 2022: MP Jose I. Lorena added clauses on Cotabato City as the government center and on the organic law’s provision for a Bangsamoro Pilgrimage Authority; accepted as reworded by MP Omar Yasser C. Sema to “presently hosts the government center”.
21 December 2022: Approved, with all Members present included as co-authors.
readings.insight: The resolution does not say when or why the office closed, how many residents need passports, or what the trip costs, and it sets no deadline or follow-up. It is the only adopted resolution in the index on passports or DFA services. The adopted text is marked PR89.

readings.insight: Its count of people affected, 568,969, differs from the 570,285 in the thank-you resolutions to national officials adopted 2 days earlier (Nos. 283 to 292). It is the only Paeng resolution aimed at non-government givers, and it keeps a line from the draft, 'this Proposed Resolution aims to recognize'. The adopted text is marked PR128.

Parliament condemns in the strongest terms the killing of Jocelyn S. Palao, ex officio Commissioner of the Bangsamoro Women Commission and Chief of the Ancestral Domain Division of the Ministry of Indigenous Peoples' Affairs. A copy is to be presented to her family.

Authored by MP Eddie M. Alih and 47 others. Adopted on 22 December 2022.
readings.whyProposed: Citing Cotabato City Police Station 2 chief Major Amil Andungan Jr., the resolution says Palao was heading home in a van at about 5:30 p.m. on 20 December 2022 when riding-in-tandem gunmen who had followed her from work shot her on Teodoro V. Juliano Avenue, Barangay Rosary Heights XI, Cotabato City. She was a Teduray from South Upi, Maguindanao del Sur, and an advocate of indigenous peoples' rights to their ancestral domains. She left her husband, 2 sons, a daughter and grandchildren.
whoIsAffected: Her family.
Indigenous peoples in the region, whose land rights she worked on.
whatChanges: Nothing changes in law. This is a condemnation.
A copy goes to her family. The resolution asks no agency to investigate.
deliberation: 21 December 2022: Treated as a simple resolution, sponsored by MP Eddie M. Alih with a supplemental speech by MP Froilyn T. Mendoza; all Members made authors and approved without interpellation or amendment, subject to style. The official proposed-resolutions index lists this measure as No. 134, not 138.
readings.insight: Adopted 2 days after the killing, with 48 authors. It condemns but does not call for an investigation or a report, and the pledge to 'strengthen the fight for the rights of the IPs' in a WHEREAS clause is not carried into any RESOLVED clause. It is the only adopted resolution in the index on her death. The adopted text is marked PR134.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament thanks President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. for appointing Carlito G. Galvez Jr., the Presidential Adviser on Peace, Reconciliation and Unity, as Secretary of National Defense, and congratulates Galvez. A copy is to be presented to the Office of the President, copy furnished to Secretary Galvez.

Authored by MP Amilbahar S. Mawallil and 7 others. Adopted on 16 January 2023.
readings.whyProposed: On 9 January 2023 the President named Galvez the 37th Secretary of National Defense. The resolution credits him with leading the campaign for the plebiscite and ratification of the Bangsamoro Organic Law, the appointment of an inclusive Parliament and the reunification of Bangsamoro leaders. It recounts his military record: Philippine Military Academy class of 1985, former Armed Forces Chief of Staff, commander in Basilan and Sulu, the defense of Lamitan, the liberation of Marawi, and his medals, including 2 Philippine Legion of Honor medals and 40 Military Merit and Commendation medals.
whoIsAffected: Secretary Carlito G. Galvez Jr.
The Office of the President.
whatChanges: Nothing changes in law. This is an expression of thanks.
A copy goes to the Office of the President and to Secretary Galvez.
deliberation: 16 January 2023: MP Amilbahar S. Mawallil said the appointment of Secretary Carlito G. Galvez, Jr. to National Defense was a testament to his and the President’s success in the peace process.

16 January 2023: Consolidated with Proposed Resolution No. 143 and treated as a simple resolution; after MP Amilbahar S. Mawallil’s sponsorship speech, interpellations and amendments were dispensed with and it was approved, subject to style, with all Members present as authors.
16 January 2023: Consolidated with Proposed Resolution No. 141 and approved with it.
readings.insight: It came 55 days after Resolution No. 280 (22 November 2022) thanked the President for reappointing Galvez as peace adviser. The move did not last: Resolution No. 363 (17 July 2023) thanked the President for reappointing him to OPAPRU. The title and RESOLVED clause call the office 'Peace, Reconciliation, and Unification', while the WHEREAS clauses use the correct 'Unity'. The adopted text is marked 'Con: PR141 and PR143', a consolidation of 2 proposals.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament amends Resolution No. 265 to add the omitted sitting days of the 3rd week of March 2023 to the calendar of the First Regular Session of the Second Parliament. The full calendar runs from the inaugural session on 15 September 2022 to a mandatory adjournment on 21 March 2023. The final blocks are 13 to 16 March and then a resumption on 20 March, with the mandatory adjournment the next day, 21 March 2023.

Authored by MP Sha Elijah B. Dumama-Alba and 40 others. Adopted on 16 January 2023.
readings.whyProposed: Parliament's rules hold plenary sessions Monday to Thursday in the 3rd and 4th weeks of each month. The calendar adopted by Resolution No. 265 on 20 September 2022 left out the 3rd week of March 2023. The Committee on Rules caught the omission at its 4th meeting on 10 January 2023 and approved adding it.
whoIsAffected: Members of Parliament and the Secretariat.
Anyone following Parliament's sitting days.
implementedBy: Bangsamoro Transition Authority Parliament
whatChanges: This one binds Parliament: it adds sitting days on 20 and 21 March 2023 to its own calendar and fixes mandatory adjournment on 21 March 2023.
deliberation: 16 January 2023: Treated as a simple resolution; interpellations and amendments dispensed with and approved, subject to style.
readings.insight: Although it restores 'the session days of the third week', the added block is 2 days long, Monday 20 to Tuesday 21 March, because the mandatory adjournment falls on 21 March. The index dates the resolution 15 January 2023, but the adopted page reads 16 January 2023. The next calendar, for the Second Regular Session, came in Resolution No. 336 (18 May 2023). The adopted text is marked PR144.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament expresses appreciation, recognition and commendation to Dr. Tanaka Akihiko, President of the Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA), for his contributions to the Bangsamoro. A copy is to be presented to him.

Authored by MP Pangalian M. Balindong and 8 others. Adopted on 17 January 2023.
readings.whyProposed: Dr. Tanaka was reappointed JICA President from 1 April 2022, having led it before from 2012 to 2015, and was president of the National Graduate Institute for Policy Studies of Japan. He holds a doctorate in political science from the Massachusetts Institute of Technology and received the Medal with Purple Ribbon. The resolution says JICA has run programs in the region since the former ARMM and credits it with investment in bureaucratic capacity and infrastructure.
whoIsAffected: Dr. Tanaka Akihiko and JICA.
whatChanges: Nothing changes in law. This is a commendation.
A copy is presented to Dr. Tanaka.
deliberation: 17 January 2023: MP Omar Yasser C. Sema said Dr. Tanaka Akihiko, JICA president from 2012 to 2015 and reappointed in 2022, helped leadership development and peace building in the region.

17 January 2023: MP Baintan A. Ampatuan amended the whereas clauses to cite his reappointment from 1 April 2022 and JICA’s programs since the ARMM; MP Don Mustapha A. Loong added “for his impactful and substantial contributions to the Bangsamoro people” to the title; both accepted.
17 January 2023: Approved, subject to style.
readings.insight: It names no JICA project, amount or place. It was adopted the same day as Resolution No. 302, which commends JICA itself, and its lead author is the Speaker, MP Pangalian M. Balindong. The adopted text is marked PR139.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament recognizes and commends the Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA) for its support and assistance to the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region. A copy goes to JICA for information.

Authored by MP Omar Yasser C. Sema. Adopted on 17 January 2023.
readings.whyProposed: JICA worked in the old Muslim autonomous region before BARMM existed, and buildings it built and donated in the Bangsamoro Government Center now house the Bangsamoro Human Rights Commission and other agencies. On 8 June 2022 it signed a grant agreement with the national government for up to 1,800 million yen for the Program for Urgent Improvement of Socioeconomic Infrastructures in Bangsamoro Region in Mindanao, which includes rebuilding a vocational training center in Marawi City for former combatants.
whoIsAffected: JICA, as the institution commended.
whatChanges: None in force. It is a commendation; a copy is sent to JICA.
deliberation: 17 January 2023: MP Baintan A. Ampatuan asked whether other development partners deserve similar recognition in later sessions; MP Omar Yasser C. Sema agreed.
17 January 2023: MP Nabil A. Tan asked whether the measure duplicated Proposed Resolution No. 139; MP Omar Yasser C. Sema said JICA has a personality separate from its president.
17 January 2023: Approved, subject to style.
readings.insight: It was adopted the same day as Resolution No. 301, which separately commends JICA's president, Dr. Tanaka Akihiko. The one figure in the text is the grant ceiling of 1,800 million yen signed in June 2022; the resolution does not say how much has been released or spent.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament approves the 2nd Bangsamoro Development Plan (BDP) 2023-2028, the region's medium-term development plan. A final clause says improvements can still be incorporated into the plan after approval.

Authored by MP Sha Elijah B. Dumama-Alba, MP Raissa H. Jajurie, MP Mary Ann M. Arnado, MP Anna Tarhata S. Basman and MP Jose I. Lorena. Adopted on 18 January 2023.
readings.whyProposed: Under the Bangsamoro Organic Law, the Bangsamoro Economic and Development Council (BEDC) is the planning and coordinating body for the region's development plans, set up by BAA No. 6 with the Bangsamoro Planning and Development Authority (BPDA) as its secretariat. The 1st BDP 2020-2022 was approved by Parliament on 3 July 2020. The BEDC adopted the 2nd plan at its meeting on 23 December 2022 and endorsed it to Parliament; the BPDA gave copies to Members on 11 January 2023. The plan carries the Bangsamoro Government's 12-Point Priority Agenda and is described as consistent with President Marcos's 8-Point Socioeconomic Agenda and the Philippine Development Plan 2023-2028. It also guides use of the Special Development Fund for conflict-affected communities.
whoIsAffected: Ministries and offices of the Bangsamoro Government, whose programs and budgets are meant to follow the plan.
Residents of the region, as the plan sets development priorities through 2028.
implementedBy: Bangsamoro Economic and Development Council
Bangsamoro Planning and Development Authority
whatChanges: The 2nd BDP 2023-2028 carries Parliament's approval and serves as the basis for multi-year planning, programming and budgeting.
The plan's attachments, the Bangsamoro Development Investment Program, the Results Matrices and the Policy Research Agenda, were not approved here; the text says they would be submitted later.
The plan stays open to amendment after approval.
deliberation: 18 January 2023: MP Laisa M. Alamia asked why the poverty target was conservative beside aggressive growth targets; Director General Mohajirin T. Ali said a high GRDP does not automatically reduce poverty incidence.

18 January 2023: MP Laisa M. Alamia asked how the plan tackles poor absorptive capacity; Director General Mohajirin T. Ali cited capacity-building led by the finance ministry and permanent finance, planning and budget officers.

18 January 2023: MP Froilyn T. Mendoza said the plan’s human rights section on Indigenous Peoples cited only clan conflict and ignored land conflict and uninvestigated cases; Director General Mohajirin T. Ali said ministries such as MAFAR, MENRE and MIPA would address them.

18 January 2023: MP Ali B. Sangki said his proposals were left out, noting no Shari’ah district or appellate courts under PD 1083 and no plan to acquire Al Amanah Islamic Bank; Director General Mohajirin T. Ali said the bank acquisition was under discussion.

18 January 2023: MP Don Mustapha A. Loong disputed claims that the Bangsamoro is 100% electrified and noted Sulu’s missing growth centers, old tourism list, lack of a landfill and weak connectivity coverage.

18 January 2023: MP Baintan A. Ampatuan objected that the plan’s wording on Madaris education becoming “dominant” and on the Parliament not passing priority codes should be revisited; Director General Mohajirin T. Ali agreed.
18 January 2023: Approved, subject to style, approving the 2nd Bangsamoro Development Plan 2023-2028.
readings.insight: Parliament approved the plan 1 week after Members received copies on 11 January 2023, and before its investment program and results matrices were submitted. The resolution itself flags that the plan can still be changed. It follows Resolution No. 78 (3 July 2020), which approved the 1st BDP; 2 months later Resolution No. 321 asked development partners to help prepare master plans and feasibility studies for the big-ticket projects this plan identifies.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament thanks Senator Imee R. Marcos and Atty. Gilbert Teodoro for their immediate response and assistance to people in the Bangsamoro hit by Severe Tropical Storm Paeng. A copy goes to their offices.

Authored by MP Jose I. Lorena. Adopted on 19 January 2023.
readings.whyProposed: Paeng struck the region on 26 October 2022. The Bangsamoro Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Council reported about 570,285 people affected, 53 dead, 12 missing and 38 injured, 371 houses destroyed and 480 partly damaged, and losses of almost ₱600,000,000 in infrastructure and agriculture. Chief Minister Ahod B. Ebrahim declared a state of calamity on 29 October 2022. The resolution says Marcos and Teodoro visited affected areas, including the 65 barangays of the Special Geographic Area in Cotabato Province, and delivered relief goods.
whoIsAffected: Senator Imee R. Marcos and Atty. Gilbert Teodoro, who are thanked.
whatChanges: None in force. It is an expression of thanks; copies go to the 2 people named.
deliberation: 19 January 2023: Periods of interpellation and amendments dispensed with; approved, subject to style.
readings.insight: One of more than 10 Paeng thank-you resolutions: in December 2022 Parliament adopted a series (Resolutions No. 283 to 292 and 297) thanking senators, the Vice President, the President and private groups. The title calls both men senators, but the body names Gilbert Teodoro only as Atty.; it does not describe what or how much he and Senator Marcos delivered.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament urges the Department of Transportation (DOTr), through the Civil Aviation Authority of the Philippines (CAAP), to act immediately to finish the renovation of Cotabato Airport, adding personnel, equipment and materials as needed. It asks DOTr and CAAP to monitor the work closely and, if there are further delays, to impose financial penalties or terminate the contract, and to hold the contractor liable for added costs and any damage to airport facilities.

Copies go, through the Intergovernmental Relations Body, to DOTr, CAAP, the contractor, airport management and the media. Authored by MP Baileng S. Mantawil, MP Mary Ann M. Arnado, MP Sha Elijah B. Dumama-Alba and MP Eddie M. Alih. Adopted on 19 January 2023.
readings.whyProposed: CAAP's own project status report shows the expansion of the Cotabato passenger terminal started on 29 September 2020 and was due on 1 August 2021, then moved to 4 December 2021. As of June 2022 CAAP's website put it at 64.94% complete, with liquidated damages of ₱23,636.12 for every day of delay. The authors say the delay inconveniences travellers, poses a potential health hazard and hampers airport operations.
whoIsAffected: Travellers using Cotabato Airport.
The renovation contractor, whom the resolution wants held to account.
implementedBy: Department of Transportation
Civil Aviation Authority of the Philippines
Intergovernmental Relations Body
whatChanges: Nothing binding. DOTr and CAAP are national agencies the BTA cannot direct; the resolution urges.
Copies go to DOTr, CAAP, the contractor, airport management and the media through the Intergovernmental Relations Body.
deliberation: 19 January 2023: MP Mawallil asked about the status and cost of the renovation; MP Mantawil said the DOTr project was funded under the 2019 GAA at ₱41,427,313.00, started 29 September 2020, was due 1 August 2021, and stood at only 75.81% complete when work stopped on 4 December 2021.

19 January 2023: MP Mantawil listed the causes of delay from the DOTr status report: late delivery of materials, inadequate manpower, no contractor engineer on site and slow progress; MP Ampatuan added that the DOTr may take legal action against a contractor who fails its obligations.

19 January 2023: MP Tan asked about BARMM's role; MP Mantawil said it is a national government project implemented by the DOTr, with BARMM as beneficiary and the MOTC only facilitating, and there was no change of contractor.

19 January 2023: MP Loong (DM) noted that the Civil Aviation Authority of the Philippines conducted the bidding and moved to insert CAAP into the title and text, plus a whereas clause citing 64.94% completion as of June 2022 and liquidated damages of ₱23,636.12 per day of delay; accepted.
19 January 2023: Approved as amended, subject to style.
readings.insight: The figures come from CAAP's own reporting: 64.94% done as of June 2022, against a deadline that had already passed twice, with liquidated damages of ₱23,636.12 a day. The resolution does not name the contractor or the contract price and sets no date for a reply. Airports came up again: Resolution No. 398 (September 2023) invited CAAP and others to explain the status of Awang Airport's rehabilitation.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament amends Resolution No. 97 and adopts a validated list of 65 Bangsamoro winners of international Qur'an competitions: 37 reciters (1st to 3rd place, male and female categories) and 28 memorizers (1st to 3rd place), with each person's province of origin, competition venue and year.

It requests the Office of the Chief Minister, through the Bangsamoro Commission for the Preservation of Cultural Heritage (BCPCH), to award plaques of recognition or other tokens to those listed. Copies go to Chief Minister Ahod B. Ebrahim, the BCPCH and the honorees. Authored by MP Eddie M. Alih and 41 others. Adopted on 19 January 2023.
readings.whyProposed: Resolution No. 97 recognized Bangsamoro Qur'an reciters who had placed in international competitions since 1969. Formal participation by Muslim Mindanao delegates began in 1979 after the 1976 Tripoli Agreement, but Muslim Filipinos had competed since 1969 and the authors say they also deserve recognition. To carry out Resolution No. 97, the Office of the Chief Minister set up a technical working group, which formed a validation committee to review the list of awardees; this resolution adopts the result.
whoIsAffected: The 65 reciters and memorizers listed, several marked as deceased.
The Bangsamoro Commission for the Preservation of Cultural Heritage, asked to present the awards.
implementedBy: Office of the Chief Minister
Bangsamoro Commission for the Preservation of Cultural Heritage
whatChanges: Resolution No. 97's honoree list is replaced by the validated list of 65.
The Chief Minister's office and the BCPCH are asked, not required, to award plaques or other tokens.
deliberation: 19 January 2023: MP Ampatuan pointed out that the committee report's pages cite 1979, not 1969; MP Alih conceded the correct year is 1979, since the data on Bangsamoro reciters' wins ran from 1979 onward.

19 January 2023: MP Ampatuan moved to replace every 1969 with 1979 and to add a whereas clause that 1979 marks formal participation of Muslim Mindanao delegates after the 1976 Tripoli Agreement; accepted by MP Alih.
19 January 2023: Approved as amended, subject to style.
readings.insight: This follows up Resolution No. 97 of 17 December 2020, which recognized reciters only; the amendment adds memorizers to the title and the list, more than 2 years later. The earliest win on the validated list is 1974 (Malaysia); none dates from 1969, the year both titles cite. Not all honorees are from the region: several memorizers come from South Cotabato, Sultan Kudarat, General Santos City, Zamboanga del Sur and North Cotabato. The resolution names no budget for the plaques.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament congratulates and commends Atty. Faydah Maniri Dumarpa on her appointment as a Member of the 6th Commission en banc of the Commission on Human Rights, dated 28 December 2022. A copy goes to Commissioner Dumarpa.

Authored by MP Khalid M. Hadji Abdullah. Adopted on 24 January 2023.
readings.whyProposed: President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. appointed Dumarpa as Third Member of the Commission's 6th en banc on 28 December 2022; the appointment reached the Commission on 5 January 2023, for a 7-year term from 2022 to 2029. She is a native of Lanao del Sur and, the resolution says, the first Bangsamoro woman appointed a Commissioner and the second Bangsamoro appointee after Atty. Nasser A. Marohomsalic, who served from 1994 to 2001.
whoIsAffected: Commissioner Faydah Maniri Dumarpa.
whatChanges: None in force. It is a commendation; a copy goes to the Commissioner.
deliberation: 24 January 2023: Periods of interpellation and amendments dispensed with; approved, subject to style.
readings.insight: A commendation for a national appointment. By the resolution's count, she is only the second Bangsamoro member of the Commission on Human Rights in its 6 en banc compositions, and the first woman from the Bangsamoro.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament thanks President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. for constituting the Marawi Compensation Board, and congratulates its chairperson, Maisara C. Dandamun-Latiph, and 8 members appointed on 13 January 2023. Copies go to the Office of the President, the Office of the Chief Minister and the Board.

Authored by MP Anna Tarhata S. Basman. Adopted on 24 January 2023.
readings.whyProposed: Republic Act No. 11696, the Marawi Siege Victims Compensation Act of 2022, was signed on 13 April 2022 to compensate people displaced by the 2017 siege for properties and lives lost. It created the Board, a quasi-judicial body of a chairperson and 8 members appointed by the President, to receive, evaluate and approve claims and pay qualified claimants. The 8 members named are Sittie Aliyyah Lomondot Adiong, Dalomabi Lao Bula, Mustapha C. Dimaampao, Jamaica Lamping Dimaporo, Mabandes Sumndad Diron Jr., Moslemen T. Macarambon Sr., Romaisa Lomantong Mamutuk and Nasser Macapado Tabao.
whoIsAffected: Displaced residents of Marawi City who may claim compensation.
The chairperson and members of the Marawi Compensation Board.
whatChanges: None in force. It thanks and congratulates; copies go to the President, the Chief Minister and the Board.
deliberation: 24 January 2023: MP Ampatuan asked the Board's primary function; MP Tago said it receives, evaluates and approves claims and promptly disburses compensation to qualified claimants.

24 January 2023: MP Lorena asked about funding under the Marawi Siege Victims Compensation Act of 2022; MP Tago said no amount is fixed, but the President gave ₱1,000,000,000 in initial funding and later appropriations are authorized, with the Board's term set at 5 years and extendable.
24 January 2023: MP Macatanong asked how members were chosen; MP Tago said the law sets a selection process and the Board includes an engineer, a physician, a CPA and a civil society representative.

24 January 2023: MP Babao asked whether the Board replaced Task Force Bangon Marawi and whether ₱1,000,000,000 is enough; MP Tago said it assumed the task force's functions and the amount is not enough, being only for victims' compensation.

24 January 2023: MP Tan and the Chair asked who handles the money; MP Tago said the Board disburses it, the ₱1,000,000,000 goes to reparation of victims, and salaries come from a separate ₱50,000,000 operational budget from Congress.
24 January 2023: Approved without amendments, subject to style.
readings.insight: The Board was appointed 9 months after the law was signed. Parliament had pressed for a compensation law since 2019: Resolutions No. 14, 33, 151 and 156 urged Congress to pass one, and Resolution No. 216 (February 2022) asked President Duterte to sign it. This resolution thanks rather than asks; it does not mention any claims paid.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament congratulates and commends Abdul Baterbonia Lumanggal, a University of Southern Mindanao graduate who ranked Top 10 with a rating of 92.60% in the October 2022 Licensure Examination for Teachers at the elementary level, and all Bangsamoro who passed that examination. A copy goes to Lumanggal and the Bangsamoro passers.

Authored by MP Kadil M. Sinolinding Jr., MP Diamila D. Ramos and MP Eddie M. Alih. Adopted on 25 January 2023.
readings.whyProposed: The Professional Regulation Commission held the examination on 2 October 2022 and announced on 16 December 2022 that 49,783 of 91,468 elementary-level examinees (54.43%) passed: 29,183 first-timers and 20,600 repeaters. Lumanggal, a 28-year-old Maguindanaon from Poblacion Carmen, Cotabato, graduated magna cum laude from the University of Southern Mindanao in Kabacan.
whoIsAffected: Abdul Baterbonia Lumanggal.
Bangsamoro passers of the October 2022 elementary teachers' examination.
whatChanges: None in force. It is a commendation; copies go to the honorees.
deliberation: 25 January 2023: MP Ramos, attending via Zoom, protested being barred from answering interpellations; the Chair said it had been ruled that no one on Zoom may respond to interpellations.
25 January 2023: MP Ali (L), Jr. noted many Bangsamoro passed the last teachers' exam and moved to add "and all Bangsamoros who passed" to the title and body; accepted.
25 January 2023: Approved as amended, subject to style.
26 January 2023: Treated as a simple resolution; periods of interpellation and amendments dispensed with; approved and consolidated with Proposed Resolution No. 148, approved the previous day.
readings.insight: One of many commendations of licensure examination topnotchers the BTA adopted in this period, alongside Resolution No. 310 on X-ray technologists the same day. The adopted page is dated 25 January 2023; Parliament's index lists 26 January. The resolution does not say how many Bangsamoro passed.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament congratulates and commends 4 young Bangsamoro professionals who ranked among the topnotchers of the December 2022 X-Ray Technologist Licensure Examination: Cetee Sahara Ulama Aliso (Top 2, 84.25%), Nadia Sindatu Nabadtog (Top 4, 82.75%), Sittie Farhanna Usop Calis (Top 7, 81.75%) and Nasrhea Usop Oyong (Top 9, 80.25%). A copy goes to each of them.

Authored by MP Diamila D. Ramos and MP Eddie M. Alih. Adopted on 25 January 2023.
readings.whyProposed: The Professional Regulation Commission and the Board of Radiologic Technology held the examination on 21 and 22 December 2022. Results released on 5 January 2023 showed 49 of 263 examinees passed the X-ray technologist exam (1,515 of 3,759 passed the separate radiologic technologist exam). All 4 honorees are Maguindanaon women aged 21 to 23 from Cotabato City; 1 studied at Notre Dame Siena College and 3 at Notre Dame Hospital & School of Midwifery.
whoIsAffected: The 4 topnotchers named.
whatChanges: None in force. It is a commendation; copies go to the 4 honorees.
deliberation: 25 January 2023: Periods of interpellation and amendments dispensed with; approved, subject to style.
readings.insight: 4 of the 49 passers nationwide, all from Cotabato City and 3 from the same school, placed in the top 10. One of many commendations of board examination topnotchers in this period; Resolution No. 309, adopted the same day, honors a teachers' examination topnotcher.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament urges the Ministry of Transportation and Communications (MOTC) to ask the national Department of Transportation and Communications to require airlines flying to airports in the region to make in-flight announcements in the major local language, and to require airport authorities in the region to make airport announcements in the major local languages, in addition to English and Filipino. A copy goes to the MOTC.

Authored by MP Mohagher M. Iqbal and MP Eddie M. Alih. Adopted on 25 January 2023.
readings.whyProposed: The Civil Aviation Authority of the Philippines transferred landside management of 6 airports to the MOTC: Awang in Maguindanao del Norte, Wao and Malabang in Lanao del Sur, Sanga-Sanga and the Mapun airstrip in Tawi-Tawi, and Jolo in Sulu. The authors argue that announcements in local languages help passengers, preserve Bangsamoro culture as the Organic Law requires, and support tourism.
whoIsAffected: Air passengers in the region who do not follow English or Filipino well.
Airlines and airport operators serving the region's airports.
implementedBy: Ministry of Transportation and Communications
whatChanges: Nothing binding. The MOTC is urged to make a request of a national department; any rule would have to come from Manila.
The resolution does not name which languages count as major local languages.
deliberation: 25 January 2023: MP Iqbal argued many rural passengers do not fully understand English or Filipino and that using the region's 13 ethno-linguistic languages recognizes Bangsamoro identity under the BOL.

25 January 2023: MP Tago, as MOTC Minister, supported it, saying cancellations and delays announced only in English or Filipino may not be understood, and pledged to ask airlines at Awang and Tawi-Tawi airports to use local languages.

25 January 2023: MP Lorena amended the title so the MOTC asks the national transport department to require airline operators and airport authorities to announce in local languages; accepted by MP Iqbal.
25 January 2023: Approved as amended.
readings.insight: The request names the Department of Transportation and Communications (DOTC) National, while Resolution No. 305, adopted 6 days earlier, addressed the Department of Transportation (DOTr). Since the MOTC already runs the landside operations of the 6 transferred airports, terminal announcements there are partly within regional control, but the resolution does not ask the MOTC to start with those.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament commends and supports Fauzia Tumbas-Lidasan, a Bangsamoro mountain climber aiming to reach the summit of Mount Everest by May 2025. It tasks the Bangsamoro Women Commission (BWC) and the Bangsamoro Sports Commission (BSC) to give her the assistance and support she needs to prepare. A copy goes to her.

Authored by MP Lanang T. Ali Jr. Adopted on 26 January 2023.
readings.whyProposed: On 26 April 2022 she and her team reached Everest Base Camp at 5,364 meters, where she raised the Bangsamoro flag, the first Bangsamoro climber to do so. She is 40, a mother of 5 from Sultan Kudarat, Maguindanao del Norte, and began climbing in 2016 after her husband died. Her stated schedule is Kilimanjaro (5,895 meters) by June 2023, Mera Peak (6,476 meters) by November 2023, Cho Oyu (8,188 meters) by April 2024, and Everest (8,848 meters) by March to May 2025.
whoIsAffected: Fauzia Tumbas-Lidasan.
The Bangsamoro Women Commission and the Bangsamoro Sports Commission, tasked to support her.
implementedBy: Bangsamoro Women Commission
Bangsamoro Sports Commission
whatChanges: The BWC and BSC are tasked to assist her, but the resolution sets no amount, form of support or deadline.
deliberation: 26 January 2023: MP Sinolinding, Jr. asked what support BARMM and the Parliament could give; MP Ali (L), Jr. said monetary and moral support and dua, and the Chair raised whether she would need leave as an MBHTE nurse.

26 January 2023: MP Ampatuan noted 2 Bangsamoro women, Atty. Lailanie Tiboron and Engr. Analisa Lumedek, had already reached Everest base camp in 2016 and 2017, and said the summit needs at least ₱5,000,000.
26 January 2023: MP Lim said Tawi-Tawi would shoulder part of her airfare after MP Ali (L), Jr. said she needs about ₱250,000 for training in Tanzania; the Chair pledged ₱20,000 from his office.
26 January 2023: MP Mitmug, Jr. moved to add a clause tasking the Bangsamoro Women Commission and Bangsamoro Sports Commission to assist her; accepted by MP Ali (L), Jr.
26 January 2023: Approved as amended.
readings.insight: Unlike most commendations, this one gives 2 regional bodies a task. It does not say what the support is or what it would cost, and the repo holds no record of what was provided or whether the 2025 summit attempt took place. The text gives Everest's height as both 8,849 and 8,848 meters.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament expresses its unequivocal support for Senate Bill No. 1272 and House Bill No. 5693, which would declare 1 February of every year National Hijab Day and promote understanding of the Muslim tradition of wearing the hijab. Copies go to the office of Senator Robinhood Padilla and the House of Representatives, with copies to the Office of the Chief Minister and the Bangsamoro Women Commission.

Authored by MP Diamila D. Ramos and 7 others. Adopted on 26 January 2023.
readings.whyProposed: Senator Padilla filed SB 1272 on 5 September 2022; it was substituted by SB 1410 under Committee Report No. 8, calendared on 7 November 2022 and pending interpellation. The House version, HB 5693, was approved on third reading on 15 November 2022. The authors cite constitutional guarantees of equality between women and men and free exercise of religion, and the Organic Law's duty to protect women from discrimination, and say the bills aim to address discrimination and misinformation about women who wear the hijab.
whoIsAffected: Muslim women and girls who wear the hijab.
Congress, whose bills are endorsed.
whatChanges: Nothing binding. It is an endorsement of national bills; copies go to Senator Padilla and the House.
deliberation: 26 January 2023: MP Parcasio said the resolution recognizes not only the cultural rights of Muslim Bangsamoro but the religion they practise, and expressed profound support.
26 January 2023: Period of amendments dispensed with; approved, subject to style.
readings.insight: Parliament endorsed the same idea in the previous Congress: Resolution No. 131 (24 June 2021) supported Senate Bill No. 2081 and House Bill No. 8249, both declaring 1 February National Hijab Day. This resolution backs the refiled versions in the 19th Congress. Resolution No. 260 (July 2022) had separately asked agencies in the region to observe a respect-for-hijab policy. The repo does not record whether the 19th Congress bills were enacted.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament thanks the Supreme Court and Chief Justice Alexander G. Gesmundo for including the strengthening of Shari'ah justice in the Judiciary's Strategic Plan for Judicial Innovations (SPJI) 2022-2027. A copy goes to the Court and the Chief Justice.

Authored by MP Sha Elijah B. Dumama-Alba, MP Anna Tarhata S. Basman, MP Raissa H. Jajurie, MP Mosber E. Alauddin, MP Mary Ann M. Arnado and MP Ubaida C. Pacasem. Adopted on 26 January 2023.
readings.whyProposed: The Supreme Court launched the 5-year SPJI in a special en banc session on 14 October 2022. Under its Outcome 3 on access, an objective titled "Strengthen the Foundations of Shari'ah Justice" commits the Court to form a Committee on Shari'ah Justice to pursue reforms supporting justice and the rule of law in the region. Shari'ah justice is one of the pillars of the Bangsamoro justice system under Article X of the Organic Law.
whoIsAffected: The Supreme Court and Chief Justice Gesmundo.
whatChanges: None in force. It is an expression of thanks; a copy goes to the Supreme Court.
deliberation: 26 January 2023: MP Tan asked what strengthening Shari'ah justice involves; MP Dumama-Alba cited a new Supreme Court Committee on Shari'ah under Justice Marvic Leonen, a first National Shari'ah Summit in March 2023, filling Shari'ah court vacancies and backing more courts outside BARMM.
26 January 2023: MP Tan asked whether a Supreme Court Jurisconsult had been appointed as PD 1083 mandates; MP Dumama-Alba said no.
26 January 2023: MP Parcasio recalled USAID support for Shari'ah justice under the former ARMM and said Muslim-populated regions outside BARMM also need Shari'ah courts.
26 January 2023: Period of amendments dispensed with; approved.
readings.insight: 2 months later Parliament went from thanks to requests: Resolution No. 326 (21 March 2023) asked the Court to create a Committee on Shari'ah Bar Integration, and Resolution No. 458 (May 2024) asked it to organize the Shari'ah High Court. This resolution does not say whether the Committee on Shari'ah Justice had been formed.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament expresses its condolences to the family of Sheikh Khalipha Usman Nando, the first Wali of the Bangsamoro, who died on 5 February 2023, and its gratitude for his contributions to the Bangsamoro struggle and the region. A copy goes to his family.

Authored by MP Sha Elijah B. Dumama-Alba and 49 others. Adopted on 17 February 2023.
readings.whyProposed: Nando was named the first Wali, the ceremonial head of the Bangsamoro Government, by consensus in Resolution No. 1 at the inaugural session on 29 March 2019, and again when the transition was extended to 30 June 2025. He was a founder of the Moro Islamic Liberation Front, a senior member of its Central Committee, chair of its Committee on Education from 1976 to 2003, Chief Justice of the MILF Supreme Shari'ah Court from 2005, and founding president of Hay-atul Ulama in the Philippines from 2008. The resolution credits him with pushing for Islamic finance and the institution of zakat.
whoIsAffected: Sheikh Nando's family.
whatChanges: None in force. It is a condolence resolution; a copy goes to the family.
deliberation: 17 February 2023: Periods of interpellation and amendments dispensed with; consolidated Proposed Resolutions No. 171, 172, 173, 174 and 180 approved, subject to style.
readings.insight: It closes one line of the Wali resolutions: Resolution No. 1 (2019) and No. 266 (2022) recorded consensus on Nando, this one mourns him, Resolution No. 327 (May 2023) let MP Said Z. Salendab act as Wali only to open a session, and Resolution No. 445 (May 2024) named a successor, Sheikh Muslim Masaglang Guiamaden. The index credits this resolution to 50 authors.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament conveys its condolences to the bereaved families and its solidarity with the people and government of Turkiye after the earthquake of 6 February 2023. A copy goes to the Turkish Embassy in the Philippines.

Authored by MP Abdulraof A. Macacua and 60 others. Adopted on 17 February 2023.
readings.whyProposed: A 7.8 magnitude earthquake hit Gaziantep, followed by aftershocks including a 7.5 quake. Citing a CNBC report of 13 February 2023, the resolution puts the combined death toll in Turkiye and Syria above 41,000. It recalls Turkish support for the Bangsamoro in the implementation of the Comprehensive Agreement on the Bangsamoro and says the Bangsamoro Government is finding ways to help.
whoIsAffected: The people of Turkiye and the families of the dead.
whatChanges: None in force. It is a condolence resolution; a copy goes to the Turkish Embassy.
deliberation: 17 February 2023: Periods of interpellation and amendments dispensed with; consolidated Proposed Resolutions No. 175 and 185 approved, subject to style.
17 February 2023: Added to the Order of Business; approved as consolidated with Proposed Resolution No. 175, subject to style.
readings.insight: The only resolution in the index on the 2023 Turkiye earthquake, with 61 authors. It mentions that the Bangsamoro Government is looking for ways to help but commits no aid itself. Syria, which the death toll includes, is not otherwise addressed.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament expresses its grief at the death of Ambassador Akmad Atlah Sakkam, Philippine Ambassador to the Hashemite Kingdom of Jordan, its sympathies to his family, and its recognition of his contributions to the Bangsamoro. A copy goes to his family.

Authored by MP Abdulraof A. Macacua and 21 others. Adopted on 17 February 2023.
readings.whyProposed: Sakkam, a Tausug from Indanan and Patikul, died on 8 February 2023 while ambassador to Jordan, with concurrent jurisdiction over Palestine. He had been ambassador to Iraq (1986-1992), Bahrain (1994-1999) and Oman (1999-2003), received a Special Presidential Award of Merit from President Corazon Aquino for evacuating Filipino workers from Kuwait and Iraq in the 1991 Gulf War, and the DFA's Distinguished Service Award in 2012. As a member of the Bangsamoro Transition Commission from 2014 to 2016 he helped draft the original Bangsamoro Basic Law.
whoIsAffected: Ambassador Sakkam's family.
whatChanges: None in force. It is a condolence resolution; a copy goes to the family.
deliberation: 17 February 2023: Periods of interpellation and amendments dispensed with; consolidated Proposed Resolutions No. 176 and 177 approved, subject to style.
17 February 2023: Approved as consolidated with Proposed Resolution No. 176, subject to style.
readings.insight: A condolence resolution adopted the same day as those for Wali Nando (No. 315) and the Turkiye earthquake (No. 316). Its reason for a Bangsamoro tribute is concrete: his role in drafting the original Bangsamoro Basic Law, the forerunner of the Organic Law.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament thanks Malaysian Prime Minister Dato' Seri Anwar Ibrahim for his continuing support and commitment to the Bangsamoro peace process. A copy goes to his office.

Authored by MP Abdulkarim T. Misuari and 18 others. Adopted on 20 March 2023.
readings.whyProposed: During his state visit to Manila on 1 March 2023, Prime Minister Anwar said Malaysia would continue supporting the peace process and offer capacity-building so that former fighters can find normal employment. He then met Chief Minister Ahod B. Ebrahim and spoke by phone with MNLF founding chairman Nur P. Misuari about reconciliation among Muslims in the south and the success of former MILF and MNLF fighters.
whoIsAffected: The Government of Malaysia, as the party thanked.
whatChanges: None in force. It is an expression of thanks; a copy goes to the Prime Minister's office.
deliberation: 20 March 2023: Approved as amended on 20 March 2023, subject to style.
readings.insight: Its 19 principal authors are led by MP Abdulkarim T. Misuari, and the text records both the Prime Minister's meeting with Chief Minister Ebrahim and his call with MNLF founder Nur Misuari. The resolution names no specific Malaysian program or amount.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament requests the Mindanao Development Authority (MinDA) to set up a BARMM desk at its main office in Davao City to strengthen coordination and linkages with Mindanao's stakeholders. A copy goes to MinDA.

Authored by MP Baintan A. Ampatuan. Adopted on 21 March 2023.
readings.whyProposed: MinDA's mandate is to coordinate the socioeconomic development of Mindanao, and the Chief Minister sits on its board under the Organic Law. The authors say MinDA and BARMM share inter-regional work on investment promotion, agriculture, connectivity, power and energy, BIMP-EAGA and barter trade, that foreign partners have shown interest in the region, and that a dedicated desk would improve cooperation and help promote the region to development partners. They also cite the Ease of Doing Business Act (Republic Act No. 11032).
whoIsAffected: MinDA, asked to create the desk.
Bangsamoro offices and development partners dealing with MinDA.
implementedBy: Mindanao Development Authority
whatChanges: Nothing binding. MinDA is a national agency; the resolution requests.
deliberation: 20 March 2023: Periods of interpellation and amendments dispensed with; approved, subject to style.
readings.insight: A request to a national agency with no deadline or follow-up. It does not say what the desk would do, who would staff it or who would pay. Parliament's later dealings with MinDA in the index are different requests: Resolution No. 509 (October 2024) asked it to report on the Mindanao River Basin Master Plan. The repo holds no record that a BARMM desk was set up.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament urges the concerned ministries of the Bangsamoro Government to monitor and enforce compliance with Section 4 of Bangsamoro Autonomy Act No. 1, which requires Bangsamoro offices, public and private schools, colleges and universities, public offices, government corporations and other instrumentalities to use and display the Bangsamoro flag. Copies go to the concerned ministries.

Authored by MP Tawakal B. Midtimbang and 8 others. Adopted on 21 March 2023.
readings.whyProposed: The Organic Law directs Parliament to adopt a regional flag, always displayed alongside the Philippine flag, and BAA No. 1 did so. During public consultations on the Bangsamoro Electoral Code and the Bangsamoro Local Governance Code, Members saw public and private schools and public offices in the region that were not displaying the flag.
whoIsAffected: Public and private schools, colleges and universities, and public offices in the region.
Ministries expected to monitor compliance.
implementedBy: Concerned ministries of the Bangsamoro Government
whatChanges: The duty already exists in BAA No. 1; this resolution only asks ministries to monitor and enforce it.
It does not name which ministries are responsible or say what happens to non-compliant offices or schools.
deliberation: 20 March 2023: Periods of interpellation and amendments dispensed with; approved, subject to style.
readings.insight: The second time Parliament has pressed on flag display: Resolution No. 66 (21 February 2020) called for the BARMM flag to be displayed in public buildings, plazas and schools. The observation of non-compliance comes from Members' own visits during code consultations, not from a survey, and the resolution gives no count of offending institutions.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament encourages development partners in the region to provide technical assistance to the Bangsamoro Government in preparing master plans and feasibility and pre-feasibility studies for big-ticket projects in the 2nd Bangsamoro Development Plan 2023-2028, and in improving its multi-year investment programs. Copies go to the National Economic and Development Authority, the Mindanao Development Authority and development partners in the region.

Authored by MP Baintan A. Ampatuan. Adopted on 21 March 2023.
readings.whyProposed: The Bangsamoro Planning and Development Authority prepared the 2nd BDP and its Bangsamoro Development Investment Program, which list priority projects. The authors say master plans are needed for health, education, social welfare, water resources, irrigation, power, the halal industry, Islamic finance, urbanizing areas, and the Ligawasan Marsh and Lake Lanao, and that feasibility studies help avoid wasted money and time. They note that the Organic Law lets the Bangsamoro Government accept grants and donations, and that partners such as the UN and JICA pledged support at the Bangsamoro Friends Forum on 18 February 2020.
whoIsAffected: Development partners such as UN agencies and JICA.
The Bangsamoro Planning and Development Authority and ministries preparing big projects.
implementedBy: National Economic and Development Authority
Mindanao Development Authority
Development partners operating in the region
whatChanges: Nothing binding. It is an invitation to donors; copies are sent for information and appropriate action.
deliberation: 20 March 2023: Periods of interpellation and amendments dispensed with; approved, subject to style.
readings.insight: This follows Resolution No. 303, which approved the 2nd BDP 2 months earlier. It asks outside partners to prepare the master plans and feasibility studies for projects already in the plan Parliament approved. It names no specific project or cost.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament encourages all ministries and agencies of the Bangsamoro Government, and local government units, to pursue quality management system certification from local or international certification bodies. Copies go to all ministries, agencies and LGUs.

Authored by MP Hashemi N. Dilangalen, MP Amilbahar S. Mawallil, MP Eddie M. Alih, MP Michael E. Midtimbang, MP Tawakal B. Midtimbang and MP Nabil A. Tan. Adopted on 21 March 2023.
readings.whyProposed: National rules already push government offices toward ISO-aligned quality management: Administrative Order No. 161 (2006) asks all agencies to set up an ISO-aligned system, and Executive Order No. 605 (2007) set up the Government Quality Management Program and extended the push to LGUs and state universities. The authors say ISO 9001:2015 certification in BARMM offices would assure the public that government performance meets global standards.
whoIsAffected: Bangsamoro ministries, agencies and offices.
Local government units in the region.
implementedBy: Ministries and agencies of the Bangsamoro Government
Local government units
whatChanges: Nothing binding. Offices are encouraged, not required, to seek certification.
No deadline, budget or reporting is set.
deliberation: 20 March 2023: MP Arnado asked whether any BARMM office was ISO-certified and what it would cost; MP Dilangalen said none yet, the Ministry of Science and Technology was pursuing it, and he did not know the exact cost.

20 March 2023: MP Lim noted quality management systems other than ISO exist and moved to change the title to certification from local or international bodies; accepted, followed by MP Arnado and MP Alih's amendments narrowing it to ministries, agencies and LGUs.
20 March 2023: Unanimously approved as amended, subject to style.
readings.insight: The resolution rests on national orders from 2006 and 2007 that already apply to government offices, and adds no regional requirement or timetable of its own. It does not say how many Bangsamoro offices already hold ISO 9001 certification.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament requests the Office of the Chief Minister to grant inflation relief assistance of up to ₱15,000 to all officials and employees of the Bangsamoro Government of whatever status, including contract of service and job order workers, to be released during Ramadhan 1444, subject to available funds. Members of Parliament, ministers, deputy ministers, directors-general and heads of offices are excluded. A copy goes to Chief Minister Ahod Balawag Ebrahim.

Authored by MP Omar Yasser C. Sema, MP Susana S. Anayatin, MP Suharto M. Ambolodto and MP Amilbahar S. Mawallil. Adopted on 21 March 2023.
readings.whyProposed: The authors cite regional inflation reported by the Philippine Statistics Authority's regional office: from 2.1% in April 2022 to 6.3% in December 2022 and 7.8% in January 2023, against 1.9% in January 2022; February 2023 was 7.5%. They expect prices to rise further during Ramadhan, due to begin by 24 March 2023, and compare the grant to the 13th month pay at Christmas. They note similar relief has been granted in past years.
whoIsAffected: Bangsamoro Government employees of all statuses, including contract of service and job order workers.
Senior officials, who are expressly left out.
implementedBy: Office of the Chief Minister

funding.detail: The resolution appropriates nothing. It asks the Chief Minister to grant up to ₱15,000 per employee from available funds, and names no fund source or total cost.

whatChanges: The Chief Minister receives a request; the grant stays his decision and depends on available funds.
It sets a ceiling of ₱15,000, not a fixed amount, and excludes MPs and heads of office.
deliberation: 20 March 2023: MP Ambolodto cited BARMM inflation rising from 1% to 2% in early 2022 to 7.8% in January 2023 and asked that contract-of-service and job-order workers also get 1 month's pay as relief.

20 March 2023: MP Esmael asked about cost and capacity; MP Ambolodto estimated ₱1,200,000,000 to ₱1,400,000,000 and said the miscellaneous personnel benefit fund and the Chief Minister's contingent fund could cover it.

20 March 2023: MP Parcasio moved to exclude MPs, ministers, deputy ministers, directors-general and heads of offices, and MP Esmael to cap the relief at 15,000 subject to available funds; both accepted.
20 March 2023: MP Anayatin urged that a Ramadhan allowance be legislated like the 13th and 14th month pays; MP Dumama-Alba said the Government of the Day supports it but faces constraints.
20 March 2023: Consolidated Proposed Resolutions No. 202 and 205 approved as amended, subject to style.
20 March 2023: Approved as consolidated with Proposed Resolution No. 205, subject to style.
readings.insight: Part of a yearly series: Resolution No. 120 (2021) and No. 237 (2022) on a Ramadhan allowance, this one in 2023, then No. 441 (2024) and No. 530 (2025), both for at least ₱10,000. This is the only one in the series that sets a ceiling rather than a floor, and the only one that excludes MPs and senior officials. One clause says the 14th month pay cushions Christmas costs, while the next cites the 13th month pay under Presidential Decree No. 851. No headcount or total cost is given.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament authorizes all its parliamentary and statutory committees to hold meetings, hearings and consultations during the recess, but not on Fridays. The authority takes effect on adoption and stays in force until amended or repealed. Copies go to the committees.

Authored by MP Sha Elijah B. Dumama-Alba, MP Raissa H. Jajurie, MP Mary Ann M. Arnado, MP Anna Tarhata S. Basman and MP Jose I. Lorena. Adopted on 21 March 2023.
readings.whyProposed: The First Regular Session of the Second BTA Parliament adjourned sine die on 21 March 2023 under Resolution No. 300. Committees still had pending work, including the Bangsamoro Local Governance Code, other bills and resolutions, and investigations in aid of legislation, and the authors wanted meetings to continue through Ramadhan. Members may join by Zoom at the committee's discretion.
whoIsAffected: Members of Parliament sitting on committees.
Resource persons and the public invited to hearings during the recess.
implementedBy: Parliamentary and statutory committees of the Parliament
whatChanges: This binds Parliament itself: committees may sit during the recess, except on Fridays.
It is open-ended, staying in force until amended or repealed.
deliberation: 20 March 2023: MP Ampatuan asked that Members be allowed to join committee work via Zoom during Ramadhan and MP Parcasio that no meetings be held on Fridays; MP Arnado agreed to both.
20 March 2023: Approved without amendments, subject to style.
readings.insight: An internal rule that does have force. It is the first of 3 near-identical recess authorities: Resolution No. 443 (February 2024) and No. 539 (February 2025) repeated it, even though this one never lapsed. The code it singled out did pass: the Bangsamoro Local Governance Code became BAA No. 49, passed and approved on 28 September 2023.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament requests Chief Minister Ahod Balawag Ebrahim to declare 27 March 2023 a special non-working holiday across the Bangsamoro region, to commemorate the signing of the Comprehensive Agreement on the Bangsamoro (CAB). A copy goes to the Chief Minister.

Authored by MP Sha Elijah B. Dumama-Alba, MP Raissa H. Jajurie, MP Mary Ann M. Arnado, MP Anna Tarhata S. Basman, MP Jose I. Lorena and MP Mohagher M. Iqbal. Adopted on 21 March 2023.
readings.whyProposed: The CAB, the final peace agreement between the Government of the Philippines and the Moro Islamic Liberation Front, was signed on 27 March 2014 after 17 years of negotiation and led to the creation of BARMM. Under the Bangsamoro Administrative Code (BAA No. 13), special holidays need a proclamation from the Chief Minister, who may proclaim local special holidays for a particular date and place.
whoIsAffected: Workers, students and offices across the region, if the holiday is declared.
implementedBy: Office of the Chief Minister
whatChanges: The holiday depends on the Chief Minister's proclamation; the resolution only asks.
The request covers 2023 only, not a recurring holiday.
deliberation: 20 March 2023: Treated as a simple resolution; all Members present made co-authors; periods of interpellation and amendments dispensed with; approved, subject to style.
readings.insight: Adopted 6 days before the date it names. It asks for a one-time holiday, so the question would return each year; the resolution does not propose a standing holiday by law. The repo does not record whether the Chief Minister issued the proclamation.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament requests the Supreme Court to create a Committee on Shari'ah Bar Integration to organize and integrate the Philippine Shari'ah Bar, and to consider adopting the draft Rules Integrating the Philippine Shari'ah Bar written by Shari'ah counselors. It forwards the resolution and endorses the draft rules to the Court for consideration, adoption and promulgation.

Authored by MP Sha Elijah B. Dumama-Alba and 13 others. Adopted on 21 March 2023.
readings.whyProposed: Section 15, Article X of the Organic Law lets the Supreme Court adopt rules integrating the Shari'ah Bar. The authors point to the integration of the Philippine Bar in 1970, which began with a Court resolution creating a Commission on Bar Integration. The Bangsamoro Attorney General's Office and The Asia Foundation worked to unite the various Shari'ah counselors' groups, and between 2019 and 2021 consultations and writeshops nationwide produced draft rules based on Rule 139-A of the Rules of Court.
whoIsAffected: Shari'ah counselors across the country.
The Supreme Court, asked to act.
implementedBy: Supreme Court of the Philippines
whatChanges: Nothing binding. Bar integration is the Supreme Court's power; the resolution requests and endorses draft rules.
