deliberation: 20 March 2023: MP Ampatuan and MP Loong (DM) asked about the draft rules; MP Dumama-Alba said the Bangsamoro Attorney-General's Office drafted them with Shari'ah practitioners from 2019 to 2021, and Justice Dimaampao advised first seeking a Supreme Court committee.
20 March 2023: Approved as amended, subject to style; the session then adjourned sine die.
readings.insight: It follows Resolution No. 314 (January 2023), which thanked the Court for putting Shari'ah justice in its 2022-2027 strategic plan. Parliament returned to the Court in Resolution No. 458 (May 2024) on the Shari'ah High Court. The repo does not record whether a Committee on Shari'ah Bar Integration was created or the draft rules adopted.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament authorizes MP Said Z. Salendab to act as Wali of the Bangsamoro Government for the sole purpose of opening the Second Regular Session of the BTA Parliament. The authority ends once that task is done. A copy goes to MP Salendab.

Authored by MP Mohagher M. Iqbal and 49 others. Adopted on 15 May 2023.
readings.whyProposed: Sheikh Khalipha Usman Nando, the first Wali, served from 29 March 2019 until his death on 5 February 2023. The Bangsamoro Administrative Code says Parliament shall appoint a new Wali within 30 days of a vacancy, chosen by consensus from a list of eminent residents submitted by the Council of Leaders. At a caucus of all Members on 11 May 2023, Members agreed to let the Chief Minister designate someone to act as Wali for the session opening on 15 May 2023, and he chose MP Salendab.
whoIsAffected: MP Said Z. Salendab.
The office of the Wali, which remained without a permanent holder.
implementedBy: Parliament of the BTA
whatChanges: MP Salendab may act as Wali only to open the Second Regular Session; the authority then lapses.
It does not fill the Wali vacancy.
readings.insight: The resolution quotes the Administrative Code's 30-day rule for appointing a new Wali, but was adopted 99 days after Nando died and still made no appointment. The permanent successor, Sheikh Muslim Masaglang Guiamaden, came only with Resolution No. 445 on 13 May 2024, more than 15 months after the vacancy. It has 50 authors in the index.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament congratulates and commends Fatima Ayesha Juwak Amirul of Bongao, Tawi-Tawi, for winning gold in women's soft tennis at the 32nd SEA Games in Phnom Penh, Cambodia (5 to 17 May 2023). It says she should be given a financial incentive of not less than ₱500,000, taken from available funds of the Bangsamoro Government subject to the Ministry of Finance, Budget and Management's determination, and invites her to receive the award in person in Parliament.

Authored by MP John Anthony L. Lim and MP Diamila D. Ramos. Adopted on 16 May 2023.
readings.whyProposed: The Philippine women's soft tennis team won gold on 9 May 2023. She was 1 of 6 players on the team. The Philippine delegation had 814 athletes in 38 sports. The authors cite the Organic Law's mandate to promote youth fitness through sports.
whoIsAffected: Fatima Ayesha Juwak Amirul.
The Ministry of Finance, Budget and Management, which decides the source of the incentive.
implementedBy: Ministry of Finance, Budget and Management

funding.detail: A financial incentive of not less than ₱500,000 for Ms. Amirul, to be taken from the available fund of the Bangsamoro Government, subject to the determination of the Ministry of Finance, Budget and Management. The resolution itself appropriates nothing.

whatChanges: A cash incentive of at least ₱500,000 is called for, subject to the Ministry of Finance, Budget and Management's determination of available funds.
She is invited to receive the commendation and award in Parliament.
readings.insight: Unlike most commendations, this one attaches money: a floor of ₱500,000. A comparable resolution 9 days later, No. 338, for Alnakran Abdilla's bronze in men's beach volleyball at the same Games, directed the Bangsamoro Sports Commission to provide incentives but named no amount. Parliament's index files this resolution under the First Regular Session; the adopted page says Second Regular Session.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament thanks President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. for appointing Abdulraof A. Macacua as Officer-in-Charge Governor of Maguindanao del Norte. A copy goes to the Office of the President.

Authored by MP Ahod Balawag Ebrahim and 70 others. Adopted on 16 May 2023.
readings.whyProposed: The President appointed Macacua on 5 April 2023. Republic Act No. 11550 split Maguindanao into Maguindanao del Norte and Maguindanao del Sur, which required the President to appoint officers-in-charge. Macacua had been chief of staff of the MILF's Bangsamoro Islamic Armed Forces, a Bangsamoro Transition Commission commissioner, secretary general of the United Bangsamoro Justice Party, minister of environment, natural resources and energy, Senior Minister, chair of BTA committees, and chair of the cabinet committee that drafted the Bangsamoro Electoral Code.
whoIsAffected: Abdulraof A. Macacua and the province of Maguindanao del Norte.
whatChanges: None in force. It is an expression of thanks; a copy goes to the President.
readings.insight: Adopted the same day as Resolution No. 330, which congratulates Macacua himself; together they carry 71 and 70 authors in the index. Macacua later became Chief Minister, and the last adopted resolution in the index, No. 578 (June 2026), expresses support for his leadership.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament congratulates and commends Abdulraof A. Macacua on his appointment by President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. as Officer-in-Charge Governor of Maguindanao del Norte, and pledges its full support and its willingness to work with him. A copy goes to the Office of the OIC Governor.

Authored by MP Ahod Balawag Ebrahim and 69 others. Adopted on 16 May 2023.
readings.whyProposed: Macacua was appointed on 5 April 2023. He had served as a Member of the BTA Parliament, Senior Minister of BARMM and chief of staff of the MILF's Bangsamoro Islamic Armed Forces. The authors call the appointment a step forward in the peace process.
whoIsAffected: Abdulraof A. Macacua.
whatChanges: None in force. It is a commendation; a copy goes to his office.
readings.insight: A companion to Resolution No. 329, adopted the same day, which thanks the President for the same appointment. Both honor a sitting colleague: Macacua is himself listed among the principal authors of the thanks resolution.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament commends Engr. Mohaimen Hadji Omar Pasawilan for ranking 10th in the April 2023 Civil Engineers Licensure Examination. A copy goes to him.

Authored by MP Aida M. Silongan and 9 others. Adopted on 18 May 2023.
readings.whyProposed: The Professional Regulation Commission announced on 29 April 2023 that 5,887 of 16,936 examinees passed. Pasawilan, a Maguindanaon from Matalam, North Cotabato, and a 2022 cum laude civil engineering graduate of the University of Southern Mindanao-Kabacan, placed 10th with a rating of 89.30%.
whoIsAffected: Engr. Mohaimen Hadji Omar Pasawilan.
whatChanges: None in force. It is a commendation; a copy goes to him.
readings.insight: One of many commendations of board examination topnotchers in the index; Resolution No. 331, adopted the same day, honors a medical technology topnotcher. Like Resolution No. 309's honoree, he is a University of Southern Mindanao-Kabacan graduate.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament thanks President Rodrigo Roa Duterte for approving Republic Act 11054, the Bangsamoro Organic Law, and for appointing the Members of Parliament, particularly the 39 nominated by the Government of the Republic of the Philippines.

A copy goes to the President at Malacañang Palace. Authored by MP Edrieza H.N. Rimbang. Adopted on 21 October 2021.
readings.whyProposed: The Organic Law was signed on 26 July 2018 and took effect on 10 August 2018, creating the interim Bangsamoro government. The President then appointed the 80 Members of Parliament: 41 from the Moro Islamic Liberation Front and 39 from the government side. The resolution treats the law's approval as proof of the President's advocacy for lasting peace.
whoIsAffected: President Rodrigo Roa Duterte, the addressee.
whatChanges: It is a statement of thanks. It sets nothing in motion beyond sending a copy to the President.
readings.insight: The thanks came more than 3 years after the law was signed, and 9 days after Resolution No. 173 (12 October 2021) asked the same President to keep the incumbent Members when he appointed a new BTA. Resolution No. 209 repeated that request in February 2022. This resolution singles out the 39 government-side appointees, the group whose reappointment Resolution No. 209 later pressed for.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament expresses its sympathy and condolences on the death of Dr. Ahmad "Jun" Engracia Alonto Jr., former president of the Mindanao State University. A copy goes to his family.

Authored by MP Eddie M. Alih and 14 others. Adopted on 21 October 2021.
readings.whyProposed: Dr. Alonto died in Cagayan de Oro City on 1 October 2021. The resolution recalls that he led a peaceful assembly of students at the Quirino Grandstand on 30 November 1979, was detained for 7 months at the Bicutan jail under the Marcos administration, joined the protests that ended in the 1986 People Power Revolution, served as the third president of the MSU System from 1987 to 1992, and in 2001 sat on the MILF negotiating panel then headed by Ahod B. Ebrahim, now Chief Minister.
whoIsAffected: Dr. Alonto's family.
whatChanges: A condolence. Its only action is sending a copy to the family.
readings.insight: Dr. Alonto was the son of Senator Ahmad Domocao Alonto Sr., whom the resolution names as the founding father of MSU. The text links him directly to the current leadership: he served on the MILF negotiating panel under the man who became Chief Minister.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament urges itself to hold consultations, for legislative purposes, with the stakeholders of the petroleum depots in Parang, Maguindanao. Copies go to the concerned BARMM ministries for information and appropriate consideration.

Authored by MP Romeo K. Sema. Adopted on 21 October 2021.
readings.whyProposed: Shell Philippines, Petron and Caltex ran depots on the Parang coast, Caltex for more than 2 decades, supplying fuel retailers in Cotabato City and parts of Maguindanao and Lanao del Sur at comparatively low prices. The resolution says the companies stopped operating 2 years earlier, so retailers now haul supply from Davao City, Digos or General Santos City and prices have risen, hurting transport, commerce, car owners and the regional economy.
whoIsAffected: Fuel retailers and consumers in Cotabato City, Maguindanao and Lanao del Sur.
The oil companies that ran the Parang depots.
implementedBy: Bangsamoro Transition Authority Parliament
whatChanges: It commits Parliament to consultations but names no committee to hold them and sets no date.
Copies go to unnamed 'concerned ministries'; the resolution asks nothing specific of them.
readings.insight: The last WHEREAS clause asks for 'a formal inquiry on the status of these petroleum depots', and the web address of the index entry still carries that wording, but the adopted RESOLVED clause softens it to 'consultations with the stakeholders'. The resolution gives no figures for the price rise it describes, and no follow-up resolution on the Parang depots appears in the index.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament urges all government agencies and the private sector in the region to foster non-discrimination on account of religion in labor and employment, education, procurement and the lease of real estate, including in hiring qualified applicants who are pious observers of the Islamic faith.

Copies go to Regional Development Councils outside BARMM, CSC-BARMM, the Ministry of Labor and Employment, MBHTE, the Ministry of Health, MTIT, all other BARMM ministries and agencies, the private sector and LGUs in BARMM, and LGUs outside BARMM with Muslim populations, for reference and guidance. Authored by MP Abdullah B. Hashim. Adopted on 16 November 2021.
readings.whyProposed: The authors say religious discrimination in employment remains a problem in the Philippines, citing a GMA News Online report of 2 August 2017 that a Muslim woman was fired for refusing her employer's request to remove her hijab at work. They note that beards for men and the hijab for women are religious observances, and cite the Constitution's free-exercise clause, the Organic Law's ban on discrimination by creed or religion, and the non-discrimination rules of the Bangsamoro Administrative Code (BAA 13) and the Bangsamoro Civil Service Code (BAA 17).
whoIsAffected: Muslim job applicants and workers, especially those who wear beards or the hijab.
Employers, schools, procuring entities and landlords in the region and beyond.
whatChanges: An appeal. It creates no penalty or complaint process; the binding rules are the Organic Law and BAA 13 and 17 it cites.
Copies go to a wide list of offices inside and outside BARMM 'for reference and guidance'.
readings.insight: The resolution cites the laws that already ban religious discrimination in government hiring, so for public offices it restates existing duties; for private employers it is a request. The same concern returns a week later in Resolution No. 190, which commends a jail officer for getting the hijab into BJMP uniforms, and in Resolution No. 260 (28 July 2022), which asks agencies in BARMM to observe a respect-for-hijab policy.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament directs the ministries and offices of the Bangsamoro Government to formulate and implement their own Career and Human Resource Development Plans, to build an effective and efficient bureaucracy. A copy goes to all BARMM ministries and offices.

Authored by MP Baintan A. Ampatuan. Adopted on 16 November 2021.
readings.whyProposed: The Bangsamoro Civil Service Code already requires each agency to prepare a career and personnel development plan covering merit promotion, performance evaluation, training, scholarships, job rotation and incentives. The authors note that BARMM's workforce mixes former ARMM staff with new hires, and propose that each agency start with Training Needs Assessments following Civil Service Commission guidelines, work with the CSC and the Development Academy of the Bangsamoro, and adopt a 3-year plan for 2022 to 2025, continuing current training in the meantime.
whoIsAffected: Employees of Bangsamoro ministries and offices.
HR units of each ministry.
implementedBy: All ministries and offices of the Bangsamoro Government
Civil Service Commission
Development Academy of the Bangsamoro
whatChanges: The directive restates a duty the Civil Service Code already imposes; the resolution adds no deadline and no report to Parliament.
Its WHEREAS clauses suggest a method (training needs assessments, a 3-year plan) but the RESOLVED clause does not require it.
readings.insight: The 3-year time frame was pegged to 'the new mandate of the BARMM (2022-2025)', reflecting Republic Act No. 11593, which had just moved the first regional election to 2025. Parliament asked for no copy of the plans, so it has no built-in way to know whether any ministry complied.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament expresses its sympathy and condolences on the death of former Representative Didagen "Digs" P. Dilangalen of the 1st District of Maguindanao with Cotabato City, a human rights lawyer. A copy goes to his family.

Authored by MP Susana S. Anayatin. Adopted on 16 November 2021.
readings.whyProposed: Dilangalen died on 6 November 2021. He represented Maguindanao's 1st district with Cotabato City from 1995 to 2004 and was the only representative of the defunct Shariff Kabungsuan province in the 14th Congress, 2007 to 2010. The resolution notes that his family donated the 5-hectare site of the Sultan Haji Hassanal Bolkiah Mosque in Cotabato City, and lists his projects, among them over 3,000 scholars, a cancer institute building at Cotabato Regional Medical Center, roads, and 37 multicabs for 37 barangays of Cotabato City.
whoIsAffected: The Dilangalen family.
whatChanges: A condolence. Its only action is presenting a copy to the family.
readings.insight: The adopted text consolidates 2 proposed resolutions (PR557 and PR559). It also records a Millennium Award given to him on 20 January 2000 as Outstanding Congressman for ARMM.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament urges the BTA Parliament and the ministries and offices of the Bangsamoro Government to pay salaries and related benefits through an automated payroll system using ATMs of recognized government depositary banks, to improve efficiency, tighten internal control over cash, safeguard government interests and promote moral governance.

A copy goes to all BARMM ministries and offices. Authored by MP Abdullah B. Hashim. Adopted on 18 November 2021.
readings.whyProposed: The 2021 budget gave the BTA ₱1,284,813,000 for Personnel Services, yet staff were still paid in cash. A BTA memorandum of 23 July 2021 had Members designate staff to collect salaries from the Cashier's Office, which meant carrying large sums to offices outside the Government Center, including staff in Basilan, Sulu and Tawi-Tawi. The resolution says the Cashier's Office counts tens to hundreds of millions in cash each month, and once had a ₱12,000 shortfall on the July 2021 payroll that its staff covered themselves.
whoIsAffected: Parliament and ministry employees paid in cash, especially those far from Cotabato City.
Staff designated to carry payroll cash, and the BTA Cashier's Office.
implementedBy: Bangsamoro Transition Authority Parliament
All ministries and offices of the Bangsamoro Government
whatChanges: For Parliament's own payroll this is an instruction to itself; for ministries it is a request.
It sets no deadline and names no bank.
readings.insight: The ₱1,284,813,000 figure matches the Personnel Services line for the BTA in BAA 15, the 2021 budget, part of a ₱3,707,969,000 allocation. The resolution records that the Cashier's Office itself supported the change.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament supports Senator Sherwin Gatchalian's proposal for the National Electrification Administration (NEA) to reallocate funding to electrify remote villages in the Bangsamoro region.

Copies go to Senator Gatchalian, Senate President Vicente Sotto and the NEA. Authored by MP Baintan A. Ampatuan. Adopted on 18 November 2021.
readings.whyProposed: The resolution says the country reached 95.3% electrification coverage in 2018, while BARMM had the lowest household electrification rate at 31.4%, even though the region supplies about 662 megawatts of hydroelectric power to Mindanao. Lanao del Sur and Maguindanao electric cooperatives have tried, but the program lags for lack of national funding, and Sulu, Tawi-Tawi and Basilan are the worst off-grid areas. It also notes that Finance Secretary Carlos Dominguez offered to help find funding, including from Islamic countries.
whoIsAffected: Unelectrified households in remote BARMM villages, especially in Sulu, Tawi-Tawi and Basilan.
Electric cooperatives in the region.
implementedBy: National Electrification Administration
whatChanges: An endorsement sent to the Senate and the NEA; it binds neither.
It names no amount and no particular villages.
readings.insight: The resolution does not say where or when the senator made the proposal, or how much he proposed. The gap it cites is wide: 31.4% household electrification against 95.3% nationally, in the region that generates about 662 megawatts for Mindanao.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament urges the ministries and offices of the Bangsamoro Government to use businesses and establishments within the region, such as hotels, restaurants and resorts, for their capacity-building activities.

Authored by MP Baintan A. Ampatuan. Adopted on 18 November 2021.
readings.whyProposed: New hires in the ministries need training, and holding it inside the region would help a regional economy hurt by the COVID-19 pandemic. The authors add that travel outside BARMM during the pandemic was risky and costly, and that the region has hotels, restaurants and resorts that can serve as venues if they meet the ministries' quality standards.
whoIsAffected: Hotels, restaurants and resorts in the region.
Ministry staff who attend trainings.
implementedBy: All ministries and offices of the Bangsamoro Government
whatChanges: A request. It sets no rule on venues and no reporting.
Unlike most resolutions of the period, it has no clause sending copies to anyone.
readings.insight: Parliament came back to this 3 months later. Resolution No. 223 (24 February 2022) reiterated Resolution No. 189 and directed ministries to avoid holding training in luxurious and first-class hotels or resorts, except activities with external funding.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament commends Jail Officer I Lorena Coquia of the Dagupan City Jail for campaigning for and contributing to the adoption of the hijab and an alternative uniform for Muslim women employees of the Bureau of Jail Management and Penology (BJMP).

Copies go to the Dagupan City Jail and the National Commission on Muslim Filipinos. Authored by MP Rasol Y. Mitmug Jr. and 6 others. Adopted on 23 November 2021.
readings.whyProposed: Coquia, a Balik-Islam officer, wrote to the NCMF North Luzon office asking it to help get the hijab into the BJMP uniform. NCMF took it up with the BJMP Chief, and the BJMP Uniform and Standard Committee approved the proposal unanimously on 27 May 2021. BJMP Resolution No. 2021-23 and a memorandum of 29 July 2021 now allow Muslim women personnel to wear the hijab with the uniform, plus an alternative uniform.
whoIsAffected: JO1 Lorena Coquia.
Muslim women employees of the BJMP.
whatChanges: A commendation. Its only action is sending copies to the jail and the NCMF.
readings.insight: The honoree works outside the region, in Dagupan City, and the change she pushed is a national agency policy. It was adopted a week after Resolution No. 184, which urged employers to stop discriminating against workers who wear the hijab.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament directs the Ministry of the Interior and Local Government (MILG) to implement programs that strengthen the civil registry services of local government units, with emphasis on the effective implementation of Muslim Personal Law in the region.

Authored by MP Baintan A. Ampatuan and 6 others. Adopted on 23 November 2021.
readings.whyProposed: The Organic Law gives the Bangsamoro Government authority over the registration of births, marriages and deaths, with copies to the Philippine Statistics Authority. The authors argue that PSA data for BARMM should be accurate, complete and timely so policies fit the region; that civil registration gives people proof of legal identity and civil status; and that the MILG, which is responsible for building LGU capacity, should help LGUs, whose city and municipal civil registrars run registration under the Local Government Code.
whoIsAffected: City and municipal civil registrars in BARMM.
Residents who need birth, marriage and death records.
implementedBy: Ministry of the Interior and Local Government
whatChanges: A directive to the MILG with no deadline, budget or report back to Parliament.
The resolution has no clause forwarding a copy, even to the MILG.
readings.insight: Muslim Personal Law appears only in the title and the RESOLVED clause; none of the WHEREAS clauses mention it, Shari'ah courts, or the registration of Muslim marriages and divorces. Parliament returned to that subject more concretely in Resolution No. 456 (22 May 2024), which urged the Civil Registrar General, the PSA and the Shari'ah courts to enforce the registration of Muslim divorces.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament expresses its condolences to the family of Linda Untal Ampatuan, a delegate to the 1971 Constitutional Convention, first Regional Director of Civil Service Commission Region XII, and former Cotabato City councilor. A copy goes to her family.

Authored by MP Baintan A. Ampatuan and 6 others. Adopted on 23 November 2021.
readings.whyProposed: Ampatuan died on 9 November 2021. She was elected to the 1971 Constitutional Convention for the lone district of Cotabato, became the first Regional Director of CSC Region XII on 15 November 1975, and oversaw its first civil service examination in 1976, which the resolution credits with producing more eligible Bangsamoro civil servants. She was later an undefeated Cotabato City councilor.
whoIsAffected: The family of Linda Untal Ampatuan.
whatChanges: A condolence. Its only action is presenting a copy to the family.
readings.insight: Her place in the record rests on firsts: first CSC regional director for Region XII and the first civil service examination there in 1976.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament urges the Philippine Congress-Bangsamoro Parliament Forum to strengthen its mechanism for cooperation on legislation under the Organic Law, by setting up a secretariat in the Manila Liaison Office to coordinate with the House of Representatives and the Senate.

Copies go to the House and the Senate. Authored by MP Rasol Y. Mitmug Jr. Adopted on 24 November 2021.
readings.whyProposed: The Organic Law created the Forum as the venue for coordinating legislation that involves both the national and regional governments, including bills creating legislative districts. Senate Concurrent Resolution No. 5 (21 January 2020) asked the BTA to name delegates, and BTA Resolution No. 63 did so, with 11 Members chosen. With Republic Act No. 11593 extending the transition to 2025, the authors want the Forum to monitor the Organic Law's implementation and any national bills affecting the region.
whoIsAffected: The Forum's 11 BTA delegates and their counterparts in Congress.
Parliament's Manila Liaison Office.
implementedBy: Philippine Congress-Bangsamoro Parliament Forum
Manila Liaison Office
whatChanges: A proposal to a joint body; Parliament alone cannot make the Forum act.
It names a place for the secretariat but no staffing, funding or date.
readings.insight: The resolution dates Resolution No. 63 to 19 February 2021; the page image confirms that wording, but Parliament's index lists Resolution No. 63 as adopted on 19 February 2020, a month after the Senate's resolution. The secretariat would sit in Parliament's own Manila Liaison Office, yet the request is addressed to the Forum rather than to Parliament's own Secretariat.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament recognizes and commends the honors received by Dr. Nassef Manabilang Adiong as an inspiration for Bangsamoro youth.

Copies go to the Chancellor and the Institute of Islamic Studies of UP Diliman, the Graduate School of the Development Academy of the Philippines, the AFP Civil Relations Service, the Turkish Embassy in Manila and the Philippine International Studies Organization. Authored by MP Baintan A. Ampatuan, MP Pangalian M. Balindong, MP Omar Yasser C. Sema, MP Amilbahar S. Mawallil, MP Laisa M. Alamia and MP Rasol Y. Mitmug Jr. Adopted on 24 November 2021.
readings.whyProposed: Dr. Adiong had more than 50 scholarly publications and, on 4 November 2021, was conferred the title UP Scientist III, which the resolution calls a first for a Moro, with about 340 Scientist titles conferred since 2005. It lists 11 honors from 2011 to 2021, among them a TOYM award in 2019 and a UP Centennial Professorial Chair in 2020, and notes he founded 3 research organizations, 5 book series and 1 journal.
whoIsAffected: Dr. Nassef Manabilang Adiong.
whatChanges: A commendation. Its only action is sending copies to the listed institutions.
readings.insight: Dr. Adiong was then Director of Policy Research and Legal Services of the BTA Parliament, so Parliament was commending a senior member of its own staff. The Speaker, MP Pangalian M. Balindong, was among the 6 authors.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament urges the Ministry of Finance, and Budget and Management (MFBM) to include in the 2022 Bangsamoro Expenditure Program the establishment or upgrading of hospitals in each province and in the Special Geographic Areas.

A copy goes to MFBM. Authored by MP Eddie M. Alih and 32 others. Adopted on 24 November 2021.
readings.whyProposed: The Organic Law tells Parliament to give health the highest budget priority and to set up a general hospital system by law. The authors say COVID-19 exposed how inadequate the region's hospitals are, and that facilities in the provinces, the hinterlands and the islands were already insufficient before the pandemic.
whoIsAffected: Patients in the provinces and Special Geographic Areas.
The Ministry of Health, which runs the hospitals.
implementedBy: Ministry of Finance, and Budget and Management
whatChanges: A request about a budget. It names no amount, no hospital and no location.
Parliament itself, not MFBM, decides the final appropriation.
readings.insight: It had 33 principal authors. It came late in the budget cycle: the 2022 budget, BAA 23, was ratified on 28 December 2021, about 5 weeks after this was adopted. A narrower follow-up came in Resolution No. 239 (24 March 2022), directing the Ministry of Health to implement MMA Act No. 245, which upgraded the Tamparan District Hospital into the provincial hospital of Lanao del Sur.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament expresses its condolences to the family of Engr. Pipalawan O. Naga, environmental advocate and former Provincial Environment and Natural Resources Officer of Lanao del Sur. A copy goes to his family.

Authored by MP Maisara Dandamun Latiph. Adopted on 25 November 2021.
readings.whyProposed: Naga died on 19 November 2021. He was technical director of the Save Lake Lanao Movement (SALLAM) from as early as 1990 and senior adviser on the environment to Governor Mamintal Alonto Adiong Jr. The resolution credits SALLAM's campaign against the impacts of the Agus-1 hydroelectric dam with 3 issuances in 1992: an Environmental Clearance Certificate for the Agus plants, Proclamation 871 creating the Lake Lanao Watershed Reservation, and Memorandum Order 421 creating its protection council.
whoIsAffected: Engr. Naga's family.
whatChanges: A condolence. Its only action is sending a copy to the family.
readings.insight: The resolution notes that Naga took part in the consultations its author held to draft BTA Bill No. 32, which seeks to create a Ranao Development Authority. Lake Lanao, it says, is one of 17 ancient lakes of the world.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament commends Engr. Rajiv Nooh Dalagan Amil for topping the November 2021 Civil Engineering Licensure Examination, and grants him a monetary gift of ₱100,000, charged against any available fund of the Bangsamoro Government.

A copy goes to Engr. Amil. Authored by MP Amilbahar S. Mawallil and 11 others. Adopted on 22 December 2021.
readings.whyProposed: The PRC announced results on 25 November 2021. Amil, from Tawi-Tawi and a graduate of Ateneo de Davao University, rated 93.25%, the highest mark, besting 6,474 other examinees; 2,374, or 36.67%, passed. He finished high school at MSU-Tawi-Tawi College of Technology and Oceanography.
whoIsAffected: Engr. Rajiv Nooh Dalagan Amil.
implementedBy: Bangsamoro Government (source of the ₱100,000 gift)

funding.detail: ₱100,000 monetary gift to Engr. Amil, charged against any available fund of the Bangsamoro Government. No specific appropriation is named.

whatChanges: Unlike most commendations, it authorizes a payment: ₱100,000 to the honoree.
The fund it is charged to is not named; 'any available fund' leaves the source to the executive.
readings.insight: This is the only topnotcher commendation in this batch to carry cash; the resolutions for Dr. Fatima Tasneem Mohammad Sali (No. 198), adopted the same day, and for later topnotchers (Nos. 203, 205, 208) give none. The adopted text consolidates 5 proposed resolutions.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament recognizes and commends Dr. Fatima Tasneem Jimlok Mohammad Sali for topping the 2021 Philippine Board of Emergency Medicine In-Service Examination. A copy goes to Dr. Mohammad Sali.

Authored by MP Amilbahar S. Mawallil and 8 others. Adopted on 22 December 2021.
readings.whyProposed: Dr. Mohammad Sali, an emergency medicine resident at Ospital ng Makati, is from Sapa, Tandubas, Tawi-Tawi. She graduated cum laude in nursing from Far Eastern University, earned a master's in nursing at UP Manila, studied medicine at Pamantasan ng Lungsod ng Maynila, and trained at UP-PGH.
whoIsAffected: Dr. Fatima Tasneem Jimlok Mohammad Sali.
whatChanges: A commendation. Its only action is sending a copy to the honoree.
readings.insight: Adopted the same day as Resolution No. 197, by largely the same authors, but without the ₱100,000 gift that resolution gave. Both honorees attended MSU-Tawi-Tawi College of Technology and Oceanography.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament condemns the ambush of Basilan mayors Darussalam Lajid of Al-Barka and Alih Salih of Akbar, expresses condolences to the families of Lajid and of Nurrudin Barad, and calls on law enforcement authorities to investigate thoroughly.

Copies go to the Office of the Chief Minister, the Chief of the PNP, the Police Regional Office BAR, the Zamboanga City Police Office and the victims' families. Authored by MP Omar Yasser C. Sema, MP Susana S. Anayatin, MP Aida M. Silongan, MP Mohagher M. Iqbal and MP Eddie M. Alih. Adopted on 22 December 2021.
readings.whyProposed: On 26 December 2021, according to the text, 4 gunmen on motorcycles attacked the 2 mayors in Barangay Baliwasan, Zamboanga City. Mayor Lajid and a security aide were killed; Mayor Salih and 2 aides were wounded. The authors note the attack came ahead of the May 2022 elections and ask the Zamboanga City Police Office to take over the investigation.
whoIsAffected: The families of Mayor Lajid and his aide.
Mayor Alih Salih and his aides.
implementedBy: Philippine National Police
Police Regional Office BAR
Zamboanga City Police Office
whatChanges: A condemnation and an appeal; it directs no regional office and the police are national.
Copies go to the police and the Chief Minister's office for 'appropriate action'.
readings.insight: The adopted text dates the ambush to 26 December 2021, 4 days after the adoption date of 22 December 2021 printed on the same document; the page image confirms both. One of the dates is wrong. The slain aide is also named 2 ways: 'Barad Nuruddin' in the WHEREAS clauses, 'Nurrudin Barad' in the title and the RESOLVED clause. The text consolidates 3 proposed resolutions.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament encourages the Government of the Day to adopt the People's Budget on the Bangsamoro Halal Ecosystem Program as part of the Bangsamoro Halal Development and Promotion Program.

Copies go to Chief Minister Ahod B. Ebrahim and the concerned agencies. Authored by MP Rasol Y. Mitmug Jr. and 6 others. Adopted on 21 December 2021.
readings.whyProposed: The Parliament's Minority Bloc held public consultations on halal from June to October 2021 with civil society groups, social enterprises and small businesses. The result is a People's Budget of 7 subprograms and 50 projects, from halal farming and fishery to trade, logistics, specialization, social inclusion, governance and consumer behavior, costing ₱3,360,142,505.63: 66% capital outlays, 28.3% operating expenses and 5.7% personnel services. The Bangsamoro Halal Board, chaired by the Trade Minister, is responsible for the halal program under the Administrative Code.
whoIsAffected: Halal producers, traders and small businesses in the region.
The Bangsamoro Halal Board and its member ministries.
implementedBy: Office of the Chief Minister
Bangsamoro Halal Board

funding.detail: The resolution appropriates nothing. It endorses a proposed People's Budget of ₱3,360,142,505.63 for the halal program, which would need its own appropriation.

whatChanges: An encouragement only. The ₱3,360,142,505.63 is a proposal, not an appropriation.
It does not ask the Halal Board, named in the text, to do anything specific.
readings.insight: The People's Budget came out of consultations run by Parliament's Minority Bloc, so the resolution asks the Government of the Day to adopt a spending plan drawn up outside the executive. It was adopted on 21 December 2021, 7 days before the 2022 budget (BAA 23) was ratified, too late to shape that budget through a resolution alone.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament urges the Ministry of Health and the Bangsamoro Darul Ifta, working with the Moro Waqf Foundation, Inc. and other institutions, to institutionalize ibadah-friendly hospital services in the region.

Copies go to the MOH, the Darul Ifta, the Moro Waqf Foundation and other institutions and hospitals in BARMM. Authored by MP Lanang T. Ali Jr. Adopted on 25 January 2022.
readings.whyProposed: Most people in the region are Muslim, but hospitals lack prayer spaces with ablution areas, qibla markers and similar services, and COVID-19 kept religious leaders out of hospitals, complicating patients' prayers and rites for the dead. The Department of Health already has issuances on prayer rooms, qibla marks in patient rooms, release of Muslim remains within 24 hours, Ramadan work hours and spiritual support in hospice care. The Moro Waqf Foundation, based at Cotabato Regional and Medical Center, leads the advocacy.
whoIsAffected: Muslim patients and their families in BARMM hospitals.
Government and private hospitals in the region.
implementedBy: Ministry of Health
Bangsamoro Darul Ifta
Moro Waqf Foundation, Inc.
whatChanges: A request. It sets no standard, deadline or report; institutionalizing it is left to the MOH and the Darul Ifta.
A private foundation is named as a partner in the request.
readings.insight: The WHEREAS clauses look to the MOH and Darul Ifta 'mandating all government and private health facilities' to provide these services, but the RESOLVED clause only urges them to institutionalize it. Several of the cited DOH rules already apply nationally.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament calls on the Government of the Day, through the Office of the Attorney General, the Bangsamoro Women Commission, the Ministry of the Interior and Local Government and other offices, to hold an annual forum on sexual harassment and on the implementation of the Anti-Sexual Harassment Act (RA 7877), the Anti-Rape Law (RA 8353) and the Safe Spaces Act (RA 11313) in the region.

Copies go to all ministries, offices, LGUs and government-owned corporations in BARMM. Authored by MP Baintan A. Ampatuan, MP Don Mustapha A. Loong, MP Amilbahar S. Mawallil, MP Paisalin P. Tago, MP Lanang T. Ali Jr. and MP Omar Yasser C. Sema. Adopted on 25 January 2022.
readings.whyProposed: The authors cite a 2016 Social Weather Stations survey in which 3 in 5 women had experienced sexual harassment, and 88% of women aged 18 to 24; and 2017 NDHS data showing only a third of women in the region who suffered physical or sexual violence sought help, while 72% told no one. They point to underreporting, cost, fear of shame (maratabat), few shelters, scarce materials in local languages and untrained responders, and note that the Safe Spaces Act tasks the interior ministry with capacity building.
whoIsAffected: Women and others at risk of harassment in the region.
LGU officials, police, social workers and prosecutors who enforce the laws.
implementedBy: Office of the Attorney General
Bangsamoro Women Commission
Ministry of the Interior and Local Government
whatChanges: A call for a yearly event; it sets no date, budget or report to Parliament.
It changes no law; the 3 statutes it covers are national.
readings.insight: The resolution opens with Qur'anic verses on modesty addressed to both men and women, then makes its case with survey figures. It asks for a recurring forum but builds in no way for Parliament to see whether one is held.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament commends Sultan Abantas Asaali for placing third in the December 2021 Radiologic Technologist Licensure Examination. A copy goes to him.

Authored by MP Amilbahar S. Mawallil and MP Eddie M. Alih. Adopted on 25 January 2022.
readings.whyProposed: Results came out on 4 January 2022. Asaali, a Universidad de Zamboanga graduate from Simunul, Tawi-Tawi, rated 90.20%; 786 of 2,177 examinees, or 36.10%, passed. He finished at the MSU-Tawi-Tawi College of Technology and Oceanography preparatory high school in 2013.
whoIsAffected: Sultan Abantas Asaali.
whatChanges: A commendation. Its only action is sending a copy to the honoree.
readings.insight: Another Tawi-Tawi topnotcher out of MSU-TCTO, like the honorees of Resolutions No. 197 and 198. Unlike No. 197, it gives no cash.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament urges the Government of the Day, through the Bangsamoro Information and Communications Technology Office, to strengthen internet access and connectivity, especially in the localities, and to report to Parliament quarterly on its compliance.

It also asks the ICT office and other ministries to report on internet service in BARMM: cell towers in each province, areas with free public Wi-Fi, the number of 2G, 3G, 4G and 5G users and other data. Copies go to Chief Minister Ahod B. Ebrahim, the ICT office and other ministries. Authored by MP Diamila D. Ramos. Adopted on 27 January 2022.
readings.whyProposed: The pandemic pushed health, schooling, work and commerce online, and the region's connection is slow and unstable. The resolution cites data that almost 45% of Filipinos (46 million) and 74% of public schools (34,500) lack internet access, and that 4G availability in BARMM trails other regions at below 60% in rural areas and 65.1% in urban areas. It suggests lower spectrum fees to help small providers, and better coordination with power companies, since 'without electricity, internet is only a blackhole'.
whoIsAffected: Internet users in BARMM, especially outside the cities.
Telecommunication providers.
implementedBy: Bangsamoro Information and Communications Technology Office
whatChanges: It asks for a quarterly compliance report to Parliament, a stronger follow-up than most resolutions, but sets no penalty if none comes.
The status report it requests has no deadline.
readings.insight: The quarterly report is the notable feature. The web address of the index entry carries an earlier title calling for free Wi-Fi for the entire region; the adopted text keeps only a request for data on where free public Wi-Fi exists. Parliament had already asked telecommunication companies to upgrade signals and add cell sites in Resolution No. 143 (24 August 2021).

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament commends Hamid Simpal Salik for placing 9th in the September 2021 Licensure Examination for Teachers. A copy goes to him.

Authored by MP Ubaida C. Pacasem, MP Ziaur-Rahman A. Adiong, MP Anna Tarhata S. Basman and MP Raissa H. Jajurie. Adopted on 27 January 2022.
readings.whyProposed: Salik, a cum laude Bachelor of Secondary Education graduate in mathematics from Cotabato State University, rated 91.40%. Of 17,863 examinees, 10,318, or 57.76%, passed.
whoIsAffected: Hamid Simpal Salik.
whatChanges: A commendation. Its only action is presenting a copy to the honoree.
readings.insight: One of 5 topnotcher commendations adopted between December 2021 and January 2022 (Nos. 197, 198, 203, 205, 208); only No. 197 came with a cash gift.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament urgently directs the Bangsamoro Inter-Agency Task Force (BIATF), especially the Ministry of Health, to strengthen its preventive response to the surge of the COVID-19 Omicron variant to stop it spreading widely in BARMM.

Copies go to the BIATF and the MOH. Authored by MP Saffrullah M. Dipatuan. Adopted on 27 January 2022.
readings.whyProposed: The WHO named Omicron a variant of concern in November 2021. On 31 December 2021 the Department of Health confirmed 14 Omicron cases in the country, 7 imported, and warned of likely local transmission. The resolution cites WHO findings that Omicron spreads faster than Delta, doubling in 1.5 to 3 days, can infect vaccinated and boosted people, raises reinfection risk, and that unvaccinated children were being hospitalized in growing numbers.
whoIsAffected: Residents of BARMM, especially unvaccinated children.
The MOH and BIATF member agencies.
implementedBy: Bangsamoro Inter-Agency Task Force
Ministry of Health
whatChanges: A directive that names no specific measure, deadline or report.
It changes no existing health protocol by itself.
readings.insight: It was adopted 27 days after the DOH confirmation the text cites, and names no specific measure. It follows earlier COVID-19 resolutions to the MOH and BIATF, including Resolutions No. 107, 113, 132 and 133 in 2021.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament condemns in the strongest terms the deaths of 6 Moro residents of Barangay Gokotan, Pikit, Cotabato Province, in a raid by a composite PNP and military team. It calls on the Ad Hoc Joint Action Group (AHJAG) and the Coordinating Committees on the Cessation of Hostilities (CCCH) to conduct a thorough and impartial investigation and file administrative and criminal cases against the perpetrators as soon as possible, and expresses condolences to the families while demanding justice.

Copies go to the PNP, the AFP, AHJAG, CCCH and the families. Authored by MP Akmad I. Abas, MP Abdullah E. Gayak, MP Romeo K. Sema, MP Abduladzis M. Esmael and MP Ibrahim D. Ali. Adopted on 27 January 2022.
readings.whyProposed: Early on 29 December 2021, police and soldiers serving an arrest warrant raided houses in Gokotan but did not catch their targets. The resolution names 5 people killed by gunfire, including 4 members of the MILF's Bangsamoro Islamic Armed Forces and Arbaya Dalid, a mother of 3, plus a 17-year-old wounded; a BIAF brigade commander drowned in a river while repositioning. 3 more residents were arrested. The raiding team did not coordinate through AHJAG, as the 2002 GPH-MILF joint communiqué requires.
whoIsAffected: The families of the 6 dead and the wounded 17-year-old.
MILF members in the area, and the GPH-MILF ceasefire mechanisms.
implementedBy: Ad Hoc Joint Action Group
Coordinating Committees on the Cessation of Hostilities
Philippine National Police
Armed Forces of the Philippines
whatChanges: A condemnation and a call to the joint ceasefire bodies; Parliament cannot order the PNP or AFP.
It asks for cases to be filed but sets no timeline and asks for no report.
readings.insight: The title calls the dead 'innocent Moro civilians', but the resolution's own list identifies 5 of the 6 as members of the MILF's armed wing; the text describes them as civilians who were also legitimate MILF members. Its core complaint is procedural: the raid skipped the AHJAG coordination agreed in 2002. Parliament raised the same issue in Resolution No. 542 (18 February 2025), condemning a raid that killed 7 MILF members. The text consolidates 2 proposed resolutions.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament congratulates the Notre Dame Hospital and Siena College of Cotabato, formerly the NDH School of Midwifery, for producing 4 topnotchers in the December 2021 X-Ray Technologist Licensure Examination, and recognizes the 4 and their families and mentors: Isnairah A. Rangan (2nd), Fairodz A. Tahir (3rd), Jalilah D. Alabat (5th) and Asmaira M. Rangan (10th).

Copies go to the 4 and the school. Authored by MP Mohagher M. Iqbal. Adopted on 27 January 2022.
readings.whyProposed: A private Cotabato City school produced 4 of the exam's top 10, which the authors present as an inspiration to the region's youth and institutions.
whoIsAffected: The 4 topnotchers.
Notre Dame Hospital and Siena College of Cotabato.
whatChanges: A commendation. Its only action is sending copies to the honorees.
readings.insight: The resolution gives no exam statistics, unlike most topnotcher commendations. The first honoree is spelled 'Isnairah' in the list and 'Isnaira' in the forwarding clause; the page image shows both.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament reiterates its appeal to President Rodrigo Roa Duterte that, should he appoint a new set of BTA members, he allow the incumbent members nominated by the government to continue, by giving them primary consideration for reappointment.

Copies go to the President, the Office of the Presidential Adviser for Unity, Peace, and Reconciliation, the Department of National Defense and the Department of the Interior and Local Government. Authored by MP Nabil A. Tan and 19 others. Adopted on 15 February 2022.
readings.whyProposed: Republic Act No. 11593, signed 28 October 2021, reset the first BARMM election to 2025 and lets the President appoint 80 new interim BTA members to serve up to 30 June 2025. The authors argue that the incumbents have nearly 2 and a half years of training and experience in the parliamentary system, an ethnically balanced makeup, and members who drafted the Organic Law, and that replacing them would disrupt pending legislation and programs. They acknowledge that appointment is the President's sole power.
whoIsAffected: Incumbent BTA members nominated by the national government.
The President, who holds the appointing power.
whatChanges: An appeal to the President, who decides alone.
It narrows Resolution No. 173's request to the government-nominated members only.
readings.insight: Resolution No. 173 (12 October 2021) asked for primary consideration for all incumbent members; this follow-up, adopted 4 months later, limits the appeal to the members nominated by the government. The second BTA was appointed under President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr.; Resolution No. 271 (26 September 2022) commended the first-BTA members he did not reappoint.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament congratulates Notre Dame University for being granted autonomous status by the Commission on Higher Education. A copy goes to the university's president.

Authored by MP Baintan A. Ampatuan and MP Amilbahar S. Mawallil. Adopted on 15 February 2022.
readings.whyProposed: CHED, with the endorsement of the Bangsamoro education ministry (MBHTE), granted Notre Dame University, the only private university in Cotabato City and run by the Oblates, autonomous status from 7 December 2020 to 7 December 2022. Before that it was a deregulated institution. Autonomy gives priority for CHED subsidies and the freedom to set its own curricula and form links with foreign schools.
whoIsAffected: Notre Dame University and its students.
whatChanges: A commendation. Its only action is sending a copy to the university.
readings.insight: The commendation came more than 14 months into a 2-year grant that ran to 7 December 2022. It was adopted 19 days after Resolution No. 208 honored another Notre Dame institution in Cotabato City, the Notre Dame Hospital and Siena College.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament strongly condemns the rape and killing of 16-year-old Rasmia Kamawit of Barangay Malanduague, Kabacan, Cotabato, and earnestly requests the Philippine National Police, the National Bureau of Investigation and the Commission on Human Rights to fast-track their investigations so the perpetrators can be brought to justice.

Copies go to the Chief of the PNP, the Director of the NBI and the Chairperson of the CHR for appropriate action. Authored by MP Bainon G. Karon and MP Aida M. Silongan. Adopted on 17 November 2020.
readings.whyProposed: Rasmia's body was found in the Dalapuan River in Barangay Malanduague by her father, who had been searching for her after she went out to gather firewood. Kabacan police confirmed she was raped before she was killed, and her father named at least 4 suspects, whose identities police were withholding. Malanduague is a Bangsamoro community outside the region, and the authors cite the Organic Law's mandate to assist such communities, along with national and international protections for women and girls.
whoIsAffected: The family of Rasmia Kamawit.
Bangsamoro communities outside the region, in whose name Parliament speaks here.
implementedBy: Philippine National Police
National Bureau of Investigation
Commission on Human Rights
whatChanges: It sends a request to 3 national bodies Parliament has no authority over; it sets no deadline and asks for no report back.
deliberation: 17 November 2020: MP Aida M. Silongan said months after the killing authorities had reported no action, and urged action so Bangsamoro outside BARMM would not feel forgotten.
17 November 2020: MP Bainon G. Karon said the body of a 14-year-old Moro girl was found on 14 September 2020 in a river in Barangay Malanduague, Kabacan, after she went to gather firewood.

17 November 2020: MP Baintan A. Ampatuan asked whether a police investigation was not already standard procedure and whether the Bangsamoro Women Commission had been briefed; MP Bainon G. Karon said the Executive Secretary told her an investigation was ongoing.

17 November 2020: MP Paisalin P. Tago, told that Kabacan police had filed no case because of the time element, said police should file on the strength of the corpus delicti and blotter even without a complainant.

17 November 2020: MP Jamel D. Macaraya said there was no formal Bangsamoro investigation and proposed a fact-finding team; MP Khadafeh G. Mangudadatu wanted committee referral, while MP Ziaur-Rahman Alonto Adiong said that would defeat the call for urgency.
17 November 2020: Consolidated with Proposed Resolution No. 318 and approved subject to style.
17 November 2020: Consolidated with Proposed Resolution No. 312 and approved subject to style.
readings.insight: The crime happened outside the region, in Kabacan, Cotabato, so Parliament could only ask national agencies to act. The resolution was adopted 65 days after the body was found. The adopted text dates the discovery to 'September 13, 2020 (Monday)'; 13 September 2020 was a Sunday.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament expresses its profound condolences to the family of Moro National Liberation Front Chairman Yusop H. Jikiri, former Sulu Governor (2001 to 2004) and former Sulu Representative (2007 to 2010), and resolves to honour his legacy in public service. The resolution is sent to his family.

Authored by MP Punduma B. Sani and 10 others. Adopted on 17 November 2020.
readings.whyProposed: Jikiri died of bone cancer on 17 October 2020. Born in Pasil, Indanan, Sulu, he rose to lead the MNLF, chairing its Council of Leaders from 2017. He was the MNLF's Chief of Staff when the 1996 Final Peace Agreement was signed, chaired the Southern Philippines Development Authority, led the MNLF at the 2015 OIC tripartite meeting, and signed an agreement with MILF Chairman Murad Ebrahim in Kuala Lumpur. The authors credit him with backing the Bangsamoro Organic Law as a convergence of all peace agreements.
whoIsAffected: The family of Yusop H. Jikiri.
The Moro National Liberation Front.
whatChanges: It records Parliament's sentiment and sends a copy to the family; it directs no office to do anything.
deliberation: 17 November 2020: MP Paisalin P. Tago said Jikiri, Chief of Staff of the Bangsamoro Armed Forces, was a pillar of the MNLF whose sacrifices deserved recognition; MP Nabil A. Tan called him a man of peace.
17 November 2020: Consolidated Proposed Resolutions No. 325, 326, 327, 333 and 335 approved subject to style on motion of MP Nabil A. Tan as amended by MP Omar Yasser C. Sema.
readings.insight: Adopted a month after his death. 2 months later Parliament mourned another MNLF leader, its own Member and Deputy Chief Minister Abdul Raji Sahrin, in Resolution 103 (26 January 2021). Both texts stress the same point: MNLF leaders who backed the Organic Law as the convergence of the peace agreements.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament urges the House of Representatives and the Senate to extend the BARMM transition period to 30 June 2025, so the Bangsamoro Transition Authority has enough time to keep exercising its powers and fulfil its mandate. The resolution goes to the Speaker of the House and the Senate President.

Authored by MP Jose I. Lorena, MP Hatimil E. Hassan, MP Eddie M. Alih, MP Ustadz Abdulmuhmin A. Mujahid, MP Muslimin A. Jakilan and MP Omar Yasser C. Sema. Adopted on 17 November 2020.
readings.whyProposed: Under the Organic Law the transition ends when the BTA is dissolved after the first regular election, synchronised with the 2022 national elections. The authors say 3 years is not enough given the size of the mandate, resource shortfalls, security threats and the pandemic. They cite the Mindanao People's Caucus midterm review, which recommended a 3-year extension to June 2025, and note that the 1996 Final Peace Agreement and the Organic Law's provisions on the rehabilitation of MILF and MNLF combatants were still not fully implemented. They also cite similar calls from the League of Municipalities (Tawi-Tawi chapter) and the provincial boards of Tawi-Tawi and Maguindanao.
whoIsAffected: The Bangsamoro Transition Authority, whose term would run 3 more years.
Voters of the region, whose first parliamentary election would be pushed from 2022 to 2025.
implementedBy: House of Representatives
Senate of the Philippines
whatChanges: Only Congress can amend the Organic Law's schedule; the resolution is a formal request to it.
deliberation: 17 November 2020: Asked by MP Nabil A. Tan, MP Jose I. Lorena said 2025 was chosen to synchronize with national elections and that normalization, including the Normalization Trust Fund, had not been implemented.
17 November 2020: MP Jose I. Lorena agreed with MP Nabil A. Tan that an extension would not guarantee reappointment of current Members, as appointment is the President's prerogative.

17 November 2020: MP Nabil A. Tan asked whether a real assessment of BARMM was needed as a basis rather than a civil society report; MP Jose I. Lorena said he relied on the Chief Minister's statement that MILF communities had not been rehabilitated.

17 November 2020: MP Omar Yasser C. Sema called the title vague and drew from MP Jose I. Lorena that elections would be postponed and that the region was not ready for 2022 elections because of the pandemic; he asked evidence be annexed for 2 whereas clauses.

17 November 2020: MP Edrieza H.N. Rimbang asked whether the sponsor was the Chief Minister's counsel and whether Members had consulted the President or the people; MP Jose I. Lorena said he stood on his own and cited 'salus populi est suprema lex'.

17 November 2020: MP Mohagher M. Iqbal said the extension was not self-serving: the MILF sought 7 years, the draft law 5, but the Organic Law gave 3, and the Normalization Trust Fund was unfunded and decommissioning's second phase unmet.

17 November 2020: Approved subject to style on motion of MP Nabil A. Tan as amended by MP Omar Yasser C. Sema, whose motions to annex evidence for 2 whereas clauses and correct the plebiscite date to 21 January were put on record.
readings.insight: The request was granted: Republic Act No. 11593 extended the transition to 30 June 2025, the exact date asked for here. Parliament asked again in Resolution 505 (22 October 2024), that time for 2028; Congress moved the election only to October 2025, and it was later reset to 14 September 2026.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament respectfully requests the Armed Forces of the Philippines to exercise utmost caution and prudence in its statements, especially about madaris (Islamic schools), which might further alienate Muslims in the Philippines. A copy goes to the AFP Chief of Staff for his information and guidance.

Authored by MP Paisalin P. Tago and MP Ustadz Abdulmuhmin A. Mujahid. Adopted on 17 November 2020.
readings.whyProposed: On 13 October 2020, AFP Chief of Staff General Gilbert Gapay said madaris were institutions of radicalisation. The authors call the statement untrue and sweeping, warning that it breeds distrust among Muslim youth, especially after the Anti-Terrorism Act of 2020. They note that the madrasah curriculum was integrated into the national system under DepEd Order No. 51, s. 2004, that the Organic Law makes the Bangsamoro Government responsible for madaris, and that Ulama summits in Cotabato City and Zamboanga City in 2017 denounced terrorism. They say any proof of madaris recruiting terrorists should be shown in the proper venue before public statements are made.
whoIsAffected: Madrasah students and teachers, estimated in the text at 100,000 to 150,000 students in 1,000 to 2,000 madaris in Mindanao.
The Armed Forces of the Philippines.
implementedBy: Armed Forces of the Philippines
whatChanges: It is a request to a national body; it sets no consequence and asks for no reply.
deliberation: 17 November 2020: MP Paisalin P. Tago urged passage even though AFP Chief of Staff Gilbert Gapay had retracted his statement on madaris, as a reference for future officials.

17 November 2020: MP Bai Maleiha B. Candao attributed the issue to a communication gap and urged dialogue between the AFP chief and Islamic leaders; MP Hamid Aminoddin D. Barra suggested asking the AFP to study Islam as a religion of peace.
17 November 2020: MP Omar Yasser C. Sema proposed toning down the language since the MILF and MNLF are now partners of the Government; the Chair agreed.
17 November 2020: Consolidated Proposed Resolutions No. 328 and 330 approved unanimously.
readings.insight: The resolution came 35 days after the statement it answers. It does not ask the AFP to retract, only to be careful and to bring any proof to a proper proceeding. The figures on madaris are estimates the text gives without a source.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament extends again the phase-out of accountable officers and employees of the Bangsamoro Government to 30 June 2021, unless they are sooner replaced or their accountability reports and physical accomplishments are settled, whichever comes first. Their heads of office must submit accountability reports to Parliament before their term ends.

Executive offices send their recommended lists to the Office of the Chief Minister, and Parliament's divisions to the Office of the Speaker, by 31 December 2020; the Chief Minister and the Speaker approve them. Those extended keep their current posts unless replaced, and their pay comes from the Miscellaneous Personnel Benefits Fund of the FY 2021 Bangsamoro Appropriations Act. Hiring continues under health protocols, and the 2 offices may issue guidelines.

Authored by MP Ubaida C. Pacasem, MP Raissa H. Jajurie, MP Anna Tarhata S. Basman and MP Paisalin P. Tago. Adopted on 16 December 2020.
readings.whyProposed: The Organic Law has the BTA phase out the abolished offices of the former ARMM, with appointive officials staying on per the phase-out schedule. Resolution 75 had extended the phase-out to 31 December 2020. The authors say quarantines stalled hiring, many deliverables are pending, new staff cannot be hired quickly even after the Administrative Code, and Parliament's own organisational structure is not yet approved. Extending the phase-out amends the transition plan, which needs a majority of all BTA members.
whoIsAffected: Accountable officers and employees carried over from the former ARMM, who keep their posts for up to 6 more months.
Applicants for new positions, whose hiring continues alongside.
implementedBy: Office of the Chief Minister
Office of the Speaker
Ministries, agencies and offices of the Bangsamoro Government

funding.detail: No new appropriation. Salaries of extended personnel are charged to the Miscellaneous Personnel Benefits Fund in the FY 2021 Bangsamoro Appropriations Act.

whatChanges: This has force: it amends the transition plan's phase-out schedule, which the Organic Law leaves to the BTA.
Offices had 15 days, to 31 December 2020, to submit their lists.
deliberation: 16 December 2020: MP Paisalin P. Tago explained that the extension of accountable officers would expire on 31 December 2020 and that without a further extension the operations of offices would be paralyzed, with about 57 accountable officers in Parliament and an estimated 100 in all.

16 December 2020: MP Amilbahar S. Mawallil asked whether 'Bangsamoro Transition Authority' meant only Parliament; MP Tago answered that it refers to the whole interim Bangsamoro Government under Article XVI of the Bangsamoro Organic Law.

16 December 2020: MP Baintan A. Ampatuan noted this was the third extension and said it would not look good on Parliament; MP Tago replied that the Deputy Minister of Finance had said the NOSCA could be issued within the next 6 months.

16 December 2020: MP Jose I. Lorena warned that the resolution must not be abused to perpetuate the accountable officers; MP Tago said 30 June 2021 is a maximum and an extension ends earlier once a regular officer is appointed.
16 December 2020: MP Don Mustapha A. Loong, MP Jose I. Lorena and MP Baintan A. Ampatuan successively amended the title to cover the Bangsamoro Government until 30 June 2021; all were accepted.
16 December 2020: MP Amilbahar S. Mawallil added a prayer requiring the extended accountable officers to report to Parliament at the end of their terms; accepted by MP Tago.
16 December 2020: Approved subject to style; recorded in the adopted index as Resolution No. 95 of 16 December 2020.
readings.insight: This is the 3rd extension. Resolution 54 extended the phase-out to 31 March 2020 and Resolution 75 to 31 December 2020; this one runs to 30 June 2021, 15 months past the first extension's end date. The text mentions Parliament's organisational structure as not yet approved, but Resolution 96, approving it, was adopted the same day. The FY 2021 fund it draws on, under BAA 15, was ₱1.78 billion.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament approves the organisational structure of the BTA Parliament, as recommended by its Committee on Accounts and Audit.

Authored by MP Anna Tarhata S. Basman and 16 others. Adopted on 16 December 2020.
readings.whyProposed: The Office of the Speaker submitted a proposed organisational structure for Parliament's secretariat. The Committee on Accounts and Audit, which under Parliament's rules has jurisdiction over the BTA's expenditures, deliberated on it on 27 October 2020 and recommended approval, as amended, in Committee Report No. 42.
whoIsAffected: Staff of the Parliament secretariat, whose offices and positions the structure sets.
Applicants for Parliament positions.
implementedBy: Office of the Speaker
Secretariat of the Bangsamoro Transition Authority Parliament
whatChanges: It has force inside Parliament: the structure is approved and can be used for staffing.
The structure itself is not in the resolution; the posted file repeats the same 1-page resolution 4 times.
deliberation: 16 December 2020: MP Diamila D. Ramos added public outreach duties for the public information division, public access to Parliament research, and a confidential inquiry service for MPs; accepted by MP Anna Tarhata S. Basman.

16 December 2020: MP Maisara D. Latiph manifested that under Section 4, Rule VII the Committee on Accounts and Audit had no jurisdiction over the organizational structure, and warned she would object if it happened again; MP Baintan A. Ampatuan replied that the committee needs a settled structure as basis for allocating funds.

16 December 2020: MP Don Mustapha A. Loong asked that the offices of the Majority and Minority Floor Leaders appear in the main organogram; MP Basman explained that officers are covered by the box of the Parliament under primus inter pares, and MP Loong yielded.
16 December 2020: MP Don Mustapha A. Loong moved to include 2 Deputy Majority Floor Leaders and 2 Deputy Minority Floor Leaders in the structure; accepted.
16 December 2020: MP Jose I. Lorena proposed 1 dental service position in the Medical and Health Services; accepted subject to identifying the position and salary grade.
16 December 2020: Approved as amended on motion of MP Jose I. Lorena; recorded in the adopted index as Resolution No. 96 of 16 December 2020.
readings.insight: The resolution approves a document the public cannot see in it: neither the structure nor the committee's amendments are attached. It was adopted 50 days after the committee report, and on the same day as Resolution 95, whose text still calls Parliament's structure unapproved and keeps former ARMM staff in place until 30 June 2021 partly for that reason.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament recognises the top-ranked Bangsamoro Qur'an reciters who represented the country in international competitions since 1969, and lists 69 placings by name, province, host country, rank and year. They include 7 champions: Hassan Sharif Noor (Tripoli, Libya), Abdulbasit Imam Tomara (Tehran, Iran, 1994), Potre Salakayan (Indonesia), Isnairah B. Parahima (Malaysia/Thailand, 2000), Nu'man M. Pimbayabaya (Libya/Melaka, 2007), Raihana G. Ambangala (Brunei, 2015) and Kamaruddin G. Zaidon (Brunei, 2019).

It requests the Office of the Chief Minister, through the Bureau on Cultural Heritage, to give the winners plaques of recognition or other tokens of appreciation. Copies go to Chief Minister Ahod B. Ebrahim, the Bureau and the reciters. Authored by MP Eddie M. Alih and MP Mudjib C. Abu. Adopted on 17 December 2020.
readings.whyProposed: The Organic Law recognises and protects the customs, beliefs and traditions of the Bangsamoro people. The authors note that Bangsamoro reciters have placed at international Qur'an reading competitions for about half a century, bringing honour to the region.
whoIsAffected: The reciters named in the list.
The Bureau on Cultural Heritage, asked to award them.
implementedBy: Office of the Chief Minister
Bureau on Cultural Heritage

funding.detail: The resolution appropriates nothing. Plaques or other tokens are requested but no amount or source is named.

whatChanges: It asks the Chief Minister's office to award plaques; it does not oblige it to.
deliberation: 16 December 2020: MP Paisalin P. Tago objected to taking up the resolution because its principal author was not physically present, citing earlier cases of MP Maisara D. Latiph and MP Bai Maleiha B. Candao; the Chair inclined to follow him for fairness.

16 December 2020: MP Nabil A. Tan moved to allow consideration and sponsorship of resolutions through Zoom, seconded by MP Maisara D. Latiph; the Majority Floor Leader said the rule was only a Speaker's guideline and the Rules would be amended in January 2021, and the measure was deferred.

17 December 2020: MP Baintan A. Ampatuan questioned why an 8th placer is recognized on par with champions; MP Ziaur-Rahman Alonto Adiong said he was amenable to limiting it but the intent was to honour all who represented the country.
17 December 2020: MP Baintan A. Ampatuan asked who would fund the activities; MP Adiong said the resolution names no source of funding for trophies or plaques.
17 December 2020: MP Ali B. Sangki recounted handling the Qur'an Reading Competition under SPDA in 1976 and noted the honoree's name is Sundigan Magdara, not Sandigan Magdara.
17 December 2020: MP Jamel D. Macaraya raised a point of order that the Chair had limited interpellators to 2 but recognized a third; the Chair still allowed MP Paisalin P. Tago to speak.
17 December 2020: MP Paisalin P. Tago said he would propose monetary awards besides posthumous recognition; MP Adiong had no objection.
17 December 2020: Unanimously approved subject to style; recorded in the adopted index as Resolution No. 97 of 17 December 2020.
readings.insight: The list counts placings, not people: some names appear twice, such as Abdul Latif Daud (2nd in Malaysia in 1999, 3rd in Iran) and Kamaruddin G. Zaidon (champion in Brunei in 2019, 2nd in Brunei in 2015). Nearly all entries come from Lanao del Sur and Maguindanao; 1 is from Basilan. Several entries give no year, and 4 give no rank. Resolution 306 (19 January 2023) later amended this resolution; its title adds Qur'an memorisers to the reciters recognised.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament expresses profound gratitude to the City Government of Cagayan de Oro, led by Mayor Oscar S. Moreno, and to the University of Science and Technology of Southern Philippines, headed by President Dr. Ambrosio B. Cultura II, for temporarily sheltering Bangsamoro locally stranded individuals (LSIs) on 7 July 2020 until they could return home to Basilan, Sulu and Tawi-Tawi. Copies go to the mayor and the university.

Authored by MP Ziaur-Rahman A. Adiong and 22 others. Adopted on 17 December 2020.
readings.whyProposed: Under the national Hatid-Tulong Program, 499 LSIs from Manila bound for Basilan, Sulu and Tawi-Tawi were made to disembark in Cagayan de Oro instead of Zamboanga City. The Bangsamoro Government and the LGUs concerned were notified only after they had landed. The city opened its borders and housed them at USTP, giving the Bangsamoro Government time to arrange their trip home.
whoIsAffected: The 499 stranded travellers from Basilan, Sulu and Tawi-Tawi.
The City Government of Cagayan de Oro and USTP.
whatChanges: It is a thank-you; it directs no one.
deliberation: 17 December 2020: The Chair suggested consolidating Proposed Resolutions No. 305 and 310; MP Ziaur-Rahman Alonto Adiong explained they concern separate events in different cities, and they were approved separately.
17 December 2020: Debate and amendments dispensed with; approved subject to style; recorded in the adopted index as Resolution No. 98 of 17 December 2020.
readings.insight: Adopted 163 days after the event. The WHEREAS clauses record a coordination failure without asking anyone to explain it: the regional government learned of 499 of its constituents only after they had been put ashore in another region. Resolution 99, adopted the same day, thanks San Juan City for similar help.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament expresses profound gratitude to the City Government of San Juan, led by Mayor Francis Zamora, and its City Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office, headed by Saripada Lucman Pacasum Jr., for helping Bangsamoro locally stranded individuals and ROFs in the city and coordinating their safe return home. Copies go to both.

Authored by MP Ziaur-Rahman A. Adiong. Adopted on 17 December 2020.
readings.whyProposed: The pandemic cost many Bangsamoro living outside the region their livelihoods and forced them to return home. San Juan City and its disaster office gave them immediate assistance and coordinated their return with the Bangsamoro Government. The authors also note that Bangsamoro communities elsewhere often face discriminatory policies.
whoIsAffected: Bangsamoro LSIs and ROFs who were in San Juan City.
The City Government of San Juan.
whatChanges: It is a thank-you; it directs no one.
deliberation: 17 December 2020: Debate and amendments dispensed with; approved subject to style; recorded in the adopted index as Resolution No. 99 of 17 December 2020.
readings.insight: One of 2 thank-you resolutions adopted on 17 December 2020 for help given to stranded Bangsamoro; the other, Resolution 98, thanks Cagayan de Oro City. The text gives no number of people helped or dates.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament approves the 2021 budget of the BTA Parliament, as recommended by its Committee on Accounts and Audit.

Authored by MP Anna Tarhata S. Basman and 16 others. Adopted on 23 December 2020.
readings.whyProposed: The Committee on Accounts and Audit, which under Parliament's rules has jurisdiction over the BTA's expenditures, deliberated on the proposed 2021 Parliament budget on 22 December 2020 and recommended its approval in Committee Report No. 51 the same day.
whoIsAffected: Members and staff of Parliament, whose operations the budget funds.
implementedBy: Secretariat of the Bangsamoro Transition Authority Parliament

funding.detail: The resolution approves Parliament's 2021 budget but states no amount; the figures are in Committee Report No. 51, not in the resolution.

whatChanges: It has force inside Parliament: the internal budget is approved.
readings.insight: The resolution names no figure. The committee met and reported on 22 December and the plenary approved the next day, 23 December 2020, the same day the region's FY 2021 budget, BAA 15, was passed and approved. Resolution 106, a month later, narrowed this committee's role to reviewing exactly this: Parliament's own budget.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament resolves to 'mandate' the Ministry of Basic, Higher and Technical Education to highly consider including the life and teachings of the Prophet Muhammad (SAW) as a subject in the elementary, secondary, tertiary and technical education curriculum. The resolution is forwarded to the ministry for information and appropriate consideration.

Authored by MP Paisalin P. Tago. Adopted on 26 January 2021.
readings.whyProposed: The authors cite the Constitution's goals for education and the Organic Law's provisions on an integrated education system and on teaching Islamic and Arabic studies to Muslim pupils in public schools. They describe the Prophet's life as a model of peace, moral values and resistance to injustice that young people should learn.
whoIsAffected: Students at every level in the region.
The Ministry of Basic, Higher and Technical Education.
implementedBy: Ministry of Basic, Higher and Technical Education
whatChanges: Despite the word 'mandating' in the title, the operative clause only asks the ministry to 'highly consider' it, and forwards it for 'appropriate consideration'.
deliberation: 26 January 2021: MP Paisalin P. Tago said students learn more about Jose Rizal than the Prophet, whose life is the basis of moral governance, and told the Chair it should be a separate subject, not part of history class.

26 January 2021: MP Romeo C. Saliga asked whether teaching it violates separation of church and state; MP Rasol Y. Mitmug, Jr. said no, since the Prophet is treated as a historical figure as well as a religious one.

26 January 2021: MP Adzfar H. Usman and MP Baintan A. Ampatuan said it should be built into the Bangsamoro Education Code, or the legality of spending public funds on religion would be questioned; MP Saffrullah M. Dipatuan disagreed, saying waiting for the code would cause needless delay.
26 January 2021: MP Hatimil E. Hassan proposed covering the lives of other prophets as well; MP Mitmug did not accept, saying it went beyond the committee's intent.

26 January 2021: MP Alzad T. Sattar, MP Adzfar H. Usman and MP Maisara D. Latiph amended the title so it mandates MBHTE to include the subject in elementary, secondary, tertiary and technical education; accepted.
26 January 2021: Unanimously approved and adopted; recorded in the adopted index as Resolution No. 101 of 26 January 2021.
readings.insight: The resolution does not say whether the subject would be for Muslim students only, as the Organic Law provision it cites is, or for all students. It sets no deadline and asks for no report.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament calls on the Commission on Higher Education to expedite the conversion of Cotabato City State Polytechnic College into a state university, in line with the requirements of Section 26 of Republic Act No. 10585.

Authored by MP Susana S. Anayatin and MP Mohagher M. Iqbal. Adopted on 26 January 2021.
readings.whyProposed: Republic Act No. 10585 converted the college into Cotabato State University, with its main campus in Cotabato City. Section 26 makes the conversion depend on meeting CHED requirements: Level III accreditation for at least 4 undergraduate and 2 graduate programs, enough qualified full-time faculty, adequate libraries and laboratories, research output, outreach, and sound academic policies.
whoIsAffected: Students and faculty of the college in Cotabato City.
implementedBy: Commission on Higher Education
