whoIsAffected: Communities around Lake Lanao, whose lake would be managed by either a national or a Bangsamoro authority.
The Bangsamoro Government, whose claim to manage inland waters is at stake.
implementedBy: Senate Committee on Government Corporations and Public Enterprises
Office of the Chief Minister
Office of the Senate President
whatChanges: This is a request to a Senate committee; it binds no one.
It states Parliament's formal position that Lake Lanao is for the Bangsamoro Government to manage, which can be cited in later talks.
readings.insight: The resolution rests its argument on the Organic Law's command that Parliament itself create authorities for specific bodies of water. Parliament has not yet done so for Lake Lanao. Its index lists 2 bills: Bill No. 155, filed on 28 February 2023, to create a Lake Lanao Rehabilitation and Development Authority, and Bill No. 352, filed by the Government of the Day on 8 April 2025, to create a Lake Lanao Management Authority. Both were still at committee stage when last updated in 2025.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament adopts the calendar for its Third Regular Session. The session opened on 15 June 2021 and runs in 20 sitting weeks, each from a Tuesday to a Thursday, ending with mandatory adjournment on 24 March 2022.

The sitting weeks are 15 to 17 and 22 to 24 June, 13 to 15 and 20 to 22 July, 17 to 19 and 24 to 26 August, 14 to 16 and 21 to 23 September, 12 to 14 and 19 to 21 October, 16 to 18 and 23 to 25 November, 14 to 16 and 21 to 23 December, 18 to 20 and 25 to 27 January, 15 to 17 and 22 to 24 February, and 15 to 17 and 22 to 24 March.

Authored by MP Lanang T. Ali Jr. Adopted on 16 June 2021, by the date on the signed text.
readings.whyProposed: Parliament's rules say the BTA convenes its regular session on the third Tuesday of the month after Eid'l Fitr and sits for as many days as a legislative calendar sets. They also set plenary sessions from Tuesday to Thursday in the third and fourth weeks of each month that Parliament is not in recess. A calendar tells Members when they must be in plenary and when they are free for constituency work.
whoIsAffected: Members of Parliament, who must attend on the listed dates.
The public and offices that follow the plenary, who can plan around the schedule.
implementedBy: Bangsamoro Transition Authority Parliament
whatChanges: This binds Parliament: it sets the dates of plenary sittings for the whole session.
It provides at most 60 sitting days, 3 in each of 20 weeks.
readings.insight: The signed text is dated 16 June 2021, the day after the session opened, while Parliament's index lists it as adopted on 17 June 2021. Every week on the calendar falls in the third and fourth weeks of the month, as the rules require.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament condemns violence by Israeli forces against Palestinians, targeting civilians including women and children, and the desecration of the Al Aqsa Mosque during Ramadhan, and urges world leaders to act for an immediate end to the hostilities.

Authored by MP Paisalin P. Tago. Adopted on 17 June 2021.
readings.whyProposed: The resolution cites the Amnesty International Report 2020-2021: Israeli forces killed 31 Palestinians, including 9 children, in the Occupied Palestinian Territories, kept the blockade on Gaza and held hundreds in administrative detention without charge. It cites the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs for the demolition of 848 Palestinian homes and livelihood structures in the West Bank, displacing 996 people. In the last days of Ramadhan, it says, more than 220 civilians were injured on the first night of violence at the Al Aqsa Mosque and some 121 on the second. It quotes Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan at length as an example for Muslim leaders.
whoIsAffected: Palestinian civilians, on whose behalf Parliament speaks.
World leaders, whom the resolution calls on to act.
whatChanges: The resolution is a statement of Parliament's position; it binds no one.
It names no recipient and orders no copy sent to any government, embassy or international body.
readings.insight: Unlike most resolutions of the period, this one has no clause forwarding it to anyone, so its call to world leaders reaches them only if it is published. Parliament returned to the subject in Resolution 407 (October 2023), which condemned violence against Palestinians and called for a ceasefire, and in Resolution 419 (December 2023).

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament recognizes and commends the role and contributions of Reverend Fr. Eliseo R. Mercado Jr., OMI, a longtime Mindanao peace advocate, to peace and development in the Bangsamoro.

A copy goes to the Oblates of Mary Immaculate Philippine Province.

Authored by MP Susana S. Anayatin. Adopted on 17 June 2021.
readings.whyProposed: Fr. Mercado died on 23 May 2021, aged 72. The resolution lists his record: President of Notre Dame University in Cotabato City from 1992 to 2002, where he set up the Institute of Peace Education; founder of the Kusog Mindanaw coalition in 1994; chair of the independent ceasefire monitoring committee of the Government and the MILF; floor leader of the consultative assembly of the Southern Philippines Council for Peace and Development; a broker of the 2000 ceasefire between the Estrada administration and the MILF; and, from 17 November 2014 until his death, a Vice-Chairman of the 6th Infantry Division's Kampilan Multi-Sector Advisory Board. It also cites 3 presidential citations for his peace work.
whoIsAffected: The Oblates of Mary Immaculate, his congregation.
The peace-building community in Mindanao.
whatChanges: The resolution is a tribute; it binds no one.
A copy is sent to the Oblates of Mary Immaculate Philippine Province.
readings.insight: Parliament adopted 2 resolutions for Fr. Mercado on the same day: this commendation and Resolution 126, a condolence. The 2 texts differ slightly on his studies; this one gives a master's in theology and missiology, Resolution 126 a master's in theology and philosophy.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament expresses its profound sympathy and sincere condolences on the death of Fr. Eliseo "Jun" Mercado on 23 May 2021, and honors his contributions to the Bangsamoro people's cause for genuine autonomy.

Copies go to his congregation, the Oblates of Mary Immaculate in Cotabato City, and are to be circulated among media outlets in the region.

Authored by MP Amilbahar S. Mawallil and MP Baintan A. Ampatuan. Adopted on 17 June 2021.
readings.whyProposed: Fr. Mercado, 72, died of cardiac arrest at 3:20 pm on 23 May 2021 at the Cotabato Regional and Medical Center, a day after testing negative for COVID-19, as he was being moved to intensive care to finish his recovery. The resolution recalls his years as parish priest in Datu Piang, his presidency of Notre Dame University from 1992 to 2002, his work in the consultative assembly of the Southern Philippines Council for Peace and Development and on the Government-MILF ceasefire committee, his chairmanship of NAMFREL in the ARMM from 2004, and his public support for the Bangsamoro Organic Law, which earned him the name "a Catholic with a passion for Islam."
whoIsAffected: The family and congregation of Fr. Mercado.
whatChanges: The resolution is a condolence; it binds no one.
Copies go to the Oblates of Mary Immaculate in Cotabato City and to media outlets in the region.
readings.insight: This is the second resolution for Fr. Mercado adopted on 17 June 2021, alongside Resolution 125's commendation. It was adopted 25 days after his death.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament expresses its profound sympathy and sincere condolences on the death of Dr. Filemon G. Romero, former Chancellor of Mindanao State University Tawi-Tawi, and honors his work as an academic and a scientist in environmental and marine sciences.

The resolution goes to his family and is to be circulated among media outlets in the region.

Authored by MP Amilbahar S. Mawallil, MP Baintan A. Ampatuan, MP Al-Syed A. Sali and MP Eddie M. Alih. Adopted on 22 June 2021.
readings.whyProposed: Dr. Romero died on the morning of 16 May 2021 aboard a commercial boat from Bongao to Zamboanga City, after his oxygen level kept falling; he later tested positive for COVID-19. Born on the island of Mapun, he taught for more than 40 years, earned a Master of Arts in Physics from MSU Marawi in 1971, and studied physical oceanography and then a doctorate in environmental science at UP Diliman. He was the first Chancellor of MSU Tawi-Tawi, from 1989 to 1994, helped found its Institute of Oceanography and Environmental Science, managed World Wildlife Fund projects in Tawi-Tawi and was known locally as "Mr. Environment" for his reef and marine resource work.
whoIsAffected: The family of Dr. Romero.
The MSU Tawi-Tawi community.
whatChanges: The resolution is a condolence; it binds no one.
Copies go to his family and to media outlets in the region.
readings.insight: Adopted 37 days after his death. MP Mawallil and MP Ampatuan had also authored Resolution 126, the condolence for Fr. Mercado, 5 days earlier.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament encourages all newly appointed employees of the Bangsamoro Government to take their Oath of Moral Governance before the Office of the Wali.

Copies go to the Office of the Wali and to all Ministries.

Authored by MP Rasol Y. Mitmug Jr. and 6 others. Adopted on 23 June 2021.
readings.whyProposed: The Bangsamoro Administrative Code (Bangsamoro Autonomy Act No. 13) already requires every public officer and employee to take an oath of office and makes the Oath of Moral Governance mandatory; the resolution quotes it in full. The Organic Law makes the Wali the ceremonial head of government, with power to administer oaths to the Chief Minister and Members of Parliament. The authors note that thousands of applicants had been screened through the Bangsamoro Job Portal and want the Wali's office to administer the moral governance oath to the new hires.
whoIsAffected: Newly appointed Bangsamoro Government employees.
The Office of the Wali, which would administer the oaths.
implementedBy: Office of the Wali
All Ministries of the Bangsamoro Government
whatChanges: Taking the oath is already mandatory under the Administrative Code; this resolution only encourages that it be taken before the Wali's office.
It sets no procedure, schedule or deadline and binds no employee.
readings.insight: The resolution adds a venue, not a duty: the oath itself was already required by law. It does not say how one ceremonial office would administer oaths to the thousands of new hires the resolution itself describes.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament supports the actions of the Moro members of Congress who stood on behalf of the Bangsamoro over the warrantless arrests of Muslims outside the region. It says the Bangsamoro Human Rights Commission should coordinate with the national Commission on Human Rights on the matter.

A copy goes to the Bangsamoro Human Rights Commission.

Authored by MP Rasol Y. Mitmug Jr. Adopted on 24 June 2021.
readings.whyProposed: On 17 February, agents of the National Intelligence Coordinating Agency and the National Capital Region Police Office, helped by local police, arrested 11 people without warrant at a construction site in Bacoor City, Cavite, reportedly asking which of them were Muslims during a check for Abu Sayyaf members. 7 were from Basilan. Their families said they had not been told where they were held. Deputy Speaker Mujiv S. Hataman called the arrests kidnapping in a privilege speech on 3 March, and he and other Moro congressmen filed resolutions for a probe. The text recalls a similar 2020 raid in Manila and cites the Administrative Code's provision allowing joint investigations with the national Commission on Human Rights when Bangsamoro are involved outside the region.
whoIsAffected: The 11 people arrested in Bacoor and their families.
Bangsamoro living outside the region.
implementedBy: Bangsamoro Human Rights Commission
Commission on Human Rights
whatChanges: The resolution expresses support; it binds no national office.
It asks the Bangsamoro Human Rights Commission to coordinate with the national commission, using the joint-investigation provision of the Administrative Code.
readings.insight: The WHEREAS clauses give the arrest and speech dates without a year, and the resolution was adopted about 4 months after the arrests. It sets no deadline or reporting duty for the Human Rights Commission. Parliament had raised killings of Moros outside the region before, in Resolution 80 (July 2020) on Polomolok and Tupi, South Cotabato.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament directs the Bangsamoro Darul-Ifta to issue a fatwa on what makes up halal conduct of public officials and employees, as khalifa, in the Bangsamoro Government under moral governance.

A copy goes to the Darul-Ifta.

Authored by MP Abdullah B. Hashim. Adopted on 24 June 2021.
readings.whyProposed: The Organic Law and the Administrative Code speak of halal only in the regulation and certification of food and non-food products. The author argues halal should also cover how public servants behave, since the Administrative Code treats public office as a sacred public trust and defines officials as khalifa, stewards of Allah on earth. The Code gives the Darul-Ifta power to issue fatwa across the whole of Islamic jurisprudence. The resolution says the fatwa could be issued in Filipino and the region's other major languages, and that Parliament could later codify it as a code of conduct.
whoIsAffected: Officials and employees of the Bangsamoro Government.
The Bangsamoro Darul-Ifta.
implementedBy: Bangsamoro Darul-Ifta
whatChanges: The Darul-Ifta is part of the Bangsamoro Government, so this is a direction to a regional body rather than a plea to an outside office.
It sets no deadline. A fatwa would not itself bind employees unless Parliament later writes it into law, as the text suggests.
readings.insight: This was Parliament's second direction to the Darul-Ifta in 3 months, after Resolution 111 (March 2021) on a unified Ramadan moon sighting. The idea of codifying the fatwa as a code of conduct appears only in a WHEREAS clause, not in what Parliament resolved.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament expresses its deepest gratitude and unequivocal support for Senate Bill No. 2081 and House Bill No. 8249, both declaring 1 February of every year as National Hijab Day and promoting understanding of the Muslim tradition of wearing the hijab.

Copies go to the Senate through Senate President Vicente Sotto III and to the House through Speaker Lord Allan Jay Velasco, with copies to the Chief Minister and the Bangsamoro Women Commission.

Authored by MP Bainon G. Karon. Adopted on 24 June 2021.
readings.whyProposed: The House passed House Bill No. 8249 unanimously on 26 January 2021; Senate Bill No. 2081 was filed by Senator Juan Miguel F. Zubiri. 1 February has been World Hijab Day since 2013. The resolution says a national day would explain the hijab as a way of life and sign of devotion, not something to fear, and recognize Muslim women's role in nation-building. The Bangsamoro Women Commission had been invited as a resource speaker for the Senate Committee on Cultural Communities' technical working group meeting on 6 July 2021.
whoIsAffected: Muslim women who wear the hijab.
Congress, whose bills the resolution backs.
implementedBy: Senate of the Philippines
House of Representatives
Office of the Chief Minister
Bangsamoro Women Commission
whatChanges: The resolution is an expression of support; it binds no one.
Copies go to both chambers of Congress, the Chief Minister and the Women Commission.
readings.insight: The bills appear not to have become law in that Congress: in January 2023 Parliament adopted Resolution 313 supporting new bills with the same purpose, Senate Bill No. 1272 and House Bill No. 5693. The footer shows this resolution consolidated 3 proposed resolutions, Nos. 384, 407 and 452.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament urges the Bangsamoro Government, through the Ministry of Health, working closely with local governments, to buy cold storage facilities, including ultra-low-temperature freezers, so the region can receive and properly store any brand of COVID-19 vaccine for an efficient rollout.

A copy goes to the Ministry of Health.

Authored by MP Mussolini S. Lidasan. Adopted on 24 June 2021.
readings.whyProposed: The national government allocated vaccines to the region by the number of people registered, and the Ministry of Health was barred from buying vaccines on its own, although it had been allocated ₱500,000,000 for vaccines on top of ₱380,000,000 for its COVID-19 Response Plan. More vaccines were expected, but the region lacked cold storage. COVID-19 vaccines were being stored with regular vaccines, including those for infant immunization, putting both at risk. The text says the Ministry should coordinate with the Ministry of the Interior and Local Government and local governments on the purchases.
whoIsAffected: Residents waiting for COVID-19 vaccination.
Infants and children whose regular vaccines shared the same storage.
implementedBy: Ministry of Health
Local government units

funding.detail: The resolution appropriates nothing. It notes that the Ministry of Health had ₱500,000,000 for vaccine purchases, besides ₱380,000,000 for its COVID-19 Response Plan, but names no amount or source for the freezers.

whatChanges: The resolution is a request to the Ministry of Health; it sets no number of units, budget or deadline.
A copy is sent to the Ministry of Health.
readings.insight: The resolution records that ₱500,000,000 had been set aside for vaccines the Ministry was not allowed to buy, but it does not ask for that money to be used on freezers or say what the freezers would cost. The same author filed Resolution 133, adopted the same day, on the low number of people registering for vaccination; together they address both ends of the supply problem. Parliament had already asked the Ministry for its vaccine distribution plan in Resolution 107 (February 2021).

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament urges the Bangsamoro Government, through the Bangsamoro Inter-Agency Task Force on COVID-19, to work closely with local governments on a region-wide, grassroots information campaign to persuade people to register for and receive COVID-19 vaccination.

Copies go to the Task Force, the Ministry of the Interior and Local Government and the Ministry of Health.

Authored by MP Mussolini S. Lidasan. Adopted on 24 June 2021.
readings.whyProposed: At the time of drafting, about 42,000 people, or 1% of the region's roughly 3.8 million, had registered for or received the vaccine, according to the Ministry of Health. Because the national government allocated doses by the number of registrants, low registration meant fewer vaccines for the region. The text proposes a barangay-level information campaign to dispel fears and rumors, possibly with an assistance program through the Ministry of Social Services and Development for those who complete both doses.
whoIsAffected: Residents of the region who had not registered for vaccination.
Local governments, asked to carry the campaign to barangays.
implementedBy: Bangsamoro Inter-Agency Task Force on COVID-19
Local government units
Ministry of the Interior and Local Government
Ministry of Health
whatChanges: The resolution is a request; it sets no target, budget or deadline.
Copies go to the Task Force, the Interior and Local Government ministry and the Health ministry.
readings.insight: The incentive idea, assistance for people who complete 2 doses, appears only in a WHEREAS clause, not in the resolved clauses. It came back 8 months later in Resolution 212 (February 2022), which urged the Government of the Day to devise incentives for the vaccine-hesitant. Parliament had earlier backed the vaccination plans and called for information campaigns in Resolution 113 (March 2021).

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament expresses its sincerest sympathies and condolences on the death of former President Benigno Simeon C. Aquino III, the 15th President of the Philippines, and posthumously recognizes his contributions to peace and development in the Bangsamoro. It recommends that national and regional flags in the region fly at half-mast for 5 days in his honor.

The resolution is to be presented to his family.

Authored by MP Baintan A. Ampatuan and 18 others. Adopted on 24 June 2021.
readings.whyProposed: Aquino died on 24 June 2021, aged 61. The resolution credits his administration with making the Bangsamoro peace agenda a national priority: the Framework Agreement on the Bangsamoro was signed on his watch, as was the Comprehensive Agreement on the Bangsamoro, which ended 17 years of negotiations with the MILF, and in 2014 he submitted the draft Bangsamoro Basic Law to Congress. It calls him the Chief Executive who laid the foundations of the current Bangsamoro government.
whoIsAffected: The family of former President Aquino.
Offices in the region asked to lower flags.
whatChanges: The resolution is a condolence; it binds no one.
The half-mast clause is a recommendation and names no office to carry it out.
readings.insight: Adopted on the day Aquino died, with 19 principal authors. The footer shows it consolidated 3 proposed resolutions, Nos. 456, 458 and 459.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament expresses its sentiment and consensus to recognize and commend Secretary Abdullah D. Mama-o as an exemplar of Muslim Filipino leadership and of Islamic diplomacy.

Copies go to the Office of the President and to Secretary Mama-o's office in Malacañang.

Authored by MP Ziaur-Rahman A. Adiong and 13 others. Adopted on 13 July 2021.
readings.whyProposed: Secretary Mama-o was then Presidential Adviser on Overseas Filipino Workers and the President's Special Envoy to Kuwait, described as the only Bangsamoro Muslim with Cabinet rank. The resolution lists his missions: helping repatriate most of an estimated 11,000 overseas workers stranded in Saudi Arabia in 2016, including persuading a group of 300 to return home; mediating the 2 Philippines-Kuwait crises after the killings of domestic workers Joanna Demafelis and Jeanelyn Villavende; securing in 2019 the return from Libya of 7 seamen of the M/T Levante and 3 kidnapped water engineers, who arrived in Manila on 18 May 2019; pressing for legal defense for 7 Muslim Filipinos detained in Qatar; gathering assurances from 7 Middle East governments on evacuating Filipinos during the 2020 US-Iran crisis; and helping secure a UAE pardon for 51 Filipino convicts.
whoIsAffected: Secretary Abdullah D. Mama-o.
whatChanges: The resolution is a commendation; it creates no award and binds no one.
Copies go to the Office of the President and to Secretary Mama-o.
readings.insight: Despite the title's reference to a grant of an award, the resolution sets up no award, criteria or ceremony; the commendation is the resolution itself. Its account of the missions comes only from its own WHEREAS clauses, which cite no source.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament recognizes the contributions of Bangsamoro Director-General Suharto A. Abas to the Bangsamoro people and government and expresses deep sympathy to his family for his passing.

Copies go to his wife and family.

Authored by MP Rasol Y. Mitmug Jr. and 6 others. Adopted on 13 July 2021.
readings.whyProposed: Suharto "Tho" Aron Abas died on 28 June 2021, survived by his wife, Fatima Mending, and their children. He had been active in the Bangsamoro Student League, managed the ARMM Act for Peace program under the UN Development Programme, and was a campaigns and policy adviser at Oxfam Philippines. As Director-General at the Ministry of Science and Technology he helped build the Bangsamoro Science and Technology Research Council.
whoIsAffected: The family of Suharto A. Abas.
The Ministry of Science and Technology, where he served.
whatChanges: The resolution is a tribute and condolence; it binds no one.
Copies go to his wife and family.
readings.insight: Adopted 15 days after his death, on the same day as Resolution 135's commendation of Secretary Mama-o.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament requests the Department of Budget and Management (DBM) to inform the Bangsamoro Government how the Supreme Court's Mandanas ruling affects the Internal Revenue Allotment of local governments in the region.

A copy goes to the DBM.

Authored by MP Baintan A. Ampatuan, MP Laisa M. Alamia and MP Amilbahar S. Mawallil. Adopted on 15 July 2021.
readings.whyProposed: In Mandanas v. Ochoa (G.R. No. 199802, 3 July 2018), the Supreme Court held that local governments' just share must be computed from all national taxes, not only national internal revenue taxes, so customs duties and other national taxes must be included. The ruling listed the taxes in the base, including, for the ARMM, the portions left after the ARMM's own shares under R.A. No. 9054 (50% of VAT and 70% of other national taxes collected there). The Organic Law now sets a different split for taxes collected in the region: 75% to the Bangsamoro Government, inclusive of its local governments' shares, and 25% to the National Government, with that 25% also going to the region for the first 10 years. The authors say the change in the base will inevitably affect the allotments of the region's local governments, and want the DBM to explain how.
whoIsAffected: Local government units in the region, whose allotments depend on how the base is computed.
The Bangsamoro Government, which shares national taxes with its local governments.
implementedBy: Department of Budget and Management
whatChanges: The resolution is a request for information; the DBM has no duty to answer it.
It sets no deadline and asks for the answer to go to the Bangsamoro Government, not to Parliament.
readings.insight: The resolution gives no figure for what the region's local governments stood to gain or lose, which is the question it puts to the DBM. It also leaves out which office in the Bangsamoro Government should receive the DBM's reply.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament directs the Ministry of the Interior and Local Government to begin drafting the implementing rules and regulations of Muslim Mindanao Autonomy Act No. 317, the Bangsamoro Public Cemetery Act of 2014. The ministry is to consult closely with local governments, the Ministry of Environment, Natural Resources and Energy and the Ministry of Health in drafting them.

Copies go to the 3 ministries.

Authored by MP Khadafeh G. Mangudadatu and 7 others. Adopted on 15 July 2021.
readings.whyProposed: MMA Act No. 317, passed by the former Regional Legislative Assembly, requires public cemeteries to be set up, maintained and run in the region in line with the different religious rites and cultural practices, with private-sector participation and compliance with health and sanitation rules. Its Section 8 named the former DILG-ARMM as lead agency and tasked it with drafting the rules, but none were issued, so the law was never fully carried out. The authors stress the need for a decent public cemetery in every local government.
whoIsAffected: Families in the region who need public burial grounds.
Local governments, which would establish and run the cemeteries.
implementedBy: Ministry of the Interior and Local Government
Ministry of Environment, Natural Resources and Energy
Ministry of Health
Local government units
whatChanges: The resolution directs a Bangsamoro ministry, which took over the role the law gave the former DILG-ARMM, to start the rules; it sets no deadline.
Copies go to the Interior, Environment and Health ministries.
readings.insight: By the resolution's own account, a 2014 law had gone 7 years without implementing rules. Parliament later moved toward replacing it with its own law: Bill No. 67, filed on 27 September 2022, and Bill No. 371, filed on 24 June 2025, both require local governments to set aside land for public cemeteries. Both were still at committee stage when Parliament's index was last updated in July 2025.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament expresses its profound sympathy and sincere condolences on the death of MP Aleem Mohammad Zainoden P. Bato.

The resolution goes to his family.

Authored by MP Maisara Dandamun Latiph. Adopted on 17 August 2021.
readings.whyProposed: MP Bato died on 15 August 2021. He was among the young Bangsamoro students at Al-Azhar University who founded the movement that led to the Bangsamoro struggle, a Meranao member of the MILF Central Committee and head of its Shura Council, and a Member of Parliament since March 2019.
whoIsAffected: The family of MP Bato.
His colleagues in Parliament and the MILF.
whatChanges: The resolution is a condolence; it binds no one.
A copy goes to his family.
readings.insight: Parliament adopted 3 resolutions on MP Bato's death on the same day: this one, Resolution 140 and Resolution 141. This one says he had been a Member since March 2019; Resolution 141 says he took his oath on 22 February 2019.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament expresses its deepest condolences and profound sympathy to the family of MP Aleem Mohammad Zainoden P. Bato on his death.

The resolution goes to his family.

Authored by MP Ziaur-Rahman A. Adiong and MP Anna Tarhata S. Basman. Adopted on 17 August 2021.
readings.whyProposed: MP Bato, from Piagapo, Lanao del Sur, was a pioneering Bangsamoro scholar and Al-Azhar graduate alongside the late MILF founder Ustadz Salamat Hashim. He was a member of the MILF Central Committee and head of its Shura Council, an active member of Ansar El Islam, the organization founded by the late Senator Ahmad Domocao A. Alonto, and was appointed to the BTA in 2019. He died on 15 August 2021 in his hometown in Lanao del Sur.
whoIsAffected: The family of MP Bato.
whatChanges: The resolution is a condolence; it binds no one.
A copy goes to his family.
readings.insight: One of 3 resolutions on MP Bato's death adopted on 17 August 2021, with Resolutions 139 and 141. This text says he died in his hometown in Lanao del Sur, which it gives as Piagapo; Resolution 141 says he died in Marawi City.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament recognizes the contribution of MP Mohammad Zainoden P. Bato to the Bangsamoro Government as one of the prime movers of the Bangsamoro cause and expresses profound sympathy and sincere condolences to his family.

The resolution is to be presented to his family.

Authored by MP Ali B. Solaiman and 10 others. Adopted on 17 August 2021.
readings.whyProposed: MP Bato, a Meranao leader from Piagapo, Lanao del Sur, was appointed by President Duterte and took his oath as a BTA Member on 22 February 2019. A senior MILF Central Committee member and chair of its Majlis As-Shura, he had been among the first Muslim Filipino students at Al-Azhar with the late Chairman Hashim Salamat, and was president of Mahad Marawi Al-Islamia. In Parliament he sat on the Special Committee for Marawi City and the committees on public works, education, environment and local government. He died on 15 August 2021 in Marawi City.
whoIsAffected: The family of MP Bato.
whatChanges: The resolution is a tribute and condolence; it binds no one.
It is to be presented to his family.
readings.insight: The third resolution on MP Bato's death adopted on 17 August 2021, with 11 principal authors. It is the only one of the 3 to list his committee work.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament urges the avoidance of profanity, especially words that degrade women, and calls for refraining from foul language as against the law and the law of God. It asks the Office of the Chief Minister to direct Cabinet members to take responsibility for awareness and implementation of the resolution.

A copy goes to Chief Minister Ahod B. Ebrahim.

Authored by MP Punduma B. Sani. Adopted on 17 August 2021.
readings.whyProposed: The Code of Conduct for public officials (R.A. No. 6713) sets a high standard of ethics and requires officials to refrain from acts contrary to good morals and customs; violations can bring a fine of up to 6 months' salary, suspension of up to 1 year, or removal. The resolution says Bangsamoro culture treats profanity as taboo, especially the curse that insults mothers, and quotes the Prophet Muhammad against cursing. It ties the request to the Bangsamoro Government's focus on moral governance.
whoIsAffected: Public officials and employees of the Bangsamoro Government.
Women, at whom degrading curses are aimed.
implementedBy: Office of the Chief Minister
Members of the Cabinet
whatChanges: The resolution creates no offense or penalty; the R.A. No. 6713 penalties it cites already apply to violations of that law.
It asks the Chief Minister to have the Cabinet carry an awareness effort, with no deadline.
readings.insight: The footer carries proposed resolution No. 226, while the other resolutions adopted in August 2021 came from proposals numbered in the 470s to 490s, so this one appears to have waited much longer before adoption. The text names no rule or policy that the Cabinet should issue.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament requests telecommunication companies to upgrade their wireless and wired signals and install more cell sites to improve connectivity in the region.

Copies go to the Ministry of Transportation and Communications, PLDT, Globe Telecom and DITO Telecommunity.

Authored by MP Narciso Co Yu Ekey and 8 others. Adopted on 24 August 2021.
readings.whyProposed: The Organic Law lets the Bangsamoro Government grant regional franchises to telecom utilities whose frequencies and main offices are in the region and to exercise quasi-judicial powers over telecom operations under rules Parliament sets. The Public Telecommunications Policy Act calls for universal, affordable service with priority for unserved areas. The pandemic raised demand for internet service, and the authors say new cell sites would improve signal in far-flung areas and create jobs. They also say local governments should ease permit requirements for cell towers.
whoIsAffected: Internet and mobile users in the region, especially in remote areas.
Telecom companies operating in the region.
implementedBy: PLDT
Globe Telecom
DITO Telecommunity
Ministry of Transportation and Communications
whatChanges: The resolution is a request to private companies; it binds none of them.
Copies go to the transport and communications ministry and the 3 telcos.
readings.insight: The text cites the region's own franchising and quasi-judicial powers over telecoms but uses neither; it only asks. Its call for local governments to ease cell tower permits appears in a WHEREAS clause, and no local government or local government ministry is sent a copy.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament commends Sergeant Hidilyn Francisco Diaz as the first Mindanaoan Filipino to win an Olympic gold medal since the Philippines first joined the Games in 1924, at the Tokyo 2020 Olympics.

A copy goes to Diaz.

Authored by MP Susana S. Anayatin. Adopted on 24 August 2021.
readings.whyProposed: On 26 July 2021 Diaz, a 30-year-old from Zamboanga City, won gold in the women's 55kg weightlifting event in Tokyo. For 97 years the country's best Olympic results had been silver medals by boxers Anthony Villanueva in 1964 and Mansueto Velasco Jr. in 1996 and a bronze by swimmer Teofilo Yldefonso in 1928. The resolution cites the Constitution's call to promote sports and the Organic Law's duty to promote youth fitness through sports, and hopes her win will draw young people in the region to sports.
whoIsAffected: Hidilyn Diaz.
Young athletes in the region.
whatChanges: The resolution is a commendation; it binds no one.
A copy goes to Diaz.
readings.insight: The text says Diaz won after lifting 123kg; Resolution 148, adopted 2 days later, gives her winning total as 224 kilograms. Parliament commended her twice in 3 days: here alone and in Resolution 148 with the 3 other Tokyo medalists. The footer shows this resolution merged proposed resolutions Nos. 476 and 477.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament requests the Philippine National Police and the Department of Justice to speed up the investigation of the kidnapping and murder of Nadia Casar and bring those responsible to justice.

The resolution is forwarded to all concerned for immediate action.

Authored by MP Ziaur-Rahman A. Adiong. Adopted on 24 August 2021, by the date on the signed text.
readings.whyProposed: On 20 July 2021 Nadia Casar, a Bangsamoro businesswoman, and the Grab driver she had hired were abducted by armed men in Nueva Ecija; the driver was released after being robbed. On 1 August 2021 her burned remains were found in a shallow grave in Palayan City. The driver identified 5 policemen and 2 civilians as suspects. PNP Chief Gen. Guillermo Eleazar ordered summary dismissal proceedings against the 5 policemen and directed the Anti-Kidnapping Group to arrest the suspects still at large. The resolution says the case outraged the region because the suspects are sworn to protect civilians.
whoIsAffected: The family of Nadia Casar.
Bangsamoro living and working outside the region.
implementedBy: Philippine National Police
Department of Justice
whatChanges: The resolution is a request to national agencies; it binds neither.
It is sent "to all concerned" without naming the offices.
readings.insight: The signed text is dated 24 August 2021; Parliament's index lists it as adopted on 17 August 2021. The same author's Resolution 146, adopted the same day, condemns the killing and states that all suspects had already been charged before the Department of Justice, while this text describes some suspects as still at large.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament condemns in the strongest terms the abduction and killing of Nadia Casar, a Bangsamoro businesswoman, in Nueva Ecija.

The resolution is forwarded to the concerned agencies for immediate action. A WHEREAS clause also states that the Bangsamoro Human Rights Commission is directed to give legal assistance to the Casar family.

Authored by MP Ziaur-Rahman A. Adiong. Adopted on 24 August 2021, by the date on the signed text.
readings.whyProposed: Casar and the ride-hailing driver she hired were seized by 5 armed men on 20 July 2021 on the way to a delivery in Sta. Rosa, Nueva Ecija; the driver was released, robbed, at 3:00 a.m. the next day. Her burned body was found in a shallow grave in Palayan City at about 2:30 a.m. on 1 August 2021. The resolution names 5 police officers from stations in Nueva Ecija and 2 civilians identified as the perpetrators, and says the PNP chief ordered the policemen's dismissal and all suspects were charged before the Department of Justice. It calls for reforms in the security sector, notes that the National Police Commission supervises the PNP, and warns that an unresolved case would deepen the injustice felt by minorities.
whoIsAffected: The family of Nadia Casar.
Bangsamoro living and working outside the region.
implementedBy: Bangsamoro Human Rights Commission
Concerned national agencies
whatChanges: The condemnation binds no one.
The direction to the Bangsamoro Human Rights Commission sits in a WHEREAS clause, not a RESOLVED clause, so its force is unclear.
readings.insight: The only concrete step in the text, legal aid to the family from the Bangsamoro Human Rights Commission, is placed among the reasons rather than in what Parliament resolved. The signed text is dated 24 August 2021, while Parliament's index lists 17 August 2021. It is a companion to Resolution 145, from the same author, which asks the PNP and the Justice Department to speed up the investigation.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament calls on the Bangsamoro Government to consider setting up drug treatment and rehabilitation centers in strategic areas of the region.

Copies go to Chief Minister Ahod B. Ebrahim and the Ministry of Health.

Authored by MP Maisara Dandamun Latiph. Adopted on 26 August 2021.
readings.whyProposed: The resolution says the Bangsamoro Government has no rehabilitation center in any province or city of the region, including the new areas. It sets out the benefits of structured treatment and notes that the Philippine Drug Enforcement Agency's community-based Balay Silangan program serves only drug personalities who are not users and are not eligible for medical treatment, leaving users who need treatment without a regional facility.
whoIsAffected: People who use drugs and need treatment, and their families.
Communities affected by drug use.
implementedBy: Office of the Chief Minister
Ministry of Health
whatChanges: The resolution asks the government to consider building centers; it sets no number, site, budget or deadline.
Copies go to the Chief Minister and the Ministry of Health.
readings.insight: Parliament later took the idea up as legislation but has not enacted it: Bills No. 197 (filed 16 June 2023) and No. 230 (filed 18 July 2023) are listed at first reading, and Bill No. 402, filed on 14 October 2025 to put a treatment center in every province, was at committee stage when the index was last updated in December 2025.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament extends its highest commendation to Olympians Hidilyn Diaz, Nesthy Petecio, Carlo Paalam and Eumir Marcial for bringing pride and honor to the country at the Tokyo 2020 Summer Olympics.

Copies go to the Philippine Sports Commission and the Philippine Olympic Committee.

Authored by MP Ziaur-Rahman A. Adiong, MP Raissa H. Jajurie, MP Ubaida C. Pacasem, MP Anna Tarhata S. Basman, MP Eddie M. Alih and MP Baintan A. Ampatuan. Adopted on 26 August 2021.
readings.whyProposed: 19 Filipino athletes competed in Tokyo from 23 July to 8 August 2021 and brought home 4 medals, 1 gold, 2 silver and 1 bronze, surpassing the record set at the 1932 Los Angeles Olympics. Diaz of Zamboanga City won the first-ever gold for the country on 26 July with an Olympic-record total of 224 kilograms in the women's 55kg weightlifting class. Petecio of Santa Cruz, Davao del Sur won silver in women's featherweight boxing on 3 August, Marcial of Zamboanga City bronze in men's middleweight boxing on 5 August, and Paalam of Bukidnon silver in men's flyweight boxing on 7 August.
whoIsAffected: The 4 Tokyo medalists.
whatChanges: The resolution is a commendation; it binds no one.
Copies go to the Philippine Sports Commission and the Philippine Olympic Committee.
readings.insight: All 4 medalists are from Mindanao, though none from the region by the text's own account. Diaz was commended alone 2 days earlier, in Resolution 144. Parliament honored Olympians again in Resolution 486 (August 2024), for the Paris medalists.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament commemorates the 60th founding anniversary of Mindanao State University and commends its contributions to the region and its people.

Copies go to MSU's 8 campuses and to 3 former CHED-supervised institutions now integrated into the MSU system: Lanao National College of Arts and Trade, Lanao Norte Agricultural College and Maigo School of Arts and Trade.

Authored by MP Rasol Y. Mitmug Jr. and MP Eddie M. Alih. Adopted on 26 August 2021.
readings.whyProposed: MSU was founded on 1 September 1961 in Marawi under R.A. No. 1387, as amended by R.A. No. 3791, on the initiative of the late Senator Ahmad Domocao Alonto, to integrate the Muslim population into national life and train technical manpower for Mindanao, Sulu and Palawan. It began with 282 college students and 12 faculty and now serves over 69,000 students with nearly 3,100 faculty across 8 campuses, with 16 colleges offering 248 courses. The Organic Law directs the National Government to continue supporting and strengthening the MSU system.
whoIsAffected: Mindanao State University, its students and staff.
whatChanges: The resolution is a commemoration; it binds no one.
Copies go to MSU's 8 campuses and 3 integrated colleges.
readings.insight: Adopted 6 days before the anniversary date. MSU campuses and units have been commended in many later resolutions, including Resolutions 273, 337, 461, 466 and 501.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament commends the Senate for steering Senate Bill No. 2214 toward enactment and approving it on second reading. The bill resets the first regular election in the region to 2025.

A copy goes to the Senate through Senate President Vicente C. Sotto III.

Authored by MP Mohagher M. Iqbal and MP Raissa H. Jajurie. Adopted on 26 August 2021.
readings.whyProposed: The Organic Law set the first regional election for 2022. The resolution says the pandemic, local security threats and resource shortfalls slowed the Bangsamoro Government's programs and Parliament's legislation. On 17 November 2020 Parliament asked Congress, in Resolution 93, to extend the transition to 30 June 2025. Senators Aquilino Pimentel III and Richard Gordon filed Senate Bills No. 2019 and No. 2025 in January 2021; the Committee on Local Government, chaired by Senator Francis Tolentino, consolidated them on 20 May 2021 into Senate Bill No. 2214, which the Senate approved on second reading on 25 August 2021.
whoIsAffected: The Bangsamoro Transition Authority, whose term the bill would extend.
Voters in the region, whose first regional election would move to 2025.
whatChanges: The resolution is a commendation; it binds no one.
A copy goes to the Senate.
readings.insight: Adopted the day after the Senate's second-reading vote. Parliament followed each step: Resolution 154 (15 September 2021) commended the third-reading approval, and Resolution 162 (16 September 2021) asked for a bicameral conference to reconcile the bill with House Bill No. 10121. The extension to 2025 was enacted as Republic Act No. 11593.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament expresses its sympathy and condolences on the death of Tausug historian Dr. Samuel Kong Tan and recognizes his work in documenting the history of the Bangsamoro and Mindanao. A copy goes to his family.

Authored by MP Amilbahar S. Mawallil. Adopted on 15 February 2022.
readings.whyProposed: Dr. Tan died on 6 January 2022 at 88. Born in Siasi, Sulu on 30 December 1933 to Chinese-Tausug-Sama parents, he wrote more than 20 books, chaired the University of the Philippines Department of History, and headed the National Historical Institute. His books include The Muslim Armed Struggle in the Philippines, 1900-1941 (1973), Internationalization of the Bangsamoro Struggle (1993) and Surat Sug: Letters of the Sultanate of Sulu (2005).
whoIsAffected: The family of Dr. Samuel Kong Tan.
whatChanges: A copy goes to the family. Nothing else follows from it.
readings.insight: Adopted 40 days after his death. The text lists 10 awards and grants he received, from a Rockefeller Foundation Fellowship (1970-1973) to a lifetime achievement award from the Philippine National Historical Society.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament urges the Government of the Day to devise strategies and an incentives mechanism to get vaccine-hesitant people in the Bangsamoro region vaccinated against COVID-19. Copies go to Chief Minister Ahod B. Ebrahim and the Ministry of Health.

Authored by MP Baintan A. Ampatuan. Adopted on 16 February 2022.
readings.whyProposed: As of 23 January 2022, the region ranked last among Philippine regions in vaccines given: 25.22% of the population fully vaccinated and 26.59% partially, against over 50% in the other regions. Herd immunity is put at 70% to 85% vaccinated. The authors cite incentives used elsewhere, such as weekly car draws in Moscow and, in Manila, a weekly 25-kilogram sack of rice for 20 vaccinated residents of Sucat.
whoIsAffected: Unvaccinated and undecided residents of the region.
The Ministry of Health and local governments that run vaccination drives.
implementedBy: Office of the Chief Minister
Ministry of Health
whatChanges: A request to the executive; it names no incentive, amount or deadline.
readings.insight: Vaccination was a recurring subject. Resolution 107 (February 2021) directed the Ministry of Health to report on its vaccine distribution plan, and Resolution 113 (March 2021) backed the national and regional vaccination plans. Almost a year later this resolution still finds the region last in coverage. It sets no target and asks for no report back.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament urges the Government of the Day, through the Ministry of the Interior and Local Government, the Bangsamoro Planning and Development Authority and the Ministry of Science and Technology, to encourage line agencies and local governments to take proactive disaster risk reduction measures, especially for recovery and rehabilitation.

It also sends the resolution to the Office of Civil Defense and the World Bank, asking that Bangsamoro agencies and local governments take part in their Ready to Rebuild program, and to the Department of Science and Technology central office for a possible partnership with the regional ministry on the GeoRiskPH platform.

Authored by MP Baintan A. Ampatuan. Adopted on 16 February 2022.
readings.whyProposed: The Organic Law gives the region authority over disaster risk reduction and requires a Bangsamoro disaster plan. The authors point to 2 existing tools: Ready to Rebuild, a joint program of the national disaster council and the World Bank that has agencies plan recovery before a disaster strikes, and GeoRiskPH, a hazard-data platform led by PHIVOLCS and run by DOST-PHIVOLCS since 2021.
whoIsAffected: Regional line agencies and local governments.
Communities exposed to disasters.
implementedBy: Ministry of the Interior and Local Government
Bangsamoro Planning and Development Authority
Ministry of Science and Technology
whatChanges: Copies go to the Office of Civil Defense, the World Bank and the Department of Science and Technology as invitations; none of them is bound.
The 3 regional offices are urged to encourage others; no one is required to act by a date.
readings.insight: The WHEREAS clauses suggest yearly participation in Ready to Rebuild, but the RESOLVED clauses do not require it. The resolution is 2 steps removed from action: it urges 3 offices to encourage agencies and local governments, and asks no one to report back.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament commends and honors the late Bai Fatima Palileo Sinsuat for her service to the Bangsamoro and the country. A copy goes to her family.

Authored by MP Susana S. Anayatin. Adopted on 16 February 2022.
readings.whyProposed: Bai Fatima was mayor of Upi from 1980 to 1986, later chaired the ARMM Board of Investments, sat on the University of the Philippines Board of Regents, and was the first Muslim woman in 30 years elected to the national board of the Philippine Red Cross. She served the Red Cross for 47 years, won the National Outstanding Volunteer Award in 2003 for her blood donation work, and in 1986 founded the Progressive Labor Union of Cotabato City dockworkers. She died at 82.
whoIsAffected: The family of Bai Fatima Palileo Sinsuat.
whatChanges: A copy goes to the family. Nothing else follows from it.
readings.insight: A posthumous commendation rather than a condolence resolution. The text does not give the date of her death.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament commends and congratulates 24 local governments of the region for qualifying as the most competitive in the region in the National Competitiveness Council's 2021 Cities and Municipalities Competitiveness Index. A copy goes to each of them.

Authored by MP Ziaur-Rahman A. Adiong. Adopted on 16 February 2022.
readings.whyProposed: The index ranks cities and towns on 4 pillars: economic dynamism, government efficiency, infrastructure and resiliency. On fiscal year 2021 data the resolution lists 2 component cities (Marawi and Lamitan), 7 class 1 to 2 municipalities, 8 class 3 to 4 municipalities and 7 class 5 to 6 municipalities.
whoIsAffected: The 24 cities and municipalities named.
whatChanges: Copies go to the 24 local governments. Nothing else follows from it.
readings.insight: By province the list holds 10 from Maguindanao, 9 from Lanao del Sur, 3 from Sulu and 2 from Basilan; none is from Tawi-Tawi. The resolution gives no score or rank for any of them.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament appeals to President Rodrigo Roa Duterte to sign the Marawi Siege Victims Compensation Act into law. The resolution goes to the President, with a copy to the Office of the Chief Minister.

Authored by MP Hamid Aminoddin D. Barra, MP Paisalin P. Tago, MP Jose I. Lorena and MP Maisara Dandamun Latiph. Adopted on 17 February 2022.
readings.whyProposed: The 5-month battle in Marawi in 2017 destroyed or cost most residents of the city their property, especially in the Most Affected Areas, and some were still displaced. Many bills had been filed in Congress since 2018; the resolution says only the House and Senate versions passed on third reading were awaiting the President's signature.
whoIsAffected: Marawi residents who lost property in the 2017 siege.
Displaced families still waiting for compensation.
implementedBy: Office of the President
whatChanges: An appeal to the President; it has no force on him.
readings.insight:
The document cites 3 different pairs of bill numbers. The title names Senate Bill No. 2420 and House Bill No. 9925; a WHEREAS clause names House Bill No. 9925 and Senate Bill No. 2240; the RESOLVED clause asks the President to sign Senate Bill No. 2240 and House Bill No. 9945. All 3 are legible on the page images.

It was one in a long line: Resolutions 14 and 33 (2019) backed compensation bills, Resolutions 151 and 156 (September 2021) urged the Senate, and Resolution 308 (24 January 2023) thanked President Marcos for constituting the Marawi Compensation Board.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament pays tribute to the late Amman Jalmaani, a swimmer from Sulu who competed in 3 Olympic Games, for the honor he brought the region. A copy goes to his family.

Authored by MP Eddie M. Alih and 6 others. Adopted on 17 February 2022.
readings.whyProposed: Jalmaani swam at the 1964 Tokyo, 1968 Mexico City and 1972 Munich Olympics. At the Asian Games he won bronze in 1966 at 18, a relay silver and 2 individual silvers in the breaststroke in 1970, and a relay bronze in 1974. The resolution says he is 1 of 3 Filipino swimmers to compete in 3 Olympics and 1 of 6 to reach an Olympic semifinal. He later served with the Armed Forces in Zamboanga City, where he died on 23 November at 72.
whoIsAffected: The family of Amman Jalmaani.
whatChanges: A copy goes to the family. Nothing else follows from it.
readings.insight: The text gives his death as Tuesday, 23 November, without a year.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament commends and congratulates Benamin Elegores Rinabor for placing 2nd in the December 2021 Criminology Licensure Examination, and directs that the resolution be presented to him.

Authored by MP Maisara Dandamun Latiph. Adopted on 22 February 2022.
readings.whyProposed: Rinabor scored 89.55%. The resolution reports 33,983 examinees, of whom 11,610, or 34.16%, passed. He graduated cum laude in criminology among 110 graduates of Lake Lanao College in Marawi City and is from Tugaya, Lanao del Sur.
whoIsAffected: Benamin Elegores Rinabor.
whatChanges: A copy is presented to the honoree. Nothing else follows from it.
readings.insight: The footer cites 2 proposed resolutions, PR654 and PR660, merged into this one. It is 1 of a long run of commendations for licensure examination topnotchers; Resolution 234 followed a month later for a psychometrician.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament expresses its sympathy and condolences on the death of Ambalang Ausalin, a master Yakan weaver from Basilan and a Manlilikha ng Bayan, and honors her work in promoting traditional Yakan textile weaving. Copies are to be circulated to media outlets in the region and sent to her family.

Authored by MP Amilbahar S. Mawallil and 9 others. Adopted on 22 February 2022.
readings.whyProposed: Ausalin, born on 24 March 1943, learned weaving young in a family of weavers and was known for intricate Yakan Tennun designs. In 2016 the National Commission for Culture and the Arts named her a National Living Treasure, 1 of 3 Mindanaoans so honored that year. She died of pneumonia at home in Lamitan City on 18 February 2022 and was buried the same day.
whoIsAffected: The family of Ambalang Ausalin.
Yakan weavers and the Yakan community of Basilan.
whatChanges: Copies go to the family and to media outlets in the region. Nothing else follows from it.
readings.insight: Adopted 4 days after her death. Besides the family copy, it directs that copies be circulated to media outlets.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament calls for the implementation of Section 24, Article XIII of the Bangsamoro Organic Law, which provides for the enactment of a Bangsamoro Cooperative Code. It names no office to act and no recipient for copies.

Authored by MP Diamila D. Ramos. Adopted on 24 February 2022.
readings.whyProposed: The authors say the duty to promote cooperatives passed to the region through the Organic Law, and that a Cooperative Code would answer Chief Minister Ahod B. Ebrahim's call to turn armed groups into a social movement, "from base commands to cooperatives", giving decommissioned combatants a livelihood.
whoIsAffected: Cooperatives in the region.
Decommissioned combatants returning to civilian life.
implementedBy: Bangsamoro Transition Authority Parliament
whatChanges: A statement of Parliament's sense; the code itself has to come as a law.
readings.insight:
The title also names Section 27 and a Social Enterprise Code, but the RESOLVED clause, checked on the page image, mentions only Section 24 and the Cooperative Code.

The code was still not law over a year later: Parliament Bill No. 210, An Act Providing for the Bangsamoro Cooperative and Social Enterprise Code, filed by MP Diamila D. Ramos and others, was at first reading as of 20 July 2023, and the registry lists no such act.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament directs the Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Agrarian Reform to report to it on how Republic Act No. 11524, the Coconut Farmers and Industry Trust Fund Act, is being implemented in the region, especially whether Bangsamoro coconut farmers are in the Coconut Farmers Registry, and to ask the Philippine Coconut Authority to extend registration for applicants from the region.

It also directs the ministry to give Parliament information on the region's coconut industry and the steps it is taking to improve it, to help Parliament consider a law. A copy goes to the Minister.

Authored by MP Don Mustapha A. Loong and 6 others. Adopted on 24 February 2022.
readings.whyProposed: Republic Act No. 11524, signed on 26 February 2021, creates a trust fund of ₱65,000,000,000 over 5 years for coconut farmers and gave the Philippine Coconut Authority 90 days to complete a farmers registry. Farmers left out of the registry are left out of the fund's benefits. The resolution notes that in 2020 the ministry, the regional trade ministry and the Coconut Authority had signed a memorandum of understanding to boost the industry.
whoIsAffected: Coconut farmers in the region.
implementedBy: Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Agrarian Reform
whatChanges: The ministry is directed to report to Parliament; no deadline is set.
The ministry is to ask a national agency for an extension; Parliament cannot grant one itself.
readings.insight: The resolution quotes the national law at length, including its split of the yearly fund: 20% for hybrid seed farms and nurseries, 10% each for credit, infrastructure, processing facilities, diversification and health, 8% each for training and scholarships, 5% for research and promotion, and 4% for crop insurance. It sets no date for the ministry's report.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament directs the Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Agrarian Reform to change the specifications in its purchase of motorized boats from fiberglass to wooden hulls, and to speed up the purchase and full rollout of its boat distribution program. A copy goes to the ministry.

Authored by MP Don Mustapha A. Loong, MP Baintan A. Ampatuan, MP Amilbahar S. Mawallil, MP Laisa M. Alamia, MP Rasol Y. Mitmug Jr. and MP Rasul E. Ismael. Adopted on 24 February 2022.
readings.whyProposed: The ministry's 2020 projects for fisherfolk, "Municipal Payao" and "Basnigan with Fishing Net", called for 30-foot fiberglass boats and 20-foot fiberglass boats with paddles. According to the ministry, bidding failed repeatedly for lack of responsive bidders, and fiberglass was chosen to follow MARINA Circular No. 2016-02. The authors answer that the circular phases out wooden-hulled passenger ships, not fishing boats, and that fishing cooperatives prefer wooden hulls because they are lighter, easier to repair with local materials, and stay afloat when damaged. The ministry had dropped motorized boats from its 2021 programs.
whoIsAffected: Small fisherfolk, especially in Basilan, Sulu and Tawi-Tawi and the coasts of Maguindanao and Lanao del Sur.
Fishing cooperatives.
implementedBy: Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Agrarian Reform
whatChanges: Parliament directs a change to a ministry's procurement specifications; it sets no deadline and asks for no report.
readings.insight: An unusually operational resolution: it tells a ministry what material to buy. By its own account the boats were allotted in 2020 and still undelivered in February 2022.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament reminds all ministries and offices of the Bangsamoro Government to hold their capacity-building activities within the region, as Resolution No. 189 of 18 November 2021 provides, and directs them "to avoid the conduct of training and other capacity-building." Copies go to all ministries and offices.

Authored by MP Baintan A. Ampatuan and 8 others. Adopted on 24 February 2022.
readings.whyProposed: The authors cite the Code of Conduct for public officials, which requires government resources to be used economically, and the procurement rules on choosing venues with prudence. They argue that training need not be held in luxurious hotels or resorts anywhere in the country when cheaper venues exist, except when it is externally funded, for example by NGOs or development partners.
whoIsAffected: Ministries and offices of the Bangsamoro Government.
Staff attending training.
implementedBy: All ministries and offices of the Bangsamoro Government
whatChanges: A reminder and a direction to the executive; it sets no penalty and asks for no report.
readings.insight:
The operative clause is cut short. The title and WHEREAS clauses speak of avoiding luxurious and first-class hotels and resorts, with an exception for externally funded activities, but the adopted RESOLVED, FURTHER clause ends at "avoid the conduct of training and other capacity-building", with no mention of hotels or the exception. This is checked on the page image. Read literally, it tells offices to avoid training altogether.

Resolution No. 189, which it reiterates, urged ministries 3 months earlier to use businesses within the region for capacity-building.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament expresses its continued trust and confidence in Interim Chief Minister Ahod B. Ebrahim and prays for the success of the Bangsamoro Government under his leadership. No recipient for copies is named.

Authored by MP Eddie M. Alih and 13 others. Adopted on 24 February 2022.
readings.whyProposed: Ebrahim was appointed and sworn in by President Duterte as Interim Chief Minister on 22 February 2019. The resolution cites his role as MILF Chairman and chief negotiator, his pursuit of moral governance, and his leadership through the pandemic. On 28 October 2021 the President signed the law extending the transition to 2025.
whoIsAffected: Interim Chief Minister Ahod B. Ebrahim.
whatChanges: A statement of Parliament's sense. Nothing follows from it.
readings.insight: Adopted 2 days after the 3rd anniversary of his appointment, and 3 days after the President, according to Resolution 229, approved keeping the transition authority's membership unchanged.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament urges the Government of the Day to set up a Bangsamoro Complaint Center and Hotline, a regional version of the national 8888 hotline created by Executive Order No. 6, series of 2016, as part of the government's grievance mechanism. A copy goes to Chief Minister Ahod B. Ebrahim.

Authored by MP Baintan A. Ampatuan and 6 others. Adopted on 15 March 2022.
readings.whyProposed: The region had no dedicated hotline or number for complaints about ministries, offices and local governments. The resolution cites the Civil Service Commission's 2020 figures for hotline 8888: 95 tickets endorsed to the commission, all acted on, 58 of them (61.05%) complaints about agencies, employees or processes.
whoIsAffected: Residents dealing with regional offices and local governments.
Frontline staff of ministries and offices.
implementedBy: Office of the Chief Minister
whatChanges: A request to the executive; it sets no deadline and names no office to run the hotline.
readings.insight: 8 days later Parliament went further on the same theme: Resolution 238 directed all offices to post citizen's charters and set up public assistance and complaints desks, with a twice-yearly report back. This resolution asks for nothing in return.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament supports the policy of the Office of the Chief Minister of having the Bangsamoro represented in the affairs of the National Government through its agencies and offices, as the Organic Law provides. A copy goes to Chief Minister Ahod B. Ebrahim.

Authored by MP Baintan A. Ampatuan and MP Amilbahar S. Mawallil. Adopted on 15 March 2022.
readings.whyProposed: Section 11, Article VI of the Organic Law says the Bangsamoro Government shall, as far as practicable, be represented in national departments and agencies that carry out national programs in the region, and Section 32, Article VII makes the Chief Minister its representative.
whoIsAffected: The Office of the Chief Minister.
National agencies operating in the region.
whatChanges: A statement of support. Nothing else follows from it.
readings.insight: The resolution does not describe the policy it supports: it gives no issuance number, date or content for the Office of the Chief Minister's policy. The same Organic Law provision is cited in Resolution 221 to argue for Bangsamoro coconut farmers' place in a national program.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament urges that the Strategic Performance Management System be set up and used in the Bangsamoro Transition Authority and in all other regional agencies. It directs every agency to review and revise its performance system to follow the system's guidelines, or write a new one, and submit it to the Civil Service Commission in BARMM for approval. It also urges the Office of the Chief Minister to set a deadline for all agencies. Copies go to the Chief Minister and all ministries, offices and agencies.

Authored by MP Laisa M. Alamia. Adopted on 15 March 2022.
readings.whyProposed: The Civil Service Commission has used the Strategic Performance Management System since 2012 to tie individual ratings to agency goals and to performance bonuses. The Bangsamoro Civil Service Code (BAA 17) relies on it for probation reviews and merit pay. The resolution reports that only 4 agencies of the Bangsamoro Government had an approved system, with the rest still drafting or awaiting approval.
whoIsAffected: Employees of the Bangsamoro Government and of Parliament.
Agency human resource offices.
implementedBy: All agencies of the Bangsamoro Government
Office of the Chief Minister
Civil Service Commission in BARMM
whatChanges: Agencies are directed to prepare and submit their systems; no deadline is set by the resolution itself.
The deadline is left to the Office of the Chief Minister.
readings.insight: It includes Parliament itself. The Civil Service Code was ratified on 24 February 2021; a year later, by the resolution's count, 4 agencies had an approved performance system.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament expresses its sympathy and condolences to the family of Dr. Camar Ampaso Umpa, former president of Mindanao State University. A copy goes to his family.

Authored by MP Ziaur-Rahman A. Adiong and 10 others. Adopted on 15 March 2022.
readings.whyProposed: Dr. Umpa, born on 3 November 1949 in Madamba, Lanao del Sur, finished political science at Mindanao State University in 3 years and earned his PhD at the University of Hawaii in 1977. He became the first Chancellor of MSU-Iligan Institute of Technology in 1988 at 38, served as MSU president from 1999 to 2005, and in 2008 led the founding of Al Khwarizmi International College. He died on 7 March 2022.
whoIsAffected: The family of Dr. Camar Ampaso Umpa.
whatChanges: A copy goes to the family. Nothing else follows from it.
readings.insight: Adopted 8 days after his death. The footer cites 3 proposed resolutions, PR686, PR687 and PR704, consolidated into this one.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament expresses full support and gratitude to President Rodrigo R. Duterte for approving the Security, Justice and Peace Cabinet Cluster's recommendation to keep the current membership of the Bangsamoro Transition Authority, and declares its renewed commitment to serve the Bangsamoro people. Copies go to the President, the Office of the Presidential Adviser on Peace, Reconciliation and Unity, the Department of National Defense and the Department of the Interior and Local Government.

Authored by MP Pangalian M. Balindong and 28 others. Adopted on 15 March 2022.
readings.whyProposed: Republic Act No. 11593 moved the first regional election to 2025 and let the President appoint 80 interim members to serve until 30 June 2025. Parliament had asked him to keep the incumbents in Resolution No. 173 (12 October 2021) and again in Resolution No. 209 (15 February 2022). The resolution says the President approved the cluster's recommendation on 21 February 2022.
whoIsAffected: The 80 members of the Bangsamoro Transition Authority.
whatChanges: A statement of thanks. Nothing else follows from it.
readings.insight: Resolution 230, adopted the same day, thanks the same people for the same decision; its page 1 dates the cluster's confirmation to 4 March 2022. The arrangement did not last until 2025: Resolution 271 (26 September 2022) commended members of the first transition authority who were not reappointed by President Marcos to the second.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament thanks President Rodrigo Roa Duterte for appointing Atty. Saidamen B. Pangarungan as Chairman of the Commission on Elections, Atty. Abdullah D. Mama-o as Secretary of the Department of Migrant Workers, Atty. Guiling A. Mamondiong as Secretary of the National Commission on Muslim Filipinos, Atty. Basari D. Mapupuno as President of Mindanao State University, and other appointees from the region, and congratulates them all. Copies go to the President and the appointees.

Authored by MP Edrieza H.N. Rimbang, MP Nabila Margarita P. Pangandaman and MP Maisara Dandamun Latiph. Adopted on 16 March 2022.
readings.whyProposed: The appointments came between 4 and 8 March 2022: Mama-o on 4 March, Pangarungan on 7 March, and Mamondiong and Mapupuno on 8 March. The resolution adds that the President appointed several other Moro professionals to executive and judicial posts, without naming them.
whoIsAffected: The 4 named appointees and other appointees from the region.
whatChanges: Copies go to the President and the appointees. Nothing else follows from it.
readings.insight: The footer cites 6 proposed resolutions, PR681, PR682, PR683, PR684, PR691 and PR705, consolidated into this one. Parliament has thanked presidents for appointments before and since, such as Resolution 105 (January 2021) for a Court of Appeals justice and Resolution 363 (July 2023) for the reappointment of Carlito G. Galvez Jr.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament calls on the Government of the Day to take a whole-of-government approach in crafting policies, plans, programs and projects for Bangsamoro domestic workers, especially women. It requests the Overseas Workers Welfare Administration and the Philippine Overseas Employment Administration to give the regional Ministry of Labor and Employment reports and data on Bangsamoro women working abroad as domestic workers, for use in legislation. Copies go to the concerned ministries and offices.

Authored by MP Diamila D. Ramos and MP Baintan A. Ampatuan. Adopted on 17 March 2022.
readings.whyProposed: The resolution cites national figures: an average of 86,000 Filipino migrant domestic workers deployed each year from 1992 to 2015, and, of 2.3 million overseas workers from April to September 2018, 437,000 from the region, with women making up 55.8%. Domestic work, hidden in private homes and informally arranged, leaves women exposed to exploitation, forced labor, trafficking and abuse.
whoIsAffected: Bangsamoro women working abroad as domestic workers, and their families.
implementedBy: Ministry of Labor and Employment
Overseas Workers Welfare Administration
Philippine Overseas Employment Administration
whatChanges: A request for data to 2 national agencies, which Parliament cannot compel.
The call on the regional government names no lead office and no deadline.
readings.insight: The regional call names no lead office, and the "concerned ministries and offices" that receive copies are not named. The data request goes to 2 national agencies, to be delivered to a regional ministry rather than to Parliament, though the stated purpose is legislation.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament expresses serious concern over reported civilian casualties in Ukraine, especially women and children, and joins the international call for an immediate end to the war. Copies go to President Rodrigo R. Duterte and the Secretary of Foreign Affairs.

Authored by MP Romeo C. Saliga. Adopted on 17 March 2022.
readings.whyProposed: The authors cite the Constitution's renunciation of war, the Organic Law's acceptance of human rights and international law, the worsening humanitarian situation and refugee numbers in Ukraine, and the effect on global food security. They quote the Quran: whoever saves one life, it is as if he had saved mankind entirely.
whoIsAffected: Civilians in Ukraine.
whatChanges: A statement of Parliament's position, sent to the President and the foreign affairs department. Nothing else follows from it.
readings.insight: The resolution does not name any party to the war. Resolution 124 (June 2021) on Palestine, by contrast, named Israeli forces in its title.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament commends and congratulates Piamae Keil Roslin, a graduate of Notre Dame University, for placing 9th in the February 2022 Psychometrician Licensure Examination. Copies go to her and to Notre Dame University.

Authored by MP Narciso Co Yu Ekey and 9 others. Adopted on 17 March 2022.
readings.whyProposed: Roslin scored 81.80%. The Professional Regulation Commission reported 969 passers out of 2,241, about 43%. She is from Parang, Maguindanao, and graduated from Notre Dame University in Cotabato City.
whoIsAffected: Piamae Keil Roslin.
Notre Dame University.
whatChanges: Copies go to the honoree and her university. Nothing else follows from it.
readings.insight: It is 1 of a long run of commendations for licensure examination topnotchers; Resolution 218 commended the 2nd placer in the criminology examination a month earlier.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament expresses its sympathy and condolences to the family of Guiamia "Babo Mia" M. Hussain, former chairperson of the Social Welfare Committee of the Moro Islamic Liberation Front, and recognizes her role in the Bangsamoro struggle. A copy goes to her family.

Authored by MP Aida M. Silongan. Adopted on 17 March 2022.
readings.whyProposed: Hussain chaired the Social Welfare Committee, the women's wing of the MILF Central Committee, and fought alongside the late MILF Chairman Ustadz Salamat Hashim. She died at home in Mahad Mindanao, Pikit, Cotabato on 15 March 2022.
whoIsAffected: The family of Guiamia M. Hussain.
whatChanges: A copy goes to the family. Nothing else follows from it.
readings.insight: Adopted 2 days after her death. The WHEREAS clauses quote a 2017 study by Silongan on Maguindanaon women in the armed struggle; the principal author is MP Aida M. Silongan.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament thanks the United Nations General Assembly for proclaiming 15 March the International Day to Combat Islamophobia. A copy goes to the United Nations office in the Philippines.

Authored by MP Baintan A. Ampatuan and 6 others. Adopted on 22 March 2022.
readings.whyProposed: The 193-member General Assembly unanimously adopted a resolution put forward by the Organization of Islamic Cooperation and Pakistan, co-sponsored by its 57 members. The authors cite FBI figures for the United States: 257 anti-Muslim incidents in 2015, up 67% from 154 in 2014, and anti-Muslim hate groups rising from 34 in 2015 to 101 in 2016. They add that the MNLF, a party in the transition authority, has observer status in the OIC.
whoIsAffected: Muslims in the region and elsewhere.
whatChanges: A copy goes to the United Nations office. Nothing else follows from it.
readings.insight: Adopted a week after the first observance. The WHEREAS clauses say the Bangsamoro should encourage dialogue and organize activities to mark the day, but the RESOLVED clauses direct no one to do so.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament authorizes the Office of the Chief Minister to grant a Ramadhan allowance to all officials, personnel and employees of the Bangsamoro Government regardless of employment status, subject to available funds and standard accounting and auditing rules. The Ministry of Finance, and Budget and Management is to issue the guidelines. Copies go to Chief Minister Ahod B. Ebrahim and that ministry.

Authored by MP Omar Yasser C. Sema and 72 others. Adopted on 23 March 2022.
readings.whyProposed: Ramadan was to begin in the first week of April 2022. The authors say an allowance would motivate staff through the month of fasting and help families cope with rising prices driven by fuel costs. A bill for a Ramadan Economic Assistance and Relief was still in committee and might not pass in time.
whoIsAffected: Officials and employees of the Bangsamoro Government, of whatever employment status.
implementedBy: Office of the Chief Minister
Ministry of Finance, and Budget and Management

funding.detail: The resolution appropriates nothing. It authorizes an allowance from available funds and names no amount, fund source or total cost.

whatChanges: The Chief Minister is authorized, not required, to grant the allowance.
The ministry is to issue guidelines.
readings.insight: This is part of a yearly series: Resolution 120 (2021) requested a Ramadhan allowance, this one authorized it, and Resolutions 323 (2023), 441 (2024) and 530 (2025) asked for inflation relief during Ramadhan, with a ceiling of ₱15,000 in 2023 and a floor of ₱10,000 in 2024. Unlike those later ones, this resolution names no amount.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament directs the Bangsamoro Government to fully set up citizen's charters and public assistance and complaints desks in all government offices in the region. A consolidated report on compliance is to reach Parliament, through the Office of the Speaker, within 1 month after each semester. Copies go to all government offices in the region.

Authored by MP Abdullah B. Hashim. Adopted on 23 March 2022.
readings.whyProposed: The Ease of Doing Business Act of 2018 requires every government office to post a citizen's charter and keep a staffed public assistance desk, with penalties for violations.
