The resolution reports that only 2 of 38 surveyed offices in the Bangsamoro Government Center had a citizen's charter and only 6 of 38 had a public assistance desk.
whoIsAffected: Residents transacting with regional offices.
Frontline staff of all government offices in the region.
implementedBy: All government offices of the Bangsamoro Government
whatChanges: Offices are directed to comply with an existing national law.
Parliament is to receive a compliance report twice a year.
readings.insight: It attaches a reporting duty, but does not say which office consolidates the report. It follows Resolution 225, adopted 8 days earlier, which urged a regional complaints hotline without any report back.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament directs the Ministry of Health to implement Muslim Mindanao Autonomy Act No. 245, which upgraded the Tamparan District Hospital into the provincial hospital of Lanao del Sur. Copies go to the Ministry of Health and the Ministry of Finance, and Budget and Management.

Authored by MP Paisalin P. Tago and 7 others. Adopted on 24 March 2022.
readings.whyProposed: The ARMM Regional Legislative Assembly enacted MMA Act No. 245 on 11 June 2008, after the old provincial hospital in Marawi, Amai Pakpak, became a national medical center. The act upgraded the Tamparan District Hospital, moved the former provincial hospital's assets and funding to it, and placed it under the regional health department. The Organic Law keeps ARMM laws in force unless inconsistent with it or repealed, and the authors say this one is neither.
whoIsAffected: Patients in Lanao del Sur served by the Tamparan hospital.
Hospital staff.
implementedBy: Ministry of Health
whatChanges: A direction to carry out a 2008 regional law; it sets no deadline and asks for no report.
readings.insight: The direction came nearly 14 years after the law. 4 years later the hospital still carried the old name: Parliament Bill No. 439, filed on 6 March 2026, would rename the Tamparan District Hospital to Lanao del Sur Provincial Hospital, and it was at first reading as of 21 April 2026.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament authorizes all its parliamentary and statutory committees to keep working during the mandatory break in 2022. Copies go to the Office of the Chief Minister, the Office of the Speaker and all members.

Authored by MP Pangalian M. Balindong, MP Omar Yasser C. Sema and MP Lanang T. Ali Jr. Adopted on 24 March 2022.
readings.whyProposed: The third regular session ended on 24 March 2022, as Parliament adjourned for Ramadan in April. The priority codes required by the Organic Law and other bills and resolutions were still pending in committee.
whoIsAffected: Parliament's committees and members.
Ministries and others invited to committee hearings.
implementedBy: Bangsamoro Transition Authority Parliament
whatChanges: Binding on Parliament: committees may sit during the 2022 break.
readings.insight: This is the earliest of 5 such authorities in the index; Resolutions 324 (2023), 443 (2024), 539 (2025) and 567 (2026) followed. Resolutions 443, 539 and 567 carry no end date; this one is limited to the 2022 break, and it names no specific pending code.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament thanks the Organization of Islamic Cooperation's Council of Foreign Ministers (OIC-CFM) for its concern for Muslim countries and for non-member Muslim communities such as the Bangsamoro, shown at its 48th session in Islamabad, Pakistan, on 22–23 March 2022. It also thanks the OIC for recognising the justness and legitimacy of the Bangsamoro cause and for continuing to follow the implementation of the 1996 Final Peace Agreement, particularly the consensus points of the Tripartite Review Process. The resolution is sent to the OIC-CFM.

Filed by MP Romeo K. Sema. Adopted on 24 March 2022, the day after the session closed.
readings.whyProposed: The 48th session, themed "Partnering for Unity, Justice, and Development", adopted resolutions on peace and security, economic development and the OIC's role in the Muslim world. The resolution recalls the OIC's part in the 1976 Tripoli Agreement and the 1996 Final Peace Agreement with the MNLF, and the Comprehensive Agreement on the Bangsamoro with the MILF that led to the Bangsamoro Organic Law. It notes that the MNLF, which holds permanent observer status in the OIC, is part of the BTA.
whoIsAffected: The OIC Council of Foreign Ministers, the recipient.
whatChanges: A copy goes to the OIC-CFM for its information. Nothing else follows from it.
readings.insight: One of 3 resolutions addressed to the OIC in this period, after Resolution No. 109 (24 February 2021), which commended the OIC for a resolution on Muslims in the southern Philippines. Its sole author is MP Romeo K. Sema, and its second clause centres on the MNLF track: the 1996 Final Peace Agreement and the Tripartite Review Process, not the MILF agreement.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament congratulates the Office of the Presidential Adviser on Peace, Reconciliation, and Unity (OPAPRU) on its reorganisation and its renewed commitment to peace. The resolution goes to President Rodrigo Roa Duterte, with a copy to OPAPRU.

Filed by MP Laisa M. Alamia. Adopted on 24 March 2022.
readings.whyProposed: Executive Order No. 158, s. 2021 renamed and reorganised the Office of the Presidential Adviser on the Peace Process (OPAPP), set up under Executive Order No. 125, s. 1993, into OPAPRU. The new office was launched on 24 March 2022, the day this resolution was adopted. Presidential Peace Adviser Carlito G. Galvez Jr. pledged to sustain the peace process by reintegrating former combatants and transforming conflict-affected areas.
whoIsAffected: OPAPRU, the national peace agency that handles the Bangsamoro peace process.
whatChanges: Copies go to the President and OPAPRU. Nothing else follows from it.
readings.insight: Adopted on the same day as the launch it congratulates. OPAPRU reappears often in later resolutions: Resolution No. 246 copies it on thanks to President Duterte, Resolution No. 269 thanks its head, Secretary Galvez, for bringing the MNLF into the second BTA, and Resolution No. 280 (22 November 2022) thanks President Marcos for appointing its secretary.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament commends the Mindanao State University College of Law in Marawi City and the Notre Dame University College of Law in Cotabato City for producing 94 new Bangsamoro lawyers in the 2020/2021 Bar Examinations: 46 from MSU and 48 from Notre Dame. In its preamble it also commends every Bangsamoro bar passer from other law schools. Copies go to both universities and to the Lanao del Sur and Cotabato chapters of the Integrated Bar of the Philippines.

Filed by MP Abdullah B. Hashim. Adopted on 15 June 2022.
readings.whyProposed: The 2020/2021 Bar was the first held in a localised, digital format, on 4 and 6 February 2022 at 29 testing sites, under Justice Marvic M.V.F. Leonen. Results came out on 12 April 2022 with a 72.28% passing rate. The resolution calls the 2 schools the only law schools in BARMM territory and says more Bangsamoro lawyers will widen access to justice.
whoIsAffected: MSU College of Law and Notre Dame University College of Law.
The 94 new lawyers from the 2 schools.
whatChanges: Copies go to the 2 universities and 2 IBP chapters. Nothing else follows from it.
readings.insight: One of a run of bar-exam commendations: the index also has Resolutions No. 71 (2020), 337 and 345 (2023), 423 and 477 (2024). This one honours the schools rather than individual passers, and its numbers add up: 46 and 48 make 94.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament extends its sympathy and condolences to the family of Datu Guimid "Jimmy" Matalam, former Speaker of the ARMM Regional Legislative Assembly, and recognises his contributions to the Bangsamoro people. The resolution is sent to his family.

Filed by MP Rasol Y. Mitmug Jr. and 7 others. Adopted on 15 June 2022.
readings.whyProposed: Matalam died on 18 May 2022. As a member of the first post-martial-law Congress he was one of the 2 principal sponsors of the bills creating the ARMM, passed as Republic Act No. 6734, and chaired the Committee on Muslim Affairs. He was Congressman for Maguindanao's 2nd District (1987–1992 and 2001–2004), RLA Speaker (1993–1996), ARMM Vice-Governor (1996–2001), and ARMM regional secretary for agrarian reform (1992–1993) and for the interior and local government (1996–2001). He was a son of Datu Udtog Matalam and a kinsman of Senator Salipada K. Pendatun and MILF founding chairman Hashim Salamat.
whoIsAffected: The family of Datu Guimid Matalam.
whatChanges: A copy goes to the family. Nothing else follows from it.
readings.insight: The adopted text consolidates 2 proposals, PR 731 and PR 739. It honours a figure of the ARMM, the autonomous region the BARMM replaced: Matalam sponsored the law that created it and led its legislature.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament congratulates and commends Ferdinand "Bongbong" Romualdez Marcos Jr. as President and Sara Zimmerman Duterte-Carpio as Vice-President of the Philippines. Copies go to the offices of the President-elect and Vice President-elect.

Filed by MP Baintan A. Ampatuan and 30 others. Adopted on 16 June 2022.
readings.whyProposed: Congress, sitting as the National Board of Canvassers, proclaimed the 2 on 25 May 2022. The resolution records Marcos's 31,629,783 votes, more than 16,000,000 ahead of the runner-up, and Duterte-Carpio's 32,208,417, more than 22,000,000 ahead, on an 83.11% turnout of more than 55,000,000 voters. It summarises their UniTeam platform and says the BTA supports them as it prepares to work with the new administration.
whoIsAffected: President Marcos and Vice-President Duterte-Carpio.
whatChanges: Copies go to the 2 offices. Nothing else follows from it.
readings.insight: The adopted text consolidates 4 proposals, PR 744, PR 747, PR 749 and PR 758, and the index lists 31 authors. It was the first of many resolutions addressed to Marcos: 3 months later Resolution No. 269 thanked him for appointing the second BTA.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament expresses its gratitude to President Rodrigo Roa Duterte for the passage of the Bangsamoro Organic Law, the extension of the BTA, and his administration's support for the Bangsamoro people. Copies go to the President and to OPAPRU.

Filed by MP Eddie M. Alih and 48 others. Adopted on 15 June 2022.
readings.whyProposed: Duterte signed Republic Act No. 11054, the Organic Law, on 26 July 2018; it took effect on 10 August 2018 and created the BTA as interim government. The law originally set the first regional election for 2022, with the BTA dissolving once a Chief Minister was elected. On 28 October 2021 Duterte signed Republic Act No. 11593, moving that election to 2025, which the resolution says gave the BTA the time it needed to lay the foundations of the regular government. It calls the Organic Law his greatest legacy to the Bangsamoro.
whoIsAffected: President Duterte, the recipient, at the end of his term.
whatChanges: Copies go to the President and OPAPRU. Nothing else follows from it.
readings.insight: The index lists 49 authors, including Speaker Pangalian M. Balindong. It is one of several farewells to Duterte in the closing weeks of his term: Resolution No. 255, 8 days later, urges the Bangsamoro Government to commend him too, and Resolutions No. 229, 230 and 231 in March 2022 had thanked him for specific decisions.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament congratulates Mayor Bruce Dela Cruz Matabalao, Vice Mayor Johari "Butch" Compania Abu and 10 councilors on their election as the new officials of Cotabato City. Copies go to the mayor, the vice mayor and the 10 councilors.

Filed by MP Narciso Co Yu Ekey and 15 others. Adopted on 15 June 2022.
readings.whyProposed: In the 9 May 2022 election the United Bangsamoro Justice Party (UBJP) led the race in Cotabato City. The COMELEC board of canvassers proclaimed Matabalao and Abu on the night of 10 May and the councilors on 11 May: 7 from the UBJP (Florante Formento, Hunyn Abu, Maroup Pasawiran, Abdulrakim Usman, Guiadzuri Midtimbang, Kusin Taha and Henjie Ali) and 3 from other parties (Jay Jay Guiani, Danda Juanday and Abdillah Lim). The resolution says Members are committed to support the new city administration.
whoIsAffected: The newly elected officials of Cotabato City, the seat of the regional government.
whatChanges: Copies go to the officials. Nothing else follows from it.
readings.insight: The resolution's preamble names the winning party, the UBJP, and lists which councilors belong to it, unusual detail for a congratulatory resolution. The operative text congratulates all 10 councilors, including the 3 from other parties.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament adopts the calendar for the Fourth Regular Session of the BTA. The session opens on 14 June 2022 and sits in 19 sitting weeks, each resuming on a Tuesday and adjourning on the Thursday, 2 consecutive weeks a month: June, July, August, September, October, November and December 2022, and January, February and March 2023. Mandatory adjournment falls on 16 March 2023.

Filed by MP Lanang T. Ali Jr.. Adopted on 15 June 2022, the day after the session opened.
readings.whyProposed: The BTA's rules, quoted in the resolution, have Parliament convene its regular session on the third Tuesday of the month after Eid'l Fitr and hold plenary sessions Tuesday to Thursday in the third and fourth weeks of each month when it is not in recess. A calendar guides Members in their legislative and constituency work.
whoIsAffected: Members of the BTA Parliament and the Secretariat, who plan around the sitting days.
Ministries and the public who follow Parliament's schedule.
implementedBy: Bangsamoro Transition Authority Parliament
whatChanges: This is an internal resolution with force inside Parliament: it fixes the sitting days for the session.
readings.insight:
The calendar was overtaken within weeks. It ran to March 2023, but the first BTA's last adopted resolutions in the index are dated 28 July 2022. Resolution No. 269 records that President Marcos swore in the 80 members of the second BTA on 12 August 2022, and the next adopted resolutions, from 20 September 2022, belong to a new First Regular Session with its own calendar (Resolution No. 265).

The opening date, 14 June 2022, was the second Tuesday of June, not the third that the quoted rule sets.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament congratulates and commends Robinhood "Abdulazis" Padilla for being elected the top senator in the 2022 national elections and the only Muslim senator in the 19th Congress. A copy goes to his office.

Filed by MP Diamila D. Ramos and 11 others. Adopted on 16 June 2022.
readings.whyProposed: Padilla won more than 26,000,000 votes on 9 May 2022 and topped the Senate race in 13 regions, BARMM among them. In BARMM he received 1,461,373 votes by provisional COMELEC data: 171,227 in Basilan, 323,326 in Lanao del Sur, 519,867 in Maguindanao, 304,902 in Sulu and 142,231 in Tawi-Tawi. The resolution lists his charity work and, after the Marawi siege, 4 hectares of land donated to the Bangsamoro Government for housing displaced families, ₱5,000,000 to the DSWD for children's psychosocial care and ₱5,000,000 in Islamic microfinance for displaced families' businesses. It calls him the first Muslim senator since 1995 and a supporter of the peace process, the Organic Law and the BTA extension, and lists his agenda, including a shift to a federal-parliamentary system.
whoIsAffected: Senator Robinhood Padilla.
whatChanges: A copy goes to his office. Nothing else follows from it.
readings.insight: Padilla was honoured twice on the same day: Resolution No. 250, also adopted on 16 June 2022, congratulates all 12 senators-elect and names him first. Its vote figures do not quite reconcile: the 5 provincial counts it gives sum to 1,461,553, 180 more than the BARMM total of 1,461,373 it states. Parliament thanked him again in Resolution No. 284 (20 December 2022) for disaster relief after a tropical storm.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament congratulates the 12 senators-elect of the 9 May 2022 election: Robin Padilla, Loren Legarda, Raffy Tulfo, Sherwin Gatchalian, Francis Escudero, Mark Villar, Allan Peter Cayetano, Juan Miguel Zubiri, Joel Villanueva, Jose Victor Ejercito, Risa Hontiveros and Jinggoy Estrada. A copy goes to each of their offices.

Filed by MP Ustadz Abdulmuhmin A. Mujahid. Adopted on 16 June 2022.
readings.whyProposed: The resolution counts 3 newcomers (Padilla, Villar and Tulfo) and 9 returning senators. It says the Bangsamoro people trust the new Senate to protect the peace agreement and the Bangsamoro Organic Law, and to support the incoming Marcos–Duterte administration's programmes.
whoIsAffected: The 12 senators-elect.
whatChanges: Copies go to the 12 offices. Nothing else follows from it.
readings.insight: Adopted the same day as Resolution No. 249, which honours Padilla alone. The preamble carries its purpose: the hope that the new Senate will keep the peace agreement and the Organic Law respected "in letter and in spirit". Its sole author, MP Ustadz Abdulmuhmin A. Mujahid, was among the 30 first-BTA members not reappointed to the second BTA, as listed in Resolution No. 271.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament urges the Bangsamoro Government, through the Ministry of Transportation and Communications, to conduct a feasibility study on an Inland Waterway Transport System (IWTS) for the Ligawasan Marsh and other rivers in Maguindanao. The study is to cover Buluan, Mangudadatu, Pandag, Paglat, General Salipada K. Pendatun, Sultan sa Barongis, Raja Buayan, Mamasapano, Datu Piang, Pagalungan, Datu Montawal, Northern Kabuntalan, Mother Kabuntalan, Talitay, Datu Salibo, Sultan Kudarat, Datu Odin Sinsuat, Cotabato City and 63 barangays. Copies go to the Office of the Chief Minister and the Ministry.

Filed by MP Ali O. Salik and 45 others. Adopted on 21 June 2022.
readings.whyProposed: The Organic Law lists inland waterways for navigation among the Bangsamoro Government's powers. The resolution says waterways have been the main way to travel in the Ligawasan Marsh for decades, yet no serviceable transport system has been built, for lack of policy and investment. Citing a study by an Engineer Labay, it argues water transport is cheap, safe and energy-efficient, and that terminals and reliable routes would help small fisherfolk, open business and tourism, and address areas needing dredging, cleaning and river expansion.
whoIsAffected: Residents and fisherfolk of the Ligawasan Marsh towns and the 63 barangays named.
The Ministry of Transportation and Communications.
implementedBy: Ministry of Transportation and Communications
Office of the Chief Minister
whatChanges: It asks the Ministry for a feasibility study. It sets no deadline, budget or report back to Parliament.
readings.insight: The adopted text carries proposed-resolution number PR 424, while the resolutions adopted around it carry numbers in the 700s, so it had been pending for some time. The index lists 46 authors. Nothing in the repo shows whether the study was done.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament urges all ministries, offices and attached agencies, through the Office of the Interim Chief Minister, to develop and integrate values transformation programmes that teach the principles of moral governance. It asks the Chief Minister's office to issue a memorandum of guidelines to all ministries, offices and agencies for immediate implementation. A copy goes to Chief Minister Ahod B. Ebrahim.

Filed by MP Aida M. Silongan and 7 others. Adopted on 23 June 2022.
readings.whyProposed: Chief Minister Ebrahim made moral governance the guiding principle of the Bangsamoro administration. The resolution defines it as government that is responsive, inclusive and democratic, fair and legal, transparent, and accountable, and says instilling it remains hard given the region's history of corruption, manipulation, divisiveness and nepotism. It calls values training for officials, employees and partners urgent during the transition.
whoIsAffected: Officials and employees of all Bangsamoro ministries, offices and attached agencies.
implementedBy: Office of the Chief Minister
All Bangsamoro ministries, offices and attached agencies
whatChanges: It asks the Chief Minister's office for a memorandum of guidelines. It sets no deadline, content or report back to Parliament.
readings.insight: The adopted text carries proposed-resolution number PR 220, while the resolutions adopted around it carry numbers in the 700s. Moral governance runs through the index: Resolution No. 128 (2021) on an oath of moral governance before the Wali, Resolution No. 130 (2021) asking the Darul-Ifta for a fatwa on halal conduct of officials, and Resolutions No. 576 and 578 in 2026.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament commends Commission on Higher Education (CHED) Commissioner Ronald L. Adamat as the first Filipino to receive the 2020 Mahatma Gandhi Prize for Non-Violent Peace. A copy goes to him.

Filed by MP Romeo C. Saliga and MP Susana S. Anayatin. Adopted on 23 June 2022.
readings.whyProposed: Adamat, a Teduray from Upi, Maguindanao, was principal author of Republic Act No. 8371, the Indigenous Peoples' Rights Act of 1997, as indigenous peoples' sectoral representative in the 10th Congress. He studied at Notre Dame University, including a PhD in Peace and Development. As CHED Commissioner he was behind CHED Memorandum Orders No. 1 and 2, s. 2019, which integrate peace studies and indigenous peoples' studies into higher-education curricula. The resolution also lists his books and earlier awards, including a Presidential Medal of Merit in 2005.
whoIsAffected: CHED Commissioner Ronald L. Adamat.
whatChanges: A copy goes to the honoree. Nothing else follows from it.
readings.insight: The adopted text consolidates 2 proposals, PR 715 and PR 716. It honours a Teduray from Maguindanao chiefly for national work: the IPRA and CHED's peace and indigenous studies orders.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament congratulates Saleha Sacar on receiving the Global Women Achievers Award at the 9th World Women Leadership Congress, held in Mumbai, India, in March 2022. A copy goes to her.

Filed by MP Modayao M. Sacar. Adopted on 23 June 2022.
readings.whyProposed: Director Saleha P. Sacar of the Bureau of Muslim Economic Affairs, National Commission on Muslim Filipinos, was a Philippine delegate to the congress, held at Taj Lands End in Mumbai during Women's Month. The resolution says the award made her the first Maranao to receive international recognition from the congress.
whoIsAffected: Director Saleha Sacar.
whatChanges: A copy goes to the honoree. Nothing else follows from it.
readings.insight: Its sole author is MP Modayao M. Sacar, who shares the honoree's surname; the resolution does not state any relationship. He was among the 30 first-BTA members not reappointed, as listed in Resolution No. 271.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament urges the Bangsamoro Government to commend outgoing President Rodrigo Roa Duterte. The resolution goes to the Office of the Chief Minister.

Filed by MP Narciso Co Yu Ekey and 13 others. Adopted on 23 June 2022, a week before his term ended.
readings.whyProposed: Under the Constitution, Duterte's term ended at noon on 30 June 2022. The resolution credits him with the Bangsamoro Organic Law and the creation of BARMM, a COVID-19 response including the national vaccination drive, PCR laboratories and bio-surveillance, and continued Build Build Build infrastructure. Its preamble suggests that the Bangsamoro Information Office help local governments use social media to show the Bangsamoro Government's appreciation on 30 June 2022.
whoIsAffected: The Office of the Chief Minister and the Bangsamoro Government.
implementedBy: Office of the Chief Minister
whatChanges: It asks the executive to commend the outgoing President. The social media idea stays in the preamble; the operative clauses do not direct the Information Office to do anything.
readings.insight: Parliament had already thanked Duterte itself 8 days earlier, in Resolution No. 246, for the Organic Law and the BTA extension. This one asks the executive to do the same.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament congratulates the Philippine delegation to the 31st Southeast Asian Games in Hanoi, Vietnam, the Philippine Sports Commission, and the 227 Philippine medallists, among them Alnakran "Ran" Abdilla of Tawi-Tawi. Copies go to the Sports Commission and to Abdilla.

Filed by MP Abdullah B. Hashim and MP Eddie M. Alih. Adopted on 19 July 2022.
readings.whyProposed: The Games ran from 12 to 23 May 2022, with 40 sports, 526 events and athletes from 11 countries. The Philippines finished fourth with 52 gold, 70 silver and 105 bronze medals. Abdilla won bronze in men's beach volleyball. The resolution credits the laws creating the Philippine Sports Commission (Republic Act No. 6847) and the National Academy of Sports (Republic Act No. 11470).
whoIsAffected: The Philippine SEA Games delegation and the Philippine Sports Commission.
Alnakran Abdilla.
whatChanges: Copies go to the Sports Commission and to Abdilla. Nothing else follows from it.
readings.insight: The medal counts add up: 52, 70 and 105 make 227. Abdilla, a bronze medallist in beach volleyball, is the only athlete the resolution names; the rest of the honour goes to the national team.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament commends Nur-Hafeizah Jannah I. Abinal for placing 5th, with a rating of 87.33%, among 4,442 examinees in the May 2022 Certified Public Accountant Licensure Examination. A copy goes to her.

Filed by MP Maisara Dandamun Latiph and MP Eddie M. Alih. Adopted on 19 July 2022.
readings.whyProposed: The Professional Regulation Commission released the results on 10 June 2022: 990 of the 4,442 examinees passed, 22.29%. Abinal, from Marantao, Lanao del Sur, graduated summa cum laude and class valedictorian in Accountancy from Mindanao State University–Main Campus in Marawi, with a grade average of 1.10, among 2,000 graduates of her batch. She was earlier an exchange student at Earl Warren High School in San Antonio, Texas.
whoIsAffected: Nur-Hafeizah Jannah I. Abinal.
whatChanges: A copy goes to the honoree. Nothing else follows from it.
readings.insight: One of several commendations of CPA board topnotchers; the index has others in 2023 and 2024 (Resolutions No. 360, 400 and 468). The passing-rate figures check: 990 of 4,442 is 22.29%.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament congratulates and commends the 7,145 MILF and MNLF members who passed the NAPOLCOM Special Qualifying Eligibility Examination. A copy goes to the MILF and the MNLF.

Filed by MP Baintan A. Ampatuan. Adopted on 19 July 2022.
readings.whyProposed: The Organic Law lets NAPOLCOM waive the age, height and education requirements for MILF and MNLF members entering the Philippine National Police, for 5 years after the law's ratification, with 15 years to meet the education requirement. NAPOLCOM Resolution No. 2022-0081, approved on 8 February 2022, made the special exam the eligibility for temporary appointment as Patrolman or Patrolwoman. On 29 May 2022, 11,033 MILF and MNLF members took it in Cotabato City and Lamitan City, Basilan; 7,145 passed.
whoIsAffected: The 7,145 MILF and MNLF members who passed.
The MILF and the MNLF.
whatChanges: Copies go to the MILF and the MNLF. Nothing else follows from it.
readings.insight: The resolution itself says passing does not guarantee recruitment: passers still face training, body-mass, agility, medical, dental and drug tests, background checks and a board interview. The window for the waived entry is limited to 5 years from ratification of the Organic Law. 2 small slips in the adopted text: it calls 12 July 2022, the results date, a Monday (it was a Tuesday), and gives the pass rate as 64.77% where 7,145 of 11,033 is 64.76%.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament expresses its condolences to the family of former Japanese Prime Minister Shinzo Abe and its gratitude for his contribution to peace and development in the Bangsamoro. A copy goes to his family.

Filed by MP Baintan A. Ampatuan and 6 others. Adopted on 19 July 2022.
readings.whyProposed: Abe was shot while campaigning in Nara and died on 8 July 2022, aged 67. He was Japan's longest-serving prime minister (2006–2007 and 2012–2020). The resolution recalls his support for the Mindanao peace process, from his 9 December 2006 visit to his 2014 hope that Mindanao would share in "the dividends of peace". It credits Japan under him with a grant for socio-economic infrastructure and TESDA centres in the region, support for the BTA's transition and capacity-building, and Japan's hosting of the 4 August 2011 meeting of President Benigno Aquino III with MILF Chairman Murad Ebrahim, the first step to the peace agreement.
whoIsAffected: The family of Shinzo Abe.
whatChanges: A copy goes to the family. Nothing else follows from it.
readings.insight: One of 2 condolence resolutions for foreign leaders in 2022; Resolution No. 267 followed for Queen Elizabeth II. This one rests on a direct link, Japan's role in the MILF talks and its aid to the region.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament asks government agencies operating in BARMM to respect a hijab policy in government business, and asks the Bangsamoro Human Rights Commission (BHRC) and the Bangsamoro Women Commission (BWC) to promote it. It asks regional agencies to apply Civil Service Commission Memorandum Circular No. 20, s. 2014: the hijab is allowed in all government institutions; Muslim women in hospitals and care institutions may wear it at work; and agencies that take photographs, for passports, licensure exams, clearances and the like, may set conditions that do not run against the modesty and privacy the veil represents.

It also says BARMM ministries and offices are required to put safeguards for women's modesty and privacy in place, and asks the BHRC and BWC to draft hijab guidelines and monitor them. Copies go to the Commission on Human Rights and the Philippine Commission on Women. Filed by MP Aida M. Silongan and 6 others. Adopted on 28 July 2022.
readings.whyProposed: Muslim women had reported being asked to remove the hijab or show their ears for National ID and passport photos, which the resolution says is not required in other regions such as Metro Manila, and some regional agencies had not followed national rules on religious dress. The resolution cites freedom of religion in the Constitution, Section 28 of the Magna Carta of Women, a 2013 Commission on Human Rights advisory, NBI Memorandum No. 28, s. 2008, and CSC Memorandum Circular No. 20, s. 2014.
whoIsAffected: Muslim women dealing with or working in government offices in BARMM.
Government agencies operating in BARMM, national and regional.
implementedBy: Government agencies operating in BARMM
BARMM ministries and offices
Bangsamoro Human Rights Commission
Bangsamoro Women Commission
whatChanges: It requests compliance and asks 2 regional commissions for advocacy, guidelines and monitoring.
The clause that "requires" BARMM ministries to set safeguards has no enforcement or deadline; the binding rule it relies on is the existing CSC circular.
readings.insight: The adopted text moves from requesting to requiring in its third clause, but a resolution of this kind cannot bind the national agencies, such as those issuing IDs and passports, that the complaints were about. The hijab came up repeatedly: Resolution No. 131 (2021) and No. 313 (2023) backed national bills declaring 1 February National Hijab Day, and Resolution No. 190 (2021) commended a jail officer who campaigned for hijab uniforms in the BJMP.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament commends 12 young Bangsamoro athletes who won the overall championship, with 25 medals (11 gold, 6 silver and 8 bronze), at the Pan Asian International Jiu Jitsu Competition at Ayala Malls Circuit, Makati, on 26 June 2022. The resolution is to be presented to the 12 athletes.

Filed by MP Lanang T. Ali Jr. and MP Eddie M. Alih. Adopted on 28 July 2022.
readings.whyProposed: The team was guided by coach Abdul Aziz Talusan. The resolution lists all 12 with their medals: Sittie Farhana Ebrahim won 2 golds, and Muiz, Ashzahir and Asharook Abobakar took 3 golds between them. It says the athletes did this despite limited financial support.
whoIsAffected: The 12 athletes and their coach.
whatChanges: The resolution is presented to the athletes. Nothing else follows from it.
readings.insight: Parliament honoured the same team twice on the same day. Resolution No. 263 congratulates them too, but counts 16 athletes, not 12, over 25–26 June, and names 2 coaches. Both give the same 25 medals, and the list here adds up to 11, 6 and 8. This list also includes the coach, Talusan, among the 12 athletes, with a bronze.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament extends its condolences on the murder of Atty. Ruayna Edris Sayyadi, COMELEC Election Officer of Al-Barka, Basilan. The resolution goes to her family, and a copy goes to the Philippine National Police of Isabela City for appropriate action.

Filed by MP Romeo C. Saliga, MP Ustadz Abdulmuhmin A. Mujahid and MP Eddie M. Alih. Adopted on 28 July 2022.
readings.whyProposed: Sayyadi was shot dead by an unidentified gunman at about 3:15 pm on 19 July 2022 while working on voter registration at the COMELEC satellite office in Barangay Doña Ramona, Isabela City. The resolution calls the killing cowardly and barbaric, says repeated crimes in the area call for more police visibility, and calls on authorities to investigate and bring the perpetrators to justice.
whoIsAffected: Atty. Sayyadi's family.
COMELEC staff working in Basilan and Isabela City.
implementedBy: Philippine National Police, Isabela City
whatChanges: A copy goes to the Isabela City police for appropriate action. It sets no deadline and asks for no report.
readings.insight: The adopted text consolidates 2 proposals, PR 798 and PR 799. It is not the last such case: in April 2025 Resolution No. 544 condemned the killing of another election officer, of Datu Odin Sinsuat, in a stronger form that named investigating agencies.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament congratulates the Bangsamoro martial arts athletes on their performance at the Pan Asian International Jiu Jitsu Competition at Ayala Malls Circuit, Makati. Copies go to the athletes, the Office of the Chief Minister, the Bangsamoro Sports Commission, the Bangsamoro Youth Commission and Wartime MMA Gym.

Filed by MP Abdullah B. Hashim. Adopted on 28 July 2022.
readings.whyProposed: On 25–26 June 2022, 16 Bangsamoro athletes trained by coaches Abdulaziz Talusan and Mohannad S. Biruar, with Triple A Bros Academy Jiu-Jitsu and Wartime MMA Gym in Cotabato City, won 11 gold, 6 silver and 8 bronze medals, 25 in all. Sittie Farhana N. Ebrahim won 2 golds. The resolution cites the Constitution and the Organic Law on promoting sports and youth fitness.
whoIsAffected: The athletes and their gyms.
The Bangsamoro Sports Commission and Youth Commission.
whatChanges: Copies go to the athletes, the Chief Minister's office and 2 commissions. Nothing else follows from it.
readings.insight: A duplicate of Resolution No. 261, adopted the same day for the same tournament and the same 25 medals. The 2 texts disagree on the team: 12 athletes there, 16 here. Mohannad Biruar is a coach here and one of the medalling athletes there.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament extends its sympathy and condolences to the family of Dr. Ameril Sanday Usman and honours his service to the Bangsamoro people. The resolution is sent to his family.

Filed by MP Susana S. Anayatin and 16 others. Adopted on 20 September 2022, in the second session of the second BTA.
readings.whyProposed: Usman was Director-General of the Ministry of Health and concurrent officer-in-charge of the Iranun District Hospital in Parang, Maguindanao. He started as a resident physician at Cotabato Regional and Medical Center in 2008, served at Dinaig Municipal Hospital (2014–2016), headed the ministry's disaster risk reduction health unit and was OIC Minister of Health. He led the Bangsamoro COVID-19 task force, helped set up RT-PCR laboratories in every province and cold-chain facilities, and was the first in BARMM to receive a COVID-19 vaccine. He pushed for the Iranun District Hospital, hospital modernisation and health units in every municipality and barangay.
whoIsAffected: Dr. Usman's family.
The Ministry of Health, which lost its Director-General.
whatChanges: A copy goes to the family. Nothing else follows from it.
deliberation: 20 September 2022: MP Candao supported the condolence resolutions, saying Dr. Usman had supported all her projects under her 2020 Transitional Development Impact Fund.
20 September 2022: MP Ali (L), Jr. suggested dispensing with the period of amendments and approving the consolidated resolution subject to style, as it was only an expression of condolences.
20 September 2022: The consolidated resolution (Proposed Resolutions No. 14, 15 and 29) was approved subject to style; the proposed index records it as adopted Resolution No. 264.
readings.insight: The adopted text consolidates 3 proposals, PR 14, PR 15 and PR 29, from the second BTA's new numbering. The resolution does not give the date or cause of his death.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament re-affirms the BTA's consensus on the appointment of Sheik Khalipha Usman Nando as Wali, the ceremonial head of the Bangsamoro Government, under the Bangsamoro Organic Law. A copy goes to Nando.

Filed by MP Baintan A. Ampatuan. Adopted on 21 September 2022.
readings.whyProposed: Republic Act No. 11593 extended the transition, keeping the BTA as interim government until 30 June 2025. The second BTA had just been appointed. Nando had been appointed Wali by the interim Chief Minister before the extension, and the resolution says he meets the qualifications in Section 2, Article VIII of the Organic Law, served with dedication, and has the moral standing to represent the government.
whoIsAffected: Sheik Khalipha Usman Nando.
The office of the Wali.
whatChanges: It records the second BTA's consent to keep Nando as Wali. No new appointment is made.
deliberation: 21 September 2022: MP Ramos asked whether the BOL requires a list from the Council of Leaders before the Parliament passes a resolution on the Wali; MP Ampatuan said Resolution No. 1 of 2019 was the precedent and the interim government cannot rebuild every process at once.
21 September 2022: MP Sema (OY) objected to MP Ramos calling the BOL the Members' 'bible', saying it is their basic law, and reserved his vote while awaiting the Chief Minister's position.

21 September 2022: MP Babao countered that appointing the Wali is within the Chief Minister's exclusive power and that waiting for a Council of Leaders would be difficult since the Wali convenes the session.

21 September 2022: MP Basman cited the Bangsamoro Administrative Code on the Wali's term; MP Ampatuan replied the Code cannot amend Section 4, Article VIII of the BOL and the first Wali's term should be 3 years.

21 September 2022: MP Tago said the BOL's Wali provisions apply to the regular government and the BTA's Wali continues until a successor is appointed; the Chair agreed Article VIII applies once a regular government exists.
21 September 2022: Approved subject to style; the proposed index records it as adopted Resolution No. 266.
readings.insight: This repeats Resolution No. 1 (29 March 2019), in which the first BTA expressed its consensus on Nando's appointment. The second BTA re-affirmed it within days of convening. Nando died 5 months later; Resolution No. 315 (17 February 2023) expressed condolences, and Resolution No. 445 (13 May 2024) backed a successor. The adopted text carries proposed-resolution number PR 02.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament expresses its condolences to the royal family of Queen Elizabeth II of the United Kingdom and other Commonwealth realms and recognises her as the longest-serving monarch in British history. A copy goes to the family through the British Embassy in Manila.

Filed by MP Lanang T. Ali Jr. and 6 others. Adopted on 21 September 2022.
readings.whyProposed: The Queen died on 8 September 2022, aged 96, after more than 70 years on the throne. The resolution recalls her reign through decolonisation in Africa, the Troubles, devolution, and Britain's entry into and exit from Europe, her patronage of more than 3,000 charities, and her honours for Filipinos and praise of Filipino nurses. It notes that the Philippines and the UK have had diplomatic ties since 4 July 1946, and that the UK sat on the International Contact Group that supported the government–MILF talks in Kuala Lumpur.
whoIsAffected: The British royal family.
whatChanges: A copy goes through the British Embassy. Nothing else follows from it.
deliberation: 21 September 2022: Interpellation and amendments dispensed with on omnibus motion; approved subject to style (adopted Resolution No. 267).
readings.insight: The Bangsamoro link is in a single clause: the UK's seat on the International Contact Group in the MILF peace talks. It follows Resolution No. 259 (July 2022) for Shinzo Abe, whose link was much more direct.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament adopts new Rules, Procedures, and Practices of the BTA Parliament, replacing the rules the first BTA adopted, in 34 rules over 39 pages. They cover Members' rights and duties, officers (the Speaker, Deputy Speakers, and Majority and Minority Floor Leaders), sessions, quorum, the order of business, privilege hour, the Chief Minister's Hour, question hour, committees, subpoena and contempt, bills and resolutions, debate, motions, discipline, broadcasting, and how to amend the rules.

Plenary sits from 1:00 pm, Monday to Thursday, in the third and fourth weeks of the month. Quorum is 50% plus 1 of Members, and Members may count as present by teleconference for disability, contagious illness or force majeure. There are 17 statutory committees and 7 parliamentary ones, including a Special Committee on Marawi. The Chief Minister or a Cabinet member reports on the first Wednesday of each quarter, and question hour fills the first Wednesday of other months. The rules take effect 15 days after publication in a newspaper of general circulation.

Filed by MP Sha Elijah B. Dumama-Alba and 7 others. Adopted on 22 September 2022.
readings.whyProposed: The second BTA had just taken office. Section 25, Article VII of the Organic Law says Parliament adopts its own rules, and the first BTA's rules (Resolution No. 6, 2019, as amended) had governed the old membership.
whoIsAffected: All Members of Parliament.
Ministers, resource persons and the public who appear before Parliament or follow it.
implementedBy: Bangsamoro Transition Authority Parliament
Committee on Rules
whatChanges: This is an internal-rules resolution, so it binds Parliament: it is the rulebook later resolutions amend (Resolutions No. 494 in 2024 and 566 in 2026 cite it by number).
Amending it needs a majority of all Members.
deliberation: 21 September 2022: MP Ampatuan asked whether Members attending via Zoom was governed by the proposed rules; MP Dumama-Alba said they were still observing the provisionally adopted old Rules, and the Chair said video conferencing was meant to be temporary.

21 September 2022: MP Ampatuan's proposals to delete 'as far as practicable' from the 3-day Order of Business rule and to drop the Chief Minister's written-statement option were not accepted, though her proviso that 1 vice-chairperson per committee come from the minority was accepted.

21 September 2022: MP Ramos won new committees on Women, Youth and Children (to which MP Babao added Persons with Disabilities), but her proposed committees on Cultural Heritage, Electoral Processes and Petitions were rejected by MP Dumama-Alba.
21 September 2022: MP Alamia's amendment changing a 2/3 vote to a simple majority and allowing video conference or hybrid sessions was accepted.
21 September 2022: MP Dumama-Alba counter-proposed that plenary sessions start at 1 p.m., Monday to Thursday of the third and fourth week of each month, instead of MP Ampatuan's 9 a.m. proposal.
21 September 2022: Adopted subject to style as the Rules, Procedures and Practices of the BTA Parliament (adopted Resolution No. 268).
readings.insight:
Compared with the first BTA's rules, the Chief Minister's Hour has gone from monthly (Resolution No. 31) to quarterly, sitting days run Monday to Thursday, and there are 17 statutory committees instead of 15. The text is not consistent with itself. Rule VII, Section 1 sets the quorum at 50% plus 1 "in plenary or in any committee", while Section 4 of the same rule sets committee quorum at 30%. Suspension of a Member is capped at 60 calendar days in Rule XX, at 30 days in Section 1 of Rule XXVIII, and at 6 months in Section 4 of the same rule.

The posted file's name reads "House Rules as of March 14 2023", but the document shows no amendments and is signed as adopted on 22 September 2022. It carries proposed-resolution number PR 28.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament commends President Ferdinand "Bongbong" Romualdez Marcos Jr. and thanks him for honouring and sustaining the gains of the peace agreements, which brought the MILF and MNLF together in the BTA for the first time. The resolution is presented to the President.

Filed by MP Baintan A. Ampatuan. Adopted on 22 September 2022.
readings.whyProposed: Republic Act No. 11593 let the President appoint 80 new interim BTA members to serve until 30 June 2025. Marcos swore them in on 12 August 2022, just over a month after his inauguration; the resolution quotes UN Resident Coordinator Gustavo Gonzalez praising the prompt appointment. 41 members were nominated by the MILF and 39 by the national government, some aligned with MNLF founder Nur Misuari. The resolution credits OPAPRU's "convergence" of the 1976, 1996 and 2014 agreements, quotes Secretary Carlito Galvez Jr. calling it the BTA of a "United BARMM", and also thanks Galvez.
whoIsAffected: President Marcos.
OPAPRU Secretary Carlito Galvez Jr., thanked in the preamble.
whatChanges: A copy goes to the President. Nothing else follows from it.
deliberation: 21 September 2022: MP Mantawil added a whereas clause on Chief Minister Ebrahim's vision of 'one united Bangsamoro' and struck 'warring members of' before 'MNLF and MILF'; both were accepted.
21 September 2022: Adopted subject to style (adopted Resolution No. 269).
readings.insight: The adopted text is dated 22 September 2022; Parliament's index lists 21 September. The MILF and government numbers, 41 and 39, add up to the 80 members. Resolution No. 271, 4 days later, honours the 30 first-BTA members the President did not reappoint. The adopted text carries proposed-resolution number PR 03.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament expresses its condolences on the death of Abdulwalid "Jimmy" M. Radiamoda, Base Commander of the 122nd Base Command of the Bangsamoro Islamic Armed Forces, and its gratitude for his part in the Bangsamoro struggle for self-determination. The resolution is sent to his family.

Filed by MP Ali B. Solaiman, MP Said M. Shiek, MP Basit S. Abbas, MP Abdullah G. Macapaar, MP Marjanie S. Macasalong and MP Amroussi A. Macatanong. Adopted on 22 September 2022.
readings.whyProposed: Radiamoda died on 20 September 2022. The resolution says he defended Camp Nusa in the 1977 war and led his men in defending MILF camps in the 2000, 2003 and 2008 wars, and that as commander he kept his area peaceful, helped arrest criminals, especially drug pushers and users, and settled local feuds.
whoIsAffected: Commander Radiamoda's family and the 122nd Base Command.
whatChanges: A copy goes to the family. Nothing else follows from it.
deliberation: 21 September 2022: Interpellation and amendments dispensed with; adopted subject to style (adopted Resolution No. 270).
readings.insight: Adopted 2 days after his death. The adopted text is dated 22 September 2022; Parliament's index lists 21 September. Resolution No. 454 (2024) is a later condolence for another BIAF base commander.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament commends the 30 members of the first BTA whom President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. did not reappoint to the second BTA, and sends the resolution to each of them. They are Zul Qarneyn M. Abas, Ziaur-Rahman A. Adiong, Abdulla A. Ahang, Faiz S. Alauddin, Zesar H. Alil, Muslima A. Asmawil, Hamid Aminoddin D. Barra, Abraham T. Burahan, Musa K.S. Diamla, Saffrullah M. Dipatuan, Hadji Abduladzis M. Esmael, Bainon G. Karon, Maisara D. Latiph, Mussolini S. Lidasan, Jamel D. Macaraya, Khadafeh G. Mangudadatu, Malik A. Mantawil, Datu Tucao O. Mastura, Sittie Shahara I. Mastura, Datu Midpantao M. Midtimbang, Ustadz Abdulmuhmin A. Mujahid, Edrieza H.N. Rimbang, Modayao M. Sacar, Al-Syed A. Sali, Romeo C. Saliga, Punduma B. Sani, Alzad T. Sattar, Sahie S. Udjah, Melanio U. Ulama and Narciso C. Yu Ekey.

Filed by MP Susana S. Anayatin and MP Eddie M. Alih. Adopted on 26 September 2022.
readings.whyProposed: The resolution credits the outgoing members with the laws the first BTA passed and its work on the priority codes the Organic Law assigns to the transition: the Administrative, Revenue, Electoral, Local Government and Education Codes. It thanks them for their part in crafting the Organic Law and in the peace effort.
whoIsAffected: The 30 former Members named.
whatChanges: Copies go to the 30 former Members. Nothing else follows from it.
deliberation: 26 September 2022: Interpellation terminated and approved subject to style (adopted Resolution No. 271).
readings.insight: Several of the 30 had authored resolutions only weeks earlier: MP Ustadz Abdulmuhmin A. Mujahid was sole author of Resolution No. 250 and MP Modayao M. Sacar of No. 254, and MP Romeo C. Saliga, MP Maisara D. Latiph and MP Narciso C. Yu Ekey filed several others in mid-2022. The adopted text carries proposed-resolution number PR 01, the first number in the second BTA's series. The quoted Organic Law text misnumbers "Functions and Priorities" as Section 3; the resolution's own lead-in calls it Section 4.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament urges the concerned agencies and local government units of the region to adopt measures to keep the 2019 Novel Coronavirus (2019-nCoV) out of the Bangsamoro region. It names 3 measures, without limiting the list: a public awareness campaign by the Ministry of Health and the Ministry of Education; distribution of masks, disinfectants and other hygiene kits by the Ministry of Health; and proper mandatory quarantine of arriving passengers by local governments with seaports and airports.

The resolution goes to the concerned agencies and local governments for information and immediate action. Authored by MPs Ziaur-Rahman A. Adiong, Pangalian M. Balindong, Omar Yasser C. Sema and Don Mustapha A. Loong. Adopted on 31 January 2020.
readings.whyProposed: The Organic Law charges the Bangsamoro Government with protecting the people's right to health. The resolution cites the World Health Organization's count of 7,783 confirmed cases as of 30 January 2020, 7,678 of them in mainland China, with about 170 deaths, and the Department of Health's confirmation of the first Philippine case: a 38-year-old Chinese woman from Wuhan who arrived via Hong Kong on 21 January 2020.
whoIsAffected: Residents of the region.
Passengers arriving through the region's seaports and airports, who would be quarantined.
Local governments with seaports and airports.
implementedBy: Ministry of Health
Ministry of Basic, Higher and Technical Education
Local government units of the region with seaports and airports
whatChanges: It is an urging; it sets no deadline, standard or report back to Parliament.
Copies go to the concerned agencies and local governments.
readings.insight: It is the earliest of Parliament's pandemic resolutions in the index. The text assigns the awareness campaign to a 'Ministry of Education', not the Ministry of Basic, Higher and Technical Education by name. The pandemic stayed on the agenda: Resolution 74 (18 June 2020) commended frontliners, Resolution 81 (21 July 2020) asked the education ministry for its learning continuity plan, and Resolution 113 (17 March 2021) backed the vaccination plans.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament expresses its sense that all offices and schools should develop activities to commemorate the anniversary of the Jabidah Massacre every 18 March. It requires all other ministries and commissions to hold programs and activities for the anniversary. It requires the Bangsamoro Human Rights Commission and the Ministry of Basic, Higher and Technical Education to develop comprehensive policies and programs commemorating the massacre and all other historical injustices against the Bangsamoro people, so that they never happen again.

Authored by MP Rasol Y. Mitmug Jr. Adopted on 19 February 2020.
readings.whyProposed: The Organic Law tasks Parliament with a transitional justice mechanism for historical injustices. The resolution recounts that on 18 March 1968 at least 23 Muslim army recruits of a commando unit named Jabidah were shot on Corregidor Island; that the sole survivor, Jibin Arula, was rescued by 2 fishermen; that Senator Benigno Aquino Jr. exposed the killing on 28 March 1968; and that it led to the Muslim Independence Movement and later the MNLF. It notes that President Benigno Aquino III acknowledged the massacre on its 45th anniversary in 2013, and that opinion pieces have since branded it 'fake news'. 18 March 2020 was the 52nd anniversary.
whoIsAffected: Ministries, commissions, offices and schools in the region, which are to hold commemorative activities.
Students, through any policies the education ministry develops.
implementedBy: Bangsamoro Human Rights Commission
Ministry of Basic, Higher and Technical Education
All ministries and commissions of the Bangsamoro Government
whatChanges: It sets a yearly commemoration for regional offices on 18 March, but with no format, budget or reporting.
The human rights commission and the education ministry are tasked to write policies and programs, with no deadline.
readings.insight: The title says 'requiring', and 2 clauses do require, but for offices and schools in general the operative clause only 'encourages'. No ministry is asked to report what it did. The transitional justice mechanism the first clause points to came almost 6 years later, with the Bangsamoro Transitional Justice and Reconciliation Act (BAA 89), ratified on 28 January 2026. This is the only resolution in the index to name the Jabidah Massacre.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament resolves to constitute, on its side, the Philippine Congress-Bangsamoro Parliament Forum that the Organic Law requires, and names its delegates: the Speaker, the Deputy Speaker, the Majority Floor Leader, the Minority Floor Leader and other Members the Speaker may designate.

Authored by MPs Pangalian M. Balindong and Lanang T. Ali Jr. Adopted on 19 February 2020.
readings.whyProposed: Article VI, Section 3 of the Organic Law creates the forum for cooperation and coordination of legislative initiatives. The resolution says the interim Parliament needs Congress's help, chiefly to make sure the funding the Organic Law provides is appropriated and released, and to keep Congress informed of priority legislation during the transition. The Senate and the House had already passed concurrent resolutions constituting the forum and naming their delegates.
whoIsAffected: The 4 officers of Parliament who become delegates, and any other Members the Speaker adds.
Congress's delegates, who now have counterparts to meet.
implementedBy: Bangsamoro Transition Authority Parliament
whatChanges: It fixes, for Parliament, who sits in the forum; this binds Parliament.
It gives the forum no agenda, meeting schedule or reporting duty.
readings.insight: The title speaks of urging the Speaker to designate delegates, but the operative text designates them itself, by office. Parliament came back to the forum less than 2 years later: Resolution 193 (24 November 2021) urged it to strengthen its mechanism. Congress acted first; this resolution answers concurrent resolutions the Senate and House had already passed.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament expresses its support for the passage and enactment of the bill creating the Autonomous Region of the Cordillera, House Bill No. 5687 and Senate Bill No. 1232. Copies go to Senate President Vicente Sotto III, House Speaker Alan Peter Cayetano and the Office of the Cordillera Administrative Region, for information.

Authored by MP Baintan A. Ampatuan and 24 others. Adopted on 21 February 2020.
readings.whyProposed: The 1987 Constitution provides for autonomous regions in both Muslim Mindanao and the Cordilleras, but only the first exists. The resolution traces the Cordillera bills: House Bill No. 5343 in 2017, backed by all Cordillera representatives and every provincial and city government there; Senate Bills No. 1678, 1923 and 1930 in 2018; and now House Bill No. 5687, filed by the representatives of Abra, Apayao, Ifugao, Mountain Province, Benguet, Baguio City and Kalinga, and Senate Bill No. 1232, filed by Senator Juan Miguel Zubiri on 11 December 2019. It notes that the Cordillera's Regional Development Council had backed the ratification of the Bangsamoro Organic Law.
whoIsAffected: People of the Cordillera Administrative Region.
implementedBy: Senate of the Philippines
House of Representatives
whatChanges: Nothing changes unless Congress acts; the resolution is an expression of support sent for information.
Copies go to the Senate President, the House Speaker and the Office of the Cordillera Administrative Region.
readings.insight: The adopted text is dated 21 February 2020, while Parliament's index lists it as adopted on 19 February 2020; the date on the page image is 21 February. It returns the Cordillera Regional Development Council's earlier support for the Organic Law. The resolution itself shows the Cordillera bill had already been filed under other numbers in 2017 and 2018.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament confirms the vice chairperson, members and subcommittee officers of its Committee on Social Services. The committee has 17 seats: Chairperson MP Raissa H. Jajurie, Vice-Chairperson MP Rasul E. Ismael and 15 members, among them MPs Hamid Aminoddin D. Barra, Susana S. Anayatin, Anna Tarhata S. Basman and Maisara C. Dandamun-Latiph. The Speaker, Deputy Speaker and the 2 floor leaders sit as 4 ex officio members.

It also sets 3 subcommittees: Disadvantaged Sectors, chaired by MP Anna Tarhata S. Basman with MP Susana S. Anayatin as vice chair; Displacement and Disaster, chaired by MP Hamid Aminoddin D. Barra with MP Ali B. Solaiman; and Socio-Economic Programs, chaired by MP Maisara C. Dandamun-Latiph with MP Abdulmuhmin A. Mujahid.

Authored by MP Lanang T. Ali Jr. Adopted on 21 February 2020.
readings.whyProposed: The resolution has no WHEREAS clauses. It is a housekeeping measure confirming who sits on the committee and leads its subcommittees.
whoIsAffected: Members of Parliament named to the committee and its subcommittees.
implementedBy: Bangsamoro Transition Authority Parliament
whatChanges: It settles the committee's membership and subcommittee leadership; this binds Parliament.
It does not change the committee's jurisdiction.
readings.insight: The chairperson is listed but is not among the posts the title says are being confirmed. 6 days later Parliament made this committee the repository for data on children that ministries were asked to submit (Resolution 79, 27 February 2020).

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament resolves to cause the display of the BARMM flag, alongside the Philippine flag, in all public buildings: government offices, town halls, regional, provincial, municipal and barangay halls, public plazas, institutions of learning and other places Parliament deems appropriate.

Authored by MP Basit S. Abbas. Adopted on 21 February 2020.
readings.whyProposed: The Organic Law has Parliament adopt the region's flag and requires the Philippine flag to be displayed alongside it. The resolution notes that Parliament adopted the flag through Bangsamoro Autonomy Act No. 1 on 28 August 2019, and calls the flag the symbol of the identity, integrity and self-determination of the Bangsamoro people.
whoIsAffected: Government offices, local government halls, plazas and schools in the region.
implementedBy: Bangsamoro Government offices
Local government units of the region
whatChanges: The resolution names no office to carry it out and sets no rules on how or when the flag is flown.
It adds little in law: the display duty was already in BAA No. 1.
readings.insight: Section 4 of BAA No. 1 already requires all Bangsamoro offices, public and private schools, colleges and universities, public offices and government corporations to use and display the flag, alongside the Philippine flag. The resolution restates that duty and extends the list to plazas and barangay halls, but without penalties or guidelines. The registry records BAA No. 1 as ratified on 23 August 2019 and approved by the Chief Minister on 28 August 2019, the date the resolution gives for its adoption.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament calls on the Department of the Interior and Local Government to immediately turn over Cotabato City to the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region and place it under the supervision of the Ministry of the Interior and Local Government. It encourages the BARMM Public Information Office to use mass media to dispel claims that the city is not part of the region. Copies go to the DILG and the regional ministry.

Authored by MP Omar Yasser C. Sema. Adopted on 21 February 2020.
readings.whyProposed: Under the Organic Law, Cotabato City joins the region if a majority of its voters approve. In the 21 January 2019 plebiscite the city voted 36,682 Yes to 24,994 No, and the COMELEC proclaimed the result on 25 January 2019. More than a year later the city had still not been turned over, and claims were circulating that it was not part of the region. The authors argue the law is clear and needs only to be applied.
whoIsAffected: Residents and the city government of Cotabato City.
The regional interior ministry, which would take over supervision.
implementedBy: Department of the Interior and Local Government
Ministry of the Interior and Local Government
Bangsamoro Public Information Office
whatChanges: It is a call on a national department; Parliament cannot order the turnover itself.
Copies go to the DILG and the regional ministry.
readings.insight: The Yes vote won by 11,688 votes, about 59% of the votes cast, and the resolution was adopted 13 months after the result was proclaimed. It sets no deadline and asks for no report. The city's place in the region came up again in Resolution 384 (14 August 2023), which urged Congress to create a lone congressional district for Cotabato City.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament condemns the prejudicial treatment of Muslim youth by the Manila Police District and denounces religious and all other forms of discrimination as disgraceful and unbefitting of any government agency. It appeals to fellow public servants and government institutions to be more careful in introducing policies, so that they promote inclusion rather than exclusion.

The resolution goes to Interior Secretary Eduardo M. Año, PNP Chief Archie Francisco Gamboa and Metro Manila police chief Maj. Gen. Debold Sinas for information and appropriate action. Authored by MPs Amilbahar S. Mawallil, Anna Tarhata S. Basman, Lanang T. Ali Jr. and Marjanie S. Macasalong. Adopted on 21 February 2020.
readings.whyProposed: A 31 January 2020 memorandum of the Manila Police District's District Community Affairs and Development Division, issued on the direction of PBGEN Bernabe M. Balba, ordered station commanders to list Muslim students in Metro Manila high schools, colleges and universities, as part of measures against violent extremism. The Philippine Star posted it on 20 February 2020. The authors say the order treats young Muslims as suspects because of their religion, cite the Universal Declaration of Human Rights on privacy, and warn of unjust treatment, isolation and physical harm.
whoIsAffected: Muslim students in Metro Manila schools.
Muslim families in Manila, particularly Quiapo.
implementedBy: Department of the Interior and Local Government
Philippine National Police
Manila Police District
whatChanges: It is a statement of condemnation; it does not ask for the memorandum to be withdrawn by name.
Copies go to the DILG Secretary, the PNP Chief and the Metro Manila police chief.
readings.insight: Parliament acted within a day: the memorandum became public on 20 February 2020 and the resolution was adopted on 21 February. It condemns and appeals but makes no specific demand, such as revoking the memorandum or destroying any lists made. The concern for Muslims outside the region recurred in Resolution 80 (16 July 2020) on killings in South Cotabato.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament adopts a new calendar for the rest of its First Regular Session and repeals Resolution No. 22. It sits from 17 to 19 March, 24 to 26 March and 14 to 16 April 2020, with mandatory adjournment on 21 April 2020.

Authored by MP Lanang T. Ali Jr. Adopted on 28 February 2020.
readings.whyProposed: Parliament's rules call for plenary sessions Tuesday to Thursday in the third and fourth weeks of the month. The resolution says the new calendar will guide Members in legislative and constituency work, speed up legislation, and help Muslim Members, staff and personnel observe Friday prayer and the fasting month of Ramadan.
whoIsAffected: Members and staff of Parliament.
implementedBy: Bangsamoro Transition Authority Parliament
whatChanges: It sets Parliament's own sitting days; this binds Parliament.
It repeals the calendar in Resolution No. 22.
readings.insight: The calendar sets 3 blocks of 3 days, 9 sitting days in all. It did not survive the pandemic: Resolution 75 records that Parliament suspended regular sessions because travel restrictions made a quorum impossible, and the index lists no resolution adopted between 28 February and 17 June 2020. It was the third calendar for the First Regular Session, after Resolutions 8 and 22.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament approves the enhancement of its Parliamentary Rules, Procedures and Practices made by its Committee on Rules.

Authored by MP Lanang T. Ali Jr. Adopted on 17 June 2020.
readings.whyProposed: Several Members had filed proposed resolutions to improve the rules. After a training on parliamentary rules by Malaysian Parliament experts on 22 to 24 February 2020, the Committee on Rules met on 26 and 27 February and enhanced the rules by adopting some Malaysian rules and Members' proposals. Its report was adopted in plenary on 27 February 2020; this resolution formally approves the result.
whoIsAffected: Members of Parliament, who work under the revised rules.
implementedBy: Bangsamoro Transition Authority Parliament
whatChanges: It approves amended rules for Parliament; this binds Parliament.
The amended text is not part of the resolution, so what changed cannot be read from it.
readings.insight: The resolution approves an enhancement it does not reproduce or summarize, so a reader cannot tell from it which rules changed. Plenary had adopted the committee report on 27 February 2020; this formal approval came 16 weeks later, on the second day of the next session. The next day Parliament amended the rules again, for remote sessions (Resolution 73).

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament commends and congratulates Princess Fatima T. Parahiman for being the lone Bangsamoro topnotcher in the 2019 Bar Examination, and commends all other Bangsamoro bar passers. Copies go to Ms. Parahiman and the University of the East College of Law.

Authored by MPs Rasol Y. Mitmug Jr. and Anna Tarhata S. Basman. Adopted on 17 June 2020.
readings.whyProposed: The 2019 Bar results, released on 29 April 2020, showed 2,103 of 7,685 examinees passing, 27.36%. Ms. Parahiman, the University of the East College of Law valedictorian, from Masiu, Lanao del Sur, placed second with a rating of 89.5230%. The resolution counts her as the 4th Bangsamoro bar topnotcher, after Atty. Kamar M. Boloto (2nd, 1970), Judge Mylene Amerol-Macumbal (2nd, 2008) and Atty. Soraya Salubo Laut (8th, 2015). 74 other Bangsamoro examinees passed.
whoIsAffected: Ms. Parahiman and the 74 other Bangsamoro bar passers.
whatChanges: It is a commendation; a copy goes to Ms. Parahiman and her law school.
readings.insight: It was the first of Parliament's yearly commendations of Bangsamoro bar passers, followed by Resolutions 243, 337, 345 and 423. The page is headed 'First Regular Session', although Resolution 72, adopted the same day, opened the Second Regular Session on 16 June 2020.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament adopts the calendar for its Second Regular Session. It opens on 16 June 2020 and sits Tuesday to Thursday in 2 blocks a month: 16 to 18 and 23 to 25 June 2020; 14 to 16 and 21 to 23 July; 18 to 20 and 25 to 27 August; 15 to 17 and 22 to 24 September; 13 to 15 and 20 to 22 October; 17 to 19 and 24 to 26 November; 15 to 17 and 22 to 24 December; 19 to 21 and 26 to 28 January 2021; 16 to 18 and 23 to 25 February; and 16 to 18 March 2021. Mandatory adjournment is on 25 March 2021, closing a last block that begins 23 March.

Authored by MP Lanang T. Ali Jr. Adopted on 17 June 2020.
readings.whyProposed: The rules have the BTA convene its regular session after Eid al-Fitr and hold plenary sessions Tuesday to Thursday in the third and fourth weeks of each month. The calendar is meant to guide Members in their legislative and constituency work.
whoIsAffected: Members and staff of Parliament.
implementedBy: Bangsamoro Transition Authority Parliament
whatChanges: It sets Parliament's sitting days for the session; this binds Parliament.
readings.insight: The calendar sets 20 blocks of 3 days, 60 sitting days over 9 months, including a block ending on 24 December 2020. It was adopted a day after the opening date it sets. In practice the index shows Parliament also met outside it, in special sessions on 2 and 3 July 2020 (Resolutions 77 and 78) and on 28 October 2020 (Resolution 90).

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament amends its rules (Resolution No. 6) to allow sessions and committee hearings by teleconference, video conference or other reliable electronic means. The Speaker, after consulting the 2 floor leaders, may convene Parliament remotely in case of force majeure or a national or regional emergency that prevents or limits Members' physical presence. Members on the platform count as present for quorum, debate and voting, and a limited number chosen by the Speaker with the floor leaders may attend in the hall. Committees may meet remotely on the same grounds.

The Secretary General is to recommend and set up the technology, with the Speaker's approval, and to provide safety measures, security and the archiving of recordings as part of Parliament's records. The amendment also rewrites the convening rule: the regular session opens the second Tuesday after Eid al-Fitr, and the Chief Minister presents the Government's policies and programs at its start.

Authored by MPs Amilbahar S. Mawallil, Baintan A. Ampatuan, Omar Yasser C. Sema and Suharto M. Ambolodto. Adopted on 18 June 2020.
readings.whyProposed: President Duterte declared a public health emergency through Proclamation No. 922 on 8 March 2020. From 1 June 2020 the region was under modified general community quarantine, limiting gatherings to 50% of venue capacity and giving alternative work arrangements to people aged 60 and above. Confirmed cases nationwide had reached 15,588 by 28 May 2020. The authors say quarantine should not stop Parliament from passing laws and appropriations, especially those for the pandemic response.
whoIsAffected: Members of Parliament, who may now attend, debate and vote remotely.
The Secretariat, which must run and secure the system.
implementedBy: Bangsamoro Transition Authority Parliament
Office of the Secretary General
whatChanges: This binds Parliament: remote attendance now counts for quorum and votes.
The Speaker decides when to go remote, after consulting the floor leaders, and issues the guidelines.
readings.insight: The title names Rule VIII and Rule XIII, but the resolution also amends Rule VI, Section 5, and changes when the regular session opens: Resolutions 69 and 72 quote the old rule as the third Tuesday of the month following Eid al-Fitr, and this one sets the second Tuesday after Eid al-Fitr. It was adopted the day after Resolution 70 approved a broader set of rules changes, Resolution 75, a week later, records that regular sessions had been suspended because quarantine rules made a quorum impossible.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament honors the heroism, bravery, dedication and service of all Bangsamoro frontliners fighting COVID-19. It reaffirms the Bangsamoro Government's responsibility to serve and protect the people as the spread of the disease is curbed, and resolves to publish the resolution in news outlets of general circulation.

Authored by MP Sittie Shahara I. Mastura and 10 others. Adopted on 18 June 2020.
readings.whyProposed: The resolution traces the pandemic from the first reports from Wuhan to Proclamation No. 922 and the Ministry of Health's Code Red alert in all of the region's health facilities on 10 March 2020. As of 24 March 2020, the region's task force reported 6,162 persons under monitoring, 173 persons under investigation and 4 confirmed cases, 2 of whom had died. Frontliners kept working despite exposure and shortages of protective equipment, and some had to self-quarantine.
whoIsAffected: Health workers and other frontliners in the region.
whatChanges: It is a commendation; the only action it sets is publication in news outlets.
readings.insight: The figures it cites are from 24 March 2020; the resolution was adopted nearly 3 months later, and consolidates 2 proposed resolutions (PR 223 and PR 241). It commends but provides no benefit. Resolution 155 (15 September 2021) later called on the Office of the Chief Minister to give financial assistance to frontline healthcare workers.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament extends again the phase-out of accountable officers of the former ARMM, including finance officers and selected support staff, to 31 December 2020, unless they are replaced sooner once accountability reports and physical accomplishments are settled.

Heads of ministries and agencies submit lists of officers needing extension to the Chief Minister for approval, and the Office of the Chief Minister furnishes Parliament a copy. The extended staff keep their current posts unless replaced or newly appointed, and their pay is charged to the Miscellaneous Personnel Benefits Fund in the FY 2020 Bangsamoro Appropriations Act. Heads may designate a subordinate when an accountable officer is absent or refuses to continue, hiring continues under health protocols, and the Office of the Chief Minister may issue guidelines.

Authored by MPs Eduard U. Guerra, Raissa H. Jajurie and Ubaida C. Pacasem. Adopted on 25 June 2020.
readings.whyProposed: Resolution No. 54 had extended the phase-out to 31 March 2020. Then the President declared a 6-month state of calamity on 16 March 2020, quarantines halted the region's hiring, and Parliament itself suspended sessions for lack of a quorum. In the gap, the Interim Chief Minister's Executive Order No. 02, s. 2020 let former ARMM staff serve until 30 June 2020. With financial reports, property inventories and clearances still pending after months on a skeleton workforce, Parliament judged a further extension necessary. The resolution notes that extending the phase-out amends the Transition Plan and needs a majority vote of all BTA Members.
whoIsAffected: Accountable officers, finance officers and support staff of the former ARMM whose service is extended.
Ministries and agencies still closing ARMM-era accounts.
implementedBy: Office of the Chief Minister
Bangsamoro ministries and agencies

funding.detail: No amount is named. Salaries and wages of extended personnel are charged to the Miscellaneous Personnel Benefits Fund of the FY 2020 Bangsamoro Appropriations Act.

whatChanges: It extends the service of select former ARMM personnel to 31 December 2020.
The Chief Minister approves who is extended; Parliament only receives a copy of the list.
readings.insight: After Resolution 54 lapsed on 31 March 2020, the only extension the resolution cites is the Chief Minister's executive order, though the resolution itself says such an extension amends the Transition Plan and needs a majority of all BTA Members. It was adopted 5 days before the order's 30 June cut-off. The resolution does not say how many people are covered. Resolution 95 (16 December 2020) extended the phase-out again, to 30 June 2021.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament authorizes BTA Members to use their own maintenance and other operating expenses (MOOE) for support operations and response measures needed to address the COVID-19 emergency, consistent with the national policy in Republic Act No. 11469, the Bayanihan to Heal as One Act. The Office of the Speaker is to issue guidelines, in consultation with the Committee on Finance and the Committee on Accounts.

Authored by MP Lanang T. Ali Jr. Adopted on 25 June 2020.
readings.whyProposed: The resolution argues that the region was hit hardest and helped least. It cites Philippine Statistics Authority data of 61% poverty incidence in 2018, about 2.5 million people below a poverty line of ₱11,482 a month for a family of 5; an unemployment rate of 29.8%, the highest in the country; and only 506,954 emergency cash subsidy slots, the lowest allocation of any region. A June 2020 survey it calls 'our' found 28% of respondents had received no government support and 90% had lost income. Members who chose to spend their MOOE on aid, it says, could make a substantial contribution.
whoIsAffected: Constituents affected by the pandemic who may receive aid from Members.
Members of Parliament, who gain discretion over how their MOOE is spent.
implementedBy: Bangsamoro Transition Authority Parliament
Office of the Speaker
Committee on Finance
Committee on Accounts

funding.detail: No amount is named. Members may use their existing MOOE allocations for COVID-19 assistance; the resolution sets no ceiling.

whatChanges: It lets Members redirect their office operating funds to pandemic aid; the guidelines are left to the Speaker.
Use is voluntary, and the resolution sets no reporting on what each Member spends or on whom.
readings.insight: The resolution gives no figure for Members' MOOE, no ceiling, and no requirement to report how much was spent or who received help, leaving all of that to guidelines from the Office of the Speaker. The 'June 2020 Survey Research' it cites is called 'our' survey but is not otherwise identified. It builds on Resolution No. 28 (30 August 2019), which gave the 80 Members continuing MOOE without a set figure.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament respectfully appeals to President Rodrigo Roa Duterte to veto Senate Bill No. 1083 and House Bill No. 6875, the Anti-Terrorism Act of 2020, so that Congress can review and address its vagueness, overbreadth and other concerns. Copies go to the Office of the President and the Office of the Chief Minister.

Authored by MP Mohagher M. Iqbal and 11 others. Adopted on 2 July 2020.
