readings.whyProposed: The resolution states that the Senate approved the bill on 29 February 2020 and the House adopted it on third reading on 3 June 2020, so the enrolled bill awaited the President's signature. Parliament says it supports strengthening counter-terrorism law but objects to 4 provisions: warrantless arrests beyond the Rules of Court; wiretapping on ex parte application to the Court of Appeals with no chance for the suspect to respond; detention of 14 to 24 days without a court commitment order; and designation of persons or groups as terrorists by an executive-appointed Anti-Terrorism Council with no court remedy. It draws on the Bangsamoro experience that counter-terrorism without regard for human rights cannot defeat violent extremism, and cites the Chief Minister's statement of 22 June 2020.
whoIsAffected: Residents of the region, particularly conflict-affected communities the resolution says could be targeted.
Anyone subject to arrest, surveillance or designation under the bill.
implementedBy: Office of the President
whatChanges: It is an appeal; only the President could veto the bill.
Copies go to the Office of the President and the Office of the Chief Minister.
readings.insight: It was adopted at a special session that, according to Resolution 78, the Chief Minister had requested to deliberate on the Bangsamoro Development Plan. Parliament supported the bill's aim while asking for its veto, and it names the specific provisions it objects to. The appeal did not prevail: Resolution 464 (19 June 2024) cites the Anti-Terrorism Act's definition of terrorism.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament approves the 1st Bangsamoro Development Plan (BDP) 2020-2022 of the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region.

Authored by MP Akmad I. Abas and 71 others. Adopted on 3 July 2020.
readings.whyProposed: The Organic Law makes the Bangsamoro Economic and Development Council (BEDC) the planning body whose plans Parliament approves, and ties the national Special Development Fund for conflict-affected communities to a Bangsamoro Development Plan. Parliament created the BEDC, with the Bangsamoro Planning and Development Authority as its secretariat, through BAA No. 6 on 27 December 2019. The BEDC adopted the plan at its first meeting on 5 June 2020; Chief Minister Ahod B. Ebrahim endorsed it to Parliament on 18 June 2020 with its results matrices and investment program; Parliament deliberated in a special session on 2 and 3 July 2020.
whoIsAffected: Residents of the region, especially conflict-affected communities.
Ministries and offices whose programs the plan guides.
implementedBy: Bangsamoro Economic and Development Council
Bangsamoro Planning and Development Authority
Bangsamoro ministries and offices

funding.detail: The resolution appropriates nothing. The plan guides use of the national Special Development Fund, but no amount is stated.

whatChanges: It gives the plan Parliament's approval, which the Organic Law requires.
The plan itself is not reproduced in the resolution.
readings.insight: The 72 principal authors include most Members, among them the Chief Minister. The plan was approved 15 days after its endorsement and covers 2020 to 2022, so half of its first year had passed before approval. Its successor, the 2nd Bangsamoro Development Plan 2023-2028, was approved by Resolution 303 on 18 January 2023.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament requests all relevant ministries, through Chief Minister Ahod Balawag Ebrahim, to provide data, budget allocations and the status of children they serve, and their current, proposed and potential policies and programs to protect and promote children's rights, in aid of legislation. The Ministry of Social Services is tasked to set the format and kind of data required, and the Committee on Social Services is designated as the repository of the data.

Authored by MPs Maisara Dandamun Latiph and Suharto M. Ambolodto. Adopted on 27 February 2020.
readings.whyProposed: The Organic Law requires the Bangsamoro Government to protect children's rights, especially orphans, and to fund that duty. The resolution cites UNICEF's State of Bangsamoro Children: more than 500,000 adolescents in the region were not attending school in 2017/2018. The authors want government data, budgets and plans to identify priority programs, set funding levels and improve accountability for public money spent on children.
whoIsAffected: Children in the region, particularly those affected by conflict.
Ministries that must compile and submit data.
implementedBy: Office of the Chief Minister
Ministry of Social Services and Development
Bangsamoro ministries
Committee on Social Services
whatChanges: It is a request routed through the Chief Minister; it sets no deadline for submission.
It gives the social services ministry the job of designing the data format and makes the Committee on Social Services the data's repository.
readings.insight: Though numbered 79, it was adopted on 27 February 2020, before Resolutions 69 to 78. No deadline or follow-up is set. It builds on Resolution 48 (20 November 2019), which backed the Bangsamoro Children's Declaration. The committee named as repository had its membership confirmed 6 days earlier (Resolution 65).

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament expresses deep concern over the series of killings of Moros outside the region, particularly in Polomolok and Tupi, South Cotabato. It urges the concerned authorities to conduct an impartial, full-blown investigation to bring the perpetrators to justice, and strongly recommends that the Government and MILF Peace Implementing Panels convene and set up peace mechanisms and security to protect Moros in the area.

Copies go to President Duterte, Chief Minister Ahod Balawag Ebrahim, government panel chair Gloria J. Mercado, MILF panel chair Mohagher M. Iqbal, Interior Secretary Eduardo Año and PNP Chief Archie Francisco Gamboa. Authored by MPs Aida M. Silongan and Mohagher M. Iqbal. Adopted on 16 July 2020.
readings.whyProposed: The resolution attaches a 4 June 2020 report of the MILF Coordinating Committee on the Cessation of Hostilities. It reports the killing of Ustadz Mohammad Taha Abdulgapor, an MSU General Santos professor and ceasefire monitor, shot in General Santos City on 26 May 2020, and 15 killings of MILF members and Moro civilians since 2018. Moro men in the area were said to evacuate every night for fear of killings and police surveillance. An attached MILF Koronadal committee resolution of 8 May 2020 alleges more than 20 Moro people killed or tortured since 2017, mostly by riding-in-tandem gunmen, and warns the MILF might resist with force if nothing is done.
whoIsAffected: Moro communities in Polomolok and Tupi, South Cotabato, outside the region.
Families of the victims.
implementedBy: Philippine National Police
Department of the Interior and Local Government
Government of the Philippines and MILF Peace Implementing Panels
whatChanges: It asks for an investigation and for the peace panels to act; it binds none of them.
The region has no authority over South Cotabato, which is outside the BARMM.
deliberation: 16 July 2020: MP Jose I. Lorena's amended title, expressing the BTA's deep concern over the killings, was accepted by MP Aida M. Silongan and her co-author.
16 July 2020: Period of amendments closed and approved subject to style on motion of MP Khadafeh G. Mangudadatu.
readings.insight: Co-author MP Mohagher M. Iqbal is also the chair of the MILF Peace Implementing Panel to whom the resolution recommends action and sends a copy. The counts come from MILF bodies, not police or other official sources, and the resolution names no victim besides Ustadz Abdulgapor. Killings of Moros outside the region came up again in Resolution 89 (17 September 2020), on 9 civilians shot in Kabacan, Cotabato.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament urgently directs Minister Mohagher Iqbal of the Ministry of Basic, Higher and Technical Education to report on the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on public and private schools and higher education institutions in the region, and to present to Parliament the ministry's learning continuity plan for School Year 2020-2021. A copy goes to the Minister.

Authored by MP Maisara Dandamun Latiph. Adopted on 21 July 2020.
readings.whyProposed: Classes were set to open on 24 August 2020 for basic education and by 1 September 2020 for higher education, with no face-to-face learning until a vaccine was available. The ministry had launched its learning continuity plan on 15 June 2020, preferring home-based and distance learning. But the Minister had told a Senate hearing that internet penetration in the region was only 20%, and an ICT rights advocate estimated 5% to 7%. The author wants the problems facing learners, parents and teachers identified as policies are drawn up.
whoIsAffected: Learners, parents and teachers in public and private schools and colleges in the region.
The education ministry, which must report.
implementedBy: Ministry of Basic, Higher and Technical Education
whatChanges: It directs a report and a presentation to Parliament, but sets no date for either.
A copy goes to the Minister.
deliberation: 21 July 2020: Debate and amendments dispensed with and approved unanimously subject to style (the journal prints this approval under the number 173, evidently a misprint, as No. 173's amendments had just been deferred).
readings.insight: The resolution was adopted about a month before the 24 August school opening it cites, but gives the ministry no deadline. The minister directed to report, Mohagher Iqbal, was himself a Member and co-author of Resolution 80, adopted 5 days earlier. The 20% internet figure the resolution quotes is the ministry's own.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament requests the Ministry of Labor and Employment to establish a data banking system of all Bangsamoro workers, to be called the Bangsamoro Workers Information System (BWIS), subject to the Data Privacy Act of 2012 (Republic Act No. 10173).

Authored by MP Bai Maleiha B. Candao. Adopted on 22 July 2020.
readings.whyProposed: As of 2018, 48,300 overseas Bangsamoro workers came from the region, 2.1% of overseas Filipino workers. The resolution says most Bangsamoro labor migration stems from illegal recruitment, trafficking and abuse. A master list with workers' personal and family information, skills, occupation and destination would help the ministry design policies and track workers' safety and welfare.
whoIsAffected: Bangsamoro workers, including those overseas, whose personal data would be recorded.
implementedBy: Ministry of Labor and Employment
whatChanges: It is a request; it sets no deadline and provides no funds.
Any system must comply with the Data Privacy Act.
readings.insight: The resolution's case is about overseas workers, but its operative clause covers all Bangsamoro workers. Parliament later legislated: the Overseas Bangsamoro Workers Act (BAA 19), passed on 17 June 2021, provides a registry of qualified applicant workers and Bangsamoro officers in overseas labor offices who inventory workers. Resolution 47 (24 October 2019) had earlier asked OWWA for data on distressed Bangsamoro workers.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament expresses its support for dividing the Province of Maguindanao into Northern Maguindanao and Southern Maguindanao, as provided in House Bill No. 6413, approved by the House and sent to the Senate. A copy goes to Senate President Vicente Sotto III, for information.

Authored by MPs Mussolini S. Lidasan, Datu Tucao O. Mastura and Lanang T. Ali Jr. Adopted on 22 July 2020.
readings.whyProposed: The resolution recounts how Cotabato was divided in 1967 and 1973, creating Maguindanao, and how the ARMM's short-lived Province of Shariff Kabunsuan was struck down because only Congress can create provinces. House Bill No. 6413, a substitute for House Bills No. 3405 and 4840 by Representatives Esmael Mangudadatu and Datu Roonie Sinsuat, passed third reading on 1 June 2020 and reached the Senate on 3 June 2020. The authors say 2 provinces would bring political stability and more efficient delivery of services and aid.
whoIsAffected: Residents of Maguindanao, who would be split into 2 provinces.
implementedBy: Senate of the Philippines
whatChanges: It is an expression of support, sent for information; Parliament cannot divide a province itself.
The division would still need Congress to pass a law and, under the Organic Law clause it quotes, a plebiscite.
readings.insight: The resolution quotes the Organic Law's grant to Parliament of power over municipalities and barangays only; provinces remain with Congress, which is why the region could only lend support. The division did take place under different names: later resolutions in the index refer to Maguindanao del Norte and Maguindanao del Sur (for example Resolution 537, 17 February 2025).

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament requests the security sector in the most affected area, or ground zero, of Marawi City to prohibit visitors from treating it as a tourist spot, including taking selfies, groupies and other photos, or any other conduct that devalues what happened there and adds insult to the injury of Marawi's people. Copies go to the head of Task Force Bangon Marawi, the commander of the security sector, the Mayor of Marawi City and the Governor of Lanao del Sur.

Authored by MP Omar Yasser C. Sema. Adopted on 23 July 2020.
readings.whyProposed: Social media posts showed Task Force Bangon Marawi letting residents and visitors into the most affected area, and some visitors posting content that seemed to trivialize the siege, treating the ruins as 'a tourist spot akin to a post-apocalyptic theme park'. Parliament still values documentation of the rehabilitation, as a reminder to speed up rebuilding and reparation.
whoIsAffected: Residents of Marawi, especially those displaced from the most affected area.
Visitors to the area.
implementedBy: Task Force Bangon Marawi
Security sector in the most affected area
City Government of Marawi
Provincial Government of Lanao del Sur
whatChanges: It is a request; any ban would be up to the security sector and local officials.
deliberation: 23 July 2020: Approved subject to style on omnibus motion with Proposed Resolution No. 175 (the journal prints the pair as Nos. 57 and 176).
readings.insight: It is 1 of 3 Marawi resolutions adopted on 23 July 2020, with Resolution 85 on siege-related tax delinquencies and Resolution 86 mourning Fr. Teresito Suganob, a siege hostage. It does not ask for the area to be closed, only that visitors' conduct be policed, and it keeps room for documentation of the rehabilitation.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament requests the city government of Marawi to consider measures and other legal remedies to ease the burden of taxpayers who fell delinquent because of the Marawi siege. A copy goes to the Mayor of Marawi City for information and appropriate consideration.

Authored by MP Susana S. Anayatin. Adopted on 23 July 2020.
readings.whyProposed: The fighting between government forces and the Maute group began on 23 May 2017 and lasted 5 months, forcing about 300,000 people from their homes. With livelihoods destroyed, many residents could not pay their obligations to the city, particularly real property taxes and the penalties and surcharges on them.
whoIsAffected: Marawi property owners with real property tax arrears, penalties and surcharges from the siege period.
implementedBy: City Government of Marawi
whatChanges: It is a request; any relief would need action by the city government.
It does not name a specific remedy, such as condonation or waiver of penalties.
deliberation: 23 July 2020: Committee Report No. 29 amended the title to change 'CALLING' to 'REQUESTING' and delete the words 'REAL PROPERTY TAXES'.

23 July 2020: Approved subject to style with the committee's amendments changing 'CALLING' to 'REQUESTING' and deleting 'REAL PROPERTY TAXES' (the journal prints the number as 176 in the approval heading).
readings.insight: The resolution leaves the remedy to the city and gives no figure for the arrears or the number of taxpayers affected. It was adopted the same day as 2 other Marawi resolutions, 84 and 86.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament expresses its sympathy and sincere condolences to the family of Fr. Teresito 'Chito' Suganob, Vicar-General of the Prelature of Marawi, and to the Catholic community, on his death on 22 July 2020. A copy goes to his family.

Authored by MPs Ziaur-Rahman A. Adiong, Susana S. Anayatin, Mussolini S. Lidasan and Abdulraof A. Macacua. Adopted on 23 July 2020.
readings.whyProposed: Fr. Suganob served as Vicar-General of the Prelature of Marawi for 26 years and was known for work on peace, education and interfaith dialogue. He was held hostage by Abu Sayyaf and Maute fighters from 23 May to 16 September 2017 during the Marawi siege, and afterwards campaigned for the Bangsamoro Organic Law. Archbishop Emeritus Fernando Capalla called him the 'Martyr of Dialogue'. He died of cardiac arrest in his sleep in Norala, South Cotabato.
whoIsAffected: The family of Fr. Suganob and the Catholic community.
whatChanges: It is a condolence; a copy goes to the bereaved family.
deliberation: 23 July 2020: MP Mussolini S. Lidasan amended the first whereas clause to record that the Vicar-General died of cardiac arrest in Norala, South Cotabato on 22 July 2020; co-author MP Ziaur-Rahman Alonto Adiong accepted.
23 July 2020: Approved as amended, subject to style.
readings.insight: Parliament adopted it the day after his death. It was 1 of 3 Marawi-related resolutions adopted on 23 July 2020, with Resolutions 84 and 85.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament expresses its profound sympathy and condolences to the family of the late Undersecretary Dimasangcay Alangadi Pundato of the Office of the Presidential Adviser on the Peace Process. A copy goes to his family.

Authored by MP Ziaur-Rahman A. Adiong and 14 others. Adopted on 27 August 2020.
readings.whyProposed: Pundato was among the 'Top 90', the MNLF's first batch of foreign-trained fighters during martial law. He later led the Office on Muslim Affairs under Presidents Corazon Aquino and Fidel Ramos, served as OPAPP Undersecretary on Muslim Affairs under Presidents Gloria Macapagal Arroyo and Benigno Aquino III, and supported the passage of the Bangsamoro Organic Law. He died at his home in Marawi City on 13 August 2020.
whoIsAffected: Pundato's family.
whatChanges: It is a condolence; a copy goes to the bereaved family.
deliberation: 26 August 2020: Debate and amendments dispensed with; approved.
readings.insight: Adopted 14 days after his death, at the first session after it. It is 1 of 2 condolences in this period for figures of the peace process, with Resolution 86 for Fr. Teresito Suganob.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament condemns in the strongest terms the twin bombings in downtown Jolo, Sulu on 24 August 2020, and urges the Government of the Day to give immediate assistance to the families of those killed and to the wounded. Copies go to Chief Minister Ahod Balawag Ebrahim and Jolo Mayor Kerkhar Tan for information and appropriate consideration.

Authored by MP Hatimil E. Hassan and 13 others. Adopted on 27 August 2020.
readings.whyProposed: 2 explosions near the town plaza in Walled City, downtown Jolo, killed at least 14 people and injured at least 78, including soldiers. The first blast killed at least 5 soldiers and 4 civilians as troops helped municipal officials with COVID-19 relief; a second blast, as police cordoned off the site, killed 1 more. The resolution urges law enforcement to investigate and prosecute, and says government must act quickly when citizens are already burdened by the pandemic.
whoIsAffected: Families of those killed in the bombings and the wounded.
Residents of Jolo.
implementedBy: Office of the Chief Minister
Municipal Government of Jolo

funding.detail: The resolution appropriates nothing. It urges assistance to victims but names no amount or fund.

whatChanges: It urges the regional government to assist victims; it sets no amount, fund or deadline.
The call to investigate appears only in the WHEREAS clauses, not as a resolved action.
deliberation: 26 August 2020: Asked by MP Paisalin P. Tago what immediate assistance was possible, sponsor MP Amilbahar S. Mawallil hoped the Government of the Day would allot special funds or immediate cash aid.
26 August 2020: Period of debate closed and the resolution adopted.
readings.insight: The resolution was adopted 3 days after the attack. Its copies go only to the Chief Minister and the Mayor of Jolo, not to the police or military it asks to investigate. Parliament condemned later bombings in the region too: the December 2023 attack on a religious gathering at Dimaporo Gymnasium in Marawi (Resolution 420) and the May 2024 attack on a chapel in Cotabato City (Resolution 464).

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament strongly condemns the massacre of 9 civilians in Kabacan, Cotabato Province, and respectfully requests the Philippine National Police, the National Bureau of Investigation and the Commission on Human Rights to fast-track their investigations so the perpetrators can be brought to justice and punished. Copies go to the PNP Chief, the NBI Director and the CHR Chairperson.

Authored by MP Paisalin P. Tago and 25 others. Adopted on 17 September 2020.
readings.whyProposed: On 29 August 2020, 9 people, all identified as Bangsamoro, were shot dead on a provincial road in Kabacan by unidentified gunmen with high-powered weapons. The authors say the Organic Law, as an instrument of peace, can be sustained only if violence against civilians is answered with an impartial, swift and thorough investigation, and that the killing came while the nation should be united against COVID-19.
whoIsAffected: Families of the 9 victims.
Bangsamoro communities in Cotabato Province, outside the region.
implementedBy: Philippine National Police
National Bureau of Investigation
Commission on Human Rights
whatChanges: It is a condemnation and a request to national agencies; it sets no deadline and asks for no report to Parliament.
deliberation: 17 September 2020: MP Baintan A. Ampatuan asked about the status of the Ministry of Public Order and Safety investigation to avoid duplication; MP Mohagher M. Iqbal said Minister Hussein P. Muñoz was in Davao and had tested positive for COVID-19.

17 September 2020: MP Romeo K. Sema said the Chief Minister had already created an investigation team led by the Ministry and proposed retitling the resolution to support it so Parliament and the Chief Minister would not hold 2 positions.

17 September 2020: Author MP Paisalin P. Tago replied that a Bangsamoro investigation could be called biased after its condemnation statement and that the Bangsamoro Government had no jurisdiction over those involved outside BARMM.
17 September 2020: MP Mohagher M. Iqbal urged separating facts from allegations, citing reports that Muslims and Christians were sorted and the Muslims killed.

17 September 2020: MP Raissa H. Jajurie objected to the motion to approve, saying the Ministry's draft report had already gone to the Office of the Chief Minister; the Chair said the resolution concerned the NBI, PNP and CHR, not the Ministry.
17 September 2020: MP Jose I. Lorena amended the title to urge the PNP, NBI, CHR and Cotabato provincial government to investigate and bring the perpetrators to justice; MP Paisalin P. Tago accepted.
17 September 2020: Adopted unanimously as amended, subject to style.
readings.insight: Kabacan is in Cotabato Province, outside the region, so Parliament could only ask national agencies to act. The resolution names no victim and gives no motive. It followed Resolution 80 (16 July 2020) on killings of Moros in South Cotabato, and 2 months later Resolution 91 (17 November 2020) condemned the rape-slay of a 16-year-old girl in Kabacan.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament approves and adopts the interim composition of the Recruitment, Selection and Placement Boards (RSPBs) of the BTA's ministries, offices and agencies, until regular members qualify. The ministries continue hiring through these boards. Heads of office are to prioritize filling the positions whose holders are regular board members under civil service rules, and to reconstitute the boards once such personnel are hired. All ministries, offices and agencies must submit the composition of their boards to Parliament on or before 31 January each year. The resolution goes to all BARMM offices.

Authored by MP Akmad I. Abas and 71 others. Adopted on 28 October 2020.
readings.whyProposed: The Organic Law tasks the BTA with organizing the bureaucracy and a placement process for hiring during the transition. Under the Transition Plan's hiring guidelines, each ministry has its own RSPB to screen applicants. Ministries with approved staffing actions began hiring in January 2020 with interim boards. In Resolution No. 2000769 of 28 August 2020, the Civil Service Commission recognized the BTA's power to set board composition and applied, by analogy, the rules for local government units. The Office of the Chief Minister then submitted the interim compositions to Parliament.
whoIsAffected: Applicants for positions in the Bangsamoro Government.
Ministries, offices and agencies, whose hiring boards are confirmed.
implementedBy: Bangsamoro ministries, offices and agencies
Office of the Chief Minister
whatChanges: It gives Parliament's approval to the interim hiring boards so hiring can continue.
It sets a standing duty: every office reports its board composition to Parliament by 31 January each year.
readings.insight: The resolution approves compositions 'as hereunder approved', but the 2-page adopted text published by Parliament carries no list, so who sat on the boards cannot be read from it. It was adopted at a special session, with all 72 listed Members as principal authors. 4 months later the Bangsamoro Civil Service Code (BAA 17, 24 February 2021) set up Bangsamoro Promotion and Selection Boards in each agency.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament recognises and congratulates 19 Bangsamoro students who recently graduated abroad: 17 from Al-Azhar University in Cairo, 1 from the Canadian University in Dubai and 1 from Ain Shams University in Cairo. It commends them for the recognition their achievements bring the Bangsamoro and as an inspiration to its youth, and furnishes each named graduate an official copy.

Adopted on 17 July 2023.
readings.whyProposed: The WHEREAS clauses describe the 3 universities and list each graduate and degree. Most of the Al-Azhar degrees are in Islamic law, Usuluddin (major in Tafsir), Aqeedah, Islamic studies and Arabic, with single degrees in education, agriculture and Arabic-to-English translation; the Dubai graduate took engineering and the Ain Shams graduate a Bachelor of Laws.
whoIsAffected: The 19 graduates named in the resolution.
whatChanges: Each named graduate receives an official copy. Nothing else follows from it.
readings.insight:
Filed by MP Abdulkarim T. Misuari as Proposed Resolution No. 272 on 23 May 2023, deferred on 26 June 2023 and adopted 3 weeks later. The adopted text says Al-Azhar was founded "in the 1970s by the Fatimid Caliphate", a date the resolution's own reference to the Fatimids rules out; the slip is for the 970s.

Parliament commended a later cohort of 13 Al-Azhar graduates in Resolution No. 422 (15 January 2024) and 36 Islamic University of Madinah students in Resolution No. 437 (26 February 2024).

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament thanks President Ferdinand Romualdez Marcos Jr. for reappointing Carlito Guancing Galvez Jr. as chief of the Office of the Presidential Adviser on Peace, Reconciliation and Unity (OPAPRU) and for naming former officer-in-charge Isidro Purisima to a key post there, and commends Galvez for his continuing commitment to the Bangsamoro peace process. Copies go to the President, Galvez and Senior Undersecretary Purisima, for information.

Adopted on 17 July 2023.
readings.whyProposed: Malacañang reported on 26 June 2023 that Galvez, then officer-in-charge of the Department of National Defense since 9 January 2023, would return to head OPAPRU, with Purisima as its senior undersecretary. The resolution recounts Galvez's military career in Basilan, Sulu and Marawi, his medals, his role as peace adviser and COVID-19 vaccine czar under President Duterte, his part in the campaign for the Bangsamoro Organic Law and his seat on the Intergovernmental Relations Body.
whoIsAffected: Secretary Carlito G. Galvez Jr.
Senior Undersecretary Isidro Purisima.
whatChanges: Copies go to the Office of the President, Galvez and Purisima, for information. Nothing else follows from it.
readings.insight: Filed by MP Amilbahar S. Mawallil, MP Rasol Y. Mitmug Jr. and MP Susana S. Anayatin; the adopted text consolidates PR 341 (filed 27 June 2023) and PR 358. It is one of a series on Galvez: Resolution No. 280 (22 November 2022) thanked the President for appointing him, Resolution No. 299 (16 January 2023) for moving him to Defense, and this one for bringing him back. Resolution No. 548 (29 May 2025) later urged that he be kept, and Resolution No. 574 (29 April 2026) thanked him as former Secretary.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament honours the late Grand Mufti Sheikh Abuhuraira A. Udasan and extends its deepest condolences and appreciation for his contributions to the Bangsamoro region. The resolution is presented to his family.

Adopted on 17 July 2023.
readings.whyProposed: Udasan, the region's first Grand Mufti when the BARMM was established in 2019, died at his home in Lugay-Lugay, Barangay Bagua I, Cotabato City, on 3 July 2023, aged 81. Born on 3 March 1942 in what is now Datu Piang, Maguindanao del Sur, he studied comparative religion in Jerusalem in 1966 and at the Islamic University of Medina from 1967 to 1971. The resolution names him a co-founder of the Moro Islamic Liberation Front alongside Salamat Hashim, recalls his leadership of the Bangsamoro Darul Ifta', and credits his rulings that COVID-19 vaccines are permissible in Islam and do not break the fast with easing doubts about vaccination.
whoIsAffected: The Udasan family.
whatChanges: The resolution is presented to the family. Nothing else follows from it.
readings.insight: MP Baintan A. Ampatuan and 58 others are listed as authors, Chief Minister Ahod Balawag Ebrahim among them. The adopted text consolidates 4 proposals, PR 343, 350, 351 and 360, all filed on 17 July 2023 and adopted the same day.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament strongly condemns the burning of copies of the Holy Qur'an in Sweden during Eid al-Adha. It directs that the resolution be communicated to the Swedish authorities to press for a comprehensive response and the prevention of similar acts, and that a copy go to the Swedish Embassy in Manila, in Taguig.

Adopted on 17 July 2023.
readings.whyProposed: On 28 June 2023 a copy of the Qur'an was burned outside the Stockholm Central Mosque as Muslims marked Eid al-Adha. The resolution cites freedom of religion under the European Convention on Human Rights, the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, the 1987 Constitution and the Bangsamoro Organic Law, warns that such acts can incite hatred and violence, and in its WHEREAS clauses calls on Swedish authorities to investigate, prosecute and stop anti-Islamic acts carried out "under the pretext of freedom of expression".
whoIsAffected: Muslims in the region and abroad, as a statement of position.
whatChanges: A copy goes to the Swedish Embassy in Manila. The resolution has no force in Sweden; it records Parliament's position.
readings.insight: Filed by MP Abdulkarim T. Misuari and 26 others; the adopted text consolidates PR 352 (filed by Misuari on 3 July 2023) and PR 353. The demands for investigation and prosecution sit in the WHEREAS clauses; the operative part only condemns and transmits.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament directs the Ministry of Health to speed up processing and release of all benefits owed to health care and non-health care workers in the region's COVID-19 response, and sends it a copy for immediate action.

Adopted on 17 July 2023.
readings.whyProposed: The resolution lists 5 benefits: the Special Risk Allowance, the One COVID-19 Allowance (₱3,000, ₱6,000 or ₱9,000 a month by low, medium or high risk exposure), the Health Emergency Allowance that replaced it under Republic Act No. 11712, the 2022 Service Recognition Incentive of up to ₱20,000, and the 14th month pay. It states that eligible workers in the region still had not received them.
whoIsAffected: Health care and non-health care workers in the region's COVID-19 response who are still unpaid.
implementedBy: Ministry of Health
whatChanges: A directive to the Ministry of Health with no deadline and no report required.
readings.insight: The resolution does not say how many workers are unpaid or how much is owed. It began as PR 75, filed on 25 October 2022 by MP Hashemi N. Dilangalen and 11 others, which asked the ministry to release 3 allowances; it went through the Committee on Health (Committee Report No. 11) and came out 9 months later as a directive covering 5 benefits. Earlier, Resolution No. 155 (September 2021) asked the Office of the Chief Minister to assist frontline workers hospitalised with COVID-19.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament directs the ministries, offices and agencies of the region, the BTA's own offices included, to strictly follow and immediately implement Memorandum Order No. 285, Series of 2019, the Chief Minister's ban on single-use plastics. All officials and employees are to use reusable drinking containers, tumblers, mugs or biodegradable food packs; food concessionaires and caterers are reminded to serve food in paper, plant-based or reusable containers.

The Ministry of Environment, Natural Resources and Energy (MENRE) is to give Parliament an annual report on compliance, and the Bangsamoro Information Office is to produce information materials. Adopted on 18 July 2023.
readings.whyProposed: Chief Minister Ahod B. Ebrahim issued the order on 17 June 2019. More than 3 years on, the resolution says, bottled water, plastic bags, straws, cups, cutlery, Styrofoam and plastic containers were still served at meetings and seminars in the Bangsamoro Government Center, employee compliance was "virtually nil", and caterers were not complying either. It cites the Philippines as a large source of ocean plastic, an estimated 0.75 million metric tons a year.
whoIsAffected: Officials and employees of regional ministries, offices and agencies and of Parliament.
Food concessionaires and caterers serving government functions.
implementedBy: All ministries, offices and agencies of the region, including the BTA
Ministry of Environment, Natural Resources and Energy
Bangsamoro Information Office
whatChanges: A standing annual compliance report from MENRE to Parliament, with no first due date.
Information materials from the Bangsamoro Information Office.
A rule Parliament applies to its own offices as well as the executive's.
readings.insight: This is one of the few resolutions in the period that sets a recurring report, though it names no date for the first one and no penalty for non-compliance. Filed as PR 283 on 1 June 2023 by MP Mary Ann M. Arnado and 16 others, it was titled as "urging"; the adopted version "directs".

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament urges the Bangsamoro Government, through the Ministry of Health, to conduct a feasibility study on procuring low-cost, high-efficiency oxygen generators for the region's 27 hospitals. The resolution is forwarded to the ministry, for information.

Adopted on 18 July 2023.
readings.whyProposed: No hospital in the region can produce its own oxygen, the resolution says, and most sit in geographically isolated areas. Pressurised tanks come from Zamboanga City for Basilan, Sulu and Tawi-Tawi, from Cotabato or General Santos City for Maguindanao, and from Cagayan de Oro City for Lanao del Sur, over routes disrupted by roads, weather, sea conditions and insecurity; pandemic travel restrictions made supply harder still. On-site generation is presented as the global trend.
whoIsAffected: Patients needing oxygen in the region's 27 hospitals.
Hospital managers.
implementedBy: Ministry of Health
whatChanges: A request for a study, sent "for information", with no deadline and no report back to Parliament.
readings.insight: Filed by MP Kadil M. Sinolinding Jr. as PR 57 on 12 October 2022 and adopted 9 months later after Committee Report No. 12. It asks only for a study, names no budget and asks for no findings. The PDF Parliament posted for Resolution No. 368 carries a file name about these oxygen generators.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament strongly urges the Joint Body for the Zones of Joint Cooperation to immediately finalise the delineation and demarcation of the coordinates of Bangsamoro municipal and regional waters and of the Zones of Joint Cooperation in the Sulu Sea and Moro Gulf, under Section 4, Article III and Section 18, Article XIII of the Bangsamoro Organic Law. It asks the Bangsamoro chair of the Joint Body to update Parliament on the status and a roadmap to completion, and furnishes all members of the Joint Body a copy.

Adopted on 18 July 2023.
readings.whyProposed: The Organic Law sets municipal and regional waters at 15 and 19 kilometres from the low-water mark, and gives the region revenue from natural resources in its waters. The resolution cites PSA figures putting the region first in fisheries output in the 2nd quarter of 2022, at 28.6% of the national total, mostly aquaculture from Tawi-Tawi, Sulu and Basilan. A preliminary delineation had been made but not finalised, held up by boundary disputes between BARMM and non-BARMM local governments; the resolution argues the rest can be finalised without waiting for the disputed areas.
whoIsAffected: The regional government and coastal local governments, whose revenue powers depend on fixed water boundaries.
Fisherfolk in the Sulu Sea and Moro Gulf.
implementedBy: Joint Body for the Zones of Joint Cooperation
whatChanges: A request for a status update and roadmap from the Bangsamoro chair of the Joint Body, with no deadline.
Copies to all Joint Body members, for information.
readings.insight:
As filed on 26 September 2022 by MP John Anthony L. Lim, MP Jose I. Lorena, MP Nabil A. Tan and MP Paisalin P. Tago, PR 42 was addressed to the National Mapping and Resource Information Authority (NAMRIA). The adopted text retargets the Joint Body but keeps a description that fits NAMRIA, calling the Joint Body "the government agency responsible for providing public with mapmaking services and acting as its central mapping agency".

The issue goes back to Resolution No. 23 (31 July 2019), which called for the Joint Body to be constituted for the Sulu Sea alone.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament adopts the Nutritional Guidelines for Muslim Filipinos (NGMF), with their transliterated Islamic context and dialect versions, and institutionalises them in the region. The Ministry of Health and the Ministry of the Interior and Local Government are to lead implementation, and a copy goes to the Office of the Chief Minister and its agencies.

Adopted on 20 July 2023.
readings.whyProposed: The NGMF were launched in 2015 by the National Nutrition Council BARMM with the Darul-Ifta' and the Bureau of Madaris, adapting the national Nutritional Guidelines for Filipinos (revised in 2012) with an emphasis on halal food. The resolution reproduces all 10 messages, each paired with a verse of the Qur'an or a hadith, from eating a variety of foods to exclusive breastfeeding up to 6 months, iodised salt, limiting salty and fatty food and avoiding alcohol and smoking. It also cites the 10 Kumainments, translated into Yakan, Sama, Tausug, Meranaw and Maguindanaon, and aims to carry both down to local governments.
whoIsAffected: Families and local governments across the region.
Health and local government workers who deliver nutrition programmes.
implementedBy: Ministry of Health
Ministry of the Interior and Local Government
Office of the Chief Minister and its agencies
whatChanges: The guidelines become Parliament's stated policy for the region; no programme, timeline, budget or report is set.
readings.insight: As filed by MP Kadil M. Sinolinding Jr. on 31 May 2023, PR 280 "strongly urged" the government to institutionalise the guidelines; the adopted text has Parliament adopt them itself. Parliament's index records the adoption on 20 July 2023 but leaves the resolution number blank in the proposal's history.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament urges the Ministry of Basic, Higher, and Technical Education (MBHTE) to run an information campaign on Republic Act No. 11650, the national law on inclusion and services for learners with disabilities, especially for teachers and administrators. The resolution is forwarded to the ministry, for information.

Adopted on 20 July 2023.
readings.whyProposed: Republic Act No. 11650, signed on 11 March 2022, bars schools from refusing learners because of disability, requires services based on an Individualized Education Plan, and has DepEd and local governments set up at least 1 Inclusive Learning Resource Center in every city and municipality and a Child Find System. The resolution ties this to the Bangsamoro Education Code (Sections 52 and 59) and cites DepEd figures: 93,895 enrollees with disabilities in School Year 2021 to 2022, 74% below the pre-pandemic 360,879.
whoIsAffected: Learners with disabilities in the region's schools.
Teachers and school administrators.
implementedBy: Ministry of Basic, Higher, and Technical Education
whatChanges: A request to the MBHTE, with no deadline, no target audience size and no report back.
readings.insight: As filed on 28 June 2023, PR 345 would have directed teachers and administrators through the MBHTE to deepen their understanding of the law and implement it; the adopted text asks only for information dissemination. MP Baintan A. Ampatuan and 51 others are listed as authors. Parliament returned to the law in Resolution No. 480 (July 2024), asking DepEd to speed up its implementing rules, and in Resolution No. 404 (October 2023) on the Magna Carta for Persons with Disability.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament congratulates Carolyn O. Arguillas of MindaNews on receiving the 2023 Luxembourg Peace Prize for Outstanding Peace Journalism, and presents her the resolution.

Adopted on 20 July 2023.
readings.whyProposed: Arguillas was named the awardee on 13 June 2023, the first Filipino to receive it in the 11 years the Schengen Peace Foundation and World Peace Forum have given the prize. The resolution credits her coverage of the peace process between the government, the MILF and the MNLF, lists her degrees and national awards, among them the Catholic Mass Media Awards and the Jaime V. Ongpin Awards for Investigative Journalism, and says MindaNews under her leadership earned recognition over 2 decades for constructive coverage of peace efforts.
whoIsAffected: Carolyn O. Arguillas, the honoree.
whatChanges: The resolution is presented to the honoree. Nothing else follows from it.
readings.insight: Filed by MP Susana S. Anayatin as PR 356 on 14 July 2023 and adopted 6 days later. It is the registry's closest precedent for Resolution No. 395, on Press Freedom Day, later in 2023.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament urges the Government of the Day to institute preparatory measures for the impending El Niño, and forwards the resolution to the Office of the Chief Minister for information and appropriate action.

Adopted on 25 July 2023.
readings.whyProposed: PAGASA raised an El Niño Alert on 2 May 2023, forecasting an 80% chance that El Niño would emerge in June to August and persist into the 1st quarter of 2024. The resolution warns of dry spells, drought, losses in rice, corn and fish supply, and quotes a PAGASA official that Mindanao would be hit hardest, with "at least a thirty (35) percent" drop in rainfall. The DILG had already told local officials, including the BARMM interior minister, to prepare under Memorandum Circular No. 2023-065.
whoIsAffected: Farmers and fisherfolk.
Communities exposed to drought and water shortage.
implementedBy: Office of the Chief Minister
whatChanges: A general request to the regional executive; no specific measure, agency, deadline or report is named.
readings.insight: The rainfall figure appears in the adopted text as "thirty (35) percent", the word and numeral disagreeing. Filed by MP Baintan A. Ampatuan as PR 279 on 31 May 2023, it was adopted 8 weeks later, after the June to August window the resolution itself gives for El Niño's onset had begun.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament urges the National Commission on Muslim Filipinos (NCMF) and the Department of Health's Bureau of Quarantine (BOQ) to adopt mechanisms that reduce the burden on pilgrims from the island provinces in getting the vaccinations required for the Hajj. Copies go to both, for information.

Adopted on 25 July 2023.
readings.whyProposed: Saudi Arabia requires flu and meningococcal vaccination before issuing a Hajj visa. The NCMF buys the vaccines and the BOQ gives them, but in Western Mindanao only at its Zamboanga City station and only on set days, so pilgrims from Basilan, Sulu and Tawi-Tawi pay fare and lodging on top of the vaccine. On 9 May 2023, the first scheduled day, pilgrims who lined up from 7:30 in the morning were vaccinated only at 3 pm after the NCMF's supplier delivered meningococcal vaccines in unsealed boxes without ice packs and the BOQ waited for a new batch.
whoIsAffected: Hajj pilgrims from Basilan, Sulu and Tawi-Tawi.
implementedBy: National Commission on Muslim Filipinos
Department of Health, Bureau of Quarantine
whatChanges: A request to 2 national bodies, sent "for information", with no deadline or report.
readings.insight: The WHEREAS clauses propose a concrete fix: Ministry of Health staff vaccinating pilgrims in Rural Health Units at least a week before departure under the provincial health offices. The RESOLVED clause does not adopt it and gives the regional ministry no task. Filed by MP Don Mustapha A. Loong as PR 320 on 19 June 2023, and adopted the same day as Resolution No. 376 on the 2023 Hajj.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament requests the Office of the President to look into the irregularities during the 2023 Hajj in Saudi Arabia, and forwards the resolution to that office.

Adopted on 25 July 2023.
readings.whyProposed: About 200 Filipino pilgrims were reported stranded in Muzdalifah, near Mecca, on 28 June 2023, and others complained publicly to the National Commission on Muslim Filipinos (NCMF) about transport, food and accommodation. The NCMF, created under the Office of the President by Republic Act No. 9997 in 2010, runs the annual Hajj. The resolution calls for a probe of its logistics, coordination and monitoring, to feed into legislation on the pilgrimage.
whoIsAffected: Muslim Filipino pilgrims to the Hajj.
implementedBy: Office of the President
whatChanges: A request to the Office of the President, with no deadline or report back.
readings.insight: As filed on 14 July 2023, PR 359 asked the President to "conduct an investigation ... in aid of legislation"; the adopted text softens this to "look into". The NCMF and Hajj administration are national matters, so any inquiry rests with the President. MP Tawakal B. Midtimbang and 15 others are listed as authors. It was adopted alongside Resolution No. 375, on Hajj vaccination for island pilgrims.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament thanks President Ferdinand "Bongbong" Romualdez Marcos Jr. for committing in his 2023 State of the Nation Address to grant amnesty to MILF and MNLF members and for recognising the region's performance. It also thanks him for recognising the collaborative efforts of key groups and the support of the international community, reaffirms its support for his peace efforts and pledges to work with the national government. Copies go to the Office of the President, the Office of the Chief Minister and other relevant agencies.

The adopted text dates its adoption 25 July 2023; Parliament's index records 27 July 2023.
readings.whyProposed: In his address on 24 July 2023 the President put amnesty for MILF and MNLF members on his priority agenda, acknowledged the continued rehabilitation of Marawi City, and cited the partnership with the region on energy exploration. The resolution calls the amnesty promise a crucial step to trust and lasting peace and ties reintegration programmes to full decommissioning.
whoIsAffected: MILF and MNLF members eligible for amnesty.
whatChanges: Copies go to the President, the Chief Minister and other agencies. It asks nothing of them.
readings.insight:
The adopted text consolidates PR 367, 368 and 372, filed by MP Baileng S. Mantawil, MP Mary Ann M. Arnado, MP Susana S. Anayatin and MP Romeo K. Sema. Its adoption line reads 25 July 2023, a day before PR 372 was filed on 26 July per Parliament's index, which gives the adoption as 27 July.

It sits in a run on amnesty: Resolution No. 121 (March 2021) urged Congress to concur in the proclamations, Resolution No. 277 (November 2022) asked for a longer application period, and Resolution No. 561 (November 2025) found only about 1% of safe conduct passes issued to applicants.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament directs its Committee on Health to conduct an inquiry, in aid of legislation, into the framework strategy and implementation of all types of vaccination and the status of emerging and re-emerging diseases in the region. The resolution is forwarded to the Ministry of Health, for information.

Adopted on 27 July 2023.
readings.whyProposed: The region was reported to have the country's lowest vaccination rate. The resolution recalls the National Immunization Program, launched on 12 July 1976, the DOH's "PinasLakas" COVID-19 booster drive of 26 July 2022, and a national tally of 71.4 million fully vaccinated against a goal of 23 million more boosters for 50% coverage within the "first 100 days" of the Marcos administration. It says full face-to-face classes from November 2022 exposed pupils to COVID-19 and that the regional ministry must catch up with neighbouring regions.
whoIsAffected: Children, pregnant women and older people who depend on routine immunisation.
The Ministry of Health, as the subject of the inquiry.
implementedBy: Committee on Health
whatChanges: An inquiry by Parliament's own Committee on Health, which binds the committee; no deadline or report date is set.
readings.insight: As filed by MP Baintan A. Ampatuan on 20 September 2022, PR 18 directed the Ministry of Health to brief Parliament on vaccination. It went to the Committee on Health, which reported it out (Committee Report No. 16) as an inquiry for the committee itself, adopted 10 months after filing; by then its booster target, tied to the administration's "first 100 days", was long out of date. Parliament had asked the ministry about vaccines in Resolutions No. 107 (2021) and 212 (2022), and asked again in Resolution No. 455 (May 2024).

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament directs the Ministry of Health to report on the implementation of community-intended health projects, covering facilities, equipment, human resources, extension and outreach, and training. The report is to be submitted through the Secretary-General within 30 days of adoption, and the resolution is forwarded to the ministry.

Adopted on 27 July 2023.
readings.whyProposed: The WHEREAS clauses are framed around the COVID-19 emergency and the Bayanihan to Recover as One Act, citing rising cases and the economic toll on the region. Medical outreach, vaccination and maternal and child health programmes were programmed for implementation, and Parliament wanted to know how they were going.
whoIsAffected: Communities targeted by the ministry's outreach, vaccination and maternal and child health projects.
implementedBy: Ministry of Health
whatChanges: A report from the Ministry of Health to Parliament, through the Secretary-General, due within 30 days.
readings.insight: Unusually for this period, it sets a deadline: 30 days, which put the report due in late August 2023. The registry does not record whether it arrived. As filed by MP Baintan A. Ampatuan on 20 September 2022, PR 19 asked the ministry to fast-track these projects to ease the pandemic's burden; after Committee Report No. 17 it was adopted 10 months later as a reporting directive.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament thanks President Ferdinand Romualdez Marcos Jr. for appointing General Romeo Saturnino Brawner Jr. as Chief of Staff of the Armed Forces of the Philippines, and congratulates Brawner on the appointment. The resolution is presented to the Office of the President, for information.

Adopted on 14 August 2023.
readings.whyProposed: Brawner was appointed the 60th AFP Chief of Staff on 19 July 2023. The resolution lists his posts, including 65th Commanding General of the Philippine Army, commander of the 4th Infantry Division and of the 103rd Infantry Brigade after the 2017 Marawi siege, and AFP spokesperson; says he graduated 2nd in the "Makatao" Class of 1989 of the Philippine Military Academy and led efforts against hazing there; and credits his work in Marawi's rehabilitation and in securing the plebiscite on the Bangsamoro Organic Law.
whoIsAffected: General Romeo Saturnino Brawner Jr.
whatChanges: A copy goes to the Office of the President. Nothing else follows from it.
readings.insight: MP Susana S. Anayatin and 59 others are listed as authors; it was filed as PR 365 on 24 July 2023. Resolution No. 382, adopted the same day on Brawner's successor at the Army, says Brawner belonged to the PMA "Bigkis Lahi" Class of 1990, contradicting this resolution's "Makatao" Class of 1989; both readings were confirmed on the page images. It is one of several 2023 resolutions thanking the President for appointments, alongside Resolution No. 381 the same day.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament congratulates and commends Lieutenant General Roy M. Galido on his appointment as the 66th Commanding General of the Philippine Army, and presents him the resolution.

Adopted on 14 August 2023.
readings.whyProposed: Galido succeeded General Romeo Brawner Jr., newly named AFP chief. A member of the PMA "Bigkis Lahi" Class of 1990, he served in Mindanao from his lieutenant years with the 6th Infantry "Kampilan" Division, commanded the 40th Infantry Battalion and the 601st Infantry Brigade, led the 6th Infantry Division from August 2022 to January 2023, and then the Western Mindanao Command, which covers Zamboanga Peninsula, Northern Mindanao and the BARMM. The resolution cites campaigns against terrorism under him and the command's 93% Annual General Inspection score.
whoIsAffected: Lieutenant General Roy M. Galido.
whatChanges: The resolution is presented to the honoree. Nothing else follows from it.
readings.insight: Filed as PR 381 on 8 August 2023 by MP Baintan A. Ampatuan and 61 others, and adopted 6 days later together with Resolution No. 380 on Brawner. The 2 texts disagree on Brawner's PMA class: this one calls him Galido's batchmate in the "Bigkis Lahi" Class of 1990, while Resolution No. 380 places him in the "Makatao" Class of 1989.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament directs the Ministry of Health, in aid of legislation, to brief Parliament on the status and extent of dengue cases and deaths in the region and on its measures to prevent more cases. The resolution is forwarded to the ministry, for information.

Adopted on 14 August 2023.
readings.whyProposed: From January to June 2022 the region passed the epidemic threshold, with 966 dengue cases against 270 a year earlier, 258% higher, and 11 deaths against none in 2021; Maguindanao and Lanao del Sur had the most cases. The resolution cites the mandatory disease reporting law, Republic Act No. 11332, and says Parliament needs current figures to write policy.
whoIsAffected: Communities at risk of dengue, especially in Maguindanao and Lanao del Sur.
implementedBy: Ministry of Health
whatChanges: A request for a briefing, with no deadline or format.
readings.insight: Its figures stop at June 2022: PR 11 was filed by MP Baintan A. Ampatuan on 19 September 2022, went through Committee Report No. 10, was deferred on 26 July 2023, and was adopted almost 11 months after filing. Parliament had asked for a similar briefing nearly 4 years earlier, in Resolution No. 35 (18 September 2019), during the 2019 dengue outbreaks.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament respectfully urges Congress to create a lone congressional district for Cotabato City, and forwards the resolution to the Philippine Congress-Bangsamoro Parliament Forum, for information.

Adopted on 14 August 2023.
readings.whyProposed: Under the Constitution, a city of at least 250,000 people is entitled to its own representative. The 2020 census counted 325,079 in Cotabato City, yet Section 9 of Republic Act No. 11550 keeps it within the lone district of Maguindanao del Norte, although it is an independent component city, statistically independent and the regional centre. The resolution notes that several bills for a separate district had been filed by past and present representatives, recounts the city's history from the Sultanate of Maguindanao to its 1959 charter, and points to new malls, PC Hill and the Kalanganan Baywalk as signs of growth.
whoIsAffected: Residents of Cotabato City.
Voters in the rest of Maguindanao del Norte's district.
implementedBy: Congress of the Philippines
whatChanges: A request to Congress, sent only to the Congress-Parliament forum, for information. Only a national law can create the district.
readings.insight: The resolution's growth figures do not agree with each other: it projects an increase of 3,900 people a year, about 1.2% of 325,079, while also citing a 2.38% growth rate and saying the population would double by 2029. At 2.38% a year, doubling takes about 30 years. Filed by MP Lanang T. Ali Jr. as PR 39 on 26 September 2022 and adopted after Committee Report No. 20, almost 11 months later. The repo does not record whether Congress acted.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament requests the Ministry of Transportation and Communications (MOTC) and the Bangsamoro Airport Authority to work with the national agencies and international bodies to implement Muslim Mindanao Autonomy Act No. 324, the Tawi-Tawi Airport Act of 2015. The MOTC, its Air Transportation Services and the Airport Authority, with the DOTC, Air Navigation Services and the Civil Aviation Authority of the Philippines (CAAP), are to implement the Act; copies go to the DOTC, Air Navigation Services and CAAP so they can update the airport's code and location indicator with ICAO and IATA; and the MOTC is to tell all offices and the public the airport's new name.

Adopted on 15 August 2023.
readings.whyProposed: The ARMM Regional Legislative Assembly renamed Sanga-Sanga Airport as Tawi-Tawi Airport in an Act approved by Regional Governor Mujiv S. Hataman on 17 December 2015. Under the Bangsamoro Organic Law, ARMM laws stay in force unless inconsistent or repealed, and the resolution says this one is neither. The Bangsamoro Administrative Code gives the MOTC landside management of airports and the Airport Authority control of government airports in the region.
whoIsAffected: Travellers and agencies using the Tawi-Tawi airport.
Aviation agencies that hold the airport's name and codes.
implementedBy: Ministry of Transportation and Communications
Bangsamoro Airport Authority
MOTC Air Transportation Services
Civil Aviation Authority of the Philippines
Department of Transportation and Communications
Air Navigation Services
whatChanges: Regional bodies are asked to coordinate and announce the new name; national bodies receive copies so they can update codes, which the resolution cannot compel.
readings.insight: Nearly 8 years after the renaming law, the resolution implies the old name and codes were still in use. It addresses the Department of Transportation and Communications (DOTC), as Resolution No. 311 did, while Resolution No. 305 in January 2023 addressed the Department of Transportation (DOTr). As filed by MP Don Mustapha A. Loong on 21 June 2023, PR 332 addressed a "Civil Aviation Authority of the Bangsamoro"; the adopted text names the Bangsamoro Airport Authority instead.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament congratulates and commends Aminoddin Masbud Domado for ranking 6th in the 2023 Medical Technologists Licensure Examination, along with all Bangsamoro passers, for bringing pride and honor to the Bangsamoro people. A copy is to be presented to him.

Authored by MP Diamila D. Ramos and MP Ali Montaha D. Babao. Adopted on 18 May 2023.
readings.whyProposed: The Professional Regulation Commission and the Board of Medical Technology held the examination on 8 and 9 March 2023; on 14 March the commission announced that 4,714 of 6,165 examinees, or 76.46%, passed. Domado, 23, a Maranao whose parents come from Poona Bayabao-Ramain and Poona Bayabao-Masiu, graduated magna cum laude from Far Eastern University-Dr. Nicanor Reyes Medical Foundation and scored 91.40%. The resolution also notes his research on COVID-19, carbon credits, nutrition and the effect of computer gaming on adolescents.
whoIsAffected: Aminoddin Masbud Domado.
Bangsamoro passers of the 2023 medical technology board examination, who are commended but not named.
whatChanges: Nothing changes in law. This is a commendation.
A copy is presented to Domado.
readings.insight: The figures check: 4,714 of 6,165 is 76.46%. It was adopted 2 months after the results, on the same day as 3 other board-topnotcher commendations (Nos. 333, 334 and 335, all on the April 2023 civil engineering examination). It is the only resolution in the index on the medical technology examination. The adopted text is marked PR201.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament expresses its sympathies and condolences to the families of those who died when the passenger ship MV Lady Mary Joy 3 caught fire near Baluk-Baluk Island, Basilan. It urges the Office of the Chief Minister to give financial assistance to the victims, and sends a copy to the bereaved families.

Authored by MP Baintan A. Ampatuan. Adopted on 18 May 2023.
readings.whyProposed: The ship, built in 1990 and owned by Aleson Shipping Lines, left Zamboanga for Sulu at about 9 pm on 29 March 2023 and caught fire at about 10:40 pm off Hadji Muhtamad, Basilan, then drifted aground on Baluk-Baluk Island. The resolution counts 252 people aboard: 205 passengers, 35 crew, 4 Coast Guard sea marshals and 8 Army personnel. Citing the Philippine Coast Guard, it says 33 died, including 6 children and minors, 216 were rescued and 7 were still missing. Survivors said the fire began in an air-conditioned cabin and spread to the kitchen.
whoIsAffected: Families of the 33 people who died in the fire.
Survivors, whom the Chief Minister's office is urged to assist.
implementedBy: Office of the Chief Minister

funding.detail: The resolution appropriates nothing. It urges the Office of the Chief Minister to provide financial assistance but names no amount or source.

whatChanges: The Office of the Chief Minister is urged, not directed, to give financial aid; no amount, deadline or report-back is set.
A copy goes to the bereaved families. The text does not say a copy goes to the Chief Minister's office.
readings.insight: The resolution's own figures do not add up: 33 dead, 216 rescued and 7 missing make 256, against the 252 it says were aboard. The operative clause also calls the ship 'MV Lady Joy 3', dropping 'Mary'. It was adopted 7 weeks after the fire and is the only resolution in the index on it. The adopted text is marked PR216.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament commends Engr. Casmer Dilangalen for ranking 2nd in the April 2023 Civil Engineers Licensure Examination, for bringing pride and honor to the Bangsamoro people. A copy is to be presented to him.

Authored by MP Aida M. Silongan and 9 others. Adopted on 18 May 2023.
readings.whyProposed: Dilangalen, a Maguindanaon from Barangay Kayaga, Kabacan, North Cotabato, graduated magna cum laude in civil engineering from the University of the Philippines-Diliman in 2022. The resolution says the Professional Regulation Commission announced on 29 April 2023 that 5,887 of 16,936 examinees passed, and that he placed 2nd with a rating of 90.45%.
whoIsAffected: Engr. Casmer Dilangalen.
whatChanges: Nothing changes in law. This is a commendation.
A copy is presented to Dilangalen.
readings.insight: Parliament commended Dilangalen twice on the same day. Resolution No. 335, also adopted 18 May 2023 by a different author, commends him again together with the 10th placer, Mohaimen Hadji Omar Pasawilan, whom Resolution No. 333 had also commended separately that day. The 2 texts disagree on when the results came out: this one says 29 April 2023, No. 335 says 28 April. The adopted text is marked PR225.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament congratulates and commends Casmer Blah Dilangalen and Mohaimen Hadji Omar Pasawilan for ranking 2nd and 10th in the April 2023 Civil Engineers Licensure Examination, together with all Bangsamoro passers. A copy is to be presented to both as a token of recognition.

Authored by MP Diamila D. Ramos. Adopted on 18 May 2023.
readings.whyProposed: The examination was held on 23 and 24 April 2023 in 17 testing locations, and the Professional Regulation Commission announced on 28 April that 5,887 of 16,936 passed. Dilangalen, 22, a magna cum laude graduate of the University of the Philippines-Diliman from Kabacan, scored 90.45%; Pasawilan, 23, a cum laude graduate of the University of Southern Mindanao-Main from Matalam, North Cotabato, scored 89.30%.
whoIsAffected: Casmer Blah Dilangalen and Mohaimen Hadji Omar Pasawilan.
Bangsamoro passers of the April 2023 civil engineering examination, commended but not named.
whatChanges: Nothing changes in law. This is a commendation.
Copies are presented to the 2 honorees.
readings.insight: It duplicates 2 resolutions adopted the same day: No. 333 commends Pasawilan and No. 334 commends Dilangalen, both filed by MP Aida M. Silongan and 9 others. This one, by MP Diamila D. Ramos alone, honors both again. It dates the results to 28 April 2023, while No. 334 says 29 April. It places Kabacan in the Special Geographic Area of the region; No. 334 places it in North Cotabato. The adopted text is marked PR239.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament adopts its calendar of sessions for the Second Regular Session of the Second BTA Parliament. The session opens on 15 May 2023 and sits in 20 blocks, usually Monday to Thursday in the 3rd and 4th weeks of the month, from May 2023 to February 2024, ending with mandatory adjournment on 29 February 2024.

Authored by MP Sha Elijah B. Dumama-Alba, MP Raissa H. Jajurie, MP Anna Tarhata S. Basman, MP Mary Ann M. Arnado and MP Jose I. Lorena. Adopted on 18 May 2023.
readings.whyProposed: Parliament's rules (BTA Resolution No. 268) say regular sessions follow an annual calendar and that plenary sittings run Monday to Thursday in the 3rd and 4th weeks of the month unless Parliament decides otherwise. The resolution says a calendar guides members in their legislative and constituency work.
whoIsAffected: Members of Parliament and its secretariat.
Anyone who wants to follow or attend plenary sessions.
implementedBy: The BTA Parliament
whatChanges: Unlike most resolutions, this one binds Parliament itself: it sets the days plenary can sit for the session.
Between sitting blocks, Parliament is in recess unless it decides otherwise.
readings.insight: Counting the dates, the calendar sets 79 sitting days: 19 4-day blocks plus a 3-day block from 26 to 28 December 2023. It was adopted on 18 May 2023, the 4th day of the session it schedules. The rule it quotes says the regular session convenes on the 2nd Tuesday of the month after Eid'l Fitr, but the calendar opens it on Monday 15 May. It is part of an annual series: Resolution No. 300 amended the previous calendar, and Resolution No. 442 set the next one, also at 79 sitting days. The adopted text is marked PR243.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament commends the College of Law of Mindanao State University in Marawi City and Notre Dame University in Cotabato City for producing 46 new Bangsamoro lawyers in the 2022 Bar Examinations. Copies go to both universities and to the Lanao del Sur and Cotabato chapters of the Integrated Bar of the Philippines.

Authored by MP Abdullah B. Hashim. Adopted on 25 May 2023.
readings.whyProposed: The 2022 Bar Examinations, chaired by Associate Justice Alfredo Benjamin S. Caguioa, were held on 9, 13, 16 and 20 November 2022 at 14 local testing sites. Results released on 14 April 2023 showed 3,992 passers out of 9,183, or 43.47%. The resolution calls the 2 schools the region's only law schools and counts 19 passers from Mindanao State University and 27 from Notre Dame. It cites the Organic Law's priority on quality education and says more Bangsamoro lawyers will widen access to justice.
whoIsAffected: Mindanao State University College of Law and Notre Dame University.
Their 46 graduates who passed the 2022 bar.
whatChanges: Nothing changes in law. This is a commendation.
Copies go to the 2 universities and 2 Integrated Bar chapters.
readings.insight: The figures check: 19 and 27 make 46, and 3,992 of 9,183 is 43.47%. It is part of a yearly series: Resolution No. 243 credited the same 2 schools with 94 new lawyers in 2022, and Resolution No. 423 congratulated the 2023 passers. A month later Resolution No. 345 commended the same 2022 bar passers again, singling out the 14th placer. The adopted text is marked PR247.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament commends and congratulates Alnakran Abdilla of Tawi-Tawi and his team for winning bronze in men's beach volleyball at the 32nd Southeast Asian Games in Cambodia. It directs the Bangsamoro Sports Commission to provide incentives and continued support for Abdilla's athletic career, and sends copies to his family and the commission.

Authored by MP Amilbahar S. Mawallil and 57 others. Adopted on 25 May 2023.
readings.whyProposed: The Games ran from 5 to 17 May 2023 in Cambodia. On 16 May at Otres Beach, Sihanoukville, the Philippine team of Abdilla, Jaron Requinton, James Buytrago and Jude Garcia beat Vietnam 2-0 for bronze, the country's 3rd straight bronze in the event and its only volleyball medal at these Games. Abdilla, a member of the Philippine Air Force, won silver in indoor volleyball at the 2019 Games and bronze in beach volleyball in 2021. The resolution says it is appropriate to give commensurate incentives.
whoIsAffected: Alnakran Abdilla and his family.
The Bangsamoro Sports Commission, which is told to support him.
implementedBy: Bangsamoro Sports Commission

funding.detail: The resolution appropriates nothing. It directs the Bangsamoro Sports Commission to provide incentives but names no amount or source.

whatChanges: The Bangsamoro Sports Commission is directed to give Abdilla incentives and continued support. No amount, form or deadline is set.
Copies go to Abdilla's family and the commission.
readings.insight: Unlike most commendations, it carries a directive, but an open one: 'incentives and continued support' with no figure or report-back. It was adopted 9 days after the medal match, consolidates 2 proposals (PR255 and PR267), and has 58 authors. The other team members are commended but only Abdilla is offered incentives. Parliament had congratulated the Philippine delegation to the previous Games in Resolution No. 256 (July 2022).

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament congratulates and commends Nishrien Amatonding Barua, a graduate of Mindanao State University-Marawi, for ranking 5th with a rating of 91.40% in the March 2023 Licensure Examination for Professional Teachers, elementary level. A copy is to be presented to her.

Authored by MP Kadil M. Sinolinding Jr., MP Don Mustapha A. Loong and MP Abdullah B. Hashim. Adopted on 25 May 2023.
readings.whyProposed: The examination was held on 19 March 2023 and results came out on 19 May 2023: 24,819 of 60,896 elementary takers passed, a 40.76% rate. Barua, a Maranao from Malabang, Lanao del Sur, graduated magna cum laude from Mindanao State University-Marawi in 2022 and was 2012 valedictorian of Datu Timbul Ali Elementary School in Baloi, Lanao del Norte. The resolution cites the Organic Law's priority on quality education.
whoIsAffected: Nishrien Amatonding Barua.
whatChanges: Nothing changes in law. This is a commendation.
A copy is presented to Barua.
readings.insight: The figures check: 24,819 of 60,896 is 40.76%. It was adopted 6 days after the results, together with Resolution No. 340 for the same examination's top-10 finisher Al-Zaheer Adil Abubakar. This one consolidates 4 proposals (PR256, PR257, PR260 and PR269), and PR257 is also listed among the 3 consolidated into No. 340. Parliament returned to teacher topnotchers in Resolution No. 469 (June 2024).

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament congratulates and commends Al-Zaheer Adil Abubakar, a Notre Dame University graduate, for placing in the top 10 of the March 2023 Licensure Examination for Professional Teachers. A copy is to be presented to him.

Authored by MP Don Mustapha A. Loong, MP Abdullah B. Hashim and MP Diamila D. Ramos. Adopted on 25 May 2023.
readings.whyProposed: The Professional Regulation Commission announced the results on 19 May 2023. The resolution says Abubakar, 23, a cum laude graduate from Cotabato City, rated 90.40% and placed in the top 10 among 60,896 elementary-level examinees, of whom 24,819 passed. It cites the Organic Law's priority on quality education.
whoIsAffected: Al-Zaheer Adil Abubakar.
whatChanges: Nothing changes in law. This is a commendation.
A copy is presented to Abubakar.
readings.insight: It does not give his exact rank, only 'top 10'. It was adopted the same day as Resolution No. 339 for the same examination's 5th placer. It consolidates PR261, PR268 and PR257; PR257 also appears among the proposals consolidated into No. 339, so one proposal is credited to both.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament expresses its condolences to the families of 7 members of the Moro Islamic Liberation Front (MILF) killed in a raid on 18 June 2023, and joins their call for a fair, impartial and speedy investigation. It strongly condemns the raid and voices deep concern over reported excessive force and violations of the victims' rights.

The resolution is forwarded to the Office of the Chief Minister, the Office of the Presidential Adviser on Peace, Reconciliation and Unity (OPAPRU), the Commission on Human Rights and other relevant agencies for immediate attention and appropriate action. Authored by MP Baileng S. Mantawil and MP Mary Ann M. Arnado. Adopted on 19 June 2023.
readings.whyProposed: The raid took place in Barangay Damawato, Datu Paglas, Maguindanao del Sur. The resolution names the dead, aged 18 to 53, and says all died of gunshot wounds, and that the victims were reportedly handcuffed and killed in different places, including a mosque. It notes the raid came during decommissioning and normalization under the Comprehensive Agreement on the Bangsamoro, and that the victims had applied for amnesty. It does not say which agency conducted the raid.
whoIsAffected: The families of the 7 MILF members killed.
MILF members awaiting amnesty, whose protection the resolution invokes.
implementedBy: Office of the Chief Minister
Office of the Presidential Adviser on Peace, Reconciliation and Unity
Commission on Human Rights
whatChanges: The resolution goes to the Chief Minister's office, OPAPRU and the Commission on Human Rights for 'appropriate action'. It sets no deadline and asks for no report back.
It does not itself open an inquiry by Parliament.
readings.insight: Adopted the day after the raid. It condemns the raid without naming who carried it out. The amnesty the victims were awaiting came up again a month later, when Resolution No. 377 thanked President Marcos for his commitment to grant amnesty to MILF and MNLF members. The adopted text is marked PR308.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament congratulates the Ministry of Basic, Higher and Technical Education (MBHTE) for running the 2023 Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao Athletic Association (BARMMAA) Meet. A copy is to be presented to the ministry.

Authored by MP Baintan A. Ampatuan. Adopted on 21 June 2023.
readings.whyProposed: The ministry held the meet in Cotabato City from 25 to 29 May 2023 under the theme 'Sustaining the Gains of Peace and Unity Through Sports'. The resolution cites the Constitution and the Organic Law on youth, physical education and sports, notes the meet went ahead without incident despite bad weather from Super Typhoon Mawar, and says it introduced children and visitors to Cotabato City, which joined the region in 2019 and whose inclusion the Supreme Court upheld on 10 January 2023.
whoIsAffected: The Ministry of Basic, Higher and Technical Education.
whatChanges: Nothing changes in law. This is a congratulation to a Bangsamoro ministry.
A copy is presented to the ministry.
readings.insight: One of 3 resolutions on the 2023 meet by the same sole author, MP Baintan A. Ampatuan: this one for the organizer, No. 348 for the overall champion Cotabato City Schools Division and No. 349 for host Cotabato City. It gives no count of athletes or cost. The ministry's head, Minister Mohagher M. Iqbal, was congratulated separately 5 days later in Resolution No. 361. The adopted text is marked PR285.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament expresses condolences on the death of Tausug artist Rameer Amilasan Tawasil and commends his contributions to Bangsamoro culture and arts. It asks the Bangsamoro Commission for the Preservation of Cultural Heritage (BCPCH) to explore ways to preserve and promote his artistic legacy. The resolution is presented to his family, with copies to the BCPCH and other concerned agencies.

Authored by MP Amilbahar S. Mawallil, MP John Anthony L. Lim, MP Nabil A. Tan, MP Laisa M. Alamia, MP Don Mustapha A. Loong and MP Rasol Y. Mitmug Jr. Adopted on 21 June 2023.
readings.whyProposed: Tawasil died on 6 June 2023. The resolution credits him with mastery of the ukkil style in wood carving, brassware and textiles, a Zamboanga Hermosa award and a National Commission for Culture and the Arts travelling exhibition grant in 2003, exhibitions in Manila, Kuala Lumpur and Brussels, works in collections in Germany, Korea and the United States, and the 'peace dove' logo that earned him a Peace Citation Award in 2006.
whoIsAffected: Tawasil's family.
The BCPCH, asked to act on his legacy.
implementedBy: Bangsamoro Commission for the Preservation of Cultural Heritage
whatChanges: The BCPCH is asked to 'explore avenues' to preserve his work. No program, deadline or funding is set.
Copies go to his family, the BCPCH and other agencies.
readings.insight: Parliament came back to Tawasil 11 months later: Resolution No. 452 (May 2024) asked the BCPCH to lead a campaign to nominate him for the 2025 Order of National Artists. Neither resolution records what the commission did. This one was adopted 15 days after his death. The adopted text is marked PR290.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament expresses sympathy and condolences to the family of Pastor Troy Eric O. Cordero and recognizes his part in the region's peace and development and his service as settler communities' representative to the Bangsamoro Council of Leaders. A copy is to be presented to his family.

Authored by MP Suharto S. Esmael and 9 others. Adopted on 21 June 2023.
