readings.whyProposed: Chief Minister Ahod B. Ebrahim appointed Cordero, a lifelong Cotabato City resident, to the Council of Leaders on 20 February 2023 under the Organic Law. As chair of the Metro Cotabato and Suburbs Ministerial Fellowship, he campaigned for the Bangsamoro Basic Law and for Cotabato City's inclusion in the region in the 21 January 2019 plebiscite. He died on 4 June 2023.
whoIsAffected: Pastor Cordero's family.
The settler communities he represented on the Council of Leaders.
whatChanges: Nothing changes in law. This is a condolence.
A copy is presented to his family. The resolution does not address filling his Council of Leaders seat.
readings.insight: Cordero died about 3 and a half months after his appointment to the Council of Leaders. It consolidates 2 proposals (PR291 and PR306) and is the only resolution in the index on him.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament commends and congratulates the passers of the November 2022 Philippine Bar Examinations, especially the new Bangsamoro lawyers, singling out the 14th placer, Ar-Rashid Jammih Taradji. A copy goes to the new Bangsamoro lawyers, and the resolution is to be posted on Parliament's website.

Authored by MP Khalid M. Hadji Abdullah. Adopted on 21 June 2023.
readings.whyProposed: The Supreme Court released the results on 14 April 2023, almost 5 months after the last exam day: 3,992 of 9,183 examinees, or 43.47%, passed. Taradji, from Ateneo de Zamboanga University, placed 14th among the top 30. The resolution calls the bar arguably the hardest licensure examination in the country and says the new lawyers will inspire young Bangsamoro professionals.
whoIsAffected: Ar-Rashid Jammih Taradji.
New Bangsamoro lawyers from the 2022 bar, who are not named or counted.
whatChanges: Nothing changes in law. This is a commendation.
A copy goes to the new Bangsamoro lawyers, and the resolution is posted on Parliament's website.
readings.insight: It repeats ground covered a month earlier: Resolution No. 337 (25 May 2023) commended the Mindanao State University and Notre Dame law schools for 46 new Bangsamoro lawyers from the same examination, using the same 3,992 of 9,183 figures. This one adds the top placer, from a law school outside the region. It was adopted more than 2 months after the results. The adopted text is marked PR292.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament supports President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr.'s call to create District Engineering Offices of the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) in the region, and a DPWH Regional Office to supervise them. A copy goes to the Office of the President.

Authored by MP Baintan A. Ampatuan. Adopted on 21 June 2023.
readings.whyProposed: Severe Tropical Storm Paeng (Nalgae) hit Maguindanao del Norte, Maguindanao del Sur and Cotabato City on 27 October 2022, and the resolution lists 10 damaged crossings, including Labu-labu Bridge, whose loss kept medium and heavy vehicles from bringing relief. At a briefing on the storm, the President recommended a DPWH district office in the region so bridges and national roads could be repaired quickly. The resolution cites the Organic Law provision that the national government funds and builds national roads, bridges, flood control and similar works in the region, and argues district offices are needed in the other provinces too.
whoIsAffected: Communities cut off by damaged national roads and bridges.
The national DPWH, which would set up the offices.
implementedBy: Office of the President
whatChanges: Nothing is created by the resolution. It states support and sends a copy to the President, for information.
The operative clause ends 'for consideration and approval of the BTA Parliament', which reads as though Parliament itself must still approve the offices.
readings.insight: It reverses an earlier position: in Resolution No. 37 (September 2019) Parliament objected to a House resolution calling for a national DPWH office in the region. Later resolutions such as No. 425 (January 2024) asked the national DPWH directly to repair the region's highways and bridges. Its proposal number, PR109, sits just below the PR110 to PR119 run of Paeng thank-you resolutions adopted in December 2022; this one was adopted 6 months after them. Of its '10 bridges', one is listed as Sarakan Street.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament congratulates Atty. Allan Gani Panolong on his election as Executive Vice President of the Integrated Bar of the Philippines (IBP). The resolution is presented to his office.

Authored by MP Rasol Y. Mitmug Jr., MP Mary Ann M. Arnado and MP Khalid M. Hadji Abdullah. Adopted on 22 June 2023.
readings.whyProposed: On 22 May 2023 the IBP Board of Governors elected Panolong, then president of the IBP Lanao del Sur Chapter and Governor for Western Mindanao. Under the IBP by-laws the Executive Vice President becomes President in the next term, so he is due to lead the IBP in 2025, which the resolution says will make him the first Muslim Bangsamoro to head it. He is a former board member for Lanao del Sur's 2nd district.
whoIsAffected: Atty. Allan Gani Panolong.
whatChanges: Nothing changes in law. This is a congratulation.
The resolution is presented to Panolong's office.
readings.insight: It consolidates 3 proposals (PR273, PR284 and PR293) and is the only resolution in the index on the Integrated Bar leadership. It was adopted a month after the election.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament congratulates the Cotabato City Schools Division Office for winning overall champion at the 2023 Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao Athletic Association (BARMMAA) Meet. A copy is to be presented to the division office.

Authored by MP Baintan A. Ampatuan. Adopted on 22 June 2023.
readings.whyProposed: The meet ran in Cotabato City from 25 to 29 May 2023 with 21 sports and 11 schools divisions from across the region. The Cotabato City division won 67 gold, 54 silver and 47 bronze medals and a cash prize of ₱150,000. The resolution cites the Constitution and the Organic Law on sports and youth.
whoIsAffected: Cotabato City Schools Division Office and its athletes.
whatChanges: Nothing changes in law. This is a congratulation.
A copy is presented to the division office.
readings.insight: The ₱150,000 cash prize mentioned is the meet's own award, not money from this resolution. It is one of 3 resolutions on the 2023 meet by MP Baintan A. Ampatuan, with No. 342 for the organizing ministry and No. 349 for the host city; Nos. 348 and 349 were adopted the same day. The adopted text is marked PR286.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament congratulates and thanks the local government of Cotabato City for hosting the 2023 Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao Athletic Association (BARMMAA) Meet. The resolution is presented to the city government.

Authored by MP Baintan A. Ampatuan. Adopted on 22 June 2023.
readings.whyProposed: The 5-day meet, held from 25 to 29 May 2023 with 21 sports and 11 divisions, passed without untoward incident, the resolution says, thanks to city security forces and police patrols, and went ahead despite the threat of Super Typhoon Mawar. It credits the event with showing off Cotabato City, the region's seat of government, which joined the region in 2019.
whoIsAffected: The city government of Cotabato City.
whatChanges: Nothing changes in law. This is a congratulation.
The resolution is presented to the city government.
readings.insight: One of 3 resolutions on the same meet by MP Baintan A. Ampatuan: No. 342 thanks the organizer, the education ministry; No. 348 the champion division; this one the host city. Its 'Whereas' clauses on law and sports are largely shared with No. 348. The adopted text is marked PR287.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament congratulates President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan on winning the 2023 Türkiye presidential election. A copy is to be presented to the Office of the President of Türkiye through its embassy in Manila.

Authored by MP Ahod Balawag Ebrahim and 41 others. Adopted on 22 June 2023.
readings.whyProposed: The resolution recalls Türkiye's role in the peace process: a 2014 visit by its Prime Minister to Manila, membership of the International Contact Group in the government-MILF talks, of the Independent Decommissioning Body, and of the Third-Party Monitoring Team. Erdoğan took 49.52% in the first round on 14 May 2023 and won the 27 May run-off with 52.14% to 47.86%, for a 5-year term to 2028.
whoIsAffected: President Erdoğan and the Turkish government.
whatChanges: Nothing changes in law. This is a congratulation to a foreign head of state.
A copy goes to the Turkish embassy in Manila.
readings.insight: One of 3 Türkiye resolutions in 2023: No. 316 (February) offered condolences after the earthquake, and No. 410 (October) marked the republic's 100th anniversary. The run-off figures add to 100%; the resolution says 99.43% of votes had been counted when they were announced. It has 42 authors, led by Chief Minister Ahod Balawag Ebrahim. The adopted text is marked PR289.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament thanks President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. for appointing Suharto T. Mangudadatu as the 14th Director General of the Technical Education and Skills Development Authority (TESDA), and congratulates Mangudadatu. Copies go to both as a token of appreciation.

Authored by MP Diamila D. Ramos and 14 others. Adopted on 22 June 2023.
readings.whyProposed: The President appointed Mangudadatu on 8 June 2023. The resolution lists his posts in Sultan Kudarat: Mayor of Lutayan from 1998 to 2004, Representative of the lone district from 2004 to 2007, and Governor from 2019 to 2022. It calls him a Bangsamoro leader and says his appointment matters for the region's development.
whoIsAffected: TESDA Director General Suharto T. Mangudadatu.
President Marcos, thanked for the appointment.
whatChanges: Nothing changes in law. This is an expression of thanks and congratulations.
Copies go to the President and to Mangudadatu.
readings.insight: It consolidates 3 proposals (PR296, PR301 and PR302) and has 15 authors. It was adopted 2 weeks after the appointment and the same day as Resolution No. 353, another congratulation on a presidential appointment. Sultan Kudarat, where Mangudadatu served, is outside the Bangsamoro region.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament requests the Judicial and Bar Council (JBC) to extend, for Muslim applicants, the deadline for applications and documents for judgeships in Regions IX to XII to 4 August 2023. The resolution is forwarded to the JBC for consideration.

Authored by MP Sha Elijah B. Dumama-Alba. Adopted on 22 June 2023.
readings.whyProposed: The JBC opened applications for these judgeships on 19 May 2023 with a 4 July 2023 deadline. That window overlapped with the Hajj, which the resolution dates from 19 June to 18 July 2023; pilgrims spend about a month in Mecca and would miss the deadline. The resolution cites the JBC rule allowing extensions for justifiable reasons, and the Supreme Court's view that religious freedom holds a preferred position.
whoIsAffected: Muslim lawyers applying for judgeships in Regions IX to XII who are performing the Hajj.
The Judicial and Bar Council.
implementedBy: Judicial and Bar Council
whatChanges: The JBC receives a request. Parliament has no authority over it, and the decision stays with the JBC.
It asks for a separate deadline for Muslim applicants, not a general extension.
readings.insight: The requested date sits just outside the rule the resolution itself cites: JBC extensions may not exceed 30 calendar days from the original deadline, and 4 August is 31 days after 4 July. It was adopted 3 days after the Hajj began. The repo does not record the JBC's answer. Parliament later wrote to the JBC again, in Resolution No. 516 (January 2025), on vacant Shari'ah District Court judgeships. The adopted text is marked PR298.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament congratulates former Congressman Mohammed Hussein P. Pangandaman on his appointment by President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. as Administrator of the Authority of the Freeport Area of Bataan (AFAB). A copy is to be presented to his office.

Authored by MP Baintan A. Ampatuan and 10 others. Adopted on 22 June 2023.
readings.whyProposed: Pangandaman served as Representative of the 1st District of Lanao del Sur. The resolution says his political experience and leadership record make him an excellent choice for AFAB, which is charged with developing a freeport in Bataan.
whoIsAffected: AFAB Administrator Mohammed Hussein P. Pangandaman.
whatChanges: Nothing changes in law. This is a congratulation.
A copy is presented to Pangandaman's office.
readings.insight: It has 3 'Whereas' clauses and gives no date for the appointment. It has 11 authors, led by MP Baintan A. Ampatuan. It was adopted the same day as Resolution No. 351, thanking the President for another appointment, Suharto T. Mangudadatu at TESDA. The adopted text is marked PR300.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament expresses condolences to the family of Hadji Abdullah 'Bobby Buldon' Pacasem and thanks him for his contributions to the Bangsamoro struggle and the Bangsamoro region. The resolution is presented to his family.

Authored by MP Ahod Balawag Ebrahim and 76 others. Adopted on 22 June 2023.
readings.whyProposed: Pacasem, described as one of the 'Top 300' of the MILF and the MNLF, fought alongside MILF founding chairman Hashim Salamat, sat on the MILF Central Committee and headed its Central Research Agency. He died at home in Parang, Maguindanao del Norte, on 20 June 2023. The resolution names his wife and 11 children.
whoIsAffected: Pacasem's family.
whatChanges: Nothing changes in law. This is a condolence.
The resolution is presented to his family.
readings.insight: Adopted 2 days after his death, with 77 authors. The children it lists include Atty. Ubaida C. Pacasem, which is also the name of a sitting MP who co-authored other resolutions of this period, such as No. 334; that name is not among this resolution's authors. The adopted text is marked PR337.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament expresses its 'strong sense and resolve' that President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. grant executive clemency to former ARMM and Maguindanao Governor Datu Zacaria Candao and former Bangsamoro Development Agency chair Dr. Abas Candao. The resolution is forwarded to the Office of the President, for information.

Authored by MP Ahod Balawag Ebrahim and 19 others. Adopted on 22 June 2023.
readings.whyProposed: The resolution credits Zacaria Candao as an MNLF legal officer from 1974 and negotiator of the 1976 Tripoli Agreement, later MILF legal counsel and adviser to its chairmen, the first elected ARMM Governor in 1990 and a figure in starting the government-MILF talks in 1997. It says both men were listed in military orders of battle and a 2000 intelligence report as MILF supporters. It states plainly that they were accused of corruption in 1994 and convicted in 2008, and that they are considered fugitives from justice, but argues that at 80 and 77 they qualify for clemency on humanitarian grounds and that clemency fits the spirit of the Comprehensive Agreement on the Bangsamoro.
whoIsAffected: Datu Zacaria Candao and Dr. Abas Candao.
The President, whose sole discretion the resolution acknowledges.
implementedBy: Office of the President
whatChanges: The President receives an expression of Parliament's view. Clemency is his alone to grant, as the resolution itself says.
It does not describe the 2008 conviction or say what sentence is outstanding.
readings.insight: Parliament repeated the appeal 4 months later: Resolution No. 413 (24 October 2023) asked specifically for an absolute pardon and added Israel Haron. The text quotes the Constitution that clemency comes 'after conviction by final judgment' while describing the 2 men as fugitives. It has 20 authors, led by Chief Minister Ahod Balawag Ebrahim and including Speaker Pangalian M. Balindong. The adopted text is marked PR335.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament urges the concerned Bangsamoro ministries and local governments to provide housing for people in the region left homeless by Typhoon Paeng. A copy goes to them, for information.

Authored by MP Susana S. Anayatin. Adopted on 22 June 2023.
readings.whyProposed: The resolution says Severe Tropical Storm Paeng, on 31 October 2022, affected 1,193,961 people, or 244,050 families, in the region. It lists affected areas: 5 municipalities in Basilan, 6 in Lanao del Sur, 31 across the 2 Maguindanao provinces, 1 in Sulu, Bongao in Tawi-Tawi, Cotabato City and 63 barangays of the Special Geographic Area. It cites the Organic Law's housing provisions, the Ministry of Human Settlements and Development's mandate, the national Pambansang Pabahay program and the Chief Minister's KAPYANAN housing program.
whoIsAffected: Families left homeless by Paeng in the region.
Bangsamoro ministries and local governments asked to house them.
implementedBy: Ministry of Human Settlements and Development
Concerned Bangsamoro ministries
Local government units in affected areas

funding.detail: The resolution appropriates nothing. It notes that some agencies' settlement projects already have appropriations but names no amount.

whatChanges: Ministries and local governments are urged to provide housing. No ministry is named in the operative clause, and there is no target, deadline or report-back.
It does not say how many people were left homeless.
readings.insight: Its figures differ from Parliament's other Paeng resolutions. It dates the storm to 31 October 2022, while Resolution No. 346, adopted the day before, says 27 October. Its count of 1,193,961 people affected is about twice the 570,285 in the December 2022 thank-you resolutions (Nos. 283 to 292). It was adopted about 8 months after the storm. Its proposal number, PR101, is lower than those of the Paeng thank-you resolutions (PR110 to PR119) adopted in December 2022.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament congratulates and commends Dr. Mohammad Salih A. Nur for receiving the Outstanding Distinction Award at the University of Oklahoma's 2023 commencement. The resolution is presented to him.

Authored by MP Kadil M. Sinolinding Jr. Adopted on 26 June 2023.
readings.whyProposed: Nur, a Maguindanaon from Datu Odin Sinsuat, Maguindanao del Norte, graduated summa cum laude in Doctor of Physical Therapy studies from the University of Oklahoma. The resolution says the award, which he received at the 131st commencement on 10 May 2023, is the university's highest academic honor for professional degree graduates.
whoIsAffected: Dr. Mohammad Salih A. Nur.
whatChanges: Nothing changes in law. This is a commendation.
The resolution is presented to Nur.
readings.insight: It is the only resolution in the index on the honoree. The adopted text is marked PR248, next to the PR247 of Resolution No. 337, which was adopted a month earlier.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament condemns 'in the strongest possible terms' the practice of some vendors at the General Santos City Public Market of coating tuna with pig's blood to make it look fresh. The resolution is forwarded to the General Santos City government for information and appropriate action.

Authored by MP Baintan A. Ampatuan. Adopted on 26 June 2023.
readings.whyProposed: On 15 May 2023 the General Santos City Market Vendors' Association found vendors selling tuna slices thinly coated with pig's blood; packs of blood were seized, and the city ordered 4 stalls closed pending disciplinary proceedings. The resolution says pork and its derivatives are forbidden to Muslims, so the practice both deceives buyers and makes the fish unfit for Muslim consumers, including those from the Bangsamoro region. It cites the Constitution's guarantees of human dignity and religious freedom and the Consumer Act.
whoIsAffected: Muslim consumers who bought tuna at the market.
The vendors involved.
implementedBy: City Government of General Santos
whatChanges: Nothing changes in law. The city government, which is outside the region and had already closed the stalls, receives a copy for 'appropriate action'.
readings.insight: It has a twin adopted the same day by the same sole author, MP Baintan A. Ampatuan: Resolution No. 359 urges the Bangsamoro Human Rights Commission and trade ministry to seek justice for affected consumers. Together they are the only resolutions in the index on the incident. The adopted text is marked PR275.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament urges the Bangsamoro Government, through the Bangsamoro Human Rights Commission (BHRC) and the Ministry of Trade, Investment and Tourism (MTIT), to bring justice to Muslim consumers affected by vendors at the General Santos City Public Market who coated tuna with pig's blood. Copies go to both offices for information and appropriate action.

Authored by MP Baintan A. Ampatuan. Adopted on 26 June 2023.
readings.whyProposed: The facts repeat those of Resolution No. 358: on 15 May 2023 vendors were caught selling tuna coated with pig's blood, and 4 stalls were closed pending disciplinary proceedings. This resolution adds that an investigation is needed to protect religious freedom, recommend prosecution of those responsible and prevent a repeat, and that the BHRC and MTIT are the bodies to act.
whoIsAffected: Muslim consumers, including those from the region, who bought the tuna.
The BHRC and MTIT, asked to act.
implementedBy: Bangsamoro Human Rights Commission
Ministry of Trade, Investment and Tourism
whatChanges: The BHRC and MTIT are urged to act. No deadline, inquiry or report to Parliament is set.
The resolution does not say how either body could act in General Santos City.
readings.insight: General Santos City is not part of the Bangsamoro region, and the Organic Law power the resolution quotes is limited to the region's territorial jurisdiction; the text does not explain how a Bangsamoro commission or ministry would pursue vendors there. It is the companion to Resolution No. 358, adopted the same day by the same author. The adopted text is marked PR276.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament commends and congratulates Rayhanah Nuestro Decampong for placing 2nd in the May 2023 Certified Public Accountant Licensure Examination, and all Bangsamoro passers. A copy is to be presented to her.

Authored by MP Kadil M. Sinolinding Jr., MP Diamila D. Ramos and MP Khalid M. Hadji Abdullah. Adopted on 26 June 2023.
readings.whyProposed: The resolution says 2,239 of 7,376 examinees, or 30.36%, passed, and that Decampong, a Meranaw from Bayang, Lanao del Sur, and a De La Salle University-Manila graduate, placed 2nd with a general average of 89.33%.
whoIsAffected: Rayhanah Nuestro Decampong.
New Bangsamoro CPAs, commended but not named.
whatChanges: Nothing changes in law. This is a commendation.
A copy is presented to Decampong.
readings.insight: The figures check: 2,239 of 7,376 is 30.36%. It consolidates 3 proposals (PR281, PR288 and PR294). CPA topnotchers are a recurring subject: Resolution No. 257 (July 2022), No. 400 (October 2023) and No. 468 (June 2024) honor others.

readings.whatItDoes:
Parliament congratulates Minister of Basic, Higher and Technical Education Mohagher M. Iqbal on receiving an honorary Doctor of Philosophy in Public Administration, conferred under Commission on Higher Education (CHED) en banc Resolution No. 093-2023. The resolution is presented to his office.

Authored by MP Susana S. Anayatin and MP Eddie M. Alih. Adopted on 26 June 2023.
readings.whyProposed: Cotabato State University awarded the degree on the recommendation of its faculty and with the authority of its Board of Regents and CHED. The resolution lists Iqbal's awards and his career: propaganda chair of the Kutawato Revolutionary Committee from 1973, MILF Central Committee member since 1979, chair of the MILF peace panel since 2003, chair of the Bangsamoro Transition Commission from 2013 to 2016, MP since 2019 and education minister. It names 3 books he wrote.
whoIsAffected: Minister Mohagher M. Iqbal.
whatChanges: Nothing changes in law. This is a congratulation to a sitting MP and minister.
The resolution is presented to his office.
readings.insight: The text gives 2 dates for the same degree: 17 May 2023 in the first 'Whereas' clause and 17 June 2023 in its list of awards. Its list also includes the 2021 Saceda Youth Lead 'Most Inspiring Teacher' award twice. The title says CHED conferred the degree; the body says Cotabato State University did. Iqbal, a Member of Parliament, is not among the authors; 5 days earlier Resolution No. 342 congratulated his ministry on the 2023 BARMMAA Meet. The adopted text is marked PR338.
